title: Schematic/PCB connectivity identical (both boards)
claim: Partition comparison ignoring names: cur_db 284/284 groups identical (338 parts, 1078 pins), ord_db 269/269 (310 parts, 1015 pins). Values, footprints and LCSC fields match. The repo claim of 0 differences holds.
evidence: work/B01.../parity.py, cur_db_parity.txt, ord_db_parity.txt
suggested_fix: None.

title: 54 (cur) / 57 (ord) net_conflicts are NC pins, not connectivity
refs: U1 x21, U102 x17, U12 A1/A4, U13 5Y/6Y, U14/U3 NC+PG, U6/U7 NC, J3/J102 SWO
claim: Every net_conflict reads 'Pad missing net given by schematic (unconnected-(REF-PIN-PadN))'. Each is a single-pin net flagged no-connect in the schematic and a netless pad on the PCB. It is a name difference only.
evidence: drc_kicad9.json schematic_parity; parity.py name categories {unconnected single pin vs no net: 54/57}
suggested_fix: None; optionally mark the pads NC in the PCB.

title: Parity footprint_symbol_mismatch x6 benign
claim: The footprints carry exclude_from_bom and exclude_from_pos (Tag-Connect pads, M3 holes). The symbols do not. The flags are correct, since no part is placed or fitted.
evidence: pcb_footprints.csv exclude_from_bom=1; J3/J102/H1 absent from fab BOM/CPL
suggested_fix: None.

title: DRC: 199 lib_footprint_issues are tool artefacts
claim: The messages say the stock footprint libraries (Resistor_SMD, Capacitor_SMD and others) are not in the KiCad 9 configuration. The footprints are embedded in the PCB, so this is not a design fault. The repo's own report has the same per-library counts.
evidence: drc_kicad9.json; fab_drc_report.txt
suggested_fix: None.

title: DRC has zero clearance/hole/mask/unconnected violations
claim: A severity-all KiCad 9 run reports only courtyards_overlap (error) and silk or library warnings. There are no clearance, hole, mask-bridge, edge or unconnected items. The same totals (495 and 474) appear in the repo's own report.
evidence: drc_kicad9.json types counter; fab_drc_report.txt
suggested_fix: None.

title: Courtyard overlaps (101 cur / 91 ord) real but JLC-placeable
claim: All are small top-side passives, diodes and SOT parts. Exact pad-to-pad gaps are at least 0.200 mm (0805/0805 R51/R52 etc.) and typically 0.2-0.3 mm. Applying the repo's JLC spacing table (0.18, 0.2, 0.25, 0.4 mm by package pair) gives 0 violations, with a minimum margin of 0.006 mm. Approximate F.Fab body gaps are 0 to 0.1 mm for D37/D36, D41/U101, D40/C105, U13/C66, C104/R109 and U7/U6.
evidence: work/B01.../exact.py, spacing.py, cur_court.json; jlc_spacing.py table
suggested_fix: Nothing required for assembly. The JLC article was not re-fetched, so confirm in JLC's DFM preview whether D37/D36 and D41/U101 bodies touch.

title: ERC: 5 power_pin_not_driven errors are missing PWR_FLAGs
claim: The schematic has no PWR_FLAG. These nets are fed through a ferrite, inductor, fuse or GND, so they have no POWER_OUT pin. Each net does have a real source, so this is an artefact.
evidence: erc_kicad9.json; own_erc.py section 4; grep PWR_FLAG = 0
suggested_fix: Add PWR_FLAG symbols if a clean ERC is wanted (cosmetic).

title: ERC: 986 library warnings are artefacts; no pin-conflict, duplicate-ref, label or unconnected-pin findings
claim: 646 symbol and 340 footprint library warnings come from libraries missing in the KiCad 9 configuration. ERC reports no pin-type conflict, duplicate reference, dangling label or unconnected pin. Every NC pin carries a flag.
evidence: erc_kicad9.json type counter; own_erc.py sections 1,2,6-9
suggested_fix: None.

title: Unused logic inputs and open-collector outputs handled
refs: U12 B1/B4 pins 21,18; U13 5A/6A pins 11,13; U9 OUT_A/B
claim: Unused level-shifter and inverter inputs are tied to GND. The 74HCT04 unused outputs are open, which is fine. The LM2903 outputs have pull-ups (R55/R77, R60/R78). Checked and correct.
evidence: pcb_nets.txt; own_erc.py section 12
suggested_fix: None.

title: Schematic vs PCB connectivity identical on all 9 motherboards
claim: Net-partition comparison (names ignored) of sch_netlist.xml vs pcb_nets.txt/pcb_pads.csv finds 0 differences on 4 current and 5 ordered boards; 0 value/footprint diffs. KiCad parity issues are artefacts.
evidence: work/B02.../partition_out.txt; groups 87/110/96/103 and 84/80/110/96/103 equal
suggested_fix: None.

title: Harness unconnected pads match README lists exactly
claim: Unconnected J1 pads on PCB equal the README 'Not connected' sets (12/44/29/35); no connected pad is missing from the pin tables. 1999-2000 has 12 extra bay pads XA-XL with no harness plug (documented).
evidence: script comparison of pcb_pads.csv vs README lines (8995 l.95, 9697 l.85, 9900 l.88, 0105 l.92)
suggested_fix: None.

title: starved_thermal DRC errors are benign
claim: The only error-severity DRC type: GND pads with 1 spoke to a small zone island. Not a connectivity fault (0 unconnected items, islands have stitching vias); only weaker pad-to-plane tie.
evidence: drc_kicad9.json; geom.py zone island areas 0.37-130 mm2
suggested_fix: Optional: set GND pad connection to solid for these pads or add a track to the main pour.

title: ERC and library warnings are artefacts
claim: footprint_link_issues/lib_symbol_issues (53-74) come from missing library tables in KiCad 9 run; power_pin_not_driven on MPX5700AP VS/GND = no PWR_FLAG; no real ERC errors.
evidence: erc_kicad9.json
suggested_fix: None.

title: VIGN_IN floating on 1996-2000 boards (intentional)
claim: Daughterboard ignition sense is wired to the harness only on 1989-95 (1C) and 2001-05 (4S); on 96-00 it is a single-pin net, matching documented firmware handling (battery-voltage sense).
evidence: pcb_nets.txt VIGN_IN lines; VERIFICATION.md l.139-153
suggested_fix: None.

title: USB-C NPTH hole 0.194 mm from GND pads
claim: Repo's own KiCad 7 DRC reports 4 hole_clearance errors (0.194 mm vs 0.25 rule) on every board, inherent to the GCT USB4105 land pattern; JLC acceptance of 0.19 mm NPTH-to-copper is not verified. Shield slot also 0.30-0.34 mm from a GND via/slots.
evidence: fab_drc_report.txt; geom_all.txt hole-to-hole
suggested_fix: Check in JLC's DFM/order preview; the footprint is the vendor pattern so likely accepted.

title: Vias inside SMD pads (12-19 per board)
claim: 0.3 mm vias lie within SMD pads of caps, diodes, fuses, J4 GND pads; unfilled via-in-pad can wick solder (minor yield risk).
evidence: viapad.py output
suggested_fix: Move vias off the pads or accept for large pads; check mask tenting.

title: 1989-95 family J1 pad ring only 0.203 mm
claim: Ring 0.203 mm vs 0.35 mm on other years; likely above JLC minimum (limit from memory 0.15, unverified); also 49 silk-over-pad warnings (pin labels crowd pads; JLC clips silk).
evidence: geom_all.txt; drc silk_over_copper 49
suggested_fix: None required; confirm in JLC DFM.

title: Via-in-pad on 4-layer order: 664 of 1423 vias inside SMD pads, fill status unrecorded
claim: 664 of the 1423 vias are inside same-net SMD pads: 404 in the Q1-Q8 tabs and about 260 under passives, ICs and diodes. The README tells the owner to order epoxy-filled and capped vias, but no file records that the order did so. JLC gives filled vias free only on 6+ layers.
evidence: vip.py on ord_db.kicad_pcb (via centre inside pad bbox); daughterboard/README.md lines 37 and 321; JLC news page (web search 2026-11-16) says POFV is chargeable on 4-layer
suggested_fix: Check the JLC order confirmation for 'Epoxy filled & capped'. If unfilled, inspect DPAK and 0402 fillets and X-ray or thermal-test the drivers before trusting them. Order 6-layer or filled on the next run.

title: Q1-Q8 inputs have no series resistor on the ordered db
refs: U11.3-10 to Q1-Q8 pin 1; R152-R159 absent
claim: The SN74LVC4245 outputs go directly to the VND7NV04 inputs, so the ST 150 ohm RIN MIN rule is not met. The consequence is not quantified by ST. The repo documents the problem; the rework is by hand on 8 DPAK inputs.
evidence: delta_db.txt: nets /Outputs/*_IN contain U11.x and the driver pin in ordered; current has R152-R159 220 ohm; audit A1
suggested_fix: Before power-up, lift each Q input lead and bridge it with 220 ohm 0603, or cut the track and bridge it with 220 ohm 0402.

title: Ordered mb and db consistent; MCU pin map matches frozen firmware
refs: J1/J2 vs JD1/JD2; U1 vs miata_pins.h
claim: All 80 mating pins match by net on all five ordered motherboards, with identical (14.5, 42.0) mm offsets. Every MCU pin used by the frozen firmware matches the ordered daughterboard netlist, including the PD8-PD11 wideband flash lines crossing correctly to the F103. The only mismatch, HTR_GND on J2-39/40 landing on GND, looks intentional.
evidence: work/B03/mate.py, u1map.py; miata_pins.h; wideband_uart_flash.cpp:338-343
suggested_fix: None.

title: Ordered 1989-95: tach output wired straight to harness 2I, default ON in firmware
claim: There is no jumper between the ZXMS6004 tach driver and 2I. A fresh tune enables tachOutputPin. With the stock igniter driving 2I the two outputs contend.
evidence: evidence/ord_mb8993/pcb_nets.txt OUT_TACH = J1.2I JD1.11; ABOUT.md known points
suggested_fix: Set the tach output to none in TunerStudio before the first connection to a car with the stock igniter. A hardware fix would need cutting the 2I track.

title: 1989-93 ordered mb: R23/R24 fitted pairs two drivers per injector wire
claim: R23 and R24 are populated by default, so INJ1||INJ4 drive 2U and INJ2||INJ3 drive 2V. The repo's current decision is one driver per wire. Two paralleled drivers do not share the turn-off clamp energy evenly, so the first-off driver or TVS takes it.
evidence: pcb_footprints (R23/R24 have LCSC); VERIFICATION.md 'one driver per injector wire'; audit A11
suggested_fix: Remove R23 and R24. INJ1 then drives 2U and INJ2 drives 2V, with no firmware change. Keep D3/D4. For sequential, fit R25/R26 instead, and never R26 on an automatic.

title: Ordered db has no injector clamps; 1994-2005 turn-off energy goes into the driver clamps
claim: The ordered db lacks D42-D49, and only the 1989-93 motherboard has D3/D4. On the other boards the VND7NV04 clamps (VCLTH 36 V) absorb every injector turn-off (about 15 mJ per shot at 20 mH, repo simulation). Injector inductance is unknown.
evidence: delta_db.txt; audit A2/A3/A4
suggested_fix: Measure the injector inductance and driver case temperature on the bench with a real injector before the car. Optionally wire an external TVS from the injector pin to VBAT_IN.

title: Logic supply F1 0.5 A and L1 500 mA rating are tight for cranking
claim: The buck draws about 0.45 A at 8 V while cranking, which is at the limit of both parts. A hot PTC holds less, and F1 plus L1 drop about 0.45 V at 0.45 A.
evidence: parts_manifest.md lines 252/256; VERIFICATION.md external review
suggested_fix: Hot-soak and weak-crank test. If it trips, swap F1 for a roughly 1 A 1206 PTC and L1 for a matching 1210 inductor.

title: Ordered battery sense taken after D7 and F1
claim: R11 sits on the +12V net with F1.2, behind D7 and F1, so VBAT reads about 0.4-0.6 V low and load dependent.
evidence: delta_db.txt (R11.1 +12V vs VBAT_IN); evidence/ord_db/pcb_nets.txt
suggested_fix: Optional: move R11 pin 1 to VBAT_IN, for example J1 pin 1 or D7 pad 2. Or accept it and apply a firmware trim.

title: Check-engine lamp driver sits behind the shared driver enable on the ordered db
claim: The CEL cannot light while DRV_EN_N is high, which includes a fatal error. The current design drives it from CEL_CTL directly.
evidence: pcb_nets.txt /Outputs/CEL_G = Q13.1 RN3.1 U12.6; CEL_CTL = U1.3 U12.18
suggested_fix: Optional rework: cut U12.6 to the Q13 gate, wire PE4 to the gate, and ground U12.18. Otherwise document it.

title: AUX header on ordered boards: 0.5 A F4, no flyback diode, no CAN, UART pins double as flex/N2O
claim: The ordered J5 is 16 pins. It has no D5 flyback diode on the boost output and no CAN pins. J5-12/13 are PC6/PC7 with a 10k series resistor and a BAT54S, with no pull-up and no RC filter. The frozen firmware does not configure them as flex or nitrous inputs. A flex sensor needs an external 4.7k pull-up to J5-14. Nitrous on PC7 shares EXTI line 7 with HALL1 on PE7, so use it polled.
evidence: mb pcb_pads J5 listing; init_flex.cpp:25; delta files
suggested_fix: Document the external pull-up and diode. Set the pins in TunerStudio. Replace F4 with 1 A only after checking the track.

title: Ordered 1999-2000 mb uses 64-pin 176122-6; current uses 76-pin header
claim: The ordered board has a 64-pin TE 176122-6 footprint (68 pads), while the current design uses TE 178780-1 76P_NB1 (80 pads). The header and footprint changed between revisions, not just the board rev.
evidence: pcb_footprints.csv ord_mb9900 vs cur_mb9900
suggested_fix: Confirm which plug the owner's car needs before fitting the harness header. Do not mix headers.

title: Staged bring-up plan with measurable expectations
claim: Power the bare daughterboard first at 0.1-0.3 A limit. Expected: +5V 5.0, +3V3 3.3, V5_EXT/SENS about 5, DRV_EN_N 5 V until firmware runs. Then mate the motherboard and check MAP 0.85 V at 101 kPa. Test outputs with dummy loads, then the wideband with a dummy heater at 3 A.
evidence: notes section 4; LMR14020 0.75 V ref with 68k/12k; firmware MAP 0.2-4.7 V = 0-700 kPa
suggested_fix: Follow the plan; record the idle current as the first real number.

title: Via-in-pad is on ~300 ordinary pads, not only DPAK tabs and TVSs
refs: vias vs pads of C/R 0402-1206, SOT-23, SOIC-8, TSSOP, LED, RN, microSD, TO-252, D_SMC
claim: 719 of 1349 via holes (0.3 mm, open to the pad mask opening) touch SMD pad copper; about 300 are in non-thermal pads, while README 'Before ordering' item 9 names only DPAK tabs and clamp TVS pads. Unfilled they wick solder and cause tombstoning and starved joints.
evidence: work/B04.../scripts/vip2.py on the rev 0.10 board; maskpaste.py: no mask flash at any via centre. JLC capabilities page: epoxy filled and capped is the default for 6-layer and above.
suggested_fix: Order with via covering = epoxy filled and capped for ALL vias, check it on the order summary, and widen README item 9 to say so. Optionally move edge-of-pad vias off passive pads.

title: Ordered 4-layer rev 0.9 has vias in all 8 injector-driver tab pads; fill is not the 4-layer default
refs: Q1-Q8, Q101 TO-252 tab pads; ~730 via holes touching SMD pads
claim: 373 via holes sit in the TO-252 tab pads and about 350 more touch other SMD pads. JLC states epoxy fill and cap is the default only for 6-layer and above, so a 4-layer order with default via covering leaves open vias in the pads. Reflow solder wicks away from the tabs, and the thermal model assumes solid tabs.
evidence: vip2.py on ord_db pcb: TO-252-2 [413,373,336]; JLC capabilities page; ordered-board README says to order epoxy filled and capped.
suggested_fix: Check the actual order record for 'epoxy filled and capped'. If it was not selected, inspect the tabs after assembly (X-ray or section a sample), and expect voids and degraded thermal margin. This cannot be reworked in fabrication.

title: SOT-23 rotation offset (+180) conflicts with an older community table (-90)
claim: The repo's CPL adds +180 for SOT-23 and SOT-23-5, based on the rev 0.5 JLC preview. matthewlai's community table lists ^SOT-23 as -90, and I could not retrieve the current Bouni table. A wrong offset swaps pins on 22 polarised parts, including all the output switches.
evidence: order_bom.py:217-224; cpl_rotations_db.csv ('^SOT-23',-90); rotation offsets uniform +180 in bomcpl.py output
suggested_fix: Confirm every SOT-23 in JLC's assembly preview against the pin-1 pad before paying, and fix the CPL if it differs.

title: TO-252, PG-DSO-8, microSD, TS-1187A, D46-D49 and LED rotations unconfirmed
refs: Q1-Q8,Q101 (+180); U3,U14 (+270 by analogy); J4 (0, origin 0.55 mm off pad centre); SW1,SW2; D46-D49; D1-D5,D101-D103
claim: No community entry exists for these families, and JLC's models were checked only for rev 0.5 parts (README item 2 says J4, the clamp TVSs and the diodes are new and unchecked). The U3/U14 PG-DSO-8 +270 is an extension of the SOIC rule. J4 has no centre offset in JLC_OFFSET.
evidence: order_bom.py JLC_ROT/JLC_OFFSET; origin.py: J4 pad-bbox centre -0.55 mm in the footprint y, TO-252 -0.84 mm; notes section 4
suggested_fix: Review these refs in JLC's preview and record the confirmed offsets in JLC_ROT/JLC_OFFSET; check LED cathode marks per LCSC part.

title: Gerber set, drills and outline are complete and match the PCB
claim: Six copper files named F_Cu.gtl, In1-4 .g2-.g5, B_Cu.gbl with FileFunction L1-L6 headers; 8-segment closed outline 125.0 x 76.0 mm; PTH 1429 (1349 x 0.3 + 80 x 1.0) and NPTH 10 (4 x 3.2, 6 x 0.991) equal the PCB hole for hole. JLC says it understands KiCad/Protel naming (G2L/G3L for inner layers on a 4-layer board; no explicit 6-layer table, so the .g2-.g5 mapping is inferred).
evidence: g1_stats.py, g2_outline_drill.py, zipcheck.py; JLC Suggested Naming Patterns page
suggested_fix: None. After upload, check in JLC's viewer that the layer stack shows L2-L5 in order.

title: BOM, CPL and PCB agree exactly; coordinates match the pos file
claim: 330 (rev 0.10) and 302 (rev 0.9) SMD footprints appear once each in both the BOM and the CPL; there are no THT parts, no DNP and no bottom-side parts. CPL X/Y equal the pos file within 0.001 mm (Y negated, gerber frame). Designators and LCSC codes agree with the parts manifest, and every LCSC code resolves to a real part of the matching package.
evidence: scripts/bomcpl.py output; kb/parts_manifest.md
suggested_fix: None.

title: Order options for 6-layer rev 0.10
claim: Needed: 6 layers, 1.6 mm, 1 oz outer / 0.5 oz inner (default), via covering epoxy filled and capped (default at 6 layers, set explicitly), ENIG (HASL not offered at 6 layers; OSP possible), no impedance control. README item 11 omits the surface finish and the via covering reminder. Min via 0.15 hole / 0.25 via, 0.09 mm track and space: design uses 0.3/0.6 and 0.15 mm, so there is margin.
evidence: JLC pcb-capabilities page (fetched today)
suggested_fix: Add finish and via covering to README item 11.

title: Design qualifies for JLC economic assembly
claim: All 330 SMD parts are on the top side and the board is 125 x 76 x 1.6 mm, 6 layer, within JLC's stated economic limits (2/4/6 layers, 0.8-1.6 mm, one side of SMT, 2-50 pcs). The BOM has 48 basic, 7 preferred-extended and 38 non-preferred extended lines, so about 38 extended-part loading fees (amount unverified) apply.
evidence: JLC assembly capability pages via search summary; manifest library column count
suggested_fix: Select economic assembly on the order form; confirm the quote and the fee total; swap extended passives to basic where equivalents exist to cut fees.

title: Paste apertures: thermal pads windowed, no bottom paste
claim: Each TO-252 tab (6.4 x 5.8) has 4 apertures of 3.05 x 2.75 (about 90 % area); U2/U3/U14 exposed pads have 4 windows; B_Paste is empty, which is correct. A 90 % paste coverage over via-in-pad tabs relies on the vias being filled.
evidence: maskpaste.py (F paste 1030 apertures = F.Paste pads)
suggested_fix: Optionally reduce tab paste to about 50-60 % to limit float and voids.

title: U4 USBLC6 CPL rotation 180 is only assumed
claim: CPL rotates the SOT-23-6 ESD diode by +180 (rule seen on SOT-23/-23-5, 'SOT-23-6 assumed the same'). If JLC's model orientation differs, pin 5 (USB_VBUS) and pin 2 (GND) are exchanged, shorting VBUS to GND through the ESD diodes.
evidence: scripts/order_bom.py JLC_ROT comment; fab CPL U4 rot 180 vs PCB 0; pcb_nets USB_VBUS=U4.5, USB_DP=U4.1/U4.6, USB_DM=U4.3/U4.4
suggested_fix: Check U4 pin-1 marker in JLC's placement preview before production; also check D1/D2/D5 cathode.

title: F2/F3 fuse C46641168 nearly out of stock
claim: SMD1812-200-30 (hongjiacheng) has 57 pieces at JLC (55 at LCSC) and is single-sourced, while 2001-05 needs 2 per board. BSMD1812-200-30V C960026 (same BHFUSE family as F4) has 194k in stock at $0.11 and is 2 A hold / 30 V.
evidence: tools/lcsc.py C46641168 live 2026-11-16: stock 57; search '1812 PPTC 2A 30V' C960026 stock 194145
suggested_fix: Switch F2/F3 to C960026 (or C18198342) for the next release.

title: No per-year seller sheet; shunt count wrong
claim: The seller must set JP3 (FAN2) and JP6 on every 1989-95 board, plus JP4/JP1/JP2 on 1994-95, but the BOM lists 6 shunts as Required and the repo has no per-year assembly sheet. Open JP3 is electrically safe but leaves the A/C or condenser fan relay undriven. R20-R22 pull-ups are car-dependent with no default stated.
evidence: self_order_bom line 3 qty 6; 1989-95/README.md lines 135-148; order_all_boards.csv line 5
suggested_fix: Add a per-year assembly sheet: 1989-93 shunts JP3(90-93) and JP6(AFM) only; 1994-95 JP1,JP2 SEQ, JP3(94-95), JP4, JP6; JP5 open. Say how R20-R22 are decided.

title: J5 add-on header has no pin labels
claim: The 20-pin add-on header (COP, boost, alternator, knock, CAN, 5 V, 12 V) has only an outline and a square pin 1 on the silkscreen: no pin functions or pin-1 text. Option parts R20-22/R27/R28/R30/R37 and JP4/JP5 carry only reference names.
evidence: gr_text list of miata_mb_*.kicad_pcb (no J5 text); top_all.png crop of J5
suggested_fix: Add a compact pin legend near J5 (J5 is 1 x 2.54 mm pitch, 2 rows) and 'FIT/OPEN' hints at JP4/JP5.

title: MAP sensor is the dominant cost and thinly stocked
claim: MPX5700AP costs $29.12 each at JLC up to 29 pcs ($27.49 at 30+) with only 155 in stock; it is hand-fitted so it is not in the JLC BOM, and it is about 20x all SMD parts on the board combined.
evidence: tools/lcsc.py C90152 live: price tiers 29.12 / 27.49, stock 155
suggested_fix: Cost owner should evaluate alternatives (e.g. other absolute MAP sensors) in the sensor review.

title: JLC assembly cost is small; alternatives save little
claim: Economic PCBA: about $22 fixed per design-order plus $3.07 per extended line (4 on 8995/9697, 5 on 9900/0105) and about $1.3 per board (52 SMT joints, parts about $1.2). Per board about $3.5-3.9 at 10, $2.2 at 25, $1.7 at 50. All-basic substitution saves $12-15 per order, moving parts to the daughterboard cannot remove J4/R2/R3/U4, hand assembly only wins below about 5 boards.
evidence: jlcpcb.com/help/article/pcb-assembly-price (fetched today); parts_manifest prices; fab BOMs
suggested_fix: Keep JLC for SMD; do not redesign for basic parts. Order the 4 years in one batch only if JLC panelisation lowers setup ($8.18 per extra design).

title: BOM lacks LCSC codes that exist
claim: Self-order BOM sends JST S08B-PUDSS-1, the 2x10 box header, 1x2 headers and the 1k 2512 resistor to Digi-Key, although LCSC stocks equivalents: C412098 (JST, 10084 in stock, $0.36), C3405 (2x10 IDC box header, $0.15), C54315 (1k 2512 1%), C32713268 (1x2 header $0.016).
evidence: tools/lcsc.py -s searches today; self_order_bom lines 10, 13-15
suggested_fix: Add LCSC codes (check footprint/pin dimension equivalence for the JST and box header) so a single LCSC order covers all but the harness header.

title: Socket C124412 has 65 pieces in stock
claim: Ckmtw B-2200S40P-A120 1x40 socket (2 per motherboard) shows 65 at JLC; fine for the 8 needed now, limits a production run to about 30 boards.
evidence: tools/lcsc.py C124412 JLC stock 65
suggested_fix: Qualify a second source with the same 8.5 mm height before volume.

title: J4 NPTH pegs 0.194 mm from GND pads
claim: KiCad flags 4 hole_clearance errors (0.194 mm vs the 0.25 mm rule) between the USB-C 0.65 mm NPTH pegs and the outer GND signal pads; it comes from the GCT footprint geometry and is present on the ordered boards too. Likely accepted by JLC, but unconfirmed.
evidence: fab_drc_report.txt hole_clearance x4 on 8995, 9697, ord_mb8993
suggested_fix: Confirm in JLC DFM output; accept if no warning.

title: USB-C CPL pad-centre offset verified
claim: CPL Mid Y -206.46 equals the centre of the copper pad field (207.6 - 1.14); the connector mating face points to the board edge. Whether JLC's model centre equals the pad centre is the repo's preview observation (not re-verifiable).
evidence: pcb_pads.csv J4 y 203.92-208.675; order_bom.py JLC_OFFSET; fab CPL
suggested_fix: Re-check in JLC's preview with the real order.

title: BOM, CPL and PCB agree on all boards
claim: Designator sets of JLC BOM and CPL are identical (17/15/16/18) and equal PCB SMD footprints minus deliberately unfitted options; positions equal PCB except the J4 offset and U4 rotation. Ordered boards likewise.
evidence: script over pcb_footprints.csv, fab_jlcpcb_bom/cpl for 9 boards
suggested_fix: None.

title: Gerber/drill set complete; slots and plated M4 ok
claim: 14 files, 2 layers 1.6 mm, closed edge, plated 0.6 x 1.4/1.7 G85 slots (JLC min plated slot 0.5 mm, length >= 2 x width), 4.5 mm plated M4 holes with 7 mm GND pad, NPTH 3.2/3.5/1.65/0.65. Silk/mask 'flashes' in the silk files are clear-polarity subtraction, harmless. Repo zips are identical to the evidence gerbers.
evidence: drill_summary.py, gerber_bbox.py, zipcmp.py output; jlcpcb.com/capabilities/Capabilities
suggested_fix: None.

title: Thermal model uses free-air h=10 per face; closed metal case likely 3-6 and case-to-cabin rise omitted
claim: Board mean rise is ~P/(2*0.0095 m2*h), so it scales with 1/h. In a closed metal case the board loses heat with gap conduction (~1.7 W/m2K) plus weak radiation to bare metal, so h is likely 3-5, not 10. The repo also gives the rise only 'above the air around the board', and the case-to-cabin rise under carpet (~10-20 K) is missing. Allowable air around the board for the MCU (105 C junction) at sustained 7200 rpm falls from the repo's 65-73 C to ~54 C (with pin conduction) or ~34 C (without), before adding the case rise.
evidence: Reran repo script on the board file: h=10 seq 31 C mean, MCU +40 (matches repo); h=5 no pins 63 C mean, MCU +71, TVS +83; h=5 with pins 41 C mean, MCU +51, TVS +61; h=3 no pins 104 C mean. h and case rise are my assumptions (unverified).
suggested_fix: Re-run the model with h=4-5 per face plus a case-to-cabin conductance; state the limit as cabin temperature; measure a built board in the actual case at ~3 W and ~6 W.

title: Total dissipation by operating point agrees with repo; idle ~3 W is base load
claim: Own sum of MCU 0.33, buck 0.5, LDO 0.43, two trackers 0.72, D7 0.14, wideband/CAN ~0.4, clamps 0.22/0.83/2.0 W at 800/3000/7200 rpm (20 mH) gives ~3.1 / 3.9 / 6.0 W, vs repo 5.9 W at 7200. The repo model is electrically sound; the tracker current (35/50 mA) is assumed. At the 150 mA rating U14 alone would dissipate 1.3 W.
evidence: repo board_thermal.py losses(); TLS115 150 mA rating; my arithmetic (13.5-5 V)x0.15 A.
suggested_fix: Measure +12V input current and U14/U3 load on the first board.

title: F1 PTC hold current at hot air is close to the logic-supply load
claim: The datasheet derating table gives 1.10 A hold at 25 C, 0.71 A at 60 C, 0.66 A at 70 C and 0.52 A at 85 C (also the part's operating limit). The logic supply draws about 0.4-0.55 A (the repo says ~0.45 A cranking at 8 V), and F1 sits beside the hot TVS and diode in an enclosure. Margin vanishes above ~70-85 C air at a weak crank, so the 5 V rail could drop out.
evidence: datasheets/txt/C883150_BSMD1812-110-33V.txt derating table row BSMD1812-110; VERIFICATION.md line 684
suggested_fix: Use a 1.5 A hold 1812/2920 part (derates to >0.8 A at 85 C) or move F1 away from D6/D7 and L1; the 33 V rating is already needed.

title: U4 LDL1117 3V3 regulator: weakest heat path (1 via, 2.9 mm2 F.Cu island)
claim: The SOT-223 tab is on +3V3, which has no F.Cu pour. The tab has 1 via and a 2.9 mm2 local island, so ~0.43 W (0.25 A, 5->3.3 V; more with SD writes) goes only through that via into the 15 um In4 plane. The model puts the junction at +44 C at h=10 and +76 C at h=5 over air, hotter than the drivers.
evidence: measured with shapely from pcbnew export (b07_ep.py); model run h=5
suggested_fix: Add 4-6 vias in the tab pad or a 3V3 pour on F.Cu/B.Cu under the tab (check clearance); or feed U4 from a 3.3 V buck output instead.

title: Heater FET Q101 has no thermal vias and only 48 mm2 of F.Cu drain copper
claim: Warm-up draws 2.3 A rms for ~14 s (repo N5), i.e. 0.4-0.7 W in Q101 on a copper island with no vias and no inner copper; the README's drain-copper claims only cover Q1-Q8. Estimate +25-45 C for the short warm-up and ~0 steady state. Acceptable but not the 'thermal vias per driver' the README implies for the board; hot-soak warm-up near the AD8628/REF3033 may shift offsets.
evidence: b07_ep.py: Q101 pad 2 vias in pad 0; no zone fills on LSU_HTR_N; track widths 1.0 mm (pcb_net_routing)
suggested_fix: Optional: stitch 6-8 vias from the Q101 tab to a B.Cu pour.

title: Drain copper and via-count claims verified (small differences)
claim: Measured drain copper F.Cu 93.6-101.6 mm2, In2/In3/B.Cu 105.2-109.9 mm2 each, 41-45 vias per net (25 in the tab pad of 37.1 mm2). README says F.Cu 84-100, inner 95-108, 34-42 vias: close, slightly low. Clamp TVS pads: K-side 172-210 mm2 over four layers, 1-3 vias in pad, 4-8 in the zone; D48 K and D49 A sides have the fewest (4 and 3).
evidence: b03_inj.py, a04_drivers.py, b05_loop.py output in work dir; table in notes
suggested_fix: Update the README numbers or leave; optionally add 2-3 vias to D48 K and D49 A.

title: Injector, valve, ground and heater current paths checked: no bottleneck
refs: J1.19/22/25/28 etc.; J1 GND pins; Q1-Q8 source pads
claim: Each tab-to-J1-pin path is a 6-6.9 mm four-layer pour (~0.15 mOhm), joined to the pad by ring contact of 89-100% on all four layers. Sources have 1 via in pad and 4-11 vias in the local island, then solid In1 to 17 J1 GND pins (each 100% on In1). Heater 1.0 mm track 2 A gives 6.6 C by IPC-2221 (matches repo). The single 0.64 mm header pin per output is the limit, not the copper.
evidence: b03_inj.py, b06_pin.py, a05_gnd_at_pads.py; hand IPC-2221 I=0.048 dT^0.44 A^0.725
suggested_fix: None.

title: In1 GND and In4 3V3 plane integrity checked
claim: In1 is a single connected zone (8383 mm2, 88% cover; 95% under U1, 97% under U2, 99% in the buck area); the largest voids are 24 mm2 via fields under the DPAK tabs (2.5 mm necks between them). No slots under regulators or MCU. In4 3V3 is also one component (82% cover; 66% under the driver strip) but fragments if eroded by 1 mm, which is harmless at <0.5 A.

title: Buck hot loop, SW node and FB routing checked
claim: C71 (100n) is 2.2 mm from VIN with a GND via at 0.28 mm; C17/C18 are 5-7 mm away; SW to D9 3.4 mm; D9 anode and U2 EP have vias within 0.4 mm; BUCK_SW exists only on F.Cu (19.6 mm2) with solid In1 beneath; FB (0.2 mm, 8.6 mm) is 3.5 mm from SW. title: Repo thermal model also pessimistic in places

title: F407 VDDA/VREF+ filter caps 9-11 mm from pins, none at the pin
claim: Only C11 (1u) and C12 (100n) decouple +3V3A, and they sit at the ferrite FB1, 9.2-9.6 mm pad-to-pad from U1 pins 21/22, routed 9.9-11.3 mm with 2 vias and a B.Cu hop. No cap at the VDDA/VREF+ pins. ST wants them as close as possible to the chip.

title: Ordered 4-layer DB has ~620 vias inside SMD pads; JLC fills only by default on 6+ layers
refs: Q1-Q8 tab pads (373 vias), 0402/0603 R/C, SOT-23, SOD-323, SOIC, TSSOP, SMA, 1206
claim: Of 1423 vias (all 0.6/0.3 mm), about 620 have their centre inside an SMD pad: 373 in DPAK pads and at least 245 in 0402/0603/SOT/SOIC/TSSOP/diode pads. Epoxy-filled and capped via-in-pad is the JLC default only for 6+ layers; on 4 layers it is an optional extra. If the order did not select it, expect solder wicking, starved joints and tombstoning well beyond the DPAK tabs the repo mentions.
evidence: work/B08/vip.py and dpak.py on ord_db geometry; JLC capabilities page line 189 ('default for 6-layer and above'); JLC 2022 POFV blog ('affordable for four-layer'); repo README item 9 covers only the DPAK tabs
suggested_fix: Check the order confirmation / DFM sheet for epoxy filled and capped on ALL vias. If not filled, inspect Q1-Q8 and the 0402 parts on arrival and rework them by hand. For future orders, fill vias or move them out of the 0402/0603 pads.

title: Current 6-layer rev 0.10 relies on default via fill (about 640 vias in pads)
claim: cur_db has 366 vias in DPAK pads and about 270 in other SMD pads. This is acceptable because JLC makes filled vias the default for 6+ layers (0.3 mm drill is within 0.15-0.55). The repo's README note is right for DPAK but should say it applies to every pad with a via.
evidence: vip.py; capabilities_pcb-capabilities.txt line 189
suggested_fix: Keep the 'epoxy filled and capped' check in the order checklist and extend it to all via-in-pad parts.

title: Courtyard overlaps (101 cur / 91 ord) are harmless: minimum pad gap 0.200 mm
claim: Across all overlapping courtyard pairs the smallest pad-to-pad gap is 0.200 mm (0805-0805) then 0.219 mm (0402-0603). JLC's table needs 0.18 for these and 0.2 chip-SOT; JLC measures body to body, so pad gap is conservative. 0 pairs are under 0.2 mm. Checked, correct.

suggested_fix: None; optionally shrink the courtyards of those parts to quiet KiCad DRC.

title: J2 header pins hand-soldered 0.18-0.22 mm from 0603 resistor pads

Four J2 pins have only 0.18-0.22 mm between their 1.7 mm annulus and 0603 pads of different nets (analog inputs), so an iron or solder blob can bridge or knock off the 0603s. The DPAK tabs are not a problem (at least 2.76 mm from any pin).

title: No test points, fiducials or rails; wideband SWD pads on the bottom only

DFU on the F407 works only when mated via the motherboard USB-C. A production test needs a bed-of-nails or probes on component pads.
evidence: misc.py (no TP refs); pcb_pads.csv J3/J102 rows; kb/interconnect.md J2.30/31 USB
suggested_fix: Add 1 mm TPs for VBAT, +5V, +3V3, GND, NRST and the key I/O, a bottom-accessible or edge SWD for the F103, and have JLC program the chips if the interface is described to them.

title: Mounting hardware clearances: only GND copper or mask-covered tracks near standoffs
claim: Nothing can short or be crushed. DB H1-H4 have only GND vias and pours within 3.2 mm. MB HD3 has the LSU_HTR_N track edge 3.14 mm from hole centre (hex corner 3.17, pan head 3.0) and HD2 on mb8995 has HARN_2O at 3.15 mm, both mask-covered. M4 H3/H4 on mb8995 have OUT_ALT / IN_AUX3 at 3.95-4.09 mm. M4 holes are plated GND pads, so the screws ground the board to the case. DB hole offsets match the MB HD offsets.
evidence: work/B08/holes.py, hd.py, m4.py
suggested_fix: Use nylon or insulating shoulder washers under standoffs if worried; keep tracks out of 4 mm of the M4 holes on the next layout.

title: JLC adds rails and fiducials; boards qualify for Economic PCBA
refs: board outline, bottom side only THT
claim: Boards carry no fiducials or rails (parts at least 1.9 mm from the edge). JLC standard PCBA needs 5 mm rails and 3-4 fiducials of 1 mm (it adds them and ships with rails attached). SMD is top-only, so Economic PCBA (single-sided, 2-6 layers, 2-50 pcs, no rails needed, fixed 255 C reflow) is applicable and may be cheaper. The 52-point outline needs mouse bites, not V-cut.
evidence: help_article_how-to-add-edge-rails...txt; capabilities_pcb-assembly-capabilities.txt table; misc.py
suggested_fix: Quote both Economic and Standard PCBA; confirm the 255 C reflow suits the microSD socket and other plastics.

title: Tombstoning risk on GND-pour 0402/LED pads (crude estimate)
claim: 33 of 220 two-pad chips have more than 10x copper imbalance between pads (GND pour against a thin trace), which can tombstone in reflow. This overstates the risk if the pour connects through thermal spokes; vias in pads add to it.
evidence: work/B08/tomb.py (crude metric: pad area plus same-net copper within 2 mm)
suggested_fix: Check the thermal spokes on those pads and the first-article reflow result; rely on JLC's DFM report.

title: Conformal coating: parts and ports to mask
refs: J3, J102, J4 microSD, SW1/2, USB-C, MPX5700AP port, JD1/JD2, J5, JST PUD, JP1-6
claim: All vias are tented and the LQFP/0402 parts are coatable. Mask the programming pads, microSD, buttons, USB-C, MAP sensor port (and its vent), sockets and header pins before coating.

suggested_fix: Add a masking note to INSTALL/assembly docs.

title: 1B battery trunk: 0.6 mm x 46 mm carries heater + logic + AUX; worse than documented
refs: VBAT_IN, J1.1B to first split, mb_route.py:90
claim: All current entering at pin 1B (LSU heater up to 2.3-3 A, logic about 0.5 A, J5-15 load up to 1.1 A hold) passes 46 mm of 0.6 mm track (38 mOhm). VERIFICATION.md quotes about 20 C at 2.3 A heater only. With logic and a 0.5 A AUX load it is 48 C, with heater hold current plus full AUX 1.1 A about 103 C (IPC-2221, conservative), on top of up to 85 C cabin air.
evidence: a02_paths.txt VBAT_IN J1.1B->JD1.1: B0.6x11.8 + F0.6x14 + B0.6x20.1; mb_route.py:90 BW=min(w,0.6); VERIFICATION.md:682; ipc2221 calc in notes section 2

title: Ground pour continuity between harness and daughterboard pins: checked, correct
refs: GND zones F.Cu/B.Cu, J1.2A-2D,2F, JD1/JD2 GND pins
claim: Both GND pours plus 971 vias form one connected network; all 54 GND pads are in it. Resistance from the five harness ground pins to all JD1 ground pins is 0.37 mOhm, to all JD2 ground pins 0.66 mOhm, to a single worst JD pin 1.2 mOhm. The long horizontal tracks do not cut the pour.

title: Jumper JP1-JP6 and option links traced: correct; no damaging wrong setting
claim: Pin-to-net maps and silk labels (PAIR/SEQ, 90-93/94-95, AFM/BOOST) match the README table and INSTALL.md. claim: With R28 fitted and the stock throttle switch present, V5_EXT is shorted to ground at every idle (documented). The daughterboard CLT/IAT 2.7k pull-ups also hang on V5_EXT, so coolant and air temperature inputs lose their bias at the same time; the README mentions only the shorted 5 V.

claim: Outline 154.0 x 161.5 vs Hellen NA6 a/b 154.13 x 161.63; H1,H3-H6 match its holes to 0.1 mm. A 0.6 mm trace and no freewheel diode are fine for a resistive load.

title: +3V3 shunt clamp 70 mV margin at 1 A is not robust
claim: The 3.93 V peak against the 4.0 V MCU abs max reproduces, but it depends on assumed parameters: the 2x100 uF X5R counted at 50 %, a TL431 modelled as a 7 A/V transconductance with a 1.8 kHz pole, and BCP53 hFE 60. With bulk capacitance at 25 % the peak is 4.18 V; with the TL431 pole at 500 Hz, 4.39 V; with both plus hFE 30, 4.86 V. Realistic faults are R108-limited (about 0.22-0.37 A), which stay below 4.0 V in most variants, so the clamp is probably adequate; the stated margin is not a margin.
evidence: own/shunt.py (reproduces 3.93 V; sensitivity table); circuit_sim_full.py:1823-1870; VERIFICATION.md L574, board_checks Q20 1.22 W row
suggested_fix: Bench-test with a current-step injector into +3V3; consider a bigger or lower-ESR bulk capacitor and a TL431 compensation network; do not quote the 70 mV margin.

Inside a closed stock ECU case, natural convection plus radiation is plausibly 3-8 W/m2K, and the case adds roughly P/(hA) of about 11 K (8.6 W, 0.08 m2, 10 W/m2K) over cabin air. The 23-46 K board rise could be 1.5-3 times larger, which moves the processor (105 C) and clamp-TVS (150 C) margins.

At 16 V the driver takes a small share, which is harmless (EAS 200 mJ). The real limit is a 40 V supply fault (177.9 mJ, CHECK).

title: Direct check passed: MAP, Molex J2 footprint, diode polarity, USB, AUX header
claim: MPX5700AP pads 1 Vout / 2 GND / 3 Vs match the datasheet, with 1 uF, 10 nF and 470 pF as in its decoupling figure. J2 footprint (pin 1 at the right edge row, 4-6 above) matches the Molex 43045 drawing. SS34 (K to +12 V) and SMCJ30A (K to injector) are oriented correctly. USBLC6 pin use and the 5.1 k CC resistors are right. J5 numbering and row assignment match INSTALL.
evidence: pcb_pads.csv; sch_netlist.xml D1/D3 K/A pins; datasheets C127367 p1, C90152 txt l.270-275; work/B17.../img/molex_crop2.png

title: Shipped ordered-board documents describe the ordered boards
claim: The harness pin tables in all five READMEs equal the PCB (including the not-connected lists), ABOUT's revision and header table is correct, and there are no references to later-revision features (2x10 header, JST/AEM connector, R35-R37, D5, JP2-JP6, microSD). ABOUT's commit 4f34615 is the parent of the freeze commit with no board change between.
evidence: readme_check.py output; grep of docs; git log e44b46c/4f34615
suggested_fix: None.

title: 1989-93 ordered boards keep paired drivers (R23/R24 fitted); current policy is one driver per wire
claim: The ordered board ships with INJ1+INJ4 on 2U and INJ2+INJ3 on 2V in parallel. Commit 6e346af changed the current policy to one driver per wire, which is a documented decision. Removing R23/R24 gives the current behaviour, and the firmware is unchanged (B03 P7).
evidence: fab BOM 'R23,R24,R29'; commit 6e346af; research/other_miata_pnp_boards.md l.108

title: Injector drivers take all turn-off energy: no clamp network on the ordered db
claim: With no per-injector clamp, each VND7NV04 clamps (VCLTH 36 V, 45 V typ) the injector turn-off energy. Repo's board_thermal.py on the ordered 4-layer PCB gives driver junction +78-86 K above the air around the board at sustained 7200 rpm with 20 mH (+46-50 K at 8 mH) at h=10, and +121-129 K (20 mH) / +75-80 K (8 mH) at h=5. At 85 C air and 20 mH that is over thermal shutdown (150 C min).
evidence: work/B18.../thermal_runs.txt; losses() 'rev09' case (15.3 mJ/shot at 20 mH, 1.06 W per driver); VND7NV04 datasheet Table 4 (VCLTH, Tjsh 150/175/200)
suggested_fix: Measure injector inductance and tab temperature on a dummy-load bench before sustained high rpm; wired external TVS (16 V class) from OUT_INJx to VBAT_IN at the harness; 1989-93 mb already has D3/D4. Limit sustained rpm until measured.

title: Safe continuous current per output on this board is set by driver temperature, not copper
claim: Drain copper is 84-108 mm2 per layer on F/In2/B with 35-42 vias and 93-100 % ring contact to the J1 pin; source returns via 2-19 local vias, In1 and 17 J1 GND pins: <1 mohm, ~0 K. The model gives 24-29 K/W junction per driver (h=10), 30-38 (h=5), 38-46 (h=3). For Tj<=125 C, 85 C air, Rds 0.12 ohm hot and 2.6 W base load: about 2.7-3.0 A per output at h=10, 1.7-1.9 A at h=5, none at h=3 (1.4-1.5 A at 70 C air).
evidence: work/B18.../c1.py, c6.py, thermal_single.txt; datasheet C155605 Table 4
suggested_fix: Use <=1.5 A continuous per output until the case air temperature and h are measured; header pin rating (UNVERIFIED ~3 A) is the other ceiling.

title: F1 0.5 A hold PTC + L1 500 mA inductor undersized on the logic supply
claim: F1 nSMD050-33V: hold 0.5 A, trip 1.0 A, R 0.15-0.7 ohm; L1 rated 500 mA, 300 mohm. Buck input is 0.25 A at 13.8 V but 0.45-0.6 A at 6-8 V cranking, so a hot ECU can trip or run F1 hot. At 6 V battery and 0.6 A, U2 Vin is about 4.8-5.2 V (D7 0.4 V + F1 + L1), below the buck dropout start (5.4-5.6 V), so +5V sags to ~4.5-4.9 V (rev 0.10: 4.8-5.0 V).
evidence: datasheets/txt/C70077 table II; kb/parts/P16 sections 3.1 (derating 0.34/0.24 A INFERRED), P05 F8
suggested_fix: Replace F1 with a 1206 1.1 A PTC (e.g. 1206L110/33NR C48985884) and L1 with a >=1 A 1210 or 0 ohm link; fits the pads. Test first: supply current at 6/8/13.8 V and voltage across F1, L1, D7.

title: No 220 ohm input resistors: ST states only a rating, risk is real but unquantified and low in normal drive
claim: ST (Doc ID 7383 Rev4 Table 2 p.7) lists RIN MIN 150 ohm and IIN +-20 mA with no stated mechanism; p.10 even says the input may be driven from a low-impedance source (Igf 15 mA fault sink, no requirement beyond IISS). With U11 at 5 V (below VINCL 6-8 V) IIN is ~0.1 mA and Igf 15 mA is within U11's 24 mA, so normal switching cannot reach 20 mA. It bites only when the input is forced outside -1..+6.8 V (ESD/transients, 5 V rail excursion) or via faster edges than ST characterised (all tr/tf/Eas figures use 150 ohm).
evidence: datasheet C155605 Table 2, Table 4 (VINCL, IISS, Igf), section 3; pcb_nets /Outputs/*_IN = Qn.1 + Rxx.1 + U11.x
suggested_fix: Optional: cut the 0.2-0.3 mm track 1-2 mm from each pin-1 pad and bridge with a 220 ohm 0402 (8 sites, delicate); or scope gate/drain at stage 6 and accept.

title: Via-in-pad under DPAK tabs: fill status of the order unknown, no record anywhere
claim: About 25 open 0.3 mm holes lie in each 37 mm2 tab (664 vias in same-net pads board-wide). README says order epoxy-filled and capped, but the gbrjob/drill files carry no fill information, the repo has no order record, and JLC fill is free only at 6+ layers. Open holes (2.8 mm3 per tab) can swallow about the same volume as the paste on the tab (~2 mm3, stencil thickness assumed), giving voided or starved tab joints and higher Rth.
evidence: gbrjob (no via-fill field), daughterboard/README.md lines 37, 321; c1.py (24-26 vias in tab); B03 P9, B04
suggested_fix: Check the JLC order confirmation; X-ray or inspect tab fillets, thermal-camera all 8 drivers at the same current; add solder around tab edges if starved.

title: Battery sense taken after D7 + F1
claim: R11.1 is on net +12V (F1.2/L1.1/D12), after SS34 and the PTC, so VBATT reads about 0.4-0.8 V low and load dependent.
suggested_fix: Wire R11.1 to VBAT_IN (D7 pad 2 / J1.1) or use a TunerStudio offset; compare against a DMM at 9/12/14 V.

title: Buck input hot loop weaker than rev 0.10: no C71 100 nF, bulk caps 4-8 mm from VIN
refs: U2 pins 2/3, C17, C18, C71 absent
claim: C17/C18 (10 uF 1206) pads are 4.3-7.8 mm from U2 VIN; no 100 nF at the pin (C71 absent on ord, 2.2 mm on rev 0.10). More VIN spike/EMI; abs max 44 V vs D12 Vc 53 V in a dump (P05 F5).
evidence: pcb_footprints (C71 absent), pcb_pads distances; BUCK_SW 6.2 mm F.Cu only over solid In1
suggested_fix: Scope VIN at the pin; add 100 nF 50 V 0603 across VIN/GND by hand if spikes are seen.

title: DRC/ERC/parity triage: all 474/63/920 items are artefacts or cosmetic
claim: 474 DRC = 199 lib_footprint (no libs) + 117 silk_overlap + 67 silk_over_copper + 91 courtyards_overlap (pad gaps >=0.2 mm meet JLC table); 0 unconnected/clearance/hole/edge. 63 parity = 57 NC-pin name differences + 6 BOM-excluded footprints. ERC 920 = 603 + 312 library warnings + 5 power_pin_not_driven (no PWR_FLAG). Checked, no real electrical error.
evidence: counts recomputed by python from the JSON; B01 proof (partition parity 269/269 groups)

title: Plane stack: GND In1 solid, 3V3 In2 solid, drain columns cut the 3V3 plane under the driver strip
claim: In1 GND 88.5 % cover, one polygon, only via antipads and eight 24-31 mm2 voids under the tab via fields; In2 +3V3 74.9 %, one polygon, 0.1 % cover under the strip (drain pours). Buck (100 %), MCU (93/91 %), wideband U102 83 %, U105 81 % cover. 8.5 % of critical signal length crosses In1 antipads; 34 % of it on B.Cu refers to the 3V3 plane. No slots under USB, CAN, HSE, analog.
evidence: work/B18.../c2.py, c9.py, c10.py

title: Current paths: tracks and vias well within limits; weakest link is the PTC/inductor
claim: VBAT_IN J1 to D7: 1.0 mm 20.5 mm, ~11 mohm; D7-F1-L1: 0.8 mm, <1 K at 0.5 A (2.8 A at 20 K); +5V 0.5 mm main, ~2 K at 0.64 A; heater LSU_HTR_N/HTR_GND 1.0 mm F.Cu (+2.5 mm B.Cu), 9 K at 2.3 A, 14 K at 2.8 A (IPC-2221), pins paired. 0.25 mm VBAT_IN track (130 mm) feeds only R120 100k.
evidence: c3.py, c5.py path trace; IPC-2221 hand calc

title: Heater FET Q101 drain has F.Cu-only copper, no vias
claim: LSU_HTR_N is 50.5 mm2 on F.Cu with 0 vias and no inner copper; 2.3 A rms warm-up x 70 mohm max = 0.37 W for ~14 s, about +20-25 K; steady state 0.04 W. Acceptable.
evidence: c8.py; VND14NV04 datasheet C2649436 (Rds 35/70 mohm, Rthj-case 1.7)

title: MCU decoupling, VDDA and crystal geometry identical to rev 0.10 (same weaknesses)
claim: VDD pin to 100 nF distance 2.7-7.8 mm, pins 11/19/28 share C3, VDDA caps 9.2-9.6 mm from pins 21/22, HSE traces 12.6/15.3 mm: all equal to rev 0.10 within 0.5 mm, so B07's weaknesses apply. Wideband crystal routing is slightly better (all F.Cu).
evidence: c4.py, pcb_net_routing.csv ord vs cur

title: CEL lamp behind shared driver enable (carried from B03)
claim: CEL_G = Q13.1 RN3.1 U12.6, so the lamp is dead when DRV_EN is off or firmware dead.
evidence: pcb_nets.txt /Outputs/CEL_G
suggested_fix: Cut U12.6-Q13 gate, wire PE4 (U1.3), tie U12.18 to GND; or accept.

title: 4-layer inner copper and heat spreading less than rev 0.10 (assumed 0.5 oz inner)
claim: 35 um-equivalent copper per driver is about 248 mm2 (F 90 + In2 105 x 0.5 + B 105) vs ~298 on rev 0.10, assuming JLC default 0.5 oz inner; copper weight is not in the gbrjob. Included in the thermal model numbers.
evidence: c1.py; gbrjob has no weight; JLC default from memory
suggested_fix: Confirm copper weight in the JLC order.

title: Ordered firmware drives tach output into 2I on 1989-95
claim: The ordered firmware lacks miataNoTachOutput(), so the 1989-93 and 1994-95 presets leave tachOutputPin on PE3. The ordered 1989-95 motherboards wire OUT_TACH straight to 2I, which the FSM-based PIN notes show is the igniter signal INTO the ECU. The ECU will pull 2I low twice per revolution with no pull-up and disturb the tach and the igniter signal.
evidence: diff repo/firmware/board vs ordered-boards/2026-11/firmware/board (miata_board.cpp, NA6/NA94 cases); kb/interconnect.md lines 1071-1123 and 1257-1309 (2I = OUT_TACH); kb/pinouts PIN-8993 item 5, PIN-9495 item 6
suggested_fix: Before the car is started, set Tach output to none in TunerStudio after pressing each 1989-95 year button, or flash firmware that includes miataNoTachOutput().

title: A/C switch input polarity never set (reads active-high)
claim: The firmware never sets acSwitchMode, so rusEFI treats a HIGH pin as an A/C request. R16 (a secondary FSM voltage table) says 1989-93 pin 1Q is below 2.5 V when A/C is on (active-low), and the 1989-95 motherboard pulls the pin up to VBAT. With A/C off the ECU would see an A/C request: fans run, idle-up applies and the A/C relay output is energised. The polarity on 1994-2005 is not established by any source read.
evidence: miata_board.cpp setInputs() has no acSwitchMode; rusEFI hw_layer/debounce.cpp:109-115 (inverts only for PI_PULLUP); kb/research/R16 (1Q); cur_mb8995 R21 4.7k to VBAT_IN; PIN-9900 row 1P (cannot verify)
suggested_fix: Confirm the 1Q/1P level on a car, then set acSwitchMode (PI_PULLUP for active-low) in the year presets, or document the TunerStudio setting.

title: CEL stays dark on fatal error on ordered rev 0.9 boards
claim: On the ordered daughterboard the CEL gate is behind the shared driver enable, and the ordered firmware has no direct CEL drive. After a critical firmware error the injectors are disabled and the dash lamp stays dark, so the driver sees no warning (only the red LED inside the case).
evidence: evidence/ord_db pcb_nets.txt CEL_CTL = U1.3 U12.18; diff board_configuration.cpp (lightCelOnFatalError exists only in the current firmware); the code comment says 'On a rev 0.9 board the lamp is behind the enable and stays dark'
suggested_fix: Tell the owner. A hardware rework is not practical, so rely on the board LEDs or TunerStudio during bring-up.

title: Clutch switch input reads inverted
claim: clutchDownPinMode defaults to PI_PULLUP and getClutchDownState() returns the raw pin level, so 'clutch down' means HIGH. The stock switch (1989-93 pin 1V) is 0 V with the clutch in or in neutral, so the state is inverted. Only launch control and shift torque reduction use it, and both are off by default.
evidence: rusEFI engine_configuration.cpp:223, engine.cpp:235, io_pins.cpp:158; kb/research/R16 (1V)
suggested_fix: Set clutchDownPinMode = PI_INVERTED_PULLUP (or the verified polarity) in the presets.

title: Every Burn drops all behind-enable outputs (documented)
claim: Every Burn calls applyNewHardwareSettings(), which disables the 15 low-side drivers (injectors, pump, relays, 2003-05 main relay) for the reconfiguration time. The README documents this. The duration is unmeasured, and on 2003-05 the main relay coil releases during it, so do not Burn with the engine running.
evidence: board_configuration.cpp:115-132; rusEFI engine_configuration.cpp:142 and hardware.cpp:139; firmware/README.md:132
suggested_fix: Measure the window on the bench and state 'no Burn while running' in INSTALL.md.

title: Pin map, dividers, MAP and thermistor model checked correct
claim: All firmware pins match the U1 pads and nets on both daughterboards (the yaml J1/J2 ids too). The analog divider is 1.56 and the battery divider 5.853, recomputed from R11-R44. MPX5700AP 0.2 V to 4.70 V at 0 to 700 kPa is right. The CLT/IAT bias (2.30 k behind 4.262 V) matches the 2.7k pull-up loaded by 15.6k. vbatt correctly bypasses the 1.56 divider.
evidence: work/F01.../u1.txt, chk.py; pcb_footprints.csv values; rusEFI init_vbatt.cpp, init_thermistors.cpp:51
suggested_fix: None.

title: Output polarity and PA8 enable sequencing checked correct
claim: The chain is MCU 3.3 V push-pull, then LVC4245 (DIR pin 2 = GND, B to A), then VND7NV04 or ZXMS6004, all non-inverting and active high. The ignition path (TC4427 plus 74HCT04 inverter into the ZXMS pull-down) is low at reset because of the RN1 pull-downs. PA8 is open drain with an R71 5 V pull-up, so every driver stays off through reset and the bootloader. The code releases the drivers after 4 slow ticks and parks unused control pins as pull-down inputs.
evidence: cur_db pcb_nets.txt U11/U12 pin nets; board_configuration.cpp:35-148
suggested_fix: None. The LVC4245 OE input reference rail was not checked in the datasheet.

title: EXTI, timer and CAN2 requirements checked, no conflicts
claim: Triggers, VSS and flex all use EXTI lines (7, 8, 9, 6). Nitrous arming is polled, so PC7 does not collide with PE7. No timer or ICU is needed. CAN2-only works because rusEFI's ChibiOS fork enables the CAN1 clock on CAND2 start and installs default accept-all filters. That was read from the master branch, not the pinned commit.
evidence: rusEFI digital_input_exti.cpp, init_flex.cpp:25, nitrous_controller.cpp:143; rusefi/ChibiOS master hal_can_lld.c lines 662-694
suggested_fix: Confirm on the first board with caninfo and a wideband frame.

title: Stale code comment: CAN transceiver is TCAN1042V
claim: The comment names an SN65HVD230. The board has a TCAN1042VDRQ1 (U10), with 5 V VCC and 3.3 V VIO.
evidence: pcb_footprints.csv U10; miata_board.cpp:41
suggested_fix: Update the comment.

title: NA presets carry TPS 0.5-3.25 V calibration from the author's car
claim: The rusEFI NA presets set tpsMin = 100 and tpsMax = 650 counts, which are 5 mV per count, so 0.5 V and 3.25 V of sensor voltage. A stock TPS with a higher wide-open voltage would read 100 % early. The NB presets leave the 0-5 V default.
evidence: mazda_miata_1_6.cpp; tps.h:17 TPS_TS_CONVERSION
suggested_fix: Add a TPS calibration step to the first-start checklist.

title: Failed MAP falls back to flat 60 kPa estimate, no boost cut
claim: If the MAP sensor is invalid, speed density uses mapEstimateTable which rusEFI defaults to a flat 60 kPa and the presets do not change. At WOT or boost the engine is fuelled for 60 kPa; boost cut is also blind because it needs a valid MAP.
evidence: speed_density_airmass.cpp:175-193; default_fuel.cpp:405; limp_manager.cpp:168-171
suggested_fix: Set mapEstimateTable to realistic MAP vs rpm/TPS values (e.g. ~35 kPa closed throttle to ~95 kPa WOT) in all presets, and ship a TunerStudio warning/limp rev limit on MAP failure.

title: Protection defaults all off: boost cut, lambda protection, CLT rev limit
claim: boostCutPressure=0 (off), lambdaProtectionEnable=false, useCltBasedRpmLimit off, no oil protection sensor. A boosted car on the base tune has no automatic fuel cut for overboost, lean or overheat.
evidence: limp_manager.cpp:165-180; default_fuel.cpp:336; default_base_engine.cpp:432-440
suggested_fix: Set boostCutPressure about 150-160 kPa (about 8 psi) on all presets unless the owner sets it; enable lambdaProtection with sensible limits; add CLT-based rev limit (e.g. 3000 rpm above 115 C); document in README.

title: NB VE table is flat 80% above 116 kPa and untuned under boost
claim: All NB VE rows from 116 to 220 kPa are 80 (invented fill, README says 'about 100 kPa'). Boosted NB cars get fuel proportional to MAP at fixed VE; real VE differs, and STFT in the power region can add only +10 %, remove 5 %.
evidence: miata_nb_tune.cpp:64-68; miata_board.cpp:150-152
suggested_fix: Do not claim a boost-capable base; ship a lean-safe richer boost target or require tune; add a visible TunerStudio notice; set boost cut.

title: NA/NB boost ignition rows still aggressive for 91 octane
claim: NA table gives 22 deg at 2300 rpm and 18-21 deg at 3900-8000 rpm at 160 kPa (8.7 psi); NB gives 24-25 deg at 6800-8000 rpm at 158 kPa. Combined with untuned fuel this is unsafe on pump gas. Only forum rules of thumb (about 1 deg/psi pull) were found as comparison.
evidence: table rows printed in notes; web sources only anecdotal
suggested_fix: Cap advance above 110 kPa at about 10-12 deg in the shipped tables; keep NA light-load map.

title: NA6/NA94 idle PID pinned to +20% and generic open-loop idle curve
claim: NA common settings set idleRpmPid.minValue=20 while maxValue stays the default 20, so PID output is clamped to a constant 20 % and the README's closed-loop idle does not exist on 1989-95. The base open-loop curve is rusEFI's generic 75->50 % because the tuned 28->20 % curve is commented todo, so idle may be very high or unstable.
evidence: mazda_miata_1_6.cpp idle block; engine_configuration.cpp:524-525,365-371; efi_pid.cpp:114-118; mazda_miata_base_maps.cpp:33-34
suggested_fix: Set idleRpmPid.maxValue (e.g. 40) and use the 28->20 % open-loop curve for NA presets; test on a car.

title: Constant 4 ms dwell with no voltage correction
claim: Dwell is 4 ms constant, voltage correction 1.0 from 8-15 V; at cranking/low battery coils may be under-charged and at 14 V a high-energy coil may overheat. No source for stock NA igniter or NB coil pack dwell was found.
evidence: default_ignition.cpp:112-115; web search found only anecdotes (3.0-3.5 ms)
suggested_fix: Set dwell per year from Mazda/Haltech/MS Miata values and add voltage correction curve.

title: Trigger angle offset default 0: timing correct only after timing light check
claim: No Miata preset sets globalTriggerAngleOffset (only the 36-1 NB2 variant does). Until the owner checks with a timing light the real timing error equals any decoder/CAS offset (NA CAS is rotatable). README step 11 documents it but it is step 11, far from first start.
evidence: mazda_miata_vvt.cpp:491; README:249-251
suggested_fix: Make fixed 10 deg timing lock the default first-boot state (timingMode fixed) with a one-time prompt, and put it in the quick-start.

title: Fuel closed-loop on by default is bounded and fails safe
claim: STFT: +-10 % idle/cruise, +10/-5 power, waits 60 s and CLT>60 C, no trim if wideband invalid or AFR outside 12-17. Checked as safe; failed CLT forces fan on; failed CLT warm-up correction=1.
evidence: closed_loop_fuel.cpp getCorrectionState/getLearningState; default_fuel.cpp:196-203; fan_control.cpp:78
suggested_fix: None.

title: 1994-95 fan 100/96 C inconsistent with other years 92/88
claim: Only the 1994-95 preset sets fan on at 100 C and fan2 at 95 C (fan2 below fan1); other years use rusEFI default 92/88. Marginal for hot or boosted cars.
evidence: mazda_miata_1_6.cpp:282-285; fan_control.cpp:264
suggested_fix: Set common 92/88 (fan2 at 97/93) for all years.

title: 1.6 VE table (VE up to 130 %) reused for 1.8 years
claim: VE values 104-130 % at 99-128 kPa are not physical VEs; the table absorbs injector flow/dead-time/MAP calibration of the source 1.6 car and is applied with different displacement (1.8/1.839) and injectors (254/265). README already warns of more wideband correction.
evidence: mazda_miata_1_6.cpp VE rows; miata_board.cpp presets
suggested_fix: Verify with sim or a real car per year; lean-safe skew.

title: Wideband MCU has no watchdog; hang can leave heater on
claim: IWDG is disabled in the port. If the F103 firmware hangs while TIM2_CH3 output is high, the VND14NV04 stays on and drives the LSU heater at full battery voltage (Bosch max 13 V effective). The same is true of upstream firmware.
evidence: mcuconf.h:225 STM32_WDG_USE_IWDG FALSE; heater_control.cpp pinned limits only voltage/duty in software; Bosch LSU49 datasheet p2 heater strategy 13 V max
suggested_fix: Enable the IWDG in the port and kick it from the heater thread, so a hang resets the MCU and the R126 pull-down turns the heater off.

title: Main MCU reset mid-flash leaves F103 in ROM bootloader / blank
claim: If the F407 resets during a flash, PD10 floats and R129 pulls BOOT0 low but nothing resets the F103. It stays in the bootloader with a partial or erased image. After a power cycle the wideband is dead until the user re-runs the flash. Recovery is always possible because the ROM bootloader is immutable, and the heater stays off.
evidence: wideband_uart_flash.cpp:356-361 init only releases pins; net WB_BOOT0 R129.2 U1.57 U102.44
suggested_fix: Document it. Optionally have init pulse NRST once when the wideband CAN frames are missing.

title: Blank F103 means no wideband until first flash
claim: A JLC-assembled F103 has empty flash, so the wideband does nothing until the ECU runs and the user presses Flash on-board wideband (or SWD J102 is used). The seller should flash it before shipping and the install guide must say so.
evidence: firmware/wideband/README.md: no bootloader, ECU flashes via ROM bootloader
suggested_fix: Flash and test in the assembly or QA step. State it in INSTALL.

title: Engine-stopped check only at flash start
claim: rpmCalculator.isStopped() is checked only once. The engine could be cranked during the 10-15 s flash, with the wideband (heater, CAN) off and in reset. The effect is mostly loss of the lambda trim.
evidence: wideband_uart_flash.cpp:372-379; the thread never re-checks
suggested_fix: Abort in the thread loop if RPM > 0.

title: VM_RESISTOR_VALUE 11.6 subtracts R109, which is outside the measured loop
claim: The diff-amp reference R103 sits on WB_VMS, which is the sensor side of R109 (behind the PTC F2). The measured ESR therefore includes F2 but not R109. Subtracting 11.6 gives about -10 ohm bias, roughly 4.5 C at 300 ohm. Upstream uses the same convention, so it is negligible.
evidence: pcb_nets WB_VMS C104.1 F2.2 R103.1 R109.1; Bosch-derived table lsu49 250 ohm=806 C, 350 ohm=761 C
suggested_fix: Use 1.6 if exact calibration is wanted, or leave as is.

title: Preheat 2.0 V and ramp start 7 V differ from the Bosch strategy graph
claim: Condensation phase is 2.0 V (Bosch graph 1.5 V). The ramp starts at 7 V (Bosch 8.5 V) at 0.4 V/s to 12 V (Bosch max 0.4 V/s, 13 V). PWM is 390 Hz (>=100 Hz required), target ESR 300 ohm, supply on above 9.5 V. All are within or conservative of the Bosch limits except the slightly higher condensation voltage, which is upstream's choice.
evidence: LSU49_bosch.pdf p2 heater strategy graph and electrical data
suggested_fix: None needed.

title: Pin, ADC, timer, CAN and clock checks passed
claim: All port pins match the PCB nets. LQFP48 numbering was used. TIM2 partial remap 2 puts CH3 on PB10. 8 MHz x6 gives 48 MHz, APB1 24 MHz, CAN 500 kbit/s at 87.5 %, ADC 12 MHz. CAN index 0 gives ID 0x190 base. Gain 2.7, Ip gain 10 and the 100k/10k divider match the fitted parts.
evidence: pcb_nets.txt lines 95-130,228-231; board.h; mcuconf.h:44-55; f1 port_shared.cpp
suggested_fix: None.

title: Committed wideband binary: hash matches, reproducibility depends on compiler
claim: The sha256 of the committed bin matches the .txt. The source is rusEFI wideband 27e115b (MIT) plus the port, and the image only reproduces with gcc 13.2.1 (CI compares). The .txt does not record the port's own repo commit. I did not rebuild it (no arm gcc). Redistributing the image requires the MIT and Apache notices.
evidence: sha256 fa9eece8...5e68 recomputed; .gitmodules gitlink 27e115b
suggested_fix: Record the repo commit in the .txt.

title: AN3155 sequence in flasher consistent with spec (checked from memory)
claim: Sync 0x7F, Get with N excluding the version byte, GetID 0x410, mass erase 0x43 with FF 00, 256-byte write, 64-byte read-back verify, 8E1 at 115200, 10 s erase timeout: all match AN3155 as recalled. The st.com documents could not be fetched, so this is not verified against the primary source.
evidence: code read; ST PDFs unreachable from sandbox
suggested_fix: Confirm against AN3155 rev text. Add a test against real silicon.

title: No matching online ini for this board
claim: The build disables the rusefi.com ini upload, so the firmware signature (rusEFI master.<date>.miata-ecu.<hash>) has no online ini; a customer's TunerStudio/console cannot fetch a match and must use the ini from the exact same build. Date and config hash are in the signature, so every rebuild changes it.
evidence: .github/workflows/firmware.yaml build step 'uploads: ""'; rusEFI wiki INI lookup logic (signature format, one ini per build); ini signature line in firmware/tunerstudio/generated/*.ini
suggested_fix: Ship the ini with every board (release asset, QR, USB stick) with step-by-step project creation; pin one release per year; or get the board accepted upstream for online ini.

title: Firmware only as expiring CI artifacts, no release
claim: Customers are told to open a GitHub Actions run and download artifacts. There is no release/tag, checksum, version note or sign-off checklist; any push touching firmware/ makes a new run. Artifact expiry and login requirement are from memory.
evidence: firmware/README.md 'Getting the firmware'; firmware.yaml has only upload-artifact steps and permissions: contents: read
suggested_fix: Publish tagged GitHub Releases with fixed URLs, SHA-256, matching ini, wideband image version and a release checklist (pin tested rusEFI commit, run sims, flash a real board).

title: Seller can pre-flash everything and pre-select the year
claim: INSTALL's bench check makes the customer pick the year and flash the wideband; both can be done at the bench by the seller (USB only), since the year-specific motherboard is sold with the order. This removes the wrong-NB2-button no-fuel/no-spark trap and a tune wipe by pressing a year button later (buttons reset the tune).
evidence: INSTALL.md:123-126; firmware/README.md 'Choosing the year' ; board_popular_vehicles.ini; board.mk default NA6
suggested_fix: Pre-flash main MCU and wideband, press the year, save/ship a .msq, confirm CAN lambda; keep the buttons as service only.

title: F4 build cannot carry its own ini
claim: EFI_EMBED_INI_MSD defaults FALSE on F4; embedding is not an option here: a rusEFI ini is ~930 kB (about 196 kB gzipped, measured on the f407-discovery ini as a proxy) against 77 kB spare flash.
evidence: firmware/ext/rusefi/firmware/config/stm32f4ems/efifeatures.h:406-409; gzip size computed; VERIFICATION.md:102
suggested_fix: Do not rely on the ECU supplying the ini; ship it with the product and microSD card.

title: Brick recovery needs BOOT button inside the case
claim: First flash and DFU recovery need BOOT+RESET on the daughterboard, which sits in the stock case; INSTALL.md lists case openings for J2, USB-C, ribbon and hose, not for the buttons. Normal updates go over OpenBLT without buttons, so a brick should be rare (OpenBLT recovery not verified).
evidence: firmware/README.md steps 1-2; INSTALL.md:140-157; wiki HOWTO Update Firmware (DFU only as advanced recovery)
suggested_fix: Pre-flash; document opening the case; consider a pinhole/access hole; offer swap/return service; test that a corrupted app leaves OpenBLT reachable.

title: Wideband flash is a fragile customer step
claim: The flash refuses with the engine turning, erases the wideband settings, and a failed flash leaves the F103 blank (needs retry or SWD pads). The button is a numeric board action in the ini, so a mismatched ini gives the wrong button behaviour. rusEFI's own Update wideband firmware button is the wrong one for this board.
evidence: VERIFICATION.md:196-199; board_commands.ini; firmware/README.md 'Flashing the on-board wideband'
suggested_fix: Flash and check wbo_uart_status at the bench; hide or relabel the button for customers.

title: Pinned rusEFI is already 239 commits behind master
claim: Pin is dated 2026-10-30; master is 239 commits ahead 17 days later. There is no scheduled bump workflow (fw-custom-example has a daily one). Each bump needs re-running pin checks, image checks, simulations and ideally a car test. Pin to a release/LTS ref (the action supports branches named lts*).
evidence: git log in submodule; GitHub compare API 1374bd07...master ahead_by 239 (2026-11-16); custom-board-build/action.yaml 'lts' handling; Custom-Firmware wiki
suggested_fix: Freeze a customer-release commit, bump on a schedule, record it in release notes.

title: Software costs and free alternative not stated to customers
claim: INSTALL says only 'TunerStudio'. EFI Analytics lists TunerStudio MS $89.95 list/$69.95 sale, Ultra $129.95/$99.95 (integrated log viewer, trim analyze), MegaLogViewer HD $69.95/$49.95, MS $49.95/$34.95. rusEFI's wiki recommends its own free rusEFI tuner with built-in log viewing first; free TunerStudio limits were not found.
evidence: efianalytics.com/register/browseProducts.jsp (fetched via summarising tool); wiki.rusefi.com Connectivity page
suggested_fix: State the cost, recommend rusEFI tuner for logs and basic tuning, test the ini and the Popular Vehicles buttons in it.

title: Official rusEFI or FOME acceptance trade-off
claim: Official rusEFI boards need a board folder, gen_config.sh entry, build-firmware.yaml entry and connector yaml; benefit is build-server bundles and online ini. FOME has fixed dated release assets but only Hellen-type boards; it diverges from rusEFI, so porting means a second code base. Acceptance policy not read; Miata-specific FOME differences not verified.
evidence: readme.md new board procedure; FOME releases via GitHub API (release_260501_02, 2026-06-04); search summary
suggested_fix: Stay on rusEFI custom build until hardware is proven, then approach rusEFI for official listing; revisit FOME only if a stable release cadence is needed.

title: Ordered rev 0.9 injector driver junctions +78..+86 C over air at 20 mH (tool output)
refs: Q1-Q4 VND7NV04 (driver's own clamp), board_thermal.py case rev09
claim: board_thermal.py on the ordered 4-layer board gives driver junctions +46..50 C at 8 mH but +78..86 C at 20 mH (sequential, 7200 rpm, h=10, 1.2 A at 80% duty). The tool adds no ambient, so 85 C case air would give about 165-171 C. The 8 vs 20 mH uncertainty is documented; the 20 mH figure for the ordered board is quantified here.
evidence: work/F05.../thermal_ord.log; board_thermal.py:62-90 losses(); sim_inj_clamp DRV 20 mH 15.3 mJ/shot = 1.84 W batch
suggested_fix: Measure the injector L with an LCR meter before the first run, and put a thermocouple or IR camera on Q1-Q4 in a hot box. Keep engine tests short at high duty until measured.

title: track_current.py never checks the INJn_CL nets (net-name mismatch)
claim: The PCB net is '/Outputs/INJ1_CL' but the tool looks for 'INJ1_CL'. It finds no copper and prints '[OK] 0.0 C 0.00 A in 0.0 mm'. The check passes vacuously. Real exposure is small (0.2 A rms on 0.8 mm track).
evidence: grep of kicad_pcb: (net 71 "/Outputs/INJ1_CL"); today's run output; evidence/cur_db/pcb_net_routing.csv 0.8 mm
suggested_fix: Match nets by suffix or full name, and make 'no copper found for a loaded net' a CHECK.

title: circuit_sim.py (run in CI) is hard-coded and models a superseded driver
claim: The docstring says values come from design.py, but the file imports nothing from design. The low-side section simulates NCV8406A with a 60 V clamp, 8 mH and SMCJ40A (rev 0.5/0.6), not the fitted VND7NV04 (36-55 V clamp). The CI-green result and the 'as built' row 96 say nothing about the current driver.
evidence: circuit_sim.py:3 and 226-333; grep for 'design' shows only the docstring; design.py:334,529 mention NCV8406A in comments only; today's output rows 'NCV8406A gate drive', 'SMCJ40A (rev 0.6)'
suggested_fix: Import design.py and assert values as circuit_sim_full does, or retire the section and rely on sim_inj_clamp and circuit_sim_full. Update VERIFICATION.md row 96.

title: circuit_sim_full.py crashes on the current tree layout
claim: It loads motherboards/1989-93/... and mb/release_8993/..., which do not exist in today's tree (1989-93 survives only under ordered-boards/). pcbnew.LoadBoard returned None and the script died with AttributeError 'NoneType' has no Zones. It works after pointing at the ordered copy: 93 OK / 11 CHECK / 1 REF, matching VERIFICATION.md:861.
evidence: run log work/F05.../csf.log; repo find shows no motherboards/1989-93
suggested_fix: Point the loader at motherboards/1989-95 or ordered-boards, and fail clearly if the board cannot be loaded.

title: Renode firmware-in-the-loop does not test the board wiring and is not automatic
claim: Stimulus is ideal voltages at named MCU pins using divider constants hard-coded in run_ecu.py, and the LSU plant uses the firmware's own scale factors, so a wrong divider, pin or connector on the PCB would not be seen. Many peripherals (ADC, DMA, NVIC, F103 ROM bootloader) are the authors' own models. The workflow runs only on workflow_dispatch, yet VERIFICATION.md:594 calls it 'in CI'. Not run here (no Renode).
evidence: sim.yaml on: workflow_dispatch; LsuSensor.cs header comment; sim/README.md gaps table
suggested_fix: Treat a pass as 'firmware config is self-consistent'. Confirm with a hardware-in-the-loop trigger/sensor rig on the real board.

title: Schematic/netlist checks compare design.py with a schematic generated from design.py
claim: Both sides come from the same Python source, so these checks catch generator bugs (split or merged nets) but not wrong pin numbering vs the real part or design errors. The only independent pin reference is check_mcu_pins vs ST XML, and it covers the F407 only. With no human schematic review, 'schematic matches design' is weak evidence.
evidence: check_sch_netlist.py:15-20 (exp from design.parts); gen_sch.py generates the schematic
suggested_fix: Add datasheet-derived pin tables (kb pinouts) as an independent check for each IC, and manually review pin 1 and orientation on the ordered boards.

title: sim_inj_clamp.py verdicts are mostly not computed from results
claim: rec() defaults to 'OK'. At 24 V the F row prints 50 mJ per shot in the driver clamp yet is OK, because the verdict is just vb>30. For SMCJ15A/16A/18A the worst case puts 97-100% of the heat in the driver clamp yet B is OK. Fitted 1.5SMC16A shows 0% in the driver, so the fitted part is not affected, but the verdict column is not pass/fail evidence.
evidence: sim_inj_clamp.py lines for groups B and F; today's inj.log
suggested_fix: Compute verdicts from limits (EAS, peak vs driver clamp, TVS power vs derated rating).

title: sim_inj_clamp today: values for the two clamp schemes (reference numbers)
claim: Ran OK (exit 0). At 20 mH, 14.4 V, 12 ohm: driver-clamp (ordered) peak 42.7 V and 15.3 mJ/shot (1.84 W batch at 7200 rpm). Rev 0.10 TVS-to-VBAT_IN: peak 31.9 V, 8.3 mJ/shot in TVS. At 40-45 V supply the driver clamp takes 178-225 mJ/shot (EAS 200 mJ). Single-driver pair, worst case: TVS 1.17-2.34 W. The model assumes VBAT_IN is a 0.05 ohm + 10 uF source, injector L swept, TVS tempco 0.1%/C assumed.
evidence: work/F05.../inj.log
suggested_fix: Measure the real injector L and the VBAT_IN impedance on the bench; the model cannot be better than those inputs.

title: board_thermal.py: assumed loads, no ambient, uncertain h; needs undocumented tools
claim: Loss table is hard-coded (1.2 A at 80% duty per injector, rail loads guessed), h=10 W/m2K (stated to be good only to a factor of 1.5), Rth_jc from maker figures, laminate k recalled. No case-air offset. Self-test gives 54 C/W at h=10 against 'recalled 40-50'. It needs rsvg-convert, kicad-cli, scipy and pcbnew together; I shimmed rsvg-convert with cairosvg. Today rev 0.10 seq: TVS junction +50..52 C, batch1 D46 +116 C, Q1 +72 C.
evidence: board_thermal.py:36-90, 270-300; thermal.log; th_self.log
suggested_fix: Validate with thermocouple/IR measurements in a hot box inside the stock case; document the tool dependencies.

title: board_checks.py reproduces: 1602 OK / 265 CHECK / 4 FAIL, but car loads and cavity table are the repo's own
claim: Runs in 29 s. The 4 FAILs are the documented LSU drive resistors R108/R110. The repo claims 1606/263/4 (VERIFICATION.md:860), a small unexplained drift. Method is DC steady state with assumed car loads and a cavity-function table from sim_report.py; board_copper rebuilds connectivity from geometry independent of net names (strong). It runs the current mb_* modules, so it is not proven to cover the frozen ordered boards.
evidence: bc.log; board_checks.py docstring MODEL NOTES
suggested_fix: Run the same checks against ordered-boards/ (pass board paths), and add transient cases (load dump, coil spikes).

title: check_mcu_pins.py and check_pins.py pass; the independent reference covers only the F407 pin map
claim: 79 processor pads match ST's pin XML and no supply pin is left open; check_pins matches 41 defines and 39 connector entries to design.py. Both check design.py, not the .kicad_pcb or the ordered rev 0.9 netlist.
evidence: run output 'OK: every pad matches'; 'pins OK'
suggested_fix: Run the same against the ordered netlist (evidence/ord_db/sch_netlist.xml) and the F103 XML.

title: track_current.py covers only rev 0.10 and treats pours as perfect conductors
claim: It imports design.py (rev 0.10), so it was not run on the ordered boards. Pours are perfect conductors and via resistance is a fixed 1 mOhm, so necks and thermal reliefs are invisible. OUT_VVT was checked (6.9 mm pour, 4 layers, fine). Today: 34 nets, 41 cases, 0 FAIL, worst 7.2 C (VBAT_IN inner layer).
evidence: track.log; zone_neck.py output
suggested_fix: Check 1.2 A injector, 2 A heater and 1.1 A supply paths on the ordered rev 0.9 board by hand or with an adapted script.

title: Failure classes no repo tool can see
claim: No tool tests footprint-pad to part-pin mapping and pin-1 orientation, JLC CPL rotation, EMC and signal integrity (CAN, USB, crystal, wideband analogue), buck loop stability, tolerance stacks, ESD, ADC noise or real case temperature. CI runs only check_pins, check_mcu_pins, check_image, circuit_sim.py, the unit-test engine sim and the wideband build; board_checks, circuit_sim_full, sim_inj_clamp, thermal and Renode are not in CI.
evidence: workflows grep; tool docstrings
suggested_fix: See the bench test list in the notes: ring-out, current-limited first power, injector bench with LCR and scope, HIL trigger rig, hot-box thermal, wideband free-air calibration.

title: MCU stock 74 at JLC: supply risk
claim: C12345 is an extended part with only 74 in stock at JLC and LCSC today, so a batch of 100 boards cannot be built from it. Pin-compatible STM32F405VGT6 C56621 has 1050 in stock at $5.4-7.6 (extended); DS8626 covers both and the LQFP100 pin tables are the same.
suggested_fix: Buy a reserve of C12345 now, and qualify F405VGT6 as a second source (firmware target define; rusEFI F405 build support not verified here). Alternates APM32F407VGT6 C2990873 (stock 1107) and F427VGT6 C117815 were not datasheet-checked and are not recommended.

title: VDD pins 11 and 28 lack a local 100 nF
claim: There are six 100 nF caps for six VDD pins, but pins 11 and 28 have none within 5.1 mm and 7.2 mm (both rely on C3, which sits at pin 19), and C4 is 7.5 mm from pin 50. ST's rule is one 100 nF per VDD pin, close to it.
