evidence: pcb_pads.csv/pcb_footprints.csv distances computed; In4 +3V3 and In1 GND planes exist on the cur_db 6-layer board
suggested_fix: Move C4 next to pin 28 or add 100 nF 0402s at pins 11 and 28 (optional; ordered rev 0.9 can add one by hand).

title: Low junction-temperature margin at 85 C
claim: IDD max 102 mA (168 MHz, all peripherals, 85 C) gives about 0.34-0.36 W; with thetaJA 43 C/W TJ is about 100-103 C against the 105 C limit for the -6 suffix, and the 465 mW PD limit at 85 C is close. A stock ECU case may be hotter than the 85 C cabin figure.
evidence: DS8626 Table 20, Table 14 (PD 465 mW, TJ 105), Table 98 (43 C/W)
suggested_fix: Keep the PLL/peripheral load realistic and measure case air temperature in the first test; consider disabling unused peripheral clocks.

title: LED current very low with 1k at 3.3 V
claim: Green and blue LEDs (Vf about 3.1 V at 5 mA per the manifest) on a 3.3 V rail through 1k run well under 1 mA and will be dim; the LEDs are inside a closed case anyway.
evidence: parts_manifest D1/D2 rows; arithmetic (3.3-3.1)/1k
suggested_fix: Use 330-470 ohm for green/blue/power if they are meant to be seen, or drop some LEDs.

title: Pinout and peripherals checked correct
claim: Every U1 pad net matches ST's pin definitions, and every peripheral used (CAN2 PB12/13, USB FS PA11/12, USART3 PD8/9, USART6 PC6/7 on ord, SPI2 PB10/14/15 on cur, SWD PA13/14, ADC channels) exists on that pin. VBAT, VDD, VSS, VSSA, VREF+, VDDA, VCAP, BOOT0, BOOT1 and NRST are on the right pins.
evidence: pcb_pads.csv; research/st/STM32F407V(E-G)Tx.xml; check_mcu_pins.py output 'OK: every pad matches' (79 pads)
suggested_fix: None.

title: Crystal, VCAP, boot and reset circuit checked correct
claim: The 33 pF C0G pair gives CL of about 19-20 pF for 5-7 pF stray, against 20 pF specified; the critical Gm is 0.51 mA/V against 5 mA/V available (about 10x margin; ESR 80 ohm, C0 5 pF). VCAP is 2x2.2 uF X5R (ESR under 2 ohm) and the BOOT0/BOOT1 pull-downs and the NRST 100 nF are correct.
evidence: YXC YSX530GA p.1; DS8626 Tables 16 and 32; pcb_nets.txt
suggested_fix: None.

title: Backup-domain, PA8 and JTAG-pin reset behaviour OK
claim: PC13/PC14 drive only CMOS inputs (no load; 3 mA / 2 MHz rule met) and the LSE is disabled in firmware. PA8 (FT) drives the shared OE of the U11/U12 level shifters, pulled to 5 V, so the drivers stay off through reset. PB3/PB4 float or pull up at reset, but behind the disabled shifters.
evidence: DS8626 Table 9 note 3; SN74LVC4245A text (control powered by VCCA); pcb_nets.txt R71 to +5V
suggested_fix: None.

title: ST AN4488 and ES0182 not read
claim: st.com was unreachable from this machine, so the F4 errata (CAN, OTG_FS, ADC, SPI) were not checked against the firmware usage. A search fragment mentions OTG_FS FIFO erratum 2.14.1 in ES0182 Rev 18.
evidence: curl HTTP/2 INTERNAL_ERROR, page fetch timeout
suggested_fix: Read ES0182 manually for USB OTG FS, bxCAN and ADC items affecting rusEFI.

title: U102 full pin map checked: every pad, net and function correct
claim: All 48 U102 pads have the same net in the PCB and the schematic on both boards, and the schematic pin names equal ST's LQFP48 names. Every firmware function sits on a pin that has it: ADC IN0/2/3/8 on PA0/PA2/PA3/PB0, TIM3_CH1 on PA6, TIM2_CH3 on PB10 via partial remap 2, CAN on PA11/PA12, SWD on PA13/PA14, USART1 on PA9/PA10. Port register values decode to the intended modes.
evidence: evidence/*/pcb_pads.csv + sch_netlist.xml via work/P02-stm32f103-wideband-mcu/u102_table.py (all OK); repo/scripts/wideband.py U2_PADS; board.h CRL/CRH; port.cpp SQR3; DS5319 pin table
suggested_fix: none

title: Boot/reset/UART link to the main MCU correct
claim: PD8 (TX) goes to PA10 (RX) and PD9 (RX) to PA9 (TX), so the cross is right. BOOT0 has a 10k pull-down and is driven by PD10; BOOT1 (PB2) has a 10k to GND; NRST has 100 nF and is driven open-drain by PD11. This matches ROM bootloader entry (BOOT0=1, BOOT1=0, USART1 8E1, 0x7F sync). The flasher checks PID 0x410, erases, writes and verifies; PD10 floats at F407 reset so the F103 boots from flash.
evidence: pcb_nets.txt WB_PROG_TX/RX/BOOT0/NRST; firmware/board/wideband_uart_flash.cpp lines 1-372; design.py lines 165
suggested_fix: none

title: REF3033 pinout, D30 polarity, decoupling and footprint checked
claim: U103 1=+5V IN, 2=VDDA OUT, 3=GND matches the TI SOT23-3 pinout; no output cap is required and 1 uF + 100 nF is allowed; the load is about 3 mA of 25 mA. D30 has K on +3V3 and A on VDDA, the intended clamp direction. 100 nF sits 2-3.6 mm from each VDD pad and from VDDA. The LQFP48 footprint is the IPC/KiCad standard with numbering CCW from pad 1.
evidence: C36658 cover pinout and Fig. 2, abs max 7 V, ISC 45 mA; C124205 cathode band; pcb_pads.csv distances; DS5319 Fig. 63
suggested_fix: none

title: VDDA/VDD limit is 50 mV in ST datasheet, repo says 0.3 V; LDO tolerance exceeds it
refs: U103, D30, U4, repo/scripts/wideband.py D30 comment
claim: DS5319 Table 6 lists |VDDx| variation between VDD power pins as 50 mV max; the repo comment justifying D30 says ST allows 0.3 V. The LDL1117S33R is +-3 % over temperature (3.20-3.40 V) against REF3033 3.2934-3.3066 V, so steady VDD-VDDA differences up to about 0.1 V are possible, and D30 only clamps VDDA above VDD at about its forward drop (about 0.5 V at the REF's 45 mA limit). Functionally harmless because the ADC is ratiometric to VDDA and firmware assumes 3.3 V.
evidence: C8734 datasheet l.2121-2123 (Table 6); C435835 l.196-198; wideband.py D30 comment
suggested_fix: Correct the comment/doc. If strict compliance matters, feed VDDA from VDD through a ferrite or 10 ohm plus caps instead of the separate REF, at an accuracy cost. Otherwise accept.

title: HSE crystal has no fallback; upstream F1 wideband boards use HSI
claim: The port starts only from the HSE (STM32_HSE_ENABLED TRUE, PLL source HSE, no clock-security fallback), so a crystal that fails to start or an open solder joint leaves the wideband dead, and a blank chip with a bad crystal is also un-flashable only by the ROM loader (which uses HSI and still works). Upstream f1_rev2, f1_rev3 and f1_dual run from HSI with the same 48/24/12 MHz tree; only f1_dual_rev1 uses an 8 MHz HSE.
evidence: repo/firmware/wideband/miata_f1/mcuconf.h:44-49; ext/wideband-rusefi/firmware/boards/f1_rev3/mcuconf.h:44-53, f1_rev2/f1_dual board.h HSECLK 0
suggested_fix: Optional: keep HSE (accuracy) but verify crystal start-up at -40/+85 C on the first board; the 20 pF load and ESR 80 ohm give a gain margin of about 50 (inferred).

title: Option: drop Y101, C119, C120 and run the F103 from HSI like upstream
claim: Upstream rusEFI F1 wideband boards run the CAN at 500 kbit from HSI x12 = 48 MHz with BRP 3. The port could do the same with a firmware config change and the three parts left unfitted, saving about $0.19-0.25 per board plus 3 placements. Trade-off: HSI tolerance versus CAN timing margin, and the author chose HSE on purpose.
evidence: upstream f1_rev3 mcuconf.h PLLSRC_HSI, PLLMUL 12; port_shared.cpp CAN BTR identical; Y101 $0.183 @100 (parts manifest)
suggested_fix: Only if bench CAN tests with HSI pass over temperature; set STM32_HSE_ENABLED FALSE, PLLSRC HSI, PLLMUL 12, HSECLK 0 and mark parts DNP.

title: Clone F103C8 parts are not worth the saving
claim: C8734 is the genuine ST part at $1.14 @30 / $1.01 @250 with 191k+ stock (Preferred). Clones at JLC (GD32F103C8T6 C77994 about $1.04-1.62, APM32 C393540, CKS32 C556576, CH32 C2687451, FCM32 C3151837 about $0.45-0.91) save at most a few tenths of a dollar, differ in ADC timing, flash and bootloader, and the flasher's PID 0x410 check would not necessarily reject them. I did not read the clone datasheets.
evidence: tools/lcsc.py -s F103C8T6 results 2026-11-16; wideband_uart_flash.cpp WBO_PRODUCT_ID
suggested_fix: Keep C8734; if a clone is ever used, validate ADC, CAN and flash behaviour on it before changing the BOM.

title: J102 SWD pads are on the bottom side, not reachable once stacked
claim: The Tag-Connect TC2030-IDC-NL footprint is on the daughterboard bottom, which faces the motherboard after assembly, so the documented SWD fallback needs the stack taken apart (inferred from placement side). Pin assignment 1 VTref, 2 SWDIO, 3 NRST, 4 SWCLK, 5 GND matches the usual TC2030-NL ARM mapping (from memory).
evidence: pcb_footprints.csv J102 side bottom; pcb_pads.csv J102.1-6
suggested_fix: None needed for a first build; mention in docs that SWD recovery requires separating the boards.

title: R110 pump sense resistor is 0.62 ohm, not 62 ohm (C25341)
claim: BOM part C25341 is UNI-ROYAL 1206W4F620LT5E. The 11th code L means x10^-3, so it is 620 mOhm. Firmware assumes 61.9 ohm x gain 10, so measured pump current is about 100x too small and lambda reads about 1.0 whatever the exhaust is. The Nernst loop still closes, so the sensor is heated and pumped correctly but the reading is useless.
evidence: datasheets/txt/C25341_1206W4F620LT5E.txt sec 2.4.3 (L=10^-3); lcsc.py C25341 description '620mΩ'; fab BOM rev0.9_jlcpcb_bom.csv:76 and evidence/*_db/fab BOM list '62,R110,C25341'; sampling.cpp:44
suggested_fix: Change to C17971 (1206W4F620JT5E, 62 ohm 1%, ext, stock 123k, $0.0053). On the ordered rev 0.9 boards hand-replace R110 with a 62 ohm 1206 before first power-up.

title: VM_RESISTOR_VALUE 11.6 assumes F2 at its datasheet minimum
claim: nSMD010 is 1.6 ohm minimum, 15 ohm max (R1max), and it varies with trip history and temperature. The firmware constant uses 1.6 as typical. It only enters the ESR subtraction (sampling.cpp:91), not lambda. The Nernst tap (R103) is on the sensor side of F2, so the subtraction is already a constant bias. Effect is about 0.45 degC/ohm near 300 ohm, so roughly 5-7 degC.
evidence: C70065 datasheet table Rimin 1.600 / R1max 15.000; repo/firmware/wideband/miata_f1/wideband_board_config.h; sampling.cpp:86-91; lsu49 table 806 degC@250 ohm to 761@350
suggested_fix: Set the constant to 0 (or to R109 only) and check the LSU temperature at a known hot-sensor ESR; or use about 8 ohm if keeping the subtraction. No hardware change.

title: F2 PTC does not affect lambda or loop stability (checked)
claim: Pump current is U105 output minus the VM ADC reading. U105 is a differential amp across R110, referenced to the WB_VM op-amp output. The Nernst amp senses UN_BUF minus WB_VMS (sensor side). U101D feedback is taken at its output, before R109/F2. So F2 only costs up to 15 ohm x 2.25 mA = 34 mV of compliance, and its series resistance isolates the C104 load.
evidence: pcb_nets.txt / pcb_pads.csv nets WB_VMS (C104.1, R103.1, R109.1, F2.2), WB_VM; sampling.cpp:44, 80-91, 118; pump_control.cpp:70
suggested_fix: None.

title: U101 MCP6004 and U105 AD8628 pinouts correct
claim: All 14 TSSOP-14 pins and all 5 SOT-23-5 pins match the datasheet functions. U105 has OUT=1, V-=2 (GND), +IN=3, -IN=4, V+=5 (+3V3). The footprints use standard pitch and span. The unused-section problem does not arise (all four MCP sections used).
evidence: pcb_pads.csv U101/U105 rows (identical in cur_db and ord_db); MCP6004 DS20001733L pin table; AD8628 datasheet pin configuration
suggested_fix: None.

title: Netlist matches the mck1117 module apart from intended changes
claim: All reference nets and passive values map one-to-one (refs +100). The only deviations are 1206 fault-current resistors, R110 value, X7R C103 (better than Y5V), added F2/R137(22k)/D40/D41, and the removed VM sense on PA1 (ADC uses PA0/PA2/PA3/PB0 only). D40/D41 are oriented correctly as clamps to +3V3.
evidence: work/P03-wideband-analog/netcmp.py output; miata_f1/port.cpp:40-49
suggested_fix: None.

title: MCP6004 low stock; AD8628 is the largest cost item in the block
claim: MCP6004T-I/ST is an extended part with stock 1747 and $0.39 at qty 30. AD8628ARTZ is extended, stock 22.9k, $2.27 at qty 30 / $2.03 at qty 100 (about $2.3 per board). No alternate was evaluated, since no datasheet has been read for one.
evidence: tools/lcsc.py C50282 C29309, run 2026-11-16
suggested_fix: Keep for first builds; if cost matters, evaluate a cheaper low-offset op-amp for the 10x sense stage.

title: F1 PTC may nuisance-trip at ramp start in hot ECU case
claim: At ramp start (7 V effective, cold heater about 3.2 ohm, 14.4 V supply) heater RMS current is about 2.2 A. F1 hold derates to 1.99 A at 60 C and 1.34 A at 85 C, so at 85 C case air (trip about 2.2 A scaled) a cold-sensor warm-up can trip F1. The wideband then reports no heat and Stops.
evidence: 2920L derating table p.4 (3.00/1.99/1.34 A at 25/60/85 C); heater_control.cpp ramp 7 V +0.4 V/s; R_cold 3.2 ohm is a secondary web value (not in the Bosch datasheet); RMS = 7/3.2
suggested_fix: Use 2920L400/30GR (4 A hold, 1.79 A at 85 C) or 2920L500/30GR; check the harness wire and the JST 3 A contact. Or start the ramp at lower V/longer time when the F1 area is hot. Measure heater R and case temperature on the first build.

title: H- harness short to ground bypasses Q101 and F1 cannot protect the sensor
claim: If the heater return wire (J2 pin 2, or Micro-Fit pin 3 on ordered boards) shorts to chassis ground, the heater is powered continuously at about 14 V (4.5 A cold falling to about 2 A hot). That is below F1 trip (5 A at 25 C) and above Bosch's 13 V maximum, and firmware cannot switch it off.
evidence: Bosch DS p.2: 13 V max effective; F1 hold 3 A / trip 5 A; Q101 drain is the only switch
suggested_fix: Document it; optionally add a heater-current or Nernst-overtemp backstop that opens a high-side switch. Not worth hardware unless a high-side switch is already planned.

title: Q101 pinout, gate network and footprint checked correct
claim: Pad1 = INPUT via 1k from WB_HTR_PWM (PB10), tab pad2 and four side pads = DRAIN = LSU_HTR_N, pad3 = SOURCE = HTR_GND. This matches ST DPAK pins 1 input, 2 drain, 3 source. RIN MIN is 10 ohm, so 1k is fine. R126 pulls the gate low at reset. Pad pitch 4.56 mm and tab 6.4x5.8 are standard DPAK.
evidence: evidence/cur_db/pcb_pads.csv:425-431, ord_db pcb_pads.csv:387-393; pcb_nets.txt:102-103,157,184; VND14NV04 DS p.5 fig 1, table 2
suggested_fix: None.

title: Firmware heater profile within Bosch limits; supply sense is adequate
claim: 390 Hz PWM (Bosch minimum 100 Hz). Preheat 2.0 V for 5 s (Bosch graph shows 1.5 V in the condensation phase, a minor excess). Ramp starts at 7 V (Bosch steps to 8.5 V) at 0.4 V/s as Bosch specifies, capped at 12 V (Bosch 13 V). Duty = (Veff/Vbat)^2. Heater is off at >=23 V. Vbat is sensed by R120/R121 100k/10k on PB0 from VBAT_IN, ahead of F1, so the error is under 1%.
evidence: LSU49_bosch.pdf p.2 heater strategy; heater_thread.cpp:9-14; wideband_config.h:43-53; port.cpp:77-91; pinned 27e115b = built image (miata_wbo_f103.txt)
suggested_fix: Optionally lower preheat to 1.5 V. ext/wideband-rusefi HEAD differs from the pinned commit.

title: Q101 thermal and electrical stress acceptable
claim: Realistic dissipation is at most about 0.5 W (conduction 4.5 A peak x 0.06 ohm x duty plus switching about 0.1 W). With about 0.4 cm2 of drain copper (Rth about 75-80 C/W), Tj is about 125 C at 85 C air, below the 150 C shutdown. The TVS (SMCJ30A) acts before Q101's 40-55 V clamp. Gate at about 3.1 V is above the typical threshold but below the 5 V RDS(on) spec point, so margin at worst-case Vth (2.5 V) is thin.
evidence: DS tables 2-4, fig 11/12/15/34; q101_fcu.png; D6 SMCJ30A on VBAT_IN
suggested_fix: Optional: add a pour or a few thermal vias on the drain tab; check that the PB10 high level reaches at least 3.2 V.

title: Header pins, tracks and connectors carry the heater current
refs: J2.37-40, JD2.37-40, HTR_PWR, LSU_HTR_N, JST PUD J2 (current), Molex 430450600 J2 (ordered)
claim: Each net uses 2 header pins (2.25 A peak, about 1.1 A RMS per pin). All tracks are 1.0 mm. Total loop resistance is about 0.2 ohm, so about 0.9 V is lost at 4.5 A pulses, which PID absorbs. The JST PUD contact (3 A per the repo, not opened) is thin against 2.2-3 A RMS at ramp. Ordered Molex Micro-Fit contacts are 8.5 A rated.
evidence: pcb_net_routing.csv for all 9 motherboards and the daughterboard; pcb_pads.csv JD2.37-40; INSTALL.md; C127367 params
suggested_fix: None required; if F1 is raised, re-check the JST 3 A limit and the harness wire gauge.

title: No cheaper equivalent for VND14NV04 with the same protections
claim: C2649436 costs $1.36 at 100 (extended, stock 1902). VND7NV04 (C155605, $1.66 at 100) has the same footprint but about 6 A class limiting, so it is neither cheaper nor adequate. A plain logic MOSFET (about $0.10-0.19, e.g. IRLR2905-class) would save about $1.2 per unit but drops current limit, over-temperature and clamp, and a 3.3 V gate is marginal. Its datasheet was not read, so it is not recommended.
evidence: tools/lcsc.py lookups 2026-11-16
suggested_fix: Keep VND14NV04 unless the owner analyses a discrete MOSFET with a heater-short strategy.

title: Output capacitance about 25-30 uF vs TI '47 uF needed for stability'
claim: TI states 'for stability consideration, one 47 uF output capacitor is needed at least' for the 1 MHz / 5.5 uH example. The board has 3 x 10 uF at the buck output plus C26, which is about 25-30 uF after DC-bias derating (derating UNVERIFIED), at 2.3 MHz / 10 uH. The datasheet gives no formula to scale 47 uF to other fSW and L, so stability is not provable from the datasheet.
evidence: SNVSAA5B p.19 section 7.2.2.4; design.py:239-241; Samsung CL21A106KAYNNNE is X5R 25 V 0805 (C15850)
suggested_fix: Bench-measure load-step and Bode on the first board. Cheap hedge: swap C22/C23 for 22 uF 10 V 0805 X5R parts, or add one more 10 uF, to reach at least 47 uF nominal.

title: Ordered F1 0.5 A PTC and 1210 L1 are tight at hot temperature
claim: On the ordered rev 0.9 the +12V logic feed passes a 0.5 A hold PTC (about 47 % of hold at 85 C by the BSMD family derating table; the nSMD050 curve itself was not read). The buck draws about 0.2-0.35 A at 12-14 V and about 0.7 A at 5.4 V while cranking, plus tracker loads. That is at or above the hot hold current, so nuisance trips are plausible. Cross-check with P16.
evidence: BSMD1812-110 derating row: 1.10 A -> 0.52 A at 85 C (C883150 datasheet); manifest ord_db F1 C70077; design.py:211-223 comments; load budget in notes
suggested_fix: Check the nSMD050 hold-current vs temperature curve; if the margin is thin, rework the ordered board with a 1812 1.1 A fuse (as on rev 0.10) before first power-up.

title: VIN abs-max margin in an unsuppressed load dump
refs: U2 pin 2/3, D12 SMAJ33A, D6, F1
claim: D12 SMAJ33A starts conducting at 36.7-40.6 V and clamps to 53.3 V at 7.5 A, with a slope of roughly 2 Ohm. U2 VIN/EN/SW are rated 44 V, BOOT 49 V. With D6 SMCJ30A clamping up to 48.4 V and the PTC (0.25 Ohm) in series, the buck input can briefly see about 45-47 V in an unsuppressed dump until the PTC trips. Suppressed dumps (35 V) and the 24 V jump start are safe.
evidence: C223988 table (VBR 36.7-40.6, VC 53.3 @7.5 A); C224048 (VC 48.4 V @31 A); TI SNVSAA5B p.4 abs max; slope computed from datasheet numbers
suggested_fix: Overlaps P06. Accept the risk, or use SMAJ28A / SMBJ28A at D12 (breakdown about 31 V), which leaves the 36 V suppressed dump near the knee. Weigh against the leakage and heating of a lower-voltage TVS in a 14.4-16 V system.

title: RT 10 k sets 2.295 MHz, above TI's 2.2 MHz value; tolerance can exceed 2.5 MHz
claim: fSW = (32537/10)^(1/1.045) = 2.295 MHz. TI's table gives 10.5 k for 2.2 MHz. The spec at 500 kHz is +-20 %, so the top of the spread could pass the recommended 2.5 MHz maximum. That costs only switching loss and minimum on-time margin at 24 V or more, not function.
evidence: SNVSAA5B eq.5, table 6-1, section 5.6 fSW 400-600 kHz at 49.9 k, section 5.3 range 200-2500 kHz
suggested_fix: Optional: use 10.5 k (E96) or 11 k, giving 2.2 / 2.1 MHz, at the cost of a non-basic or less common value. Not urgent.

title: Doc/BOM comment overstates L2 Isat (5.5 A)
claim: design.py says Isat 5.5 A (it takes JLC's listing). The Sunlord series sheet gives 5.2 A typ and Irms 4.5 A typ for the 10 uH part; the 5.5 A figure belongs to the 8.2 uH part. The conclusion is unchanged: Isat 5.2 A is above the 3.8 A maximum current limit.
evidence: Sunlord MWSA series sheet (datasheets/extra/MWSA_chipdip.pdf) row MWSA0603S-100MT: 10 uH, 68 mOhm, 5.20 A, 4.50 A; design.py:234
suggested_fix: Correct the comment. No hardware change.

title: Cranking dropout: 5 V falls to about 4.8-5.0 V at 6 V battery
claim: With 6 V at the battery, D7 (about 0.4 V) and the PTC (up to 0.25 Ohm cold) leave U2 about 5.3-5.5 V. The buck then drops out (TI fig 5-8 shows the knee near Vin 5.4-5.6 V) and +5V follows Vin to about 4.8-5.0 V. The 3.3 V LDO still regulates; TCAN needs 4.5 V. Only a crank below about 5 V at the battery takes +5V under spec.
evidence: SNVSAA5B fig 5-8 (page image p.8); BSMD1812-110 R1max 0.25 Ohm; SS34 Vf
suggested_fix: None needed; the choice of a low-drop PTC and the L1 29 mOhm part already helps. Verify on a bench with a 6 V crank profile.

title: Via-in-pad on the U2 exposed pad
claim: The two 0.3 mm EP vias are tented but sit inside the paste opening, so reflow solder can wick down them and leave voids. TI says vias under paste should be filled, plugged or tented. Thermal impact is negligible at about 0.4 W (Tj about 100 C at 85 C air).
evidence: pcbnew: via tented True on F and B; SNVSAA5B DDA0008B note 10
suggested_fix: Optionally ask JLC for resin-plugged vias or move the vias to the pad edge. Low priority.

title: Checked, correct: U2 pinout, D9 polarity, L2 and U2 footprints
claim: The pins map as 1 BOOT, 2 VIN, 3 EN (tied to VIN), 4 RT (R8 10 k to GND), 5 FB (68 k / 12 k, Vout = 5.000 V), 6 SS (10 nF), 7 and 9 GND, 8 SW. D9 pad 1 = SW (cathode). The L2 land pattern equals the Sunlord recommendation (2.35 x 3.5 mm pads, 6.05 mm centres). All values meet TI's requirements except the open capacitance point (F1).
evidence: pcbnew pad dump of cur_db and ord_db; design.py:227-241; SNVSAA5B p.3; Sunlord series sheet p.2; KiCad D_SMA convention (pad 1 cathode)
suggested_fix: None.

title: No cheaper drop-in for LMR14020; alternates rejected
claim: U2 costs $0.445 @100 (extended, 14.5k stock). AP63205WU-7 C2071056 is cheaper but 3.8-32 V and 85 C only, so it fails the clamp/jump-start input range. TPS5430DDAR C9864 (basic, $0.35-0.58) is 5.5-36 V with a different pinout and 500 kHz in the AM band. AP64200SP-13 C3192345 ($0.46 @100) is not cheaper. XL1509-5.0 (basic, 150 kHz) is noisy and needs a different pinout. Savings would be at most a one-off extended-part fee. Datasheets for these were NOT read (LCSC listing parameters only), so they are not recommended.
suggested_fix: Keep the LMR14020. Do not spend effort here; total buck BOM is about $0.95.

title: Ordered 0.5 A PTC and 500 mA ferrite L1 have no hot margin
claim: The ordered F1 holds 0.50 A at 25 C and probably about 0.23-0.25 A at 85 C (proxy: BHFUSE 050 row 0.50->0.23). L1 is a 500 mA, 0.3 ohm multilayer ferrite chip. Repo figures are 0.15 A steady and 0.45 A at 8 V cranking (about 0.6 A at 6 V). A hot, weak crank can exceed the hot hold current and trip the PTC (brown-out). This is already flagged in VERIFICATION 684; the numbers are new.
evidence: datasheets/txt/C70077 Table II (Ihold 0.5, Itrip 1.0, R1max 0.7); C883150 derating chart row 050; design.py L212-218; evidence/ord_db footprints (F1 1206, L1 1210)
suggested_fix: Hand-rework on ordered boards: 1206 PTC of about 1 A hold and a 1210 inductor of at least 1 A (the pads allow it), then hot-soak and weak-crank test.

title: Rev 0.10 F1 1.1 A PTC holds only 0.52 A at 85 C
claim: The rev 0.10 fix (1.1 A hold) derates to 0.52 A at 85 C ambient per the maker's table, against the repo's 0.45 A at 8 V cranking and about 0.6 A at 6 V (constant-power scaling). There is no margin for a hot-soaked case plus a weak crank, and the card adds up to 0.04 A at 12 V. Between hold and trip (about 1 A) the PTC may or may not trip.
evidence: datasheets/txt/C883150_BSMD1812-110-33V.txt Thermal Derating Chart (85 C: 0.52 A); VERIFICATION.md L684; design.py L212
suggested_fix: Bench hot-soak plus crank test. If it trips, use a higher-hold 33 V 1812 PTC (BSMD1812-160 is 0.63 A at 85 C, little gain) or drop F1 for a 0 ohm link, accepting that an internal short then waits for the car fuse.

title: TVS energy rated for suppressed load dump only
claim: ISO 16750-2 test A (unsuppressed 79-101 V, Ri 0.5-4 ohm, 400 ms) puts about 250-1200 J into the TVS and 13-68 A through it. D6 is rated 1500 W at 10/1000 us (about 2 J, Ipp 31 A) and D12 400 W. D6 fails short and blows the car fuse, or D12 fails short and latches F1 tripped (ECU dead). Survival depends on the Miata alternator clamping the dump (UNVERIFIED; the repo says unknown). Extra detail beyond the documented item.
evidence: datasheets/txt/C224048 (PPPM 1500 W, Vc 48.4 V @31 A, failure mode short); C223988; computed (Us-Vc)/Ri x Vc x 0.4 s
suggested_fix: State that the design assumes a suppressed (test B) dump. If an unsuppressed one must be survived, use an SM8S/SMDJ-class 33 V TVS (kW-class, with a 400 ms rating) for D6, or verify the alternator on a car.

title: D6/D12 breakdown bands overlap at 85 C
claim: The repo says D12 sits above D6 so that D6 takes the dump. At 85 C junction D6 maximum VBR is about 39.0 V and D12 minimum is about 38.9 V (alphaT 0.1 %/C x 60 K). In the worst tolerance corner D12 can conduct first or together with D6 above about 39 V, pushing the current through F1. It matters only for events above 38 V.
evidence: C224048 and C223988 tables and alphaT note (0.1 %); computed 36.8x1.06 vs 36.7x1.06
suggested_fix: Accept (events above 38 V are already outside the design), or use a 36 V-class D12 (SMAJ36A, VBR 40-44.2 V) so that it stays above D6 hot; check the buck's 44 V limit against that Vc.

title: Reverse-battery crowbar holds for low loop resistance only
refs: D6 forward path, car EGI/ECU fuse
claim: With 10-40 mOhm of harness and fuse loop, D6 (VF 3.5-5 V @100 A) carries 166-290 A for about 1 ms until the fuse opens, which is within IFSM 200 A / 8.3 ms (1-8 J). With a high-resistance reversed path (about 0.3 ohm, 37 A) a 15 A fuse takes seconds and D6 dissipates about 80 W for that time, so it would be lost, failing short (the safe direction for the car, the ECU is dead). The repo's 'blows within milliseconds' is therefore conditional. Fuse time-current curve not read.
evidence: C224048 IFSM 200 A, VF 3.5/5.0 V @100 A, 'typical failure mode is short'; VERIFICATION.md L1173; computed
suggested_fix: Word the claim as 'ECU may be destroyed, car safe'; keep the crowbar (a reverse MOSFET would remove the fuse-blowing path).

title: Pinout, polarity and footprints of the input chain checked correct
refs: D6 D7 D8 D12 F1 L1 R7 C16
claim: D6 K=VBAT_IN A=GND; D7 A=VBAT_IN K=+12V_IN; D8 A=VIGN_IN K=+12V_IN; D12 K=+12V A=GND; F1 +12V_IN to +12V; L1 +12V to +12V_F. The schematic symbols (K/A pin functions), PCB nets and datasheet cathode/anode agree. Pads match the DO-214AB/AC, SOD-123, 1812 and FXL0530 land patterns (L1 pads 1.9x2.5 at 4.1 mm vs a=2.2, b=6.0, c=2.5, a 0.3 mm shortfall, closing the repo's open item).
evidence: evidence/cur_db/pcb_nets.txt, pcb_pads.csv, sch_netlist.xml; C177247 land pattern table
suggested_fix: None.

title: ISO 7637-2 2a surge keeps buck VIN under 44 V; slew ring case only theoretical
claim: ngspice (D6 33.3-36.8 V, D12 36.7-40.6 V, F1 0.15 ohm, L1/C17 derated) gives buck VIN 35.2-38.9 V for 50 V / 2 ohm / 50 us, below the 44 V (LMR14020) and 45 V (TLS115) absolute maxima, so the repo's 36.4 V is consistent. A hypothetical 14->40 V step with a milliohm source and under 1 us edge rings the L1/C17 filter to about 52 V with or without the damper, but ISO pulses are source-limited and do not do this.
evidence: work/P06-power-input-protection/p2a.sh, lc0.cir, lc1.cir; C187824 line 187; C3743696 Table 1
suggested_fix: None; a bench scope capture of VIN during a pulse is the closing check.

title: Key-off: no permanent battery pin wired, ECU draws 0 at key-off
claim: VBAT_IN is the main-relay output on every year (1B on 89-95 / 99-00, 4B on 96-97, 4AF on 2001-05). VIGN_IN is the START signal (1B/1C, 89-95), IG1 sense 4S (2003-05), or unconnected (96-97, 99-00, 2001-02). No battery-permanent pin is connected, so nothing keeps logic powered or drains the battery. The cost is that there is no keep-alive supply (rusEFI needs none; Hellen had an optional 3I jumper). D8 'wake' has a function on 2003-05 only.
evidence: kb/interconnect.md rows for 1B/1C/4B/4AF/4S; motherboards/1989-95/README.md L58-59; pinouts_9605.md conflict 3
suggested_fix: None; optionally note it in INSTALL.

title: 1989-95: D8 can feed logic from the START wire while cranking
claim: 1C is the starter signal, a battery-level wire only while cranking. When VBAT_IN sags below it, D8 conducts and the whole 0.4-0.6 A logic load may be drawn through the START wire (gauge and fuse of that circuit not checked). Harmless ride-through if the wire is heavy, an unintended load on the starter-signal circuit if not.
evidence: nets D8.2 = VIGN_IN = J1 1C; motherboards/1989-95/README.md L59
suggested_fix: Leave D8 unfitted (or add 100 ohm in series) on 1989-95 builds since 1C is not an ignition-on wire; this needs a wiring check against the factory manual.

title: Swap D6 SMCJ30A to MDD C408374
refs: D6 (also D3/D4 on 1989-93 motherboards, same C224048)
claim: MDD SMCJ30A has the same key specs in its datasheet (VBR 33.3-36.8 V, Vc 48.4 V @31 A, 1500 W, IFSM 200 A, RthJL 15 / RthJA 75 C/W; datasheets/extra/C408374_SMCJ30A_MDD). Stock 7,064, extended, same DO-214AB. Price $0.1303@50, $0.1174@150 vs Littelfuse $0.237@50, $0.211@150, which saves about $0.11 per D6 (D3/D4 too). VF at 100 A not listed on the MDD sheet; brand quality untested.
evidence: tools/lcsc.py C408374 / C224048 today; datasheets/extra/C408374_SMCJ30A_MDD.txt L86-95, L141
suggested_fix: Use C408374 if the MDD VF curve (page 3) is acceptable, otherwise keep Littelfuse.

title: Swap D12 SMAJ33A to MDD C113966
claim: MDD SMAJ33A has the same VBR 36.70-40.60 V, Vc 53.3 V @7.5 A and 400 W; its IFSM is 40 A vs 60 A, irrelevant because D12 never conducts forward behind D7/F1. Stock 11,365, extended. Price $0.0331@200 and $0.0416@1 vs Littelfuse $0.1117@50, which saves about $0.07 each for D12 and D11. Combined with D6: about $0.18-0.25 per unit.
evidence: datasheets/extra/C113966_SMAJ33A_MDD.txt L72-77, L126; tools/lcsc.py C113966
suggested_fix: Change C223988 to C113966 on D11/D12 (check D11's forward duty first; it belongs to another review).

title: R7 + C16 damper has little effect (candidate removal)
claim: The L1/C17-C18 filter has Z0 about 0.43 ohm and Q about 2, so its peak output impedance is about 0.7-0.9 ohm against |Zin| about 10 ohm of the buck at 6 V cranking (Middlebrook margin >10x without a damper). In ngspice the damper changes the ISO 2a buck VIN peak by about 1-1.3 V (38.9 -> 37.6 V). Removal saves about $0.10-0.12 per unit (C16 $0.075-0.121 + R7 $0.003 + two placements). Hellen's module uses the same network (R420 1 ohm + C427 4.7 uF), so it is a proven pattern.
evidence: work/P06-power-input-protection/p2a.sh output; ext/hellen-one power_12and5V 0.3 schematic
suggested_fix: Keep for now; if a bench scope shows no ringing at hot-plug and key-on, delete C16/R7 on the next spin.

title: D12 cannot be removed; Hellen has no equivalent clamp on VIGN
claim: D6 sits on VBAT_IN only. The ignition path via D8 enters behind D6, so D12 is the only clamp for IG1 / START surges on the +12V node. Hellen's equivalent module clamps only V12_RAW (SMCJ30A before the PTC) and leaves its VIGN diode D417 unclamped. Removing D12 would expose the buck (44 V) to the IG wire. D12 and D11 share C223988, so it adds no unique extended part.
evidence: nets +12V_IN = D7.1 D8.1 F1.1; ext/hellen-one/modules/power_12and5V/0.3 schematic
suggested_fix: Keep D12.

title: Sensor readings scale with the +5V sag; ADC reference is the 3.3 V LDO
claim: V5_SENS/V5_EXT follow +5V (tracker +-5 mV) while the ADC reference stays 3.3 V (LDL1117 holds to about 3.7 V in), so MAP/TPS/AFM/CLT/IAT read low by 1-V5/5: -21.8 % at the repo's level II crank value of 3.91 V, -10 % at 4.5 V, -5 % at 4.75 V (MPX5700AP spec'd only 4.75-5.25 V).
evidence: design.py:244-247,177,253; VERIFICATION.md:580 (+5V 3.91 V); MPX5700AP datasheet Table 1 line 67/82, transfer fn line 163; LDL1117 dropout 350 mV
suggested_fix: Accept for the short crank dip, or add a divider from V5_EXT to a spare ADC pin so firmware can scale; no change needed for ordered boards.

title: No ADC channel measures any 5 V rail; static rail tolerance +-6.7 % worst
claim: No ADC input monitors +5V/V5_SENS/V5_EXT (inputs are KNOCK,TPS,MAP,CLT,IAT,AFR,AUX1-3,VBATT,VIGN), so firmware cannot correct. Gain error between independently toleranced rails: 5 V = 5.0 V +-3.7 % (LMR14020 VFB +-2 % + 1 % dividers), 3V3 +-3 % (LDL1117) = +-6.7 % worst, about +-4.1 % RSS, typical under 2 %; smaller than the MPX5700AP's own +-2.5 % span (+-17.5 kPa).
evidence: design.py:148-151; LMR14020 datasheet line 273; LDL1117 datasheet line 197-199; VERIFICATION.md:692
suggested_fix: Next revision: 10k/10k divider from V5_EXT to a spare ADC input and firmware rescale; or tighter parts (0.1 % feedback resistors).

title: Tracker output caps 1 uF X5R 0603 give no margin over the 1 uF minimum
claim: Datasheet COUT >= 1 uF applies at worst-case 30 % tolerance; 1 uF X5R +-10 %, DC bias at 5 V and cold/hot derating likely leave about 0.65-0.8 uF effective. ESR is no issue (stable region reaches 10 mOhm). Stability graph was drawn for 1 uF; U14 also drives harness capacitance. Hellen One uses the same 1 uF.
evidence: TLS115B0EJ datasheet Table 2 p.8 footnote 1, ESR graph p.15; BOM C15849 CL10A105KB8NNNC
suggested_fix: Use 2.2 uF (or 4.7 uF) 0603 X5R/X7R 16 V+ on V5_EXT and V5_SENS; ordered boards can be fine in practice, stack a second cap if oscillation is seen.

title: Harness 5 V short makes U14 dissipate about 5 W and thermally cycle
claim: Output shorted to GND at 14.4 V: limit about 350 mA x 14.4 V = 5 W (24 V: about 6.5 W), Tj hits 175 C shutdown and oscillates until the wire is cleared; datasheet says protection is not for continuous repetitive operation. U14 EP has only one via. ECU keeps running (IN is separate from the buck), MAP stays on U3.
evidence: TLS115B0EJ p.10 thermal shutdown text, p.13 current-limit graph, Table 3 RthJA 50-157 K/W; evidence/cur_db pcb vias around U14
suggested_fix: None needed for function; optionally add 3-4 more GND vias in the U14 EP.

title: Load-dump peak at tracker IN is near its 45 V abs max
claim: In an unsuppressed ISO 7637 pulse 5 the +12V node is clamped by D6 (SMCJ30A) then D12 (SMAJ33A, Vc 53.3 V at 7.5 A) behind F1; an estimate of about 45 V on IN/EN leaves no margin to the 45 V abs max.
evidence: SMAJ33A datasheet (parts_manifest C223988), design.py:202-214, TLS115 Table 1 p.7; estimate by series-resistance arithmetic, not simulated
suggested_fix: Belongs to power-input audit (P06); cheaper to verify there; margin gets better if D12 were a 30 V class TVS.

title: One tracker or none for U3 would save about $1.1/board
claim: U3 only feeds the on-board MAP (7-10 mA) and isolates it from harness faults. Feeding V5_SENS from +5V through the ferrite already used on the BOM (BLM18PG221, C80165) would save $1.09 + caps (about 0.3 % of price) and let MAP work on USB-only power; the extended line stays because U14 remains. Using one tracker for both (Hellen style) exposes the MPX5700AP to short-to-battery. Not worth reworking the ordered rev 0.9.
evidence: MPX5700AP datasheet supply current 7/10 mA; ext/hellen-one power_12and5V 0.3 BOM (single TLS115 U411); lcsc.py price
suggested_fix: Decide for next board revision; keep two if sensor-supply isolation matters more than $1.1.

title: TLS115B0EJ is sole-source and JLC stock is only 554
claim: EXTENDED part, stock 554 (JLC) / 554 (LCSC), $1.2617@1, $1.09@30, $0.913@100; two per board gives about 270 boards. Variants C3747428 (D0EJ, stock 45), C540241 (TSON, stock 6) are different parts whose datasheets were not read; TLE4250-2G (C976300, stock 15) is only 50 mA. No basic-part alternative.
evidence: tools/lcsc.py C3743696 and -s TLS115/TLE4250 on 2026-11-16
suggested_fix: Buy the stock for the first run now (or consign), plan a footprint for an alternate; if U3 is dropped the need falls to one per board.

title: USB-only bench power: tracker supplies are likely invalid
claim: On USB power +12V is back-fed to only about 4 V (repo-documented), which is the tracker 4 V minimum input; VOUT = min(ADJ, VIN-dropout) so V5_SENS/V5_EXT would be low or off and MAP/harness inputs misread on a bench.
evidence: TLS115B0EJ Table 2 VIN >= 4 V, Table 4 dropout; review brief section 6 back-feed note
suggested_fix: Document in bench instructions that sensors/MAP need +12V.

title: Pinout of U3 and U14 checked, correct (current and ordered boards)
claim: Pad 1 OUT=V5_SENS/V5_EXT, 3 and EP GND, 5 ADJ=+5V, 7 EN and 8 IN=+12V, 2/4/6 open, matches the PG-DSO-8 table; schematic symbol maps and PCB agree, rev 0.9 identical.
evidence: evidence/cur_db and ord_db pcb_pads.csv; design.py:244-247,490-493; datasheet p.6
suggested_fix: None.

title: Footprint and EP orientation match Infineon drawing
claim: 1.27 pitch, pads 1.65x0.6, EP 2.65 x 3.00 with 3.0 along the pin rows as the drawing requires; U3 has 2-4 EP vias, U14 only 1.
evidence: datasheet p.26; pcb_pads.csv; dump_pcb.py via list
suggested_fix: None; optional extra vias under U14.

title: Topology matches Hellen One (single TLS115 on same buck, 1 uF caps)
claim: Hellen One power_12and5V 0.3 uses one TLS115 off the same LMR14020 5 V (68k/12k) with 1 uF caps for all sensors; this design splits it in two. Normal loads (about 10 mA on U3, about 60 mA on U14) give 0.1 W and 0.6 W, well inside the package.
evidence: ext/hellen-one/modules/power_12and5V/0.3/power_12and5V-BOM.csv; global-replace.csv:91
suggested_fix: None.

title: Shunt clamp is required only because of D40/D41; input clamps alone do not need it
claim: Worst-case injection into +3V3 through all ordinary input clamps is 19.5 mA (all 17 inputs at 14.4 V) and 40.7 mA (24 V), at most 4.3 mA for a single input, below or comparable to the F103's 20-35 mA always-on load. The wideband pump/Vm clamps D40/D41 inject 0.22-0.43 A (pump 14.4-24 V) and 0.7-1.7 A (Vm until F2 trips). That exceeds any load, so the shunt is needed as drawn. Removing the clamp group (about $0.43/unit at qty 100 plus 2 extended-part fees) is only valid together with removing D40/D41, which exposes U101 and the MCU to a harness short.
evidence: pcb_pads.csv R108 47R, R109 10R, R110 62R, R61 4.7k, R27 5.6k/R28 10k, etc.; arithmetic in work/P08-3v3-rail-and-clamp/inj.py; notes section 4; mck1117 reference has no such clamps
suggested_fix: Keep the clamp. For a cost cut, drop it together with D40/D41 only if the owner accepts mck1117's unprotected pump/Vm behaviour. Do not remove it alone.

title: LDL1117 runs at or above its 125 C operating Tj at 85 C air; tab copper is minimal
claim: (5.0-3.3 V) x 0.2 A = 0.34 W and with theta-JA 120 K/W gives Tj about 126 C at 85 C air. At the repo's peak 0.3 A (SD writes) it is about 146 C, and 0.35 A is about 157 C, above the 150 C abs max. The tab has only one 0.3 mm via and a short trace as copper, so a real theta-JA at or above ST's 120 is likely.
evidence: LDL1117 Table 2/3 (Tj op 125, max 150, thetaJA 120); P05 3d load budget 0.2/0.3-0.35 A; vias.py: single +3V3 via at (134.5,93.25); layer crops u4_F_Cu.png
suggested_fix: Add a +3V3 copper area plus 4-6 vias under and around the U4 tab (free on the current rev); check the real 3.3 V current on the bench at 85 C.

title: Clamp worst-case threshold 3.68 V could push the peak above the 4.0 V MCU abs max
claim: Vth = (Vref+Iref*3.58k)/f spans 3.46 V (min) to 3.68 V (max) with TL431AI Vref 2.436-2.554 V incl. temperature and 1 % resistors. The repo's 3.93 V peak was simulated at nominal 3.56 V; adding the same overshoot at 3.68 V gives about 4.05 V, above the F407/F103 abs max of 4.0 V, for an ideal 1 A step. The realistic worst step is about 0.43 A, so the real overshoot is smaller.
evidence: C23892 TL431AI table (Vref 2470/2495/2520, deviation 34 mV, Iref 4 uA max); VERIFICATION.md:574 (3.93 V peak, 70 mV margin); notes 3c
suggested_fix: Lower the threshold slightly (e.g. R142 4.7k gives about 3.4 V min, which collides with the LDO's 3.40 V max, so instead keep it and re-run the sim at the max-threshold corner), or accept as theoretical.

title: Repo quotes LDO max 3.37 V; datasheet limit over temperature is 3.399 V (+-3 %)
claim: The comment 'LDO's 3.37 V maximum' uses the +-2 % at 25 C figure. ST Table 4 gives +-3 % over -40..125 C (3.201-3.399 V) plus 15 mV load regulation. The margin to the lowest clamp threshold (3.46 V) is therefore about 45 mV, not 190 mV. It still works, but it is thin and should be documented.
evidence: C435835 Table 4 (VOUT accuracy -3/+3 % for -40<Tj<125 C); design.py comment lines 528-531
suggested_fix: Fix the comment and VERIFICATION text; no hardware change needed.

title: 200 uF of ceramics on the LDL1117 output is outside ST's stability data
claim: ST's stability plot (Fig 20/21) covers COUT 1-22 uF and ESR 0.01-10 ohm. The rail carries roughly 230 uF nominal of ceramics with a few mohm ESR, which is not characterised. Likely benign because a large C lowers the output pole, but there is no datasheet guarantee and TL431 SOT-23 stability with its loop was not re-simulated.
evidence: C435835 p.10 section 6.2 and p.14 Figs 20/21 image
suggested_fix: Bench check the rail at power-up and under load steps (scope on +3V3 with the clamp populated); optionally add 0.5-1 ohm ESR in series with C63/C68 if ringing appears.

title: C63/C68 100 uF 6.3 V X5R at 3.3 V bias provide far less than 200 uF
claim: A 6.3 V X5R 1206 100 uF part at 52 % of rated voltage typically retains only about 40-60 % of nominal capacitance, so the real bulk is about 80-120 uF, weakening the repo's claim that 2 x 100 uF slows the fault step enough. The LCSC Samsung sheet has no DC-bias curve.
evidence: C15008 datasheet text has no bias curve (grep); derating figure is from memory
suggested_fix: Read Samsung's SimSurfing DC-bias data for CL31A107MQHNNNE and redo the step sim with effective C.

title: U4 pinout and footprint checked, correct
claim: LDL1117S33R SOT-223: pad 1 GND, pad 2 and tab +3V3 (VOUT), pad 3 +5V (VIN); matches ST Table 1 (1 GND, 2 VOUT, 3 VIN, tab VOUT). Land pattern is standard 2.0x1.5 pads, 2.3 mm pitch, tab 2.0x3.8, 6.3 mm span. Same on ord_db.
evidence: pcb_pads.csv U4 rows; design.py:253; C435835 p.6 Table 1
suggested_fix: None.

title: U15 TL431 DBZ pinout checked, correct
claim: TI DBZ SOT-23-3 has pin 1 CATHODE, 2 REF, 3 ANODE (the TL432 swaps 1 and 2). Board: 1 SH_K (to R141 and Q20 base), 2 SH_REF (divider mid), 3 GND. Correct, same on ord_db.
evidence: C23892 p.2 package drawing (DBZ top view); pcb_pads.csv U15 rows
suggested_fix: None.

title: Q20 BCP53 SOT-223 pinout and PNP orientation checked, correct
claim: BCP53: 1 base, 2 collector, 3 emitter, 4 collector. Board: base SH_K, collector (2 and tab) GND, emitter +3V3, so Q20 sinks current from the rail to ground as intended. Veb stays at or below 1 V (VEBO 5 V), and the tab is joined to the GND pour (good thermal path).
evidence: C85085 Table 3 pinning; pcb_pads.csv Q20 rows; q20_top.png
suggested_fix: None.

title: External clamp: needed at >=12 mH and on paired 1989-93, optional at <=8 mH; inductance unmeasured
claim: At 14.4 V, 14 ohm, 1.02 A: the driver's own 45 V clamp absorbs 3.1/6.1/10.7/15.3 mJ per turn-off at 4/8/14/20 mH, which is 0.18/0.37/0.64/0.92 W per driver at 7200 rpm sequential (+9/+18/+31/+44 C at the repo's 48 C/W). With the clamp the driver takes about 0 W and the TVS takes 0.13-0.63 W. At <=8 mH the driver is well inside ST's repetitive curve, so the 8 parts are optional there. At 20 mH, 85 C air and sustained 7200 rpm, Tj without the clamp exceeds the 125 C start condition and approaches shutdown. 8 parts cost about $0.56 plus about $0.1 assembly at qty 150, plus 2 extended-part fees.
evidence: Computed in this review with Vbat 14.4 V, R 14 ohm. ST Fig. 32 (DPAK, datasheet p.18) digitised: curve C (repetitive, 125 C start) 3.0/2.3/1.77 A at 4/8/20 mH. LCSC prices live 2026-11-16. No measured Miata injector inductance found on the web; the repo cites one 14.8 ohm port injector fit of 20.3 mH.
suggested_fix: Measure one Miata injector with an LCR meter before the next order. If it reads <=8-10 mH, make D42-D49 DNP or drop them for sequential years. Keep them for 1989-93 paired wiring and >=12 mH.

title: 1989-93 paired injectors: single driver has near-zero margin without the external clamp
claim: Two injectors in parallel on one wire draw about 2.04 A at 14.4 V. At L=20 mH each (10 mH combined), ST's repetitive 125 C curve allows 2.2 A, so there is essentially no margin if the driver's own clamp took the energy (30.7 mJ per event, 1.84 W at 7200 rpm batch). The external clamp is what makes this case viable. Keep D42/D43/D46/D47 on 1989-93, and do not make them DNP on that year.
evidence: ST datasheet Fig. 32 p.18 digitised: 2.20 A at 10 mH (curve C). Computed 2.04 A, 30.7 mJ.
suggested_fix: If any clamp-DNP option is offered, exclude 1989-93 paired wiring. Document in INSTALL that injector L must be measured for that year.

title: External clamp gives no protection at 24 V jump start or load dump (driver 40-55 V clamp wins)
claim: Clamp voltage is VBAT_IN+VBR+Vf, about 31-35 V at 14.4-16 V. At 24 V it reaches 40-43.7 V (VBR 15.2-16.8, up to about 18.9 V hot), above the driver's 40 V minimum clamp. At 35-37 V in a suppressed load dump (D6 SMCJ30A VBR 33-37 V) it would be 53 V, so the driver's 45 V clamp conducts instead. In a dump at 20 mH the driver sees about 315 mJ per turn-off against Eas 200 mJ (25 C), or about 126 mJ at 8 mH, with up to about 25 events in 400 ms. This is no worse than having no clamp, but the clamp network's benefit stops at roughly Vbat 22 V. The repo's claim of protection should be read as normal-running only.
evidence: ST Table 4 (Vclamp 40/45/55, VCLTH 36 V); Eas 200 mJ at L 24 mH, 24 V, 25 C start. D6 = SMCJ30A (pcb_footprints). Arithmetic in notes section 3c.
suggested_fix: Accept (it is the same as any ECU with a 45 V driver clamp), or pair the clamp with a higher-clamp driver such as NCV8406A (60-70 V) so the TVS wins up to about 42 V. State in VERIFICATION that the clamp only covers Vbat below about 22 V.

title: Vbat-referenced clamp lengthens injector closing and makes it supply-dependent
claim: The coil sees about 17.7 V (VBR+Vf) at turn-off, constant, instead of 45-Vbat (about 30.6 V at 14.4 V). Decay time at 20 mH, 1 A is 1.15 ms against 0.67 ms. The difference between 9 V and 14.4 V supply grows from 0.32 ms to 0.43 ms. This is mostly an offset, but the dead-time vs voltage table must be tuned at several voltages, and it hits low-pulsewidth linearity near the 1 ms idle pulse more than the repo's '0.16 ms later' suggests.
evidence: t = L*I/dV; computed table in notes section 4; README lines 15-16.
suggested_fix: Document that dead time must be measured at 9/12/14.4 V. If the clamp is kept, consider the lower-VBR TVS (SMBJ13A VBR 14.4-15.9) for a faster closing time, with the 36 V-threshold margin recomputed.

title: Cheaper TVS: SMBJ14A instead of 1.5SMC16A (about $0.5 per board)
claim: SMBJ14A (VBR 15.6-17.2 V, 600 W 10/1000 us) costs $0.03-0.066 (C152106 stock 12786, C908795 stock 3900) against $0.179 at qty 150 for C1973780 (stock 1699). The pulse energy (10 mJ, about 1.3 A) is tiny. The limit is the 0.5-0.6 W average power in a smaller SMB pad, so more copper per part is needed, and a footprint change. Do NOT use SMBJ16A: its VBR 17.8-19.7 V puts the drain at about 36 V and into the driver's clamp threshold.
evidence: tools/lcsc.py -s SMBJ14A / SMBJ16A today. Specs from JLC listing text only; manufacturer datasheet not read.
suggested_fix: Read a manufacturer SMBJ14A datasheet (Vishay/Littelfuse) and verify its thermal data, then trial the SMB footprint with the same drain copper.

title: Cheaper drivers for the four low-current channels: NCV8406A in SOT-223 (about $5.5 per board)
claim: IACV, VVT, BOOST and ALT carry about 1 A, and the first three have freewheel diodes. NCV8406ASTT3G (C459816, $0.45 at 100, stock 4875, extended) is pin-compatible in function (1 gate, 2 drain/tab, 3 source) and has a 60-70 V clamp, Ilim 5-9.5 A, Rds 210 mohm at 25 C and 445-520 mohm at 150 C, EAS 110 mJ, RthJA 100 C/W on minimum pad. This saves about $1.37 per channel against $1.82 for the VND7NV04. Conduction heat rises from about 0.12 W to about 0.5 W at 1 A hot. This needs a SOT-223 footprint, a copper recheck and the idle/VVT current confirmed. It is not suitable for the paired 1989-93 injectors (2 A). It was the rev 0.9 part.
evidence: datasheets/extra/NCV8406A_lcsc.txt (max ratings, electrical table); lcsc.py live prices.
suggested_fix: Only if cost pressure justifies a layout respin: fit SOT-223 NCV8406A on Q5-Q8 and keep DPAK VND7NV04 on the injectors. Confirm the real valve currents first.

title: Datasheet-required 150 ohm input resistor present on rev 0.10, absent on ordered rev 0.9
claim: RIN MIN 150 ohm (ST Table 2) is satisfied by the 220 ohm 0402 resistors on cur_db. ord_db rev 0.9 lacks them, which the repo already documents. With U11 5 V drive, IISS is 0.15 mA, giving 33 mV across 220 ohm, and td(off) stays fast (0.5 us). The 10 k pull-downs R19-R26 are needed to hold the gates low while U11 outputs are high-Z.
evidence: pcb_nets: INJx_DRV = R15x.1+U11, INJx_IN = Q.1+R15x.2+R19-26.1; ST p.7 and p.8.
suggested_fix: None. For ord_db consider bridging a 150-220 ohm resistor in series with each gate by hand only if reworking is feasible.

title: Checked, correct: VND7NV04 DPAK pin mapping on all 8 drivers
claim: Pad 1 = INPUT, pad 2 plus tab and 4 sub-pads = DRAIN (OUT_*, to J1 pins 19/22/25/28/31/34/37/40), pad 3 = SOURCE = GND. This matches ST's DPAK diagram (1 input, tab/2 drain, 3 source). The LCSC class label 'High Side Switch' is a catalogue mislabel; the part is a low-side OMNIFET II.
evidence: evidence/cur_db/pcb_pads.csv Q1/Q5 rows; pcb_nets.txt; ST datasheet p.1 image (work/P09.../vnd7_p1_pins_b.png) and Fig.1 p.6.
suggested_fix: None.

title: Checked, correct: clamp chain and freewheel diode polarity
claim: Drain -> ES1D (anode on OUT_INJ, pad 2; cathode on INJx_CL, pad 1) -> 1.5SMC16A (cathode on INJx_CL, anode on VBAT_IN) is the right way round: the TVS is reverse-biased in series with a forward diode and returns to the battery. Without ES1D the TVS would conduct forward from VBAT to the grounded drain. D1/D2 SS34 have cathode (pad 1, sch pin K) on the valve's +12 V feed and anode (pad 2, pin A) on OUT_IACV/OUT_VVT on all four motherboards.
evidence: cur_db pcb_nets INJ1_CL = D42.1+D46.1; OUT_INJ1 = D42.2; VBAT_IN includes D46.2; mb pcb_nets D1.1/D2.1 on VBAT_IN/IAC_12V/OCV_12V, D1.2/D2.2 on OUT_*; sch_netlist D1 pin 2 = A.
suggested_fix: None.

title: Checked, correct: drain copper and via counts match the README
claim: Filled-zone areas from the PCB: OUT_INJ1 F.Cu 94 mm2, In2/In3/B.Cu 107 mm2 each, 41 vias; OUT_INJ4 100/108 mm2, 45 vias; IACV, VVT and ALT are similar. The README's 84-100/95-108 mm2 and 34-42 vias are confirmed (vias are slightly more). The 48 C/W figure remains a model, not a measurement.
evidence: work/P09.../cu.py with pcbnew on repo/daughterboard/miata_ecu_daughter.kicad_pcb.
suggested_fix: None. Bench-measure a driver's Tj at 7200 rpm equivalent.

title: ZXMS6004FF pinout and all 11 instances checked, correct
claim: Diodes pin drawing: single lead D on one side, IN and S on the other; with TO-236 numbering, pin1 = IN, pin2 = S, pin3 = D. Every Q has pad1 = gate/SNK net, pad2 = GND, pad3 = OUT_* harness net, on both boards. The schematic netlist pinfunction IN/S/D agrees.
evidence: datasheets/C95063 p.1 pin-out image, p.8; evidence/{cur_db,ord_db}/pcb_pads.csv; sch_netlist.xml Q9; design.py:268-322
suggested_fix: None. Only assumption is that the Diodes sheet draws no pin numbers, so the JEDEC convention is used.

title: Ignition edge delays from Q16-19: dwell start 45-60 us late, spark edge about 1-5 us
claim: At 7000 rpm (0.042 deg/us), the spark (falling) edge is defined by R144-147 3.3k and line capacitance, about 1-5 us = 0.04-0.2 deg; the 5 us td(on) is not on the critical path. The dwell-start (rising) edge waits for td(off) 45 us typ plus part of 15 us fall = 1.9-2.5 deg, which shortens dwell about 1.5-2 %. The datasheet gives typical values only (no min/max or temperature data), so the spread is unquantifiable; at an assumed +-50 % it is about +-1 deg on the rising edge. This matters only if an igniter fires on the rising edge.
evidence: datasheet p.5 dynamic table; design.py:298-325 comment says 5-15 us
suggested_fix: Confirm each igniter fires on the falling IGt edge; if not, drop Q16-19 or add rusEFI ignition-offset calibration by scope. Keep R144-147 as they set the spark edge.

title: Shorted-to-battery ignition wire leaves Q16-19 in continuous thermal cycling
claim: Q16-19 are ON whenever the ignition output is idle (CTL low -> 74HCT04 high). A harness short to +12 V forces limit 1-2.2 A at 14 V (14-30 W) and then thermal shutdown, auto-restart with 10 C hysteresis, indefinitely while the engine runs. Datasheet note 9 says the part is not designed to withstand overtemperature for extended periods. The 24 V case is within VDS(SC) 36 V. A fault is plausible but rare, and the cycling heats neighbouring parts.
evidence: datasheet p.3 and p.5 note 9, TJT 150/175 C; design.py:298-300
suggested_fix: Accept and document; no readback exists. Optionally add a firmware or bench note that a persistently shorted ignition wire should be repaired promptly.

title: CEL lamp driven at 3.3 V: thin VIH margin and 0.7 A minimum current limit vs lamp inrush
claim: The pin voltage is about 3.1-3.2 V (3.3 V minus 1k x 60-100 uA) against VIH min 3.0 V (RDS(on) is still 0.6 ohm max at 3 V). ID(LIM) at 3 V is 0.7 min / 1.7 typ A versus 1-3 A cold-filament inrush of a 1.4-3.4 W lamp (UNVERIFIED lamp wattage), so the lamp may light after a few ms of limiting or thermal cycling. The datasheet advertises lamp loads. Ordered rev 0.9 uses 5 V through U12 and has no such margin issue (but the lamp cannot light while the drivers are disabled).
evidence: datasheet p.3 VIH, p.5 IIN/ID(LIM); design.py:288-296
suggested_fix: Reduce R160 to 100-330 ohm (still above the 2 mA input clamp limit) and bench-test the lamp turn-on.

title: No cheaper drop-in for the ZXMS6004FF; keep all 11
claim: The 11 parts cost $4.82 per board at qty 30 ($4.23 at 100). Basic-library alternatives (C8545 2N7002 60 V; C20917 AO3400A 30 V) have no current limit, thermal shutdown or specified clamp, and the 30 V part is below the 36 V environment. Switching saves at most about $4.3 per board and removes the short-to-battery protection the repo added to fix the ULN2003. DMN6075S-7 (C155242) and NCV8402 (C77755) are extended and not cheaper. Only listing data were read for the alternates, so none is recommended.
evidence: tools/lcsc.py C95063 and searches today; datasheet p.1
suggested_fix: None; keep ZXMS6004FF. Do not spend effort on this part for cost.

title: Relay-coil clamp energy and 85 C thermal pass with margin
claim: Relay and solenoid loads of 0.1-0.4 A give a dissipation of at most about 0.12 W (Tj 102-121 C at 85 C ambient, below 150 C, even with the thin drain copper). Coil kick energy is about 1-9 mJ (L 0.05-0.3 H assumed, UNVERIFIED) against EAS 90 mJ (roughly 36 mJ derated at Tj 100 C). No motherboard has flyback diodes and none are needed.
evidence: datasheet p.3 EAS, p.5 RDS(on); VERIFICATION.md:569; mb pcb_nets OUT_*
suggested_fix: None. Optionally measure one relay coil's resistance and inductance.

title: Footprint vs Diodes land pattern: acceptable difference
claim: The KiCad SOT-23 footprint (0.6 x 1.475 pads, 1.9 pitch, outer span 3.35 mm) vs Diodes 0.8 x 1.11, outer span 3.0 mm. The lead span 2.3-2.5 mm lands on the pads. The drain has only a thin trace for heat, the source sits on the GND pour. Not an error.
evidence: datasheet p.8; pcb_pads.csv Q9-Q19
suggested_fix: None.

title: U11/U12 4245A pinout, DIR/OE, unused channels and power-up checked correct
claim: Port A is 5 V (VCCA pin 1) and port B is 3.3 V (pins 23 and 24). DIR on pin 2 is GND, which gives B to A. OE on pin 22 is DRV_EN_N from PA8 (U1.67), pulled up to +5V by R71. A8/B8 to A1/B1 pairing is correct. Unused A3, A6 and B1, B5 are open or GND as the datasheet requires. This matches TI's power-up guidance. Firmware drives PA8 open-drain.
evidence: pcb_pads.csv; SCAS375H pin diagram p.1 and Power-Up Considerations p.5; board_configuration.cpp:41,110
suggested_fix: None.

title: U13 74HCT04, U6/U7 TC4427 pinout and thresholds checked correct
claim: HCT04 order 1A,1Y..GND,4Y,4A,5Y,5A,6Y,6A,VCC matches the pads. 5A and 6A are on GND and 5Y and 6Y are open. HCT VIH is 2.0 V and TC4427 VIH is 2.4 V min, so 3.3 V MCU logic works with both. TC4427 pins 1 and 8 are NC and VDD is +5V (rated 4.5-18 V).
evidence: Nexperia 74HC_HCT04 table 6 (HCT block); TC4427A pin table and electrical characteristics; pcb_pads.csv
suggested_fix: None. The TC4427 VIH margin is about 0.5 V against the F407 VOH.

title: Ignition outputs are low through reset/boot and survive a short to battery
claim: In reset the CTL lines are pulled low by RN1. The TC4427 output is therefore low, the HCT04 output is high, the ZXMS is on, and R144-147 also pull low. No coil-charge glitch path was found. The Schottky blocks a battery short (40 V rating against 14.4 V or 24 V). R144-147 dissipate 63 mW at 14.4 V and 175 mW at 24 V. TC4427/ZXMS overlap at each rising edge is only about 43 mA for about 50 us (ZXMS tD(OFF) 45 us + tF 15 us).
evidence: design.py:297-333; C95063 dynamic table (tD(ON) 5, tR 10, tD(OFF) 45, tF 15 us); pcb_nets IGN*_CTL
suggested_fix: None.

title: Igniter input level and threshold unknown; 100 ohm + Schottky drop may eat margin
claim: The high level at the igniter is 5 V minus about 0.3-0.4 V (Schottky) minus I*100 ohm, with R144 3.3k (about 1.4 mA) also loading it. No source for the stock NA igniter or NB coil input current and threshold was found. If an igniter input needs more than a few mA, or about 3.5 V or more, the stage may not fire it. Hellen drives these inputs directly (4245A plus 10 ohm).
evidence: ext/hellen-one/modules/ign8/0.2/ign8-BOM.csv; web search found no numbers; design.py:297-335
suggested_fix: Before first run, measure the high level on the real stock coil pack and igniter with a scope (loaded). If the level is short, reduce R15-18 to 47 ohm. Check the 1206 dissipation first (see the R15-18 finding below).

title: R15-R18 1206 dissipate about 0.185 W in an output short to ground
claim: With the TC4427 high and the output shorted to ground, I is about 43 mA through 100 ohm plus the diode. That is about 185 mW against a 250 mW rating that is valid only to 70 C. At 85 C air the derated limit is about 0.2 W, so margin is about 10 %. This only matters in a fault and an open resistor only loses the output. The repo records 72 % of rating without derating.
evidence: design.py:306-312; VERIFICATION.md:570; C17901 250 mW at 70 C (derating curve not read)
suggested_fix: Accept, or use 150 ohm / 0.5 W 1206, or note it as a fault-only item.

title: Option: replace the push-pull stage with an open-drain ZXMS plus pull-up
claim: Drive each ZXMS gate directly from the MCU with a 10k pull-UP to +5V. Reset gives Q on, so the line is low and safe. Pull the line up through 1k plus the existing Schottky. Firmware inverts ignition polarity. This removes 2 TC4427, 1 HCT04, 8 1206 resistors and 3 capacitors, saving about $1.1-1.3 per board at qty 100 plus 2 extended parts. Short-to-battery survival is kept (Schottky and ZXMS clamp), and the spark edge becomes a hard pull-down. The drawbacks are a slower, weaker high edge that depends on the igniter's input resistance.
evidence: qty-100 prices C20551 $0.476, C131317 about $0.15, C26032/C17901 about $0.003; ZXMS datasheet 3 V gate drive OK (RDS 600 mohm); design.py:297-335
suggested_fix: Only adopt after measuring igniter input data. Also check STM32 FT-pin behaviour with a 5 V pull-up when VDD=0 (not read). The ordered rev 0.9 boards cannot change.

title: Option: drop Q16-Q19 and U13 only
claim: This saves about $1.7 per board. The low state would then be held only by the 3.3k pull-down, so noise immunity against ground offset is lost. The spark edge also falls at an RC rate instead of being forced. Short-to-battery survival is kept because the Schottky still blocks. Not recommended before measuring igniter input behaviour.
suggested_fix: Prefer the open-drain option above, or keep as is.

title: IGN3/IGN4 not parked by firmware if rusEFI releases them to pull-up
claim: Firmware parks only the 15 low-side control pins. Per its own comment, a pin rusEFI releases goes to input+pull-up. For IGN3/4, 3.3 V through 30-50k against RN1 10k gives about 0.55-0.83 V, which stays under the typical TC4427 and HCT04 thresholds (guaranteed VIL is 0.8 V). No malfunction expected, but margin is thin at the datasheet minimums.
evidence: board_configuration.cpp:38-60; TC4427 VIL 0.8 V max; arithmetic
suggested_fix: Optionally add the 4 ignition pins to lowSideControlPins parking.

title: Rev 0.9 ordered: CEL lamp behind the shared driver enable
claim: On ordered rev 0.9, CEL_G is U12 pin 6 and CEL_CTL is U12 pin 18, so the lamp is off whenever the drivers are disabled (including after a fatal error). The repo documents this and rev 0.10 fixes it. The ignition stage on ord_db is identical to cur_db (empty pad-for-pad diff).
evidence: ord_db pcb_pads.csv; design.py:292-296
suggested_fix: None, just awareness.

title: 74HCT245 as 4245A substitute saves little and was not read
claim: C7859 is JLC extended (preferred) with stock 36862 and $0.393 at 30 or $0.344 at 100. A 74HCT245 TSSOP-20 (C52140501, C53436288) is about $0.09-0.10 at 1k. That saves roughly $0.13-0.2 per chip but needs new pinout and layout. I did not read their datasheets.
evidence: tools/lcsc.py searches
suggested_fix: Do not change.

title: ADC reference (3V3 +-3%) and 5 V sensor supply are independent: MAP and thermistor readings not ratiometric
refs: U4 LDL1117S33R, VDDA/FB1, U3/U14, MPX5700AP, CLT/IAT R33/R36
claim: The F407 ADC reference is VDDA from the +3V3 LDO (+-2 % at 25 C, +-3 % over temperature) while MAP/TPS/CLT/IAT are fed from the +5V buck (about 4.88-5.12 V, per P05). rusEFI assumes exactly 3.3 V and 5 V and has no VREFINT or rail compensation here. Worst-corner MAP error is about +-7 kPa at 100 kPa and +-13 kPa at 200 kPa; CLT/IAT about +-2 K at 25-80 C and +-7 K at -20 C. Typical error is about half.
evidence: datasheets/txt/C435835_LDL1117S33R.txt VOUT accuracy +-2 %/+-3 %; kb/parts/P05 Vout 4.88-5.12; miata_board.cpp:30,64-72 (adcVcc 3.3, MPX Vout=5 V x ...); adc_inputs.cpp:57 (only a +-10 % diagnostic); computed r = (V5/5)/(V3/3.3) = 1.056 worst
suggested_fix: Tune baro/offset at key-on and accept, or pull CLT/IAT up to +3V3 so they are ratiometric to VDDA. For MAP, calibrate the gain on the bench or add a firmware VREFINT/5V correction.

title: BAT54WS-7-F (Diodes) costs 8-9x same-footprint clones
claim: 11 BAT54WS-7-F cost $0.094 each at qty 50 ($0.084 at 150). Clones with identical VF/IR/CT limits: C7502694 hongjiacheng (EXTENDED+PREFERRED, $0.0107@500, stock 46.9k) and C3040452 Fuxinsemi (EXTENDED, $0.0103@500, stock 73k). Saving is about $0.8-0.9 per board. Caveat: the HJC datasheet curve shows about 3x higher 100 C leakage (about 20-30 uA vs about 6-9 uA), so hot-cabin offset error rises from about 32 mV to about 100 mV at 105 C on the 3.6 k nodes.
evidence: lcsc.py today; datasheets/extra/BAT54WS_hongjiacheng_C7502694.pdf p.2 (VF 240/320/400/500/1000 mV, IR 2 uA@25 V, CT 10 pF, cathode line), BAT54WS_fuxinsemi_C3040452.pdf; Diodes DS30098 Fig.2
suggested_fix: Use the Diodes part for the VBATT/VIGN clamps if hot accuracy matters; the clones are acceptable for the sensor clamps. Confirm Fuxinsemi pin polarity from its page images before using it.

title: Clamp leakage offset at 85/105 C
claim: BAT54WS reverse leakage (Fig.2: 0.045 uA at 25 C, about 1.7 uA at 75 C, 25 uA at 125 C at 1.3 V) interpolates to about 3 uA at 85 C and about 9 uA at 105 C. Into the 3.6 k source this is 11 mV (14 LSB) at 85 C and 32 mV at 105 C on the sensor channels, and about 17 mV on the battery node (about 0.1 V battery reading at 85 C). Acceptable; mentioned for completeness.
evidence: datasheets/txt/C124205_BAT54WS-7-F.txt, Fig.2 image work/P12-analog-inputs/bat54ws_fig2.png; log interpolation
suggested_fix: None needed; keep the Diodes part or a similar Schottky with Fig.2-class leakage.

title: Knock stage has no real anti-alias filter for 218 kSPS sampling
claim: ADC rate is about 218.75 ksps (84+12 cycles at 21 MHz) so Nyquist is 109 kHz. Only a 48 kHz single pole (R50/C46) plus the 175 kHz closed-loop amplifier BW precede the ADC, so ignition and injector noise at 100-200+ kHz aliases into the 5-15 kHz knock band. Hellen's knock module uses a multi-pole filter around the same LMV321.
evidence: knock_config.h:13-14; design.py:389-400; ext/hellen-one/modules/knock/0.1 BOM and schematic; LMV321 GBW 1 MHz (TI p.5)
suggested_fix: Lower the R50/C46 corner (for example 330 R + 47 nF, about 10 kHz) or add a feedback cap across R48, then confirm gain at 6-7 kHz; validate on a running engine.

title: Knock frequency for BP engines and gain checked
claim: Gain 5.7, bias 1.65 V (tracks 3V3), HPF 16 Hz, closed-loop BW about 175 kHz, flat at the knock frequency. First circumferential mode is about 6.1 kHz (83 mm bore, 1.8) to 6.5 kHz (78 mm, 1.6) via Draper's formula, so the amplifier is flat there. Worst-case offset (Ib 250 nA, Vos 7 mV) is about 170 mV at the output, giving a clip level of about 245 mV input versus the documented 284 mV.
evidence: TI SLOS263W p.5 (IIB, VIO, GBW); f = 1.841 c/(pi B) with c about 860 m/s
suggested_fix: None. Verify piezo capacitance and the real knock frequency on the car.

title: Checked, correct: LMV321 U8 SOT-23-5 pinout and footprint
claim: Pad 1 KN_P = IN+, 2 GND, 3 KN_N = IN-, 4 KN_OUT = OUT, 5 +3V3 = VCC+. Feedback taken at pad 4 before R50; C47 100n is 3.3 mm from pad 5. Pad geometry is standard 0.95 pitch SOT-23-5 and identical on rev 0.9 and rev 0.10.
evidence: evidence/cur_db/pcb_pads.csv U8 rows; sch_netlist.xml; design.py:399; TI SLOS263W p.3 pin diagram DBV
suggested_fix: None.

title: Checked, correct: BAT54WS clamp polarity and MCU ADC pin map
claim: All eleven clamps have pad 1 (cathode K) on +3V3 and pad 2 (anode A) on the AN node, so they clamp upward to +3V3 only. U1 pins 24/25/26/29-36 (PA1, PA2, PA3, PA4-PA7, PC4, PC5, PB0, PB1) match the firmware ADC channel defines, and VDDA/VREF+ are on +3V3A via FB1.
evidence: sch_netlist.xml D19 pinfunction K/A; pcb_nets.txt AN_* rows; miata_pins.h:58-67; Diodes DS30098 'Cathode Band'
suggested_fix: None.

title: Checked, correct: thermistor pull-up model in firmware
claim: 2.7k from V5_EXT loaded by 5.6k+10k (15.6k) is a Thevenin 4.262 V behind 2.302 k. The firmware sets bias_resistor = 2.302 k and the thermistor supply to 4.262 V, and rusEFI uses both in ResistanceFunc (R = Rb/(Vs/V-1)). At the extremes: CLT 120 C gives 0.114 V at the ADC (141 codes, about 0.33 K/LSB), and -20 C gives 2.42 V.
evidence: miata_pins.h:72-77; init_thermistors.cpp:51-52; resistance_func.cpp:33; test_miata_ecu.cpp:603
suggested_fix: None.

title: 5 V sensor output scaling and 5.2 V behaviour
claim: Ratio is 0.641, so 5.0 V reads 3.205 V (97 % FS, 118 codes headroom) and the ADC saturates above 5.148 V. 5.2 V gives 3.333 V: ADC reads 4095, no damage (clamp forward 33 mV). With +5V at +2.4 % and 3V3 at -3 %, outputs above about 4.99 V clip. MPX5700AP max 4.81 V reads 3.08 V.
evidence: computed; MPX5700AP datasheet VFSO max 4.813 V
suggested_fix: None; optionally 4.7k/10k divider to gain headroom (ratio 0.68 would be worse; 6.8k/10k gives 0.595 and 3.0 V FS).

title: TPS and MAP pins are TTa with a 4.0 V absolute maximum; clamp margin is thin at 24 V
claim: PA4 (TPS) and PA5 (MAP) are TTa pins (abs max 4.0 V). A sensor wire at 24 V through 5.6k injects 3.6 mA; pin voltage is +3V3 plus Vf (about 0.3-0.35 V), about 3.7 V on a 3.4 V rail and about 3.9 V if +3V3 is lifted to the 3.56 V TL431 level. The clamp is needed there (not removable) and the margin is about 0.1 V in that double-fault case.
evidence: STM32F407 datasheet Table 11 (any other pin -0.3..4.0 V), pin table PA4/PA5 I/O TTa; design.py:526-528 TL431 3.56 V; BAT54WS VF 320 mV at 1 mA
suggested_fix: None required; keep BAT54WS-class Schottky, do not substitute 1N4148WS.

title: 1N4148WS cannot replace the clamp Schottkys
claim: 1N4148WS (basic, $0.0086) has Vf about 0.65 V at 2 mA, which would take TTa pins to about 4.0 V, so cheap silicon diodes are not an alternative; only Schottky clones are.
evidence: JLC C2128 listing (1.25 V@150 mA); STM32 Table 11
suggested_fix: Use Schottky clones if cost matters.

title: Analog filter caps are 35-50 mm from the MCU pins on 0.2 mm single-layer traces
claim: Divider/clamp/filter clusters sit at x 120-132 mm while the ADC pins are at x 153-160 mm, so each 3.6 kOhm-source AN net runs 37-51 mm (AN_TPS 50.8 mm) with its 10 nF at the far end; no local capacitor at the MCU. Noise pickup is not bypassed at the pin; probably harmless at 12-bit/1.3 mV LSB.
evidence: evidence/cur_db/pcb_net_routing.csv, pcb_pads.csv
suggested_fix: Check on the bench; if noisy, add 100 pF-1 nF near the MCU pins.

title: Battery sense: 24 V and reverse battery survive; accuracy about +-5 % worst
claim: Ratio 0.1709 gives FS 19.3 V and a 4.7 mV battery LSB; 14.4 V is 2.46 V; source Z 5.64 k is fine. At 24 V the node is clamped to about 3.6 V with 0.62 mA in R11 (33 mW of 62.5 mW). Reverse battery injects 0.42 mA (limit 5 mA; D6 holds VBAT_IN near -1..-5 V). Accuracy: 1 % resistors +-1.7 %, ADC reference +-3 %: about +-5 % (0.7 V) worst, about +-2 % typical. Ordered rev 0.9 reads from +12V (0.3-0.6 V low, already documented).
evidence: design.py:258-263, 526-527; STM32 Table 12 (-5 mA); P06 D6 topology; R11 C25779 50 V 62.5 mW
suggested_fix: Calibrate vbattAdcOffset/gain against a meter; add VREFINT compensation if possible.

title: 1989-95 motherboard: R29 and R30 0R both tie HARN_2L to different daughterboard inputs
claim: R29 (2L -> IN_AUX1) and R30 (2L -> IN_TPS) are both 0R 0805 on the same harness cavity; if both were fitted by mistake the TPS and AUX1 inputs would be shorted. Out of scope for P12; for the owner to confirm the BOM stuffing.
evidence: kb/interconnect.md cur_mb8995 parts R29/R30
suggested_fix: Confirm the BOM fits only one of R29/R30.

title: VR conditioner (U9 + 26 passives) is free to remove; no supported car uses VR
claim: No supported Miata has a VR sensor; the VR inputs reach only AUX header J5 pins 7-10. The 27-part group costs about $0.22 per unit at qty 50, plus about $3 per order for the extended part C7549 (unique to U9, while C19726 stays for D36/D37). It also frees PE12/PE13 and board area.
evidence: lcsc.py prices 2026-11-16: C7549 $0.073 extended, 5.1k 0805 $0.0055, BAT54S $0.0145, 1n 0805 $0.0082; mb_common.py header map; research/pinouts_9605.md; notes sec.5
suggested_fix: Drop the group from the base build (or DNP-variant) unless custom VR trigger wheels are a sold feature; keep the harness pads on J5 if wanted. This shrinks the board and removes one extended part.

title: Hall 1k pull-up needs about 4.7 mA sensor sink; sink capability unverified
claim: Each hall input pulls up through 1k from V5_EXT (minus D35 drop), so the sensor must sink about 4.7 mA with Vol below the STM32 production-tested VIL of 0.99 V. Neither the NA optical CAS nor the NB BP4W sensor datasheet was found; Hellen uses 4.7k pull-ups.
evidence: design.py 436-445; STM32F407 DS8626 Table 48 (VIL 0.3VDD); calc.py: (5-0.3)/1k = 4.7 mA
suggested_fix: Bench-test the real CAS/CKP/CMP sensors for Vol at 4.7 mA and edge shape. R62/R64 are 0603, so 2.2k-4.7k is a hand-swap if needed.

title: 12 V switch inputs not guaranteed high at 6 V cranking battery
claim: The 22k/10k divider (ratio 0.3125) gives 1.875 V at a 6 V battery. That is above the by-design VIH of 1.785 V but below the production-tested VIH of 0.7 VDD = 2.31 V. Guaranteed high needs about 7.4 V at the harness and guaranteed low is at most 3.17 V. The rev 0.8 fix targeted only 9 V.
evidence: STM32F407 Table 48; design.py 447-452; calc.py (6 V -> 1.875 V, 7.4 V -> 2.31 V)
suggested_fix: If operation at 6 V matters, use 15k/10k: 6 V gives 2.4 V and the guaranteed low becomes 2.5 V. At 12-14 V the pin is still clamped at about 3.85 V. Otherwise document that these inputs are not cranking-critical.

title: Hall series 4.7k 0603 and D35 at limits under stacked faults
claim: A wire shorted to a 24 V jump-start source puts 86 mW in R61/R63, versus about 82 mW allowed at 85 C (0603, derated). A short to a 35 V load-dumped bus puts 206 mW in R61/R63 and 30 V reverse on D35 (limit 30 V). These are abnormal stacked cases and the 24 V case is already documented in design.py.
suggested_fix: Optional: 6.8k or 0805 for R61/R63. Accept the D35 margin or use a 40 V common-anode pair.

title: Ordered rev 0.9 db: same hall/SW/VR circuits; R139/R140/D36/D37 are UART parts
claim: The ordered rev 0.9 daughterboard has the same hall, SW and VR circuits (same refs, values, pads, positions). The only differences are that R139/R140 and D36/D37 serve UART_TX/RX and C72/C73 are absent, so flex and nitrous inputs exist only on rev 0.10. Findings above apply equally.
evidence: work/P13-.../cmp.py output on ord_db vs cur_db
suggested_fix: None.

title: Checked, correct: U9 LM2903 and BAT54S/BAT54A pad-by-pad, VR polarity
claim: U9 pads 1-8 match the SOIC-8 pin table (OUT/IN-/IN+/GND/IN+/IN-/OUT/VCC) and the footprint has 1.27 mm pitch and 4.95 mm span. BAT54S pad1 anode(GND), pad2 cathode(+rail), pad3 node. BAT54A pad3 is the common anode on V5_EXT. Output is high when harness N is above P; the hysteresis is 29 mV with a sensor attached.
evidence: pcb_pads.csv cur_db/ord_db; TI SLCS005X; onsemi BAT54SLT1G; JSMSEMI BAT54A p.1; calc.py
suggested_fix: None.

title: Checked, correct: MCU pins and harness mapping of digital inputs
claim: LQFP100 pins 38/39 (PE7/PE8) hall, 40-42 SW, 43/44 VR out, 63/64 (PC6/PC7) flex/N2O match design.py. JD2/J2 pin-to-net maps for IN_HALL1/2, IN_SW1-3, IN_FLEX, IN_N2O, VR1/2 agree on all four current motherboards, and hall and SW harness cavities match the per-year scripts.
evidence: design.py 152-158; kb/interconnect.md; cur_mb* pcb_nets.txt
suggested_fix: None.

title: Switch pull-ups R20-R22 unfitted: ground-switched signals read permanently low
claim: The only on-board bias for SW1-3 is the 10k pull-down. A VSS, A/C or clutch signal that switches to ground or is open collector needs R20-R22 fitted, but the JLC BOM leaves them blank. Per-year polarity of these signals was not verified.
evidence: mb_common.py 111-116; mb_na96.py 44-46
suggested_fix: Decide polarity per year from the FSM and fit R20-R22 on years that need them; state it in INSTALL.

title: TCAN1042VDRQ1 low stock; TJA1042T/3/1J is pin-identical, cheaper, deeply stocked
claim: TCAN1042VDRQ1 has 207 pcs at JLC (extended). NXP TJA1042T/3/1J (C132227) has 62k stock, $0.31@30 / $0.26@100 vs $0.60 / $0.52, extended; SO8 pinout identical (1 TXD,2 GND,3 VCC,4 RXD,5 VIO,6 CANL,7 CANH,8 STB), VIO 2.8-5.5 V, bus +-58 V. Saves ~$0.55/board with no layout change.
evidence: NXP TJA1042 Rev.12 Table 4 and limiting values; tools/lcsc.py today; TI SLLSES9C p.4
suggested_fix: Swap C485806 for C132227 on both transceivers (check JLC part-library footprint rotation in preview).

title: TCAN1042V pinout, VIO and STB wiring checked correct
claim: VCC=+5V pin3, VIO=+3V3 pin5, STB (pin 8)=GND (normal mode), TXD/RXD to MCU, CANH pin7/CANL pin6 on CAN_H/CAN_L; decoupling 100n on both supplies within ~4 mm.
evidence: evidence/cur_db/pcb_pads.csv U10/U106; TI SLLSES9C p.4 V-variant pin table

claim: CC1 (A5) and CC2 (B5) each have their own 5.1k to GND; A6/B6 joined on USB_DP, A7/B7 on USB_DM; VBUS and GND pads joined; USBLC6 pins 1&6 on D+, 3&4 on D-, 5 VBUS, 2 GND, matching ST. Same on ordered motherboards.

title: microSD socket numbering and footprint checked correct; D10 polarity correct
claim: Molex 47219-2001 pins 1 DAT2, 2 CS, 3 CMD=MOSI, 4 VDD, 5 CLK, 6 VSS, 7 DAT0=MISO, 8 DAT1 match nets; pad geometry equals Molex layout (1.10 pitch, 0.8x1.5, G pads 1.45x2.0, 13.75 x 8.3). D10 cathode on +5V, anode on VBUS: USB can feed +5V, not the reverse.

title: SOT-23 CPL rotation (+180) conflicts with community table (-90); wrong rotation ruins BAT54S/A clamps
refs: D15-D18, D35, D36, D37; repo/scripts/order_bom.py JLC_ROT
claim: All 7 SOT-23 diodes go out with CPL rotation = footprint rotation + 180 (from a rev 0.5 JLC preview per the repo). The JLCKicadTools community table has ^SOT-23 = -90, a 90 degree disagreement, so at most one is right for these parts. A misplaced dual diode shorts or opens the VR/input clamps.
