title: Injector clamp D42-49 polarity and battery-referenced TVS verified correct
claim: ES1D anode OUT_INJn, cathode INJn_CL; 1.5SMC16A cathode INJn_CL, anode VBAT_IN. In normal operation the TVS is forward biased (about 0 V reverse), so the 13.6 V standoff is not stressed at 14.4/16/24 V; ES1D reverse is at most about VBAT_IN vs 200 V.
evidence: pcb_nets/sch_netlist cur_db; design.py:359-372; 1.5SMC16A Vrwm 13.6, Vbr 15.2-16.8
suggested_fix: None.

title: BAT54S / BAT54A pinouts checked against datasheets: correct
claim: BAT54S pin 1 anode, 2 cathode, 3 common: pads 1=GND, 2=+5V/+3V3, 3=signal gives a correct two-sided clamp. BAT54A (JSMSEMI) pins 1,2 cathodes, 3 common anode: D35 pad 3 = V5_EXT, pads 1/2 = V5_H1/H2 is a correct OR to the hall supplies.
evidence: C19726 datasheet pin table p.5 (PIN 1 ANODE, 2 CATHODE, 3 CATHODE-ANODE); C916423 pin picture; pcb_pads.csv; sch_netlist libparts
suggested_fix: None.

title: All two-terminal diode/TVS/LED polarities correct on all 11 boards
claim: Pad 1 = cathode in every footprint (geometry and silk read from the PCB), matching schematic K/A pins; every net assignment matches the function in design.py/wideband.py (reverse-battery, TVS, catch, flyback, clamps, source diodes, LEDs).
evidence: list_d.py, sch_pins.py, fp_geom.json in work/P15; kb notes table
suggested_fix: None.

title: BAT54WS-7-F replaceable by a 7x cheaper BAT54WS (C7502694)
claim: Diodes BAT54WS-7-F C124205 costs $0.0937 at qty 50. hongjiacheng BAT54WS C7502694 (extended+preferred, $0.0127, 46.9k stock) has identical key specs: VRRM 30 V, IR 2 uA at 25 V, IF 200 mA, IFSM 600 mA, Tj 125 C, SOD-323 cathode line. Saves about $0.89 per daughterboard. Hot-leakage curve not compared.
evidence: lcsc.py 2026-11-16; datasheets/extra/BAT54WS_hongjiacheng_C7502694.pdf p.1-2; Diodes datasheet p.2
suggested_fix: Switch LCSC code to C7502694 on the next revision after comparing the leakage-vs-temperature graph; C3040452 is a second option (datasheet not read).

title: BAT54WS analog clamp leakage at 85-90 C gives about 20-30 LSB offset
claim: Repo comment says leakage is under 1 LSB, valid at room temperature only. Datasheet fig 2/4: about 1.8 uA at 3 V reverse, 75 C, rising steeply; about 3 uA at 90 C through 5.6k plus source gives about 17-25 mV (20-30 LSB) on CLT/IAT/etc. in a hot ECU.
evidence: Diodes BAT54WS p.3 fig 2 and 4; design.py:470-476 comment
suggested_fix: Accept (about 0.5 percent of range) or note in the docs; no hardware change needed.

title: Status LEDs at 3.3 V / 1k will be dim (green/blue Vf up to 3.1 V)
claim: KT-0603G/B Vf is 2.6-3.1 V at 5 mA; with 3.2-3.3 V drive and 1 k the current is about 0.2-0.6 mA (power LED D5 from +3V3 worst), so the LEDs may be hard to see in daylight.
evidence: C12624/C2288 datasheet table (VF 2.6-3.1 V at 5 mA); design.py:188-197
suggested_fix: Use 330-470 ohm for green/blue if visibility matters; check on first power-up.

title: D35 BAT54A 30 V rating reached when a hall wire is shorted to a load-dump battery
claim: Reverse voltage across D35 equals Vbat - 5 V when V5_H1/H2 is shorted to battery: 9.4 V at 14.4 V, 19 V at 24 V, 30 V (equal to VRRM) at a 35 V suppressed dump. Fine except a short plus load dump together.
evidence: BAT54A datasheet 30 V class; design.py:495
suggested_fix: Accept; the double-fault is remote.

title: D8 (B5819W, 40 V) can exceed rating under battery transients with ignition off
claim: D8 reverse = +12V_IN - VIGN_IN. With ignition off, a battery-rail spike clamped by D6 (Vbr 33-37 V, Vc up to 48.4 V at 31 A) can exceed D8's 40 V. Topology and parts are the same as Hellen's power_12and5V BOM, so it is inherited and probably tolerated (Schottky avalanche is not guaranteed).
evidence: B5819W 40 V; SMCJ30A datasheet; ext/hellen-one power_12and5V-BOM.csv
suggested_fix: Optional: 60 V Schottky in SOD-123/SMA for D8 (cost cents).

title: In a 24 V jump start the driver clamp, not the injector TVS, takes the flyback
claim: TVS threshold is VBAT_IN + 15.2..16.8 V + ES1D Vf (about 0.9 V); the design comment says the driver clamps from 36 V, so above about VBAT_IN 18 V the driver conducts first (24 V: about 40 V vs 36 V). This is the stated trade-off, but the energy then goes through the driver.
suggested_fix: Defer to the P09 review whether the driver survives that energy in a jump start.

title: D40/D41 carry above-1 A fault current briefly in a 24 V short on the VM wire
claim: (24 - 3.6) V / (10 + 1.6) ohm is about 1.8 A until PTC F2 trips; B5819W is 1 A average but 9 A surge. Pump path is limited to under 0.25 A by 47+62 ohm. Expected survivable.
evidence: nets WB_VM, R109=10, F2 nSMD010 in wideband.py; B5819W 1 A / 9 A
suggested_fix: None needed.

title: Heater PTC F1 derating misquoted; warm-up current exceeds hot hold current
claim: Repo says F1 holds about 2.4 A at 60 C. Datasheet table gives 1.99 A at 60 C, 1.79 A at 70 C, 1.34 A at 85 C. rusEFI warm-up ramp starts at 7 V effective, so a 2.5 ohm cold heater draws about 2.8 A rms, above hold from about 45 C ambient and above the scaled trip current (about 2.2 A) at 85 C. A hot-soaked ECU may trip F1 and the wideband times out (60 s).
evidence: datasheets/txt/C22446884 derating row 2920L300: 4.53/4.02/3.51/3.00/2.52/2.26/1.99/1.79/1.34; ext/wideband-rusefi/firmware/heater_control.cpp:109,173-176; Bosch LSU49 heater 7.5 W; cold 2.5 ohm is the repo's own figure (unverified). Trip scaling is inferred.
suggested_fix: Lower the ramp start voltage (e.g. 5.5 V) in the miata_f1 firmware port, or hot-soak test. 2920L400/30GR (C19078761) raises hold to 2.65/1.79 A but 8 A trip is poor for the 1.0 mm track.

title: Ordered db F1 (0.5 A) too small when hot
claim: Hold derates to about 0.34 A at 60 C and 0.24 A at 85 C (generic nSMD curve 68%/48%), against 0.25 A logic load at 13.8 V and 0.45 A at 8 V cranking (repo figures). Nuisance trip or brown-out when the ECU is hot. Fixed in rev 0.10 (1.1 A 1812).
evidence: datasheets/C70077 spec table 0.5 A/1.0 A; work/P16-ptc-fuses/nsmd_derate.png; VERIFICATION.md:684,1146
suggested_fix: Hand-rework to 1206L110/33NR (C48985884, 1.1 A, 33 V, 25.6k stock, $0.079@50; datasheet read, 0.72/0.55 A at 60/85 C), same 1206 pads; follow PTC iron-soldering limits (<350 C, <3 s).

title: Ordered mb F4 (0.5 A) trips with typical boost valve
claim: 0.5 A hold (0.34 A at 60 C, 0.24 A at 85 C) is below the 0.45 A boost valve the install doc cites (unverified) at high duty; current boards use 1.1 A (0.71/0.52 A), which also matches the 0.5 mm AUX_VBAT track.
evidence: ord_mb*/pcb_pads.csv F4 1206; INSTALL.md:336; datasheet C70077; 0.5 mm 1 oz track IPC-2221 about 26 C rise at 2.2 A (inferred)
suggested_fix: Rework to 1206L110/33NR (C48985884) or note a 0.3 A header limit in the ordered-board docs.

title: SMD1812-200-30 (C46641168) stock 57 pcs
claim: JLC stock today is 57 (manifest said 4); 9900 needs 1 per board, 0105 needs 2, so builds beyond about 28 boards of 0105 cannot be assembled. Same-footprint alternate BSMD1812-200-30V (BHFUSE C960026): 2.0/4.0 A, 30 V, 40 A, 20/100 mohm, same derating row, 194k stock, $0.0887@50, $0.0778@150, extended.
evidence: tools/lcsc.py C46641168 C960026 2026-11-16; datasheet C883150/C46641168 tables identical for 200 rows
suggested_fix: Change F2/F3 LCSC code to C960026 (no layout change).

title: 2 A PTCs F2/F3 derate to 0.8 A at 85 C: valve nuisance trip risk
claim: Hold is 1.45 A at 60 C, 1.09 A at 70 C, 0.80 A at 85 C. Valve mean current is D*14.4 V/R: with forum idle-valve R of 7.7-12 ohm and assumed 7.5 ohm VVT, 100% duty gives 1.2-1.9 A, so a hot cabin plus high duty can trip; normal 30-50% duty is fine.
evidence: datasheets/txt/C46641168 derating chart; coil R from forums (unverified), circuit_sim.py:229
suggested_fix: Hot-soak test at 70 C with full idle/VVT duty; if it trips, use a 2.6-3 A 1812 part and accept weaker track protection (0.8 mm track).

title: PTC F2 adds 1.6-15 ohm in the LSU pump return (VM) path
claim: Ri min 1.6 ohm, R1max 15 ohm (plus 33% thermal-shock drift) in series with R109 in the VM wire carries the pump current (about -2 to +2.5 mA): 3-40 mV VM offset away from lambda 1, not simulated. mck1117 reference has no PTC here.
evidence: datasheets/txt/C70065; wideband.py:148-190; LSU49_bosch Ip table; ext/wideband-mck1117 grep
suggested_fix: Simulate with 15 ohm in ngspice; if it matters, replace F2 by a resistor of equal fault current limit.

title: Repo claim 'no 1812 part holds 3 A above 8 V' is wrong
claim: 1812 3 A parts at 24-30 V exist (BSMD1812-300-24V C7500481 $0.139@50; 1812L300/30GR C48985875 $0.141@50). The 1812 hongjiacheng sheet shows the same derating as 2920L300 (2.01 A/1.33 A). No benefit in switching: 2920 is cheaper.
evidence: tools/lcsc.py, datasheets/txt/C46641168 derating row SMD1812-300
suggested_fix: Fix the sentence; keep 2920.

title: PTC identity, pad nets and footprints checked, correct
claim: All five LCSC codes match the BOM value and package; pad 1 is the supply side and pad 2 the load side in PCB, netlist and scripts (mb_common.py:93); PTCs are non-polarised. Ratings 30-33 V suit 24 V jump start and TVS-clamped load dump.
evidence: pcb_nets.txt, pcb_pads.csv, kb/parts_manifest.md, datasheets
suggested_fix: None.

title: R110 pump-current sense resistor is 0.62 ohm, not 62 ohm
claim: R110 is meant to be 62 ohm (the mck1117 pump sense resistor, 61.9 ohm). The BOM places C25341 = 1206W4F620LT5E, which is 620 mohm. The Uniroyal code 'L' means x10^-3. The pump-current measurement is then about 100x too small and the wideband cannot work. The ordered rev 0.9 board has the same error.
evidence: fab BOMs: '62,R110,R_1206_3216Metric,C25341'; lcsc.py C25341 desc '620mΩ'; datasheets/txt/C25341 line 51 (J=10^-1 K=10^-2 L=10^-3); design.py:64 and wideband.py:153 map '62' to C25341; VERIFICATION.md:273 intended C23222 (62 ohm 0603); ext/wideband-mck1117 rev C BOM R10 61.9
suggested_fix: Ordered boards: replace R110 by hand with a 62 ohm 1 % 1206 (C17971 1206W4F620JT5E, $0.0053) or a 61.9 / 62 ohm part. Current: change LCSC_R1206['62'] and wideband.py:153 to C17971. Add a script check of LCSC resistance against the schematic value.

title: Motherboard SW pull-ups R20-R22 (4.7k 0603) exceed rating in a 24 V jump start
claim: With the switch closed, each 4.7k 0603 (100 mW) dissipates 44 mW at 14.4 V (54 % of the derated rating at 85 C) and 122 mW at 24 V. That is 122 % of rating, and about 150 % of the 82 mW allowed at 85 C. A 35 V dump puts about 260 mW in for milliseconds.
evidence: V^2/R: 14.4^2/4.7k=44 mW, 24^2/4.7k=122 mW; Uniroyal datasheet C25341 section 9 derating from 70 C; nets in pcb_nets (VBAT_IN to R20.1)
suggested_fix: Use 1206 4.7k C17936 (BASIC, $0.0077@1) or 0805 4.7k; footprint change on the motherboards. Low urgency (rare 24 V jump start with the switch closed).

title: C102 16 V cap sits directly on the LSU_UN harness wire
claim: A cracked sensor shorting LSU_UN to the heater feed puts 14.4 V (90 % of rating, about 13 V across the cap) and 24 V in a jump start (150 %) on a 16 V part. A failed-short cap would then tie LSU_UN to WB_ESR, in a path that is already faulted. No basic 0402 100n at 25 V or more exists.
evidence: join.csv C102 nets LSU_UN / WB_ESR; manifest C1525 16 V; lcsc search --basic 100nF 50V 0402 gave none (25 V options are extended: C466234 $0.0018)
suggested_fix: Use the basic 0603 100n 50V C14663 (footprint change) or an extended 25 V 0402 such as C466234. Low priority.

title: R15-R18 100 ohm 1206 ignition series resistors marginal when hot into a short to ground
claim: A short of an ignition output to ground puts about (5-0.4)^2/100 = 212 mW in each, which is 85 % of 250 mW at 25 C and about 103 % of the derated 205 mW at 85 C. The repo comment assumes 0.25 W is enough.
evidence: design.py:310 comment; Uniroyal derating from 70 C (C25341 datasheet section 9); values inferred, 0.4 V Schottky drop assumed
suggested_fix: Accept (the resistor only gets hot and is a sustained-fault case), or use 2 W-class resistors. Nothing needed for normal use.

title: Capacitor DC-bias effective capacitance cannot be checked from files on hand
claim: The Samsung CL datasheets on file (4986 lines) contain no DC-bias curves and the Samsung web tool returned HTTP 500. Effective capacitance after bias is estimated only: 10u/25V 0805 at 5 V about 60-75 %, 100u/6.3V at 3.3 V about 40-60 %, 10u/50V at 14.4 V about 50-60 %. This agrees with P05, P07 and P08, which flag the same unknowns.
evidence: grep of datasheets/txt for bias gave no curves; kb/parts/P05, P07, P08
suggested_fix: Bench-measure ripple and the 1 uF LDO outputs, or use Samsung SimSurfing data for the final BOM.

title: Only one extended passive can be replaced by a basic part cleanly
claim: Extended passives: C17969, C25341, C26032, C106862 plus the 'preferred extended' C23221, C25771, C25917, C36871. R144-R147 (3.3k 1206) could use the basic 4.7k 1206 C17936 ($0.0077@1, 2.08 M stock): 122 mW at 24 V, 44 mW at 14.4 V, but a 1.4x slower pull-down. That removes 1 distinct extended part (4 placements, about $0.003 each, the saving being mostly the extended-part fee). The other six have no safe basic equivalent (the values set the wideband analog and fault-fuse behaviour). After the R110 fix the extended passives still number 8.
evidence: lcsc.py C26032 ext, C17936 basic, C26010 0805 basic (125 mW is too low at 24 V: 175 mW); manifest jlc_preferred flags
suggested_fix: Swap R144-R147 to C17936 after the owner confirms spark-end pull-down timing. Leave the rest.

title: Checked: C0G where needed, no Y5V, tolerances equal the reference
refs: C13,C14 (C1663 C0G), C119,C120 (C1562 C0G); wideband resistors
claim: The MCU and wideband crystal load caps are C0G 33 pF 5 %. No Y5V part exists. All wideband 1 % thick-film resistor values and grades equal the mck1117 rev C BOM, and the 1 % feedback and battery-divider resistors are adequate (about 1.3 % worst case).
evidence: join.csv; manifest params; ext/wideband-mck1117 rev C BOM
suggested_fix: None.

title: Ordered DB rev0.9 and current motherboards differ on J2.24/25
claim: Ordered DB has UART_TX/UART_RX on J2.24/25, current DB has IN_FLEX/IN_N2O, and every motherboard matches its own generation. Mixing generations connects UART to flex/N2O input lines.
evidence: kb/interconnect.md ord vs cur tables, programmatic compare today
suggested_fix: Mark generations as not interchangeable in docs; never plug ordered DB on current MB (or reverse) without checking.

title: Header C2977586 plating unspecified
claim: Zhouri sheet says 'Au or Over Ni' and LCSC lists no plating, while socket is gold over nickel. A tin or unknown header against gold sockets risks fretting on sub-mA sensor lines, the problem the repo says it fixed.
evidence: datasheets/C2977586 p.1; lcsc.py params Contact Plating '-'; C124412 sheet 'Gold Over Nickel'; VERIFICATION.md:670
suggested_fix: Confirm plating by sample or supplier, or switch to a header with stated gold plating (e.g. C2337 listed Gold; its datasheet not read).

title: Socket C124412 low stock, rating mismatch
claim: Only 65 in stock (about 32 units), extended part, single source. LCSC attribute says 1 A while the maker sheet says 3 A.
evidence: lcsc.py today: stock 65, $0.57@1, $0.40@30, $0.31@80; sheet 'Current Rate:3Amp'
suggested_fix: Stock up or qualify a second source (Wurth 61304011821, Samtec SSQ-140-01-G-S already named in repo); trust the 3 A maker sheet only after confirming.

title: VVT output 2.0 A on a single contact
claim: The VVT valve at 100 % duty (2.0 A) on one pin is at or above the derated header rating (~1.6-1.95 A at 85 C air with loaded neighbours); IACV 1.3 A and injectors 1.2 A are fine.
evidence: track_current.py:60-62; header 2.5 A, contact 20 mohm; derating computed in notes
suggested_fix: Split VVT across two header pins or cap duty; not needed for injectors/IACV.

title: Ground return across 23 GND pins: small ADC offset
claim: 23 GND pins plus 2 heater-return pins share about 8 A pulsed; at 10-20 mohm per pair the DB-to-MB ground offset is about 4-15 mV synchronous with injector pulses (about 5-18 LSB at 3.3 V/12 bit).
evidence: Pin counts from kb/interconnect.md; currents track_current.py; 20 mohm max from sheet
suggested_fix: Accept; keep sensor grounds and ADC reference at the same GND pins; average ADC outside injector edges if needed.

title: Header-in-socket jig soldering, 160 hand joints per unit
claim: Headers must be soldered while plugged into the MB sockets, so JLC cannot assemble them; hand work is 80 joints on DB plus 80 on MB per unit (JLC THT could do the MB sockets for about $0.05/joint, secondary source).
evidence: fab self-order BOM note; JLC help pages via web search
suggested_fix: Quote JLC THT for sockets only; build a fixture; consider a single-board or soldered-pin variant if volume grows.

title: Mirroring check: pure translation, passed
claim: Checked correct: all 80 pad pairs differ by exactly (+14.5, +42.0) mm in four db/mb pairs (cur and ord), pin 1 to pin 1, headers on DB bottom, sockets on MB top, no mirror.
evidence: evidence/*/pcb_pads.csv, footprints sides
suggested_fix: None.

title: Pin function match on all 9 MBs, HTR_GND to GND intentional
claim: Checked correct: all nets match for 80 pins on 9 motherboards; the only name difference is HTR_GND (DB) vs GND (MB), which is the heater return by design.
evidence: kb/interconnect.md; design.py:113-116; mb_common.py:25; gen_sch2.py:1022
suggested_fix: None.

title: Stack height 11.04 mm vs 11 mm standoffs
claim: Header plastic 2.54 + socket 8.5 = 11.04 mm; 6 mm pin fully engaged, tolerance about -0.2/+0.3 mm is harmless; M3x6 screws give 4.4 mm thread; no MB parts under DB.
evidence: Both datasheet drawings; footprint coordinates
suggested_fix: None.

title: J1 footprint matches TE drawing (checked, correct)
claim: All 48 hole positions, 1.1 mm holes, 4.5 mm row spacing, 3 pegs dia 3.5 at -5.05/33.8/79.65 and 10.2 mm peg offset equal the TE drawing; max deviation 0.003 mm. The footprint file is identical on all boards.
evidence: datasheets/extra/174917-6_lcsc-TE-drawing.pdf (rev M9, mounting view); repo/motherboards/1989-95/ecu_mb.pretty/TE_174917-6_48P.kicad_mod; evidence/*/pcb_pads.csv J1
suggested_fix: None.

title: Pin letters/chirality agree with Speeduino and Hellen (checked, correct)
claim: Pad-by-pad comparison with the Speeduino NA6 v1.3 footprint+symbol (174917-1): 48/48 names at the same positions via a proper rotation (no mirror). Lower row = A,C,E..., upper (peg side) = B,D,F.... Hellen NA6-94 net functions (GND, crank, cam, 5V, IAT, CLT, INJ1/2, idle, tach) land on the same letters (their 3x = our 2x).
evidence: ext/speeduino-hardware/.../NA6 v1.3.kicad_pcb + NA6-cache.lib; ext/hellen-miata-NA6/hellen64_NA6_94.kicad_pcb; work/P19a-harness-header-48p-NA/cmp.py
suggested_fix: Optionally confirm with a continuity check on a stock ECU before first fit.

title: Header is purchasable; repo says salvage/clone only
claim: TE page says not currently available, but LCSC/JLC C592838 (TE 174917-6, extended, stock 32) sells at $12.92/12.74/12.43/12.16 for 1/10/30/100; DigiKey (WEE marketplace) lists 2150 pcs at EUR 5.34 at 30 with 3-day ship; Newark about $6 and RS about $7 (aggregator data). The self-order BOM only gives a DigiKey search link and a salvage note.
evidence: tools/lcsc.py C592838; digikey.de/en/products/detail/wee/174917-6/26907531; te.com/en/product-174917-6.html; Octopart/RS via web search
suggested_fix: Put C592838 (and the DigiKey/Newark link) in the self-order BOM; confirm stock before ordering; consider JLC THT assembly of C592838 to save hand fitting (not checked).

title: Hellen NA6-94 uses a different, wider header geometry
claim: The Hellen NA6-94 board (sold as plug-and-play for NA6 and 94-95) places a 76-pos 178780-1 header spanning x 16..138 mm on a 154 mm board with 22-pin and 26-pin plugs about 54 mm apart, whereas this design (like Speeduino and the TE drawing) has the plugs adjacent in a 74.6 mm span centred on the board. Both cannot mate the same stock ECU; I could not determine why. Header position and overhang (about 7.4 mm past the top edge) rest on rusEFI/Speeduino data, not on a measured case.
evidence: Hellen P2 pad coordinates (work/P19a-harness-header-48p-NA/hellen.txt), board bbox 154.2x159.2; BOM bom_replace_hellen64_NA6_94-d.csv P2=178780-1; mb_na6.py:79; VERIFY list in mb_na6.py
suggested_fix: Measure a stock ECU case (header 1A offset from edges, peg holes) before fitting the ordered boards; this is already on the repo's VERIFY list.

title: Mating plug and variant numbers
claim: TE drawing note 2 lists mating plug housings 174515 (22 pos), 174516 (26 pos), 917989, 917992. Variants -1 (natural), -6 (gray), -7 (yellow) share one footprint; Speeduino used -1. LCSC C5166285 (174917-1) has 0 stock.
evidence: TE drawing p.1 notes and variant table; Speeduino connector.sch; lcsc.py C5166285
suggested_fix: Mention in docs that any 174917-x variant fits the same footprint.

title: Footprint pad declared 1.506 x 1.151 'circle'
claim: The footprint file declares circle pads with size 1.50622 x 1.15062; KiCad 9 exports 1.5062 round (0.2 mm ring), so no problem seen, but a tool reading the 1.15 mm value would leave a 0.025 mm ring.
evidence: TE_174917-6_48P.kicad_mod pad lines; evidence/cur_mb8995/pcb_pads.csv size 1.5062x1.5062
suggested_fix: Set both sizes to 1.5062 in the footprint for cleanliness.

title: Hole drill 1.1 mm vs TE recommended 1.35 +-0.10 mm
claim: TE drawing 178780 gives PCB mounting holes 76 x dia 1.35 +-0.10 (true position dia 0.2). Repo and Hellen use drill 1.1. With post 0.64 sq (diagonal 0.905) plus 0.2 position tolerance the 1.1 hole has about zero margin, so some posts may not seat. Hellen ships with 1.1, which suggests it is usually workable. Mated-in-place fit not tested.
evidence: TE 178780 rev P10 (LCSC C5166246 PDF) mounting dimensions block; TE_178780-1_76P.kicad_mod pad drill 1.1; Hellen P2 drill 1.09982
suggested_fix: Set drill to 1.3-1.35 (pad 1.8 leaves 0.22 annulus) on new boards; on ordered boards test-fit a header and open the holes with a 1.3 drill if needed.

title: Ordered 1999-2000 board needs 176122-6, which is nearly unobtainable
claim: The ordered 1999-2000 rev 0.7 board uses the 64P footprint for TE 176122-6. Web snippets show DigiKey/Mouser/Avnet at zero stock, MOQ 1600, long lead; only brokers at $12.8-18 with min 5-400. The 76P header (in stock) cannot be fitted on the 64P footprint, since the 12-bay shifts plug 2 and plug 3 by 20.7 mm. JLC C5171845 labelled 176122-6 at $0.04 is not this part.
evidence: web search snippets (undated); TE_176122-6_64P pad x 36.65/63.59 vs 76P 57.35/84.30; lcsc.py C5171845
suggested_fix: Buy a broker sample or check TE 178764-1 (64 pos, flange, DigiKey stock 1679, AUD 27.3@1) against the footprint before first assembly; use the 76P on the current rev 0.9 board.

title: 76P header on 1999-2000 car needs 20.7 mm extra plug reach
claim: On the 64P header (stock) plug 2 starts 36.65 mm from plug 1; on the 76P it starts 57.35 mm because the unused 12-bay sits between. 'Same housings' is true by number, but fit depends on the harness plugs reaching 20.7 mm further. Supported only by Hellen NB1/NA6 shipping on 178780-1 with identical geometry, not by a car test or by TE data.
evidence: footprint pad coordinates; Hellen NB1 P2 nets 23-38 at same positions; research/pinouts_9605.md:123
suggested_fix: Check on a real NB harness/ECU case before ordering many; keep the Hellen precedent in README as evidence.

title: 178780-1 price and availability
claim: Single most expensive connector. JLC/LCSC C5166246 stock 0 (LCSC 18), $24.94@1 and $24.23@30. DigiKey NL 1887 in stock, EUR16.05@1, 13.47@12, 11.58@102, 27 wk lead. Self-order BOM has no LCSC code, so it is ordered separately and hand fitted. 174915-6 (C5166478) $18.2@1, 15.9@30, 14.6@100 but stock 0, a 37 g housing vs 23.8 g 'NON FLANGE' for 178780: not a proven drop-in.

title: README names terminal 1A as origin

title: MAP error band +-17.5 kPa is too large for 35 kPa idle fuelling
claim: Datasheet accuracy +-2.5 %VFSS (VFSS 4.5 V, 6.43 mV/kPa) = +-0.1125 V = +-17.5 kPa over 0-85 C: +-50 % of a 35 kPa idle reading and +-17.6 % at 100 kPa. The absolute offset spec 0.184-0.409 V alone spans the whole budget. NXP gives no typical figure. A tune on one car absorbs the fixed part, but a shipped base map and temperature drift are exposed. Outside 0-85 C no accuracy is specified.
evidence: datasheets/C90152_MPX5700AP.pdf Table 1 p.2 (accuracy, Voff, sensitivity); MPX4250A Rev 8 Table 2 for comparison; computed.
suggested_fix: For NA cars offer MPX4250AP (+-3.5 kPa) or a 400 kPa SMD sensor. Enable the 'read MAP at start-up as baro' option (rusefi_config.txt:1242). Keep closed-loop lambda trim range wide on the base tune.

title: Pinout and orientation of U2 flat footprint checked, correct
claim: Pad 1 (notched lead, Vout) = IN_MAP, 2 = GND, 3 = V5_SENS, 4-6 unconnected, on all current and ordered motherboards. Placement is a pure rot 90 of the NXP top view (pin 1 left, leads toward viewer), with no mirroring. The footprint pad coordinates are identical to Hellen NA6's MPX4_MAP, and Hellen's ibom 867B footprint rotated 180 deg gives the same layout. The remaining assumption is the 867B plan view direction (third-angle inference), so check continuity on the first board.
evidence: evidence/*/pcb_pads.csv U2 rows (x 240.51, y 198.35..185.65); datasheet p.7-8 case 867B-04 Style 1; ext/hellen-miata-NA6/hellen64_NA6_94.kicad_pcb:3925-3943; mb_common.py:66-71.

title: Decoupling and output filter match NXP recommended circuit
claim: C1 1 uF and C2 10 nF on Vs, C3 470 pF on Vout, all 0603 within about 3-6 mm of the pads, are identical to NXP Fig 4. Supply 4.815-5.185 V from the U3 tracker lies inside 4.75-5.25 V. The V5_SENS and IN_MAP nets reach only U2, C1-C3 and the daughterboard, never a harness pin. Ordered boards identical.
evidence: datasheet Fig 4 p.4; evidence/cur_mb8995/pcb_nets.txt:29,63; pcb_footprints.csv C1-C3; P07 notes.
suggested_fix: None.

title: MPX5700AP is the dearest single part; no JLC stock for 250 kPa class; one SMD option
claim: C90152 costs $27.49 @30 (JLC extended, stock 155) and is hand fitted. MPX4250AP C2802676 and MPX4115AP C3259058 have 0 stock at JLC. MPXHZ6400AC6T1 C511770 (SMD SSOP-8, 20-400 kPa, 1.5 %VFSS = +-5.7 kPa, 12.1 mV/kPa, Vs 4.64-5.36 V) has stock 739 at $10.45 @30 / $9.49 @100 and is what Hellen NA6 uses. It would save about $17 per unit plus hand fitting and has 3x better error, but needs a new footprint and a hose/port arrangement. The HZ datasheet and port size were not read (MPXH6400A Rev 6 was).
evidence: tools/lcsc.py C90152 C511770 C2802676 today; datasheets/extra/MPXH6400A_rev6_components-ru.pdf Table 1/3; ext/hellen-miata-NA6 .../64_NA6_94-BOM.csv.

title: NRND statement is not confirmed
claim: Repo says MPX5700AP is NRND at ST. A web-search summary said the ST Japanese page shows NRND (suggested replacement FXPS7550A4S) while the ST English page and estore show Active. NXP's Japanese page reports the MEMS sensors moved to ST on 2026-02-02. I could not fetch st.com to settle it. Stock is thin (LCSC/JLC 155) and Digikey is reported at a 52-week lead time.

title: Output load 15.6 k is harmless for NA pressures
claim: The repo-documented 'load above typical source current' only matters above Vout 1.56 V = 211 kPa absolute: load current is 27 uA at 35 kPa, 54 uA at 100 kPa, versus 0.1 mA typical source current. Only full-scale boost would exceed it (0.30 mA at 700 kPa). Resolution is 0.196 kPa per 12-bit LSB.
evidence: computed: I = Vout/15.6k, Vout = 5*(0.0012858*P+0.04); P12 notes ratio 0.641.
suggested_fix: Can be reworded as irrelevant below 200 kPa; no hardware change.

title: U2 lead holes 0.8128 mm marginal for 0.68-0.84 mm leads
claim: Datasheet lead width is 0.68-0.84 mm and thickness 0.36-0.41 mm; the finished hole is 0.8128 (JLC PTH tolerance about +-0.08 mm), so a max-width lead may not enter. The footprint copies Hellen's 0.8128 (Hellen's own ibom 867B footprint uses 1.1 mm). The pad is 1.524 mm, so 1.0-1.1 mm still leaves 0.2 mm ring.
evidence: datasheet p.7 dims D 0.68-0.84, J 0.36-0.41; pcb_pads.csv U2 drill 0.8128; ext/hellen-one/ibom-data/867B.kicad_mod drill 1.1.
suggested_fix: Change U2 pad drills to 1.0 mm in mk_map_fp.py next revision; on ordered boards test-fit a real sensor and open holes with a drill if needed.

title: Sensor range is oversized for NA use
claim: At 100 kPa the output is 0.84 V (0.54 V at the ADC); idle 0.43 V. The 700 kPa span uses about 12 % of the output swing, which is the cause of the weak accuracy. A 115 kPa class (MPX4115A: 15-115 kPa) fits NA but has 0 stock at JLC.
suggested_fix: Offer a per-order sensor choice: 700 kPa only for boosted cars.

title: INSTALL hose advice consistent with barb drawing

evidence: datasheet p.7 drawing; web search summary of AN1513.
suggested_fix: None; maybe say silicone not PVC.

title: Operating accuracy range 0-85 C only
claim: NXP specifies the 2.5 % band only at 0-85 C. The ECU sits in the cabin, and cold winter starts (<0 C) and hot soak (>85 C) are outside the spec. The MPX4250A sheet multiplies its error band by 3 at -40 and 125 C; the MPX5700 sheet gives no figure.
evidence: datasheet Table 1 p.2; MPX4250A Rev 8 Fig 8.
suggested_fix: Accept; rely on closed-loop lambda after warm-up.

claim: All ordered motherboards carry a Micro-Fit 2x3 (pad n = Bosch pin n); AEM 30-3427 has a JST PUD plug and will not fit. Customer needs a custom Bosch-plug to Micro-Fit 43025-0600 lead; the ordered docs only say 'a 6-wire lead'.

title: Circuit-1 end of the JST row and AEM=JST numbering not document-verified
claim: JST catalog drawing verifies pitch, row of pin 1 relative to the boss (pin 2 +7.7 mm to boss matches PCB) but not which end of the row is circuit 1; AEM does not state its numbers are JST's. The mapping rests on an owner photo. A flip puts sense wires on wrong pads and H+ on H-.

title: JST PUD 3 A contact is thin for LSU heater ramp, single contact per heater wire
claim: JST rating is 3 A AC/DC at AWG22 including temperature rise, -25..+85 C; heater ramp RMS about 2.2 A (3.9 A at -40 C) with 4.5 A pulses, one contact per heater wire, AEM wire gauge unknown (terminal takes 22-26 AWG). Acceptable but zero margin in hot cabin/cold sensor.

suggested_fix: Confirm AEM harness wire gauge; keep heater duty-limited at start; consider fast-heating off. Micro-Fit (8.5 A) on ordered boards has no issue.

claim: Socket 8.5 mm plus ZHOURI header plastic 3.0 mm gives 11.5 mm; the 11 mm standoff leaves a 0.5 mm gap so the pins engage about 5.5 of 6 mm. It works and the standoff is the stop. A 12 mm standoff would be wrong. Hole spacing 116 x 67 mm matches on both boards.

claim: cjiang's own spec caution lists 'Transportation equipment (automobiles...)' as not intended; LCSC grade is 'Consumer grade'. title: L1 and L2 footprints match maker land patterns

evidence: pcb_pads.csv L1/L2 rows; C177247 text 'Recommended Land Pattern' table; extra/MWSA_chipdip.pdf row MWSA0603S.
suggested_fix: None.

title: L2 Isat is typical only (5.2 A); margin to 3.8 A peak limit about 27 %
claim: The Sunlord MWSA0603S-100MT sheet gives Isat 5.2 A as a typical value (30 % inductance drop), Irms 4.5 A typ; LCSC text says 5.5 A. No guaranteed minimum or hot figure is published, against the LMR14020 peak limit of 3.8 A max.
evidence: extra/MWSA_chipdip.pdf MWSA0603S table (68 mohm, Isat 5.2, Irms 4.5; notes *3 Isat typical); manifest description '4.5A 5.5A'.
suggested_fix: Accept (30 % drop at 5.2 A is still above 3.8 A even if tolerance is 15 %), or note it; no change needed unless thermal testing shows saturation.

title: X5R capacitors are rated to 85 C only
claim: Samsung temperature code A = X5R -55..+85 C. In a stock ECU case at 85 C cabin air plus self heating, these capacitors operate above their rated range (capacitance tolerance no longer guaranteed), including the buck input capacitors, which also lose capacity to DC bias at 14.4 V. All 16 V parts sit on rails of 5 V or less, so there is no overvoltage.
evidence: Samsung catalogue txt line 165-166 (A X5R 55..85, B X7R 55..125); capv.py net check; review brief 85 C air.
suggested_fix: Where cheap, choose X7R (125 C) for the buck input and LDO output; I did not find a 10u 50 V X7R 1206 stock part in one search, so check before swapping.

title: J5 2x10 box header has no LCSC code; same-series BOOMELE C3405 exists
claim: The current motherboards name an On Shore 302-S201 box header that has to be bought elsewhere. BOOMELE C3405 (2x10, 3 A listed, stock 42.6k, $0.146@1, $0.072@2000) is the 2x10 version of the C3406 2x8 header used on the ordered boards, in the same drawing family (n = 3 to 40). The JLC text for C3406 says '2x5' although the part is 2x8 (params 2x8P).
evidence: lcsc.py C3405, C3406; C3406 datasheet drawing '2.54-2xnP, 3<=n<=40', footprint IDC-Header_2x10_P2.54mm_Vertical.
suggested_fix: Name C3405 in the self-order BOM; check the C3405 sheet pin length/height first (I read the C3406 family drawing only).

title: Open-top shunts could fall off under vibration and drop an injector
claim: Four 1x3 jumpers select harness routing (e.g. JP1 pin 3 = HARN_2Y connects to INJ2 or INJ3 only through the shunt). With no retention, a lost shunt leaves that injector wire unconnected; the part is a friction-fit open-top shunt.
evidence: mb_na6.py:138-146, SHUNTS dict lines 164-165; C5305 listed as 'Open-Top Unshrouded' shunt.
suggested_fix: For fixed configurations use 0 ohm links or solder bridges selected at assembly; keep shunts only on options users change.

title: Hand-assembly load: about 260-290 joints per ECU
claim: Through-hole count: 80 (DB headers) + 80 (sockets) + 48-76 (harness) + 16 (JP) + 20 (J5) + 6 (MAP) + 8 (JST) = about 258-290 joints, about 60-90 min per ECU at 15-20 s per joint, plus 4 standoffs, 8 M3x6, 2 M3x10, 2 nuts, 6 shunts.
evidence: Self-order BOMs; fab_*_self_order_bom.csv; order_bom.py HAND set.
suggested_fix: Biggest cut: sockets and DB headers could be a pair of pre-assembled pin-header sets or selective wave, or reduce to fewer pins per row; price this against about $400 per ECU.

title: Optional ferrite and LEDs can use BASIC parts
claim: BLM18PG121SN1D (C14709, BASIC, 120 ohm, 2 A at 85 C, DCR 0.05/0.10) replaces the extended BLM18PG221SN1D for VDDA filtering (loads a few mA). Of the status LEDs only red is BASIC. Savings is a per-order setup fee (UNVERIFIED about $3 per extended part type), not per-unit.
evidence: lcsc.py -s ferrite --basic: C14709 $0.014@1 / $0.0072@top, stock 1.55M; Murata JENF243A table row BLM18PG121SN1D.
suggested_fix: Swap FB1 to C14709 only if the VDDA noise margin is not a concern (220 to 120 ohm at 100 MHz). LEDs not worth changing.

title: Green and blue LEDs run at about 0.3-0.7 mA from 3.3 V via 1k
claim: Green/blue KT-0603 VF is 2.6-3.1 V at 5 mA; with 3.3 V and 1 k the current is only a few hundred uA (estimated), while red/yellow get about 1.3 mA, so the colours will look unequal; they still light. No overstress anywhere (limit 25-30 mA).
evidence: KT-0603G/B text section 5 VF; design.py:192-197.
suggested_fix: Use 330-470 ohm for green/blue if equal brightness is wanted; optional.

title: Crystal gm margin and land pattern checked, correct
claim: X50328MSB2GI worst case gm_crit = 4*80*(2*pi*8e6)^2*(5p+20p)^2 = 0.505 mA/V against STM32F407 Gmcritmax 1 mA/V (Gm 5 mA/V). 33 pF C0G caps give CL about 19.5-21.5 pF for a 20 pF crystal. Pads 2.0x2.4 on 3.7 mm centres vs maker 1.7x2.4 on 3.7: fine.
evidence: YXC page (ESR 80 ohm max 8-16 MHz, C0 5 pF max, CL 20 pF); STM32F407 DS Table 32 (line 6128-6137); pcb_pads.csv Y1/Y101; pcb_nets.txt.
suggested_fix: None.

title: SW1/SW2 land pattern and nets checked, correct
claim: Pads 1.0x0.75 at 6.0 x 3.75 mm centres equal XKB's PCB layout (7.0/5.0 outer/inner by 4.5/3.0). Switch contacts A-B and C-D are each shorted, so the top pair is net 1 and the bottom pair is net 2 as wired. 3.3 V and under 1 mA versus rated 50 mA at 12 V. Temperature range is -30..+85 C.
evidence: C318884 page image (PCB layout, specification); pcb_pads.csv SW1/SW2 rows.
suggested_fix: None.

title: Ordered boards use FH CMI322513U2R2KT (500 mA) as L1 on a 0.5 A fuse
claim: Ordered L1 is a 1210 2.2 uH, 300 mohm, 500 mA part. Buck input reaches about 0.45 A at 8 V cranking (repo figure) so it runs at nearly its rating with small margin; 75 mW at 0.5 A. Easy to swap by hand if the first boards run warm.
evidence: parts_manifest.md ord_db L1 line; design.py comments lines 211-223.
suggested_fix: Watch its temperature in first power-up with an SD card writing; replace with C177247/C408408 (same 1210 outline is not compatible: different footprint) only if it runs hot.

title: A/C request (4F) and clutch (4I) are active-low with ECU-side pull-up; board ships no pull-up and default polarity
claim: Mazda tables show 4F <1 V with A/C on, else B+, and 4I B+ released, <1 V depressed. rusEFI's own Hellen NB2 uses acSwitchMode=PI_PULLUP and clutchDownPinMode=PI_INVERTED_DEFAULT. This board has the 22k/10k divider to ground with R21/R22 not fitted, and the preset sets no pin mode, so both inputs read 0 V always: A/C compressor never commanded. Fitting R21 without inverting the mode inverts the request.
evidence: CHARM 2003 PCM table p4 (4F, 4I); Hellen NB2 board_configuration.cpp:88-93; rusefi hw_layer/debounce.cpp:112; INSTALL.md has no per-year R20-R22 guidance; kb/interconnect.md 4F/4I nets
suggested_fix: Fit R21 and R22 by hand on the ordered NB2 board before use; in the NB2 presets set acSwitchMode=PI_PULLUP-equivalent (active low) and clutchDownPinMode inverted; document in INSTALL.md.

title: Condenser fan 2C not tied to A/C request
claim: Only fan1 (2B, radiator fan) gets fan1AcMode=Relay; fan2 (2C, condenser fan) stays Disabled and comes on only at 95 C. Hellen NB2 sets fan2AcMode=Relay on 2C (named AC Fan). Whether the stock ECU also runs the condenser fan with A/C is not shown by the Mazda tables.
evidence: miata_board.cpp:228; rusefi fan_control.cpp:289; Hellen NB2 board_configuration.cpp:99 and main.yaml 2B/2C
suggested_fix: Set fan2AcMode=Relay for the NB2 presets (and consider both fans with A/C) once F-A/C input is fixed.

title: Generator warning lamp 3U never driven
claim: Stock PCM sinks 3U: lamp lit key-on (bulb check), off when charging, lit on charging DTCs. Here 3U is open: the lamp never lights and a charging failure gives no warning. Hellen NB2 drives 3U.
evidence: CHARM 2003 p3 (3U); Hellen main.yaml 3U AWARN; motherboards/2001-05/README.md 'Not connected'
suggested_fix: Tell owners; optionally route a spare low side (J5 ribbon) to 3U in a later revision.

title: VVT valve feed PTC F3 (2 A) derates to 0.8 A hot; coil about 7.5 ohm
claim: OCV coil is about 6.9-7.9 ohm (Mazda 2.0 L spec and a 2001 Miata reading; BP-Z3 value not retrieved) so full-on current is about 1.9 A at 14.4 V, not 1 A. SMD1812-200 hold current is 1.09 A at 70 C and 0.80 A at 85 C, so a hot cabin plus moderate duty can trip F3; the valve then drops to default retard until it resets. No damage.
evidence: datasheet C46641168 derating table; VERIFICATION.md 'about 1 A'; web search summaries for OCV resistance
suggested_fix: Use a 2.6-3 A PTC or a link for F3; the VND7NV04 limits fault current anyway.

title: All connected cavities correct; 72 pads match the real connector
claim: For each of the 36 connected cavities the chain pad -> net -> JD pin -> MCU pin -> firmware assignment is consistent and the stock function matches at least two independent sources. The 72 pads equal the cavity set in the Mazda connector drawing (17+24+31; no 2L,3G,3R,4G,4Q,4Y).
evidence: kb/interconnect.md cur/ord 0105; CHARM 2003 connector figure p1; scripted set comparison; design.py mcu dict
suggested_fix: None.

title: 2001-02 vs 2003-05: verified difference and working wake path
claim: 2001 and 2002 CHARM tables both show 3H and 4S unused and 3E CDCV; 2003 shows 3H main relay (B+ key off, <1 V on) and 4S IG1. The preset difference (mainRelayPin and ignKeyAdcChannel only) is right. The 2003-05 ECU wakes from 4S through D8 and F1, boots, then closes the relay via 3H. A wrong year button gives no start.
evidence: CHARM 2001 p2 and p5 (read today), CHARM 2003 p2/p4; design.py:204 D8; miata_board.cpp:272-290; wiki rusefi 2002/2003
suggested_fix: None.

title: CHARM 2003 lists TP on 4Y; no 4Y cavity exists
claim: The 2003 Mazda table puts TP on 4Y and 4V as unused, but its own connector drawing has no 4Y; 2001/2002 tables, 2005 FSM, Hellen and rusEFI wiki all use 4V. Design (4V) is right; R19's open conflict is resolved as a manual typo.
evidence: CHARM 2003 p1 figure vs p5; CHARM 2001 p5 (4V TP)
suggested_fix: None.

title: Heaters not driven: no damage, stock narrowband slow; EGR/VTCS/purge/EVAP left idle
claim: Open 3J/3P just leave the HO2S heaters off (no harm; front sensor unused because lambda comes from the on-board LSU). EGR stepper stays wherever it was left (rest position unverified: partly open would be an idle vacuum leak). VTCS shutter solenoid and purge undriven: slightly worse cold idle, canister never purged, no engine harm.
evidence: CHARM 2003 tables p2/p3/p6; README 'Not connected'
suggested_fix: Document; owners should check the EGR valve is closed.

title: Immobiliser: engine runs, security light will flash
claim: Unit and PCM are paired; the PCM enforces. With a standalone, AMP MSPNP says the dash fault indicator illuminates and/or flashes; owners report the engine runs. No source shows a fuel cut by the unit. Years: US 2001-05 per forum (2001 unverified). INSTALL says 'may flash'; evidence says it will.
evidence: AMP MM0105 page; MiataTurbo thread; CHARM 2002 immobiliser pages (R19)
suggested_fix: State 'will flash or stay lit; pull the bulb'; leave 3S open.

title: 4AF is the only B+ cavity and carries logic, heater, valves and AUX
claim: All current (logic 0.25 A, LSU heater 2.3 A rms cold/4 A peak, IAC and OCV up to about 1.9 A, AUX 1.1 A) enters through one stock cavity and wire; the backup cavity 4AG is unused. Terminal and wire rating not found.
evidence: interconnect.md 4AF net; VERIFICATION.md current table
suggested_fix: Check wire gauge and terminal rating of 4AF on a real NB2 harness.

title: OCV, IAC, MIL, tach, fuel pump, fan polarity and pins checked correct
claim: OCV: 4D +12 V supply, 4R low side with flyback to 4D; IAC: 2P +12 V, 2Q low side, two-wire duty valve (Haltech agrees); MIL, fans, fuel pump are low-side active-high drivers matching the stock low = on logic; tach 3O must stay open-collector (also feeds A/T IG-TCM). PWM frequencies stock unknown; rusEFI default 300 Hz.
evidence: CHARM 2003 p2/p4; Hellen yaml; wiki 2002/2003; Haltech NB2 page
suggested_fix: None.

title: OCV coil 6.9-7.9 ohm verified: 2 A hold PTC F3 has no margin
claim: The 2002 FSM gives the OCV coil as 6.9-7.9 ohm at 20 C, so peak current at 14.4 V is 1.8-2.1 A. F3 is a 2 A hold PTC that derates to about 1.45 A at 60 C and 0.8 A at 85 C. At high VVT duty in a hot cabin it can trip, and the valve then falls back to full retard (lost top-end torque, no damage).
evidence: charm.li 2002 'Oil Control Valve Inspection' image 757208362 (6.9-7.9 ohm at 20 C); derating table is from kb/parts/P16-ptc-fuses.md (datasheet C46641168), not re-read; 14.4/6.9=2.09 A; firmware auxPid maxValue 90 (miata_board.cpp:294). FSM OCV scope shows about 40 % high at idle.
suggested_fix: Use a higher-hold part for F3 (and check F2), or a larger-footprint PTC or 3 A fuse. Cap VVT duty or accept the trip as fail-safe; the A-audit's 7.5 ohm assumption is now confirmed as spec.

title: Tach 3O: stock swings 0-12 V; board is low-side only with no pull-up
claim: The stock 3O waveform runs from 0 V to about 12 V (6 div at 2 V/div) at 2 pulses per rev, and rusEFI's Proteus/Hellen pin maps list 3O as a HIGH-SIDE output. The board drives 3O with a ZXMS6004 low side and has no pull-up on the motherboard. If the cluster does not supply its own pull-up the tach stays at zero. Nobody has measured the unplugged-ECU level.
evidence: charm.li 2002 oscilloscope image 1009477327 (Y5J3940W122), 3O to 4A, 2 V/div; rusEFI Proteus-NB2 page ('3O Tach High-Side 1'); interconnect.md cur_mb0105: 3O=OUT_TACH->JD1.11 only; no tach pull-up documented for NB2 in VERIFICATION/INSTALL.
suggested_fix: Add a car test: key on with ECU unplugged, measure 3O (about 12 V means a pull-up exists, 0 V means the ECU must source). Pre-fit a DNP pull-up pad (about 1-4.7k to 4AF) or a high-side option.

title: Alternator 3M: stock signal is only about 1 V amplitude; the 1k-to-5 V pull-up plan is not supported
claim: On the stock NB2 the 3M waveform measures only about 1 V peak at 0.5 V/div and 160-250 Hz, and Haltech says the NB alternator needs a high-side duty signal. The repo's optional low side plus 1k pull-up to 5 V may therefore present a wrong level or polarity to the regulator. Control ships off and is gated by the M5 car check, which already covers this.
evidence: charm.li 2002 oscilloscope image 1009475312 (Y5J3940W121; amplitude and period read by eye); Haltech BP-Z3 page ('D Grey/Red Duty signal from ECU', Drive Type High); miata_board.cpp:231-239.
suggested_fix: At the M5 check scope the stock waveform on the car first; do not assume a 5 V pull-up is safe. Consider a high-side drive option.

title: FSM 2003-05 table puts TP on 4Y, but 4Y is not a cavity; repo 4V is right
claim: The 2003 FSM table lists 4V as not used and TP on 4Y, but 4Y is not drawn in the FSM connector figure (31 cavities counted without it). 2001/2002 FSM, rusEFI 2003-alt and the Proteus page all put TP on 4V. Treated as an FSM typo; the board's 4V is correct.
evidence: pv03_5.png row 4Y vs pv03_1.png connector No.4 drawing; pv02_5.png 4V TP 0.1-1.1/3.0-4.6 V; rusEFI Proteus table '4V TPS'.
suggested_fix: None. Do not 'fix' to 4Y.

title: 72-cavity set and names match the FSM exactly
claim: The repo's 72 harness pads equal the FSM connector drawings (No.2: 17, No.3: 24, No.4: 31); absent cavities 2L, 3G, 3R, 4G, 4Q, 4Y are correctly not populated.
evidence: Script set comparison of interconnect.md cur_mb0105 harness table vs FSM drawings pv02_1/pv03_1: 72 vs 72, empty difference both ways.
suggested_fix: None.

title: 2001-02 versus 2003-05 difference verified and the firmware split is right
claim: FSM: 2001-02 has CDCV 3E and FTP 4AB, 3H and 4S unused (key-switched main relay). 2003-05 has main relay control 3H, IG1 on 4S, and EVAP leak pump 3K/4AH. The firmware nb2Early preset (no mainRelay, no ignition sense) and the 2003-05 preset match. Running the wrong preset: a 2003 car on 'early' never closes the relay (4AF dead, car will not run); an early car on '2003-05' reads key-off on a floating 4S and cuts fuel/spark.
evidence: pv01_3/pv01_5, pv02_*, pv03_* images; miata_board.cpp:272-285; rusEFI 2002/2003 pages (Starting and power).
suggested_fix: Make the preset choice prominent in INSTALL; consider a hint when 4S reads 0 V on a 2003 preset.

title: Board powers up on 2003-05 via 4S and D8, then pulls 3H low
claim: On 2003-05, 4AF exists only after the ECU closes the main relay. The board wakes from 4S through D8 (cathode on +12V_IN), runs, pulls 3H low, and then 4AF supplies the load current. The chain works; the 4S wire (a few hundred mA of logic) is the only supply until then. Checked, correct (D8 40 V rating is a known issue).
evidence: FSM 2003 3H (B+ key off, <1 V key on), 4S (IG1), 4AF; design.py:204 D8; kb/parts/P15 line 23.
suggested_fix: None.

title: FSM scopes show IAC 2P and OCV 4D as switched pins; board feeds +12 and switches the other terminal
claim: The FSM probes 2P and 4D (the 'positive' terminals) and shows 0-12 V pulses, so the stock PCM switches those pins itself. The board puts +12 V on 2P/4D through PTCs and sinks 2Q/4R low side with a flyback diode, as the rusEFI Hellen and Proteus designs do. The FSM states the OCV terminals are interchangeable, so polarity is not an issue. No harness +12 source on those pins is documented. Checked, topology OK.
evidence: charm.li oscilloscope images 884439662 (IAC) and 737352891 (OCV); OCV inspection note; rusEFI 2003 page flyback text; interconnect.md 2P/2Q/4D/4R.
suggested_fix: None; a car check of 2P/4D with ECU unplugged would settle it.

title: Not implemented items and what the driver notices
claim: Not driven: charge lamp 3U (no key-on bulb check, no warning of alternator failure), HO2S heaters 3J/3P (narrowbands only work once the exhaust is hot; nothing is damaged), VTCS 2N (cold idle tumble effect lost), EGR, purge, EVAP pump (canister never purged, fails emission test), immobiliser 3S (security light flashes). PSP 4C, brake 4B and neutral 4H are not wired, so there is no idle-up when the steering is turned fully (INFERRED).
evidence: FSM tables for each cavity; AMP MM0105 page ('fault indicator on the dashboard will illuminate and/or flash'); MiataTurbo thread; interconnect.md no-net cavities; VERIFICATION.md:1122 (3U).
suggested_fix: Mostly documented. Add PSP (4C) idle-up as a cheap option since the input is a plain 12 V switch; state in INSTALL that the charge lamp stays dark.

title: Stock sensor ground 4O is shared with injector returns on the board
claim: The FSM keeps injector GND 3A, PCM GND 3B, device GND 4A and analogue sensor GND 4O as separate cavities; 4O carries the TP, ECT, IAT, EGR and both HO2S returns. The board ties all four to one GND net. Injector pulse currents on a shared plane can offset the sensor reference; magnitude depends on layout.
evidence: interconnect.md cur_mb0105 rows 3A/3B/4A/4O (same net); FSM 2003 4O 'GND, EGR boost sensor, TP sensor, ECT sensor, IAT sensor, HO2S'.
suggested_fix: Check the copper path of 4O to the daughterboard analogue ground; a star connection near JD2.2 would help.

title: VSS 3T: board pull-up to VBAT with 22k/10k divider is untested against the cluster output stage
claim: The stock VSS waveform is about 5 V high with a rounded rise (pull-up). The board pulls 3T up to VBAT_IN through 4.7k and divides by 22k/10k, so the pin sees 3.75 V when high. If the cluster output is push-pull 5 V rather than open collector, the pin would see only 1.56 V, below an STM32 VIH, and speed would read zero. Haltech's note ('Hall effect, pull-up disabled', 2780 pulse/km) suggests a self-supplied level.
evidence: charm.li osc image 621806829 (Y5J3940W123, 1 V/div); Haltech BP-Z3 page; design.py R20-R22; miata_pins.h:36.
suggested_fix: Measure the 3T high level with the ECU unplugged and key on.

title: Checked correct: injectors, fans, A/C, FP, MIL, IGT, CKP/CMP, TP, CLT, IAT, knock, A/C and clutch switches, power
claim: For each of these cavities the board net, circuit type (low side, 5 V push-pull ignition, pull-up switch input, analog 0-5 V, AC-coupled knock) and polarity agree with the FSM test conditions. The CLT/IAT 2.7k pull-up differs from the stock one (about 1.5-1.6k, inferred from FSM voltages) but firmware calibration handles it. No error found.
evidence: FSM pinout tables 2002/2003; interconnect.md 779-856; design.py:389-396, 485; miata_pins.h.
suggested_fix: None.

title: Immobiliser is in all FSM years 2001-2003; board leaves it unanswered
claim: The 2001, 2002 and 2003 FSM tables list 3S immobiliser serial communication, and the FSM service text treats PCM, immobiliser unit and key as a registered set. Standalone ECUs (AMP, Adaptronic) run the car and only the security light flashes (AMP and a MiataTurbo thread). Which US VINs have it is not proven. INSTALL.md:256 says the light may flash, which is consistent.
evidence: pv01/pv02/pv03 3S row; charm.li 'Antitheft and Alarm Systems: Service Precautions'; AMP MM0105 page.
suggested_fix: Optionally state that the car still starts; do not promise it without a test.

title: rusEFI NB2 knock pin 4K and the 2002 page 'VVT 4S' text are wrong; do not copy them
claim: rusEFI 2003-alt maps knock to 4K, but the FSM says knock is 4M and 4K is unused. The rusEFI 2002 page also writes 'VVT 4S' where the FSM and its own 2003 page say 4D. The repo uses 4M and 4D, which match the FSM.
evidence: pv02_4.png 4M, 4K row; rusEFI 2002/2003-alt pages saved in dl/.
suggested_fix: None.

title: 2T fuel pump output is not connected to anything on a 1991 ECU; pump is AFM-switch controlled
refs: 2T, OUT_FP, JD1.6, AFM connector pump contact (LT GRN / BLK)
claim: On the 1991 NA6 ECU pin 2T carries no wire. The pump runs from the circuit-opening relay, switched by the vane AFM fuel-pump contact and the starter signal, not by the ECU. README lists 2T as 'fuel pump relay' for 1989-95. If the vane AFM is removed (speed-density, the board's premise) the pump will not run unless the AFM-plug pump contact is bridged or rewired.
evidence: 1991 wiring diagram Fig. 2: CONN#2 T has no wire; AFM terminals A(LT GRN)/B(BLK) 'FUEL PUMP SW' go to the circuit opening relay; ST SIGN FUSE VIO. rusEFI 1990 table: 3T '*'. README table row 2T.
suggested_fix: Document in INSTALL/README that 1989-93 pump is not ECU-controlled; give a bypass instruction (relay or jumper) for AFM deletion; optionally a header to re-wire the circuit-opening relay to OUT_FP. Read 1990/1992/1993 diagrams to confirm 2T is empty all years.

title: 2I is an input from the igniter; repo choice (no ECU tach) confirmed, but ordered board wires tach driver straight to 2I
claim: FSM shows 2I (BLK-WHT) coming from igniter terminal E while the tach is fed directly from igniter terminal D (YEL-BLU). So 2I is an input and no ECU tach is needed. cur_mb8995 handles this with JP5 open. ord_mb8993 has OUT_TACH hard-wired to 2I with no jumper; it is safe only while the firmware leaves tachOutputPin unassigned (the ZXMS driver then stays off); any tune or firmware that enables the tach output would fight the igniter signal.
evidence: 1991 wiring diagram Fig. 2 (igniter D/E, CONN#2 I); interconnect.md ord_mb8993 row 2I = OUT_TACH JD1.11; miata_board.cpp miataNoTachOutput(); allpinouts.org disagrees (low quality). MRE wiki: tach pull-up only with stock coils.
suggested_fix: Ordered board: cut or lift the 2I connection to the tach driver or document 'tach output must stay none'. Close the repo's unresolved 2I item for 1991; check 1989/1990/1992/1993 diagrams.

title: 1989-93 fan relay is on 1R; 1L and 1M have no wire (README and firmware labels wrong for 1L/1M)
claim: On the 1991 ECU 1L and 1M are empty; the cooling fan relay is BLK-GRN on 1R (ECU grounds the coil). README calls 1L 'radiator fan relay' and 1M 'vehicle speed sensor' for 1989-93. The real fan output on these cars is the fan2/LS7 output on 1R (JP3 in 90-93 position); firmware fanPin (1L) drives nothing and there is no vehicle-speed signal. The stock thermoswitch still runs the fan independently, so no fan is lost.
evidence: 1991 wiring diagram Fig. 2 CONN#1 L, M empty, R BLK-GRN to COOLING FAN RELAY; rusEFI 1990 table 1L/1M N/C, 1R BLK/GRN; README harness table; rusEFI fan_control.cpp:264-266 (fan2 95 C).
suggested_fix: Fix README table (1L/1M unused on 1990-91; 1R is the fan relay); tell users to set the fan on fan2/LS7; confirm 1992-93 and 1989.

title: 1V clutch input reads constant 12 V on automatics; firmware assigns clutchDownPin on every year
claim: On M/T cars 1V is BRN-WHT to the clutch switch (to ground, shared with the cruise unit). On A/T cars the same pin is BLK-BLU from the ignition switch, i.e. 12 V with key on, so an automatic would read 'clutch down' permanently. On M/T the ground-switched line may need R22 (not fitted) if no pull-up is supplied by the cruise unit.
evidence: 1991 wiring diagram Fig. 2 bottom: '(M/T) BRN-WHT' to clutch switch, '(A/T) BLK-BLU' to IGN SW; miata_board.cpp:113 clutchDownPin = MIATA_SW3; MB R22 4.7k not fitted.
suggested_fix: Unassign clutchDownPin in the NA6 preset for automatics or document it; document R22 requirement for M/T.

title: Stock inputs left unconnected: PS pressure switch 1P, heater control 1S, stop lamp 1O, diagnosis connector 1K/1D/1F, 1A
claim: Seven stock ECU connections have no net on the board. Driver-visible effects: no idle-up for power-steering load or blower, no TEN self-test connector function, no hot-at-all-times supply (not needed). Only three 12 V switch inputs exist (VSS-slot, A/C, clutch).
evidence: 1991 wiring diagram Fig. 2: 1P BLU-YEL PS pressure SW, 1S BLU-ORG heater ctrl unit, 1O GRN stop lamp, diag conn LT GRN-YEL/WHT-GRN/WHT-YEL; interconnect.md harness table '(no net)'.
suggested_fix: Mention in INSTALL; optionally bring 1P/1S to spare inputs via jumpers; rely on rusEFI idle PID for PS load.

title: Purge solenoid on 2X is wired but never driven by the NA6 preset; no EGR wire exists
claim: 2X (YEL-RED, +12 V from main relay) goes to the purge valve; the preset leaves vvtPins unassigned so purge never opens (canister never purges; emissions/odour only). No EGR solenoid is on the 1991 ECU connectors.
evidence: 1991 wiring diagram Fig. 2 CONN#2 X to PURGE SOL VALVE; miata_board.cpp NA6 case; README firmware table 'none (VVT driver = purge, not driven)'.
suggested_fix: Optional: add a generic PWM/on-off purge output on OUT_VVT in the NA6 preset.

title: README: 2F labelled 'AFM ground' but stock 2F has no wire
claim: AFM and sensor grounds are BLK-LT GRN on 2C/2D; 2F is an unpopulated extra signal-ground pin. Tying 2F to GND is harmless.
evidence: 1991 wiring diagram CONN#2 F empty, C/D BLK-LT GRN; MRE wiki states 2F not populated on stock connector.
suggested_fix: Correct the README label.

title: Checked correct: 2U YEL = injectors 1&3, 2V YEL-BLK = injectors 2&4, 12 V on WHT-RED; 2Z is the A/T unit
claim: Paired injector wiring and the A/T control unit wire on 2Z match the board and firmware comments; JP2/R26 default open is safe. 1993 California sequential wiring (2Y/2Z injector assignment) is stated by AMP only and NOT verified.
evidence: 1991 wiring diagram Fig. 2 fuel injectors; AMP MM9093 install page; interconnect.md.
suggested_fix: None; read the 1993 California diagram before offering sequential on those cars.

title: Checked correct: power, starter, CEL, igniters, A/C relay, CAS, sensors, ISC, throttle contacts
claim: These cavities match the 1991 FSM wire functions and the rusEFI 1990 table. 1N RED is the idle contact on M/T and A/T (do not fit R28 on an automatic); 2L is the M/T full-throttle contact; 1C is the starter signal, not ignition-on; CAS is open collector with Vcc from the main relay.
evidence: 1991 wiring diagram Fig. 2 (CONN#1, CONN#2, igniter, CAS, throttle sensors); rusEFI 1990 table.
suggested_fix: None.

title: A/C request polarity (1Q) and ISC valve stock frequency/polarity cannot be verified from available sources
claim: 1Q is the A/C thermo switch line but whether it is 12 V or ground when the compressor is requested is not shown; R21 pull-up is not fitted, so a ground-switching signal reads constant low. ISC duty frequency defaults to rusEFI's 300 Hz, not a stock value.
evidence: 1991 wiring diagram shows only the bracketed switch; DEFAULT_SOLENOID_FREQUENCY 300 in generated header.
suggested_fix: Measure on a car (key on, A/C switch on) before shipping; add to install checklist.

title: 2I direction resolved: igniter output into ECU, tach not through ECU
claim: In the 1991 Mazda diagram ECU cavity 2I is BLK-WHT, wired to igniter pin E. Haltech's igniter table calls that pin IGf, an igniter-to-ECU signal. The tach wire YEL-BLU runs from igniter pin D to the cluster without passing through the ECU. This resolves the review brief's open item and matches the repo's current choice (JP5 open, no tach output).
evidence: Mazda 1991 wiring PDF p.4 (Fig. 2) crop work/PIN-8993-B-car-inward/pg/c1.png; Haltech NA6 89-93 igniter table; rusEFI MRE wiki JP55 'tach pullup'
suggested_fix: Record 2I as an input in the docs. Years other than 1991 are unchecked.

title: Ordered mb 0.11 wires OUT_TACH (low-side FET) directly to 2I
claim: The ordered board has no JP5 and no pull-up. The ZXMS6004 low-side drain sits on the igniter's output cavity. The NA6 preset unassigns tachOutputPin, so the FET stays off. If a different engine preset or a TunerStudio tach setting enables it, the FET pulls the igniter's confirm line low.
evidence: kb/interconnect.md ord_mb8993 '2I | OUT_TACH'; miata_board.cpp:95 sets tachOutputPin, 143-144 unassigns it for NA6
suggested_fix: Keep the tach output off in the shipped default for any year. Rev 0.13's JP5 already fixes this on the current board.

title: Fan: the only ECU fan wire in 1989-93 is 1R; 1L has no wire
claim: In the 1991 diagram 1R (BLK-GRN) is the cooling fan relay wire and 1L has no wire (S2 also lists 1L as N/C). The repo README says early cars use 1R and later cars use 1L, and calls 1L the 'radiator fan relay'. On the ordered board the 1R wire is driven by fan2Pin (rusEFI NA6 preset: on 95 C, off 91 C), and fanPin on 1L is unconnected. The stock thermoswitch also runs the fan, so there is no overheating hazard.
evidence: Mazda 1991 p.4 conn #1 lines A-H,J,K,N-S,U,V (no L); rusEFI 1990 wiki 1L N/C, 1R BLK/GRN; mazda_miata_1_6.cpp:284; miata_board.cpp:92-93
suggested_fix: State that on 1989-93 the fan is on 1R and its thresholds are the fan2 settings. Note that fan1 on 1L is unused.

title: M/T clutch/neutral input (1V) never changes level on delivered board
claim: In the diagram 1V (BRN-WHT) goes to the clutch and neutral switches, both to ground. R22 (12 V pull-up) is an unfitted option, so the input sits low in both switch states. On automatics 1V carries the ignition-switch 12 V (BLK-BLU), so it reads 'clutch down' permanently if the firmware polarity is active high. The firmware sets clutchDownPin = SW3 for all years.
evidence: Mazda 1991 p.4 bottom (M/T/A/T split on the 1V wire); fab self-order BOM R22 optional; miata_board.cpp:113
suggested_fix: For M/T fit R22 by default or document it. Unassign clutchDownPin on automatics.

title: Idle-up inputs not read: power steering 1P, brake 1O, heater 1S
claim: All three are inputs on the stock ECU and are unconnected on the board. Driver notice: RPM dip when turning the wheel at a stop and with heater/defrost load, recovered only by the closed-loop idle PID. 1M (VSS) carries no wire on 1989-93, so IN_SW1 is a free input.
evidence: Mazda 1991 p.4; kb/interconnect.md ord_mb8993 harness rows 1O, 1P, 1S '(no net)'; 1M IN_SW1
suggested_fix: On the next motherboard revision, route 1P to the free IN_SW1, with a firmware idle-up setting.

title: Diagnosis connector (1D, 1F, 1K) not connected
claim: S1 shows all three cavities wired to the diagnosis connector. The board leaves them open. There are no Mazda flash codes and no TEN-jumper base-timing check. Which of the three is TEN or FEN is not settled: rusEFI says 1K is TEN, and Mazda labels were not read.
evidence: Mazda 1991 p.4 (diag conn lines); rusEFI 1990 wiki 1K 'diag connector mode switch TEN'; interconnect.md rows 1D/1F/1K '(no net)'
suggested_fix: Document that base timing is set in rusEFI instead of with the TEN jumper. The cavities can stay open.

title: 1N is the throttle-switch RED wire: R28 must stay off (checked, correct)
claim: RED appears on both the M/T 3-wire switch and the A/T 4-wire TPS in the diagram, on 1N. It is a throttle contact, not a 5 V output. R28 (5 V onto 1N) is an unfitted option, so there is no short. The repo's warning against fitting R28 with the stock switch is right. The AMP MSPNP doc reuses 1N as 5 V only for an add-on TPS, consistent with this.
evidence: Mazda 1991 p.4 throttle sensor boxes; megasquirtpnp mm9093 TPS table; fab self-order BOM R28 note
suggested_fix: None. Optionally capture the 1N-vs-2L idle/full contact assignment with a meter, as README already says.

title: Injectors 2U/2V paired map matches the car (checked, correct)
refs: 2U YEL, 2V YEL-BLK, R23, R24, D3, D4
claim: S1 shows YEL feeding injectors 1&3 and YEL-BLK feeding 2&4, with WHT-RED supply on the other side. The board's 2U = INJ1 plus INJ4 via R23 and 2V = INJ2 plus INJ3 via R24, driven as one batch pair. R25/R26 for 2Y/2Z (93 California, individual wires per AMP docs) are optional and unfitted.
evidence: Mazda 1991 p.4 injector block; interconnect.md ord_mb8993 2U/2V/2Y/2Z; miata_board.cpp:304-322; AMP MSPNP doc table 2U/2V/2Y/2Z
suggested_fix: None. The 93 California wire-to-cylinder mapping rests on a secondary source (AMP docs), so check it on a real car.

title: Sensor inputs and 5 V reference match the car (checked, correct)
claim: Cavities 2K (5 V out), 2M (A/T TPS), 2N (O2), 2O (AFM VS), 2P (IAT), 2Q (CLT), 2E (CAS 4x white) and 2G (CAS 2x yellow/blue) have the same function and colour in S1, S2, S3 and S5. The board's pull-ups and dividers suit them: CLT/IAT 2.7k to 5 V, Hall 1k to 5 V, AFM 5.6k/10k divider.
evidence: Mazda 1991 p.4 crop c1/c2; Haltech trigger table; miata_pins.h; interconnect.md ord_mb8993
suggested_fix: None. The stock pull-up values are unverified.

title: 1A permanent +B and 1U/2H/2F cavities unconnected
claim: 1A (room fuse, always-hot) has no net, so there is no ECU memory backup, which rusEFI does not need. 2H (RED-WHT, California short connector) is open. The README says 2F is the AFM ground, but S1 shows no wire on 2F (the AFM grounds are 2C/2D); harmless because it is tied to GND anyway. 1U RED-BLK was not traced.
evidence: Mazda 1991 p.4; README row 2F; interconnect.md
suggested_fix: Correct the README note on 2F.

title: 2I tach: no pull-up with stock igniters (tach may be dead)
claim: FSM shows igniter BLK/WHT joined to the cluster tach and ECU 2I. MRE says the stock ECU supplies a pull-up on 2I. Both boards give 2I no pull-up in stock config (cur: R37 only behind open JP5; ord: OUT_TACH on a FET drain, no R37), so an open-collector igniter output would leave the tach dead. Not provable from FSM.
evidence: FSM 1994 p.16 igniter/tach crop (work/.../ign94.png); mre.txt lines 134, 370; interconnect.md ord_mb9495 2I=OUT_TACH, R37 absent
suggested_fix: Test tach on a stock car before first start; on ord board rework a pull-up (5 V per MRE) onto 2I; on cur board consider a pull-up not behind JP5.

title: ECU is sole radiator-fan control on 94-95; thresholds unverified
claim: Fan relay coil is fed from the ENGINE fuse and grounded only by ECU 1L; no thermoswitch. Preset turns radiator fan on at 100 C (off 96) and condenser fan at 95/91; stock values not found. Wrong/disabled fan config overheats the car.
evidence: FSM 1994 wiring p.10 Fig.5; rusEFI mazda_miata_1_6.cpp:282-285
suggested_fix: Document that fan must be verified in the tune; consider lower default (about 90-95 C) and a fail-on rule.

title: Fuel pump relay is ECU-switched on 94-95 (2T correct)
claim: 2T LT GRN goes to the fuel pump relay coil, so board OUT_FP and fuelPumpPin are right for this year; differs from 1990-93 where the ECU does not control the pump.
evidence: FSM 1994 p.16, 1995 p.8; firmware miata_board.cpp:90
suggested_fix: None.

title: EGR solenoids 1R/1T and EGR sensor 2J not connected
claim: 1994-95 ECU drives EGR vent and vacuum solenoids and reads an EGR function sensor; board connects none, so EGR never operates (emissions/knock margin; JP3 left on 90-93 would drive the EGR vent solenoid from OUT_LS7 on cur board).
evidence: FSM 1994 p.16/18 and tests_with_codes codes 16/28/29
suggested_fix: State in README; optional: route 1T/1R to spare low sides.

title: PRC solenoid 2R wired but never driven
claim: 2R is the pressure regulator control solenoid (YEL/GRN, +12 V WHT/RED); OUT_ALT drives it but NA94 preset leaves alternatorControlPin unassigned. Hot-restart fuel pressure boost (INFERRED purpose) is lost.
evidence: FSM 1994 p.18 bottom; tests_with_codes code 25; miata_board.cpp setOutputs()
suggested_fix: Document; optionally GPPWM/on-when-hot logic.

title: No idle-up inputs: PS 1P, blower 1S, defroster 2L
claim: Stock ECU sees power-steering switch (BLU/YEL), heater control (BLU/ORG) and defroster (BLU/RED) for idle-up; board connects only 2L to AUX1 with no firmware function, so parking/blower loads may sag or stall idle.
evidence: FSM 1994 p.16/18, p.2; interconnect.md 1P/1S no net
suggested_fix: Wire 1P/1S to spare inputs or use idle-up via AUX1 and CLT/IAC bump.

title: 1M VSS likely needs the R20 pull-up (not fitted by default)
claim: 1994 VSS is a 2-terminal sensor in the cluster (signal GRN/RED + ground) so likely passive; board input has no pull-up unless R20 is fitted; MRE lists a 94+ VSS pull-up as an option.
evidence: FSM 1994 p.18 cluster VSS; mre.txt JP56
suggested_fix: Test VSS on car; fit R20 if signal is open collector/switch.

title: Airflow meter not shown to be hot-wire; type unverified
claim: FSM calls it airflow meter (terminals B,E signal; C,D IAT); Mitchell box title says mass airflow sensor; five wires (12 V, signal, IAT, two grounds), no pump contact. Type and 2O voltage range not stated, so ADC scaling (5 V -> 3.2 V) is unverified; unused with speed-density preset.
evidence: FSM 1994 p.18 top, tests_with_codes code 8/10
suggested_fix: Measure 2O on a car before using it.

title: Charging is not ECU-controlled on 1994-95; 2R is not an alternator wire
claim: Generator regulator is fed WHT/GRN from the main relay; no ECU pin involved. Name OUT_ALT on 2R only reflects driver reuse.
evidence: FSM 1995 p.8 main relay crop (c95a.png)
suggested_fix: Rename/explain in README.

title: ORD board needs JP1 STOCK shunt for 2P IAT
claim: 2P goes only to JP1.1; without a shunt on 1-2 (STOCK) IN_IAT floats, default EXT reads the external connector.
evidence: interconnect.md ord_mb9495 2P=HARN_IAT, JP1
suggested_fix: Ship with shunt fitted and say so.

title: A/C request polarity and relay drive match the car
claim: 1J BLU/BLK sinks the A/C relay coil; 1Q is 12 V when switch/thermo/pressure switches close (open otherwise), matching the board's pull-down divider; R21 must stay unfitted.
evidence: FSM 1994 p.2
suggested_fix: None.

title: Pin map correct for all driven cavities; 94 vs 95 diffs cosmetic
claim: Colours and functions match across FSM 1994, FSM 1995 and rusEFI wiki; 1995 differs only by wire colours (1K, 1R, 2O) and generator feed. Federal vs California differences not found (one diagram per year).
evidence: FSM p.16 vs 95 p.8 crops
suggested_fix: None.

title: 2I (tach/IGf) has no pull-up and no input on either 94-95 board
claim: 2I is left floating on cur_mb8995 (JP5 open, R37 not fitted) and goes to MCU low-side Q14 with no pull-up on ord_mb9495; firmware assigns no tach output (miataNoTachOutput). If the 94-95 tachometer or igniter signal relies on an ECU pull-up on 2I, the needle reads zero and the ECU never sees IGf. Both 1991 diagram and README say the igniter drives the tach itself, so this is unresolved, not proven.
evidence: FSM 1994 code 01 step 2: tach not operating -> check wiring to PCME 2I. rusEFI MRE JP55 '2I tach pull-up' default Y on 94+ (stock coils), JP54 tach-out N. interconnect.md ord_mb9495 2I=OUT_TACH JD1.11. Hellen NA6 netlist 3I -> R48.
suggested_fix: On a stock 94-95 car measure 2I at key-on with the ECU unplugged and plugged: about 5 V means an ECU pull-up is needed. Then add a pull-up option (about 1 k to 5 V) on the ordered board by rework, and for 1995.5+ tach-out check.

title: EGR, purge and PRC solenoids and baro sensor of the stock ECU are not served
refs: 1R EGR vent, 1T EGR vacuum, 2J EGR sensor, 2X purge, 2R PRC
claim: The 94-95 ECU drives EGR vent (1R), EGR vacuum (1T), purge (2X, 25 ohm) and PRC (2R) solenoids and reads an EGR function sensor (2J) and an internal baro sensor. The board leaves 1R/1T/2J open, has no purge or PRC logic, and alternator PWM on 2R would chatter the PRC solenoid if enabled. Effect: no EGR/purge (emissions, fuel smell), possible hot-restart difficulty (PRC role from memory), no engine damage.
evidence: FSM 1994 codes 14, 16, 25, 26, 28, 29; vacuum schematic 94D45305; interconnect.md 1R/1T/2J no net; miata_pins.h MIATA_ALT comment.
suggested_fix: Document as known gaps; in firmware map 2X to purge and 2R to a PRC output (not alternator) for 94-95; warn not to enable alternator control on 94-95.

title: cur_mb8995 94-95 needs JP1/JP2 on SEQ and JP3 in 94-95 position
claim: Default shipped state is 1989-93 (JP1/JP2 open). A 94-95 car left that way has injectors 3 and 4 (2Y/2Z) undriven (two dead cylinders under the sequential preset); JP3 at 90-93 sends fan2 logic to 1R, which is the EGR vent solenoid on 94-95.
evidence: README jumper table; FSM code 29 (1R = EGR vent B); interconnect.md JP1/JP2 nets; miata_board.cpp NA94 preset sequential.
suggested_fix: Ship the 94-95 board pre-jumpered and label it; check at first power-up.

title: 1994 engine uses a hot-wire MAF; board input and ground arrangement checked
claim: Stock 94-95 has a hot-wire MAF: signal RED to 2O, return to 2F, 12 V from the car harness (WHT/RED). Board reads 2O on AUX3 through 5.6 k and ties 2F to GND. Consistent with the car; default tune is speed-density so the MAF is unused.
evidence: FSM code 08 (E->2F, B->2O); Haltech MAF connector pin table; AMP JP7 MAF select.
suggested_fix: None; note colour disagreement for 2F (FSM BLK/LT GRN vs rusEFI BLK/RED).

title: Hall inputs 2E/2G match the car's ECU pull-up
claim: FSM says about 5 V at 2E with the crank sensor unplugged; board pulls up 1 k to V5_EXT via a Schottky (about 4.7 V). Checked, matches.
evidence: FSM codes 2/3; design.py lines 433-445.
suggested_fix: None.

title: CLT/IAT bias 2.7 k and ISC/purge drivers match stock sensor and coil data
claim: FSM: CLT 14.6-17.8 k (-20 C), 2.2-2.7 k (20 C), 290-350 ohm (80 C); IAT 2.21-2.69 k at 20 C; ISC valve 12 +/- 1 ohm (about 1 A), purge 25 +/- 2 ohm. Board uses 2.7 k bias and low-side drivers with SS34 flyback on 2W/2X. Matches.
evidence: FSM codes 9, 10, 26, 34; footprints R33/R36 2.7k, D1/D2 SS34.
suggested_fix: None.

title: VSS 1M has no pull-up (R20 not fitted); level not confirmed
claim: The 94-95 VSS arrives as a hall-type signal from the speedometer; Haltech says pull-up disabled (driven), MRE lists a pull-up jumper 'untested'. If the signal is open-collector the board never sees it high. Only speed features affected.
evidence: Haltech BP-ZE KB; MRE JP56; README 'R20-R22 not fitted'.
suggested_fix: Scope the stock 1M on a car; keep R20 footprint.

title: Automatic 94-95 transmission lines 1I/1N/1V not served
claim: On automatics 1I, 1N, 1V connect to the transmission PCM and the ECU reads the park/neutral switch; board leaves 1I/1N open and treats 1V as a clutch input. Shift quality or limp mode possible. Repo already lists automatics as untested.
evidence: rusEFI 1994 table; FSM schematic 94D45305 (park/neutral switch AT).
suggested_fix: State manual-only support; R28 (5 V onto 1N) must stay unfitted.

title: rusEFI 1994 pinout table is unreliable on colours; 2L is an input
claim: rusEFI 94 table lists 2L as rear defroster relay, but the FSM schematic shows rear defroster switch as a PCME input; it repeats colours (2M/2P RED/BLK, 1E/1R YEL/BLK, 2Q/2S BLU/WHT). Use FSM first.
evidence: vacuum schematic 94D45305; r94.html.
suggested_fix: Do not copy rusEFI colours into docs without FSM check.

title: 1994 FSM wiring-diagram figures are blank; pin voltage charts missing
claim: mellens.net 1994 wiring.pdf has empty figure pages for the engine circuits, so ECU terminal voltages and the 94 tach wiring were not read; 94-95 differences (95 vs 94, Federal vs California, 1995.5 tach-out) rest on secondary sources.
evidence: pdfimages shows no images on pages 17-20; blank render.
suggested_fix: Obtain a 1995 FSM or measure a stock car.

title: Chain verified: all 36 connected 1996-97 cavities map to the right stock function
claim: Each connected cavity matches the 1997 factory ECM terminal list and at least two other sources (Hellen NA96, MSPNP MM9697, rusEFI wiki); the MB-to-daughterboard pin names match everywhere except the intended HTR_GND/GND.
evidence: 1997 Mitchell wiring PDF p.16/18 (mellens.net/mazda/Mazda-Miata-1997/wiring.pdf); kb/interconnect.md cur/ord_mb9697; hellenMiataNA96 main.yaml
suggested_fix: None; cite the FSM figure in README instead of 'no factory source'.

title: Repo/wiki wire colours for 96-97 are partly wrong
claim: FSM 1997: 4G YEL/BLU (wiki GRN), 4N BRN/YEL (GRN), 4U YEL (WHT), 4V YEL/BLK (YEL), 4E GRN/ORG and 4H GRN/BLK (wiki YEL/BLK, YEL/WHT); 3L is RED idle-switch signal, not ground.
evidence: 1997 wiring PDF p.16 left terminal list (crops work/PIN-9697-A-design-outward/img/c1-c3.png); research/pinouts_9605.md rows 3L,4E,4G,4H,4N,4U,4V
suggested_fix: Replace the colour column with the FSM colours; relabel 3L as idle switch.

title: 4I is battery backup B+ (resolved); leaving open is correct
claim: 4I BLU/RED traces to the ROOM fuse (10 A, hot at all times): keep-alive supply. Board leaves it open, so no keep-alive; rusEFI does not need it. Never drive it.
evidence: 1997 wiring PDF p.18 wire 29 to ROOM fuse; Hellen R48 +12V_PERM
suggested_fix: Update README 'still to verify' to resolved; keep open.

title: 4E/4H are the OBD-II crank-pulley VR sensor (GRN/ORG, GRN/BLK, shield)
claim: Left open by design; firmware triggers from the CAS (4F/4G). Consequence: no OBD-II misfire sensing, irrelevant to the board.
evidence: 1997 wiring PDF p.18 crankshaft position sensor, wires 25 and 28
suggested_fix: Doc update only.

title: Stock ECU functions silently absent: purge 4T, EGR 4O/4P, PRC 4J, rear heater 4Z
claim: The FSM shows low-side ECU outputs for purge (YEL/RED), EGR vent (YEL), EGR vacuum (YEL/WHT), PRC solenoid (YEL/GRN) and rear HO2S heater (VIO), plus EGR boost/position inputs 3H/3J; none connected. Purge and EGR stay de-energised (safe). PRC is new (README lists 4J as unknown): possible hot-restart effect is UNVERIFIED.
evidence: 1997 wiring PDF p.16 solenoids at bottom; motherboards/1996-97/README.md 'Not connected'
suggested_fix: Document 4T/4O/4P/4J/4Z functions and their consequence; optionally expose 4T purge and 4Z rear heater on spare drivers.

title: Input polarity for clutch 1L and VSS 1M cannot be verified; pull-ups R20-R22 not fitted
claim: FSM shows 1L BRN/WHT to clutch/neutral/cruise switches (A/T: TCM) and 1M GRN/RED VSS from the cluster-mounted sensor shared with TCM and cruise, but not whether they are 12 V-driven or ground/open-collector. If open-collector, no pulses without fitting R20/R22; effect: no VSS-based features, clutch never seen.
evidence: 1997 wiring PDF p.18/34; README 'Switch inputs'
suggested_fix: Measure on a car or ship R20-R22 fitted with a note; check 1M with a scope.

title: Cooling and condenser fan control confirmed ECU-only and configured
claim: 1A BLK/GRN radiator fan relay and 1B BLU/WHT condenser fan relay are ECU-sunk coils (coil +12 V from engine fuse); no thermo switch backup. rusEFI defaults 92/88 C and fan2 95/91 apply since setMazdaMiata96 does not override; AC relay mode on. The fans work, but a firmware or CLT fault is the only protection against overheating (CLT-broken turns fans on).
evidence: 1997 wiring PDF p.10 and p.2; fan_control.cpp:264-266; fan_control.cpp getState
suggested_fix: None; consider stating fan temps in the install guide.

title: Automatic cars: A/T lines 1R,1T,4Y,3L,1L and VSS undriven
claim: FSM marks 1R GRN, 1T GRN/BLU and 4Y BLU/YEL as A/T-only transmission lines (README names only 1R/1T); the TCM also reads TPS idle switch 3L and VSS. None are driven, so an A/T car will likely run the TCM degraded (UNVERIFIED).
evidence: 1997 wiring PDF p.16 'TRANSMISSION SYSTEM (A/T ONLY)'
suggested_fix: Add 4Y and 3L to the A/T warning; keep 'manual only' on the store page.

title: Minor driver-visible losses: no idle-up for power steering (3P), headlights (1H), A/C line 1P; brake 1Q unread
claim: 3P BLU/YEL is the PS pressure switch, 1H RED/BLK a headlamp 'system' signal, 1P BLU/ORG an A/C control unit line, 1Q GRN/BLK brake switch; all open, so idle can dip when parking or with lights on.
evidence: 1997 wiring PDF p.16/p.18/p.2
