suggested_fix: Optionally route 3P to a spare 12 V switch input for idle-up.

title: Ignition: stock coil packs have built-in igniters (3 wires); tach is ECU generated
claim: Each pack has BLK, BLK/WHT (+12 V run) and a signal wire (BRN/YEL, BRN); 4L BLK/WHT goes to cluster 1H. The board's 5 V logic IGN outputs and tach low side match this.
evidence: 1997 wiring PDF p.16 coils, p.34 cluster
suggested_fix: None.

title: Front O2 heater (3M) is a low-side return; heater +12 V comes from the engine fuse
claim: 3M RED/WHT is the front HO2S heater return, driven by OUT_VVT via o2heaterPin; heater feed is BLK/YEL from the fuse block, not the ECU. Heater current not measured (UNVERIFIED), the VND7NV04 limit should be checked against it.
evidence: 1997 wiring PDF p.18 HO2S connectors; miata_board.cpp:330-332; engine.cpp:170
suggested_fix: Confirm heater current vs driver limit.

title: Ordered rev 0.7: 3K IAT reaches the MCU only with JP1 shunt on STOCK
claim: On the ordered board 3K goes to JP1.1; default shunt position is EXT (J3), so the stock MAF-body IAT is unread until the shunt is moved to 1-2. Documented but easy to miss.
evidence: kb/interconnect.md ord_mb9697 3K row; README JP1 line 90
suggested_fix: Ship with JP1 on STOCK for a stock-sensor install.

title: Wiring facts: 3I 5 V feeds TPS/EGR sensors not MAF; 1O/4A both BLK/LT GRN ground
claim: FSM MAF has no 5 V wire; 3I feeds TPS, EGR boost and EGR position sensors. 3N BLK/YEL goes to the EGR boost sensor connector (function unresolved).
evidence: 1997 wiring PDF p.18
suggested_fix: Correct the README wording.

title: Crank/cam assignment confirmed independently
claim: Factory diagram shows a 4-terminal cam-driven sensor (WHT/RED 12 V, WHT, YEL/BLU, ground) and a separate crank-pulley sensor on 4E/4H. Board reads 4F (4-pulse) and 4G (2-pulse) with a 5 V pull-up, as the repo concluded. rusEFI wiki 'Cam' label on 4F is wrong.
evidence: Mazda 1996 ECM diagram sheet 2 (wiki.rusefi.com/Images/diagrams/1996_miata_1.8_2.png); miata_board.cpp setInputs; pinouts_9605.md:94-96; search snippet 4F=4/rev, 4G=2/rev (unverified)
suggested_fix: None. Optionally probe 4F/4G with a scope on the car to confirm pulse counts.

title: 4I is permanent +B (repo row says conflict)
claim: The factory diagram joins 4I BLU/RED (wire 29) to the room-fuse BLU/RED, which is hot at all times. The repo marks 4I conflict/low/never drive. Leaving it open is correct.
evidence: 1996 ECM diagram sheet 2 wires 29 and room fuse; pinouts_9605.md:97
suggested_fix: Update the research table: 4I = keep-alive +B, never drive.

title: 3L is TPS idle switch, not signal ground
claim: Research table says 3L 'ground, probably MAF signal ground'. The diagram runs 3L RED to the TPS fourth (idle switch) terminal and to the A/T transmission system. Unconnected on the board, so harmless.
evidence: 1996 ECM diagram sheet 1 (3L RED, wire 19) and sheet 2 (TPS, trans); pinouts_9605.md:84
suggested_fix: Correct the doc. Optionally expose 3L as an idle-switch input.

title: 1D and 1I are diagnostic FEN / TEN lines
claim: 1D WHT/BLK goes to the DLC and DLC-2 (K-line/FEN) and 1I LT GRN/YEL goes to the DLC TEN terminal. Both are open on the board: no scan-tool link or self-test mode, no damage. The DLC fuel-pump jumper (LT GRN) shares the 1U net, so it still works.
evidence: 1996 ECM diagram wires 1, 3, 8 and the DLC boxes on sheet 2
suggested_fix: Document that OBD-II scanners will show no link; do not drive 1D.

title: EGR, purge and PRC solenoids and EGR sensors not served
claim: 4J YEL/GRN is the PRC solenoid, 4O/4P the EGR vent/vacuum solenoids, 4T the purge solenoid; 3H/3N/3J are the EGR boost and valve-position sensors. All cavities are open. EGR and purge stay closed. If the PRC solenoid boosts fuel pressure for hot restart (role unverified) hot restarts may be slow.
evidence: 1996 ECM diagram sheet 1 bottom and sheet 2; interconnect.md:374-452 (no net on these pads)
suggested_fix: State the loss in the README. An optional low-side output on 4T or 4J could be offered on the aux header.

title: 1B/1G/1P function unresolved (A/C system)
claim: The Mazda diagram labels 1B, 1G, 1K and 1P all 'A/C system' with no direction. The board drives 1B as fan 2 (firmware fan2Pin) and 1G as A/C relay, based on the rusEFI wiki and Hellen. 1P is left open. If 1B is really an A/C-compressor control, the fan2 logic would engage it. If 1P is an ECM A/C output, A/C may not engage.
evidence: 1996 ECM diagram sheet 1 rows 1B/1G/1K/1P; miata_board.cpp:93; pinouts_9605.md:40,45,54
suggested_fix: On a real 96-97 car, check A/C and fan behaviour with the A/C on and off, and probe 1B, 1G and 1P before shipping; keep fan2 disabled by default.

title: Load idle-up inputs not wired (headlights, defogger, power steering, brake, start)
claim: The stock ECM reads headlight (1H), defogger (1J), start (1C), brake (1Q) and power-steering pressure (3P) lines. None are connected. Expect a small idle dip when those loads switch on, since only the closed-loop idle PID reacts.
evidence: 1996 ECM diagram; interconnect.md:374-452 shows no net on these pads
suggested_fix: Optional: wire 1H/1J/3P as extra 12 V-sense inputs on spare daughterboard pins, or document the dip.

title: Automatic transmission lines not connected
claim: 1R GRN, 1T GRN/BLU and 4Y BLU/YEL are PCM-to-TCM lines (content unverified) and are open. 1L carries an A/T signal that the board reads as a clutch switch. On automatics, shift quality or limp mode may be affected. Repo already says automatics untested.
evidence: 1996 ECM diagram sheet 1 ('Transmission system, A/T only'); interconnect.md:374-452
suggested_fix: Keep the manual-only claim in the store text; disable the clutch input on automatics.

title: Both HO2S: front heater driven on 3M, rear heater not ECM-controlled
claim: Front HO2S: signal 3C, heater control 3M (low side, heater fed from ignition-switched BLK/YEL). Rear HO2S: signal 3D, heater wired to chassis, so no ECM drive. The board's 3M drive matches. The repo research claim that 4Z drives a rear heater comes only from Hellen and is not in the factory diagram.
evidence: 1996 ECM diagram sheet 2 HO2S boxes; miata_board.cpp:330-332; pinouts_9605.md:114
suggested_fix: None. Note the terminal-role reading (heater vs sensor terminals) is inferred from the sensor symbols.

title: Ignition: coil packs have built-in igniter, no IGf line
claim: Each of the two coil packs has 3 wires: BLK ground, BLU +12 V ignition, and the ECM input (4N BRN/YEL, 4R BRN). There is no ignition-confirm line, so the board needs no feedback input. The 5 V logic drive matches Hellen's, but the igniter input threshold is unverified. The rusEFI wiki colour GRN for 4N disagrees with the diagram.
evidence: 1996 ECM diagram sheet 1 ignition coils
suggested_fix: Verify spark on the first car with a scope on 4N.

title: No immobiliser and main relay is ignition-switched
claim: The diagram shows no immobiliser or transponder line, and the 12-pin connector 2 is unused. The main relay coil is fed from the ignition-switch engine fuse with no ECM pin, so there is no after-run power hold.
evidence: 1996 ECM diagram sheet 1 relay area
suggested_fix: None.

title: Board merges signal ground and power grounds into one net
claim: Factory splits ECM signal ground (1O, 4A BLK/LT GRN) and sensor return (3O BLK/BLU) from power grounds (4C/4D BLK). The board has one GND net for all five. Injector and fan return current shifts the sensor reference by an estimated 10 mV at 1 A and 10 mOhm, about 2 LSB on the 12-bit ADC at 3.3 V (x1.56 divider, so about 8 LSB). Minor.
evidence: interconnect.md:374-452 (all five on GND); 1996 ECM diagram
suggested_fix: Ensure the sensor-ground pours reach the daughterboard through a separate path, or note only.

title: Other-source pinout errors to avoid
claim: The AMP MSPNP2 MM9697 page copies 94-95 jumper text (J4 pin 4S, J6 tach on 4I) that does not match the 96-97 diagram. The rusEFI wiki has 4F labelled 'Cam', 4N colour GRN, 4U/4V colours WHT/YEL; the diagram says WHT 4-pulse signal, BRN/YEL, YEL and YEL/BLK. Do not copy colours from the wiki into the install guide.
evidence: dl/amp2.txt lines 353-363; wiki table; 1996 ECM diagram
suggested_fix: Use the diagram colours or omit colours in INSTALL.md.

title: Single cavity 4B carries board logic plus wideband heater supply
claim: Stock ECM draws well under 1 A through 4B. The board adds the wideband heater (F1 3 A hold) and AUX 1.1 A on the same cavity. Cavity and wire rating are unverified.
evidence: interconnect.md 4B row: D1 F1 F4 JD1.1 JD1.2; the car feeds injectors and solenoids from the same WHT/RED rail
suggested_fix: Check the harness terminal rating and wire gauge; log 4B current on the first wideband warm-up.

title: Charge lamp (1Q) never driven; alternator sense 1T and field 1O loop open
claim: Four sources say stock 1Q is the ECU low-side charge/battery lamp output and Haltech shows the alternator has P (feedback to ECU) and D (duty from ECU) wires. The board leaves 1Q and 1T unconnected and ships alternator control off. The dash charge lamp never lights, even at key-on bulb check, so a charging failure goes unnoticed. Whether the alternator charges normally with the ECU loop open is not verified; one forum thread reports a no-charge case.
evidence: interconnect.md cur_mb9900 1Q/1T no net; wiki Mazda-Miata-1999 1Q; MSPNP 'Charge Lamp 1Q, Alternator Sense 1T'; Haltech NB1 page alternator P/D; miataturbo thread 89391 (unverified)
suggested_fix: Route a spare low side (e.g. J5-3 OUT_BOOST, on ordered boards also) to 1Q by wire and drive it via GPPWM/Lua. State the charging consequence in the README. Test the alternator with 1O/1T open on a real car before shipping.

title: A/C condenser fan 1I not commanded with A/C (fan2AcMode never set)
claim: 1I is the A/C fan relay per wiki, Hellen, MSPNP and Alex. The NB1 preset sets only fan1AcMode=Relay (radiator fan follows A/C). fan2AcMode keeps rusEFI's default Disabled, so the 1I fan runs only above 95 C, not when the A/C is switched on.
evidence: repo/firmware/board/miata_board.cpp:228 (only fan1AcMode set); rusEFI fan_control.cpp:289 default fan2AcMode Disabled, :266 fan2OnTemperature 95
suggested_fix: Set engineConfiguration->fan2AcMode = fan_ac_mode_e::Relay in setMiataNb1 (and check how stock behaves). Confirm what 1I switches on a real car.

title: VICS solenoid 3Q never driven (no strategy)
claim: Haltech says the NB1 VICS solenoid is energised below about 5200 rpm. Here the 3Q driver exists but firmware has no function on it (mainRelayPin Unassigned for NB1), so the intake runs in a fixed VICS state and loses the stock switching. The comment in the code leaves it to the user.
evidence: miata_board.cpp:269 comment; Haltech NB1 article; wiring OK in interconnect.md
suggested_fix: Ship a default GPPWM/Lua rule: energise 3Q below 5200 rpm, as stock.

title: Ordered mb9900: JP1 default EXT leaves stock IAT sensor unread
claim: On the ordered board 2B goes to JP1.1 only; the README default shunt is on 2-3 (EXT, J3). On a car with only the stock airbox IAT, J3 is empty, the input floats to the 2.7k pull-up (about 4.3 V), and IAT reads extremely cold unless the shunt is moved to 1-2.
evidence: interconnect.md ord_mb9900 2B -> JP1.1; ordered README line 92
suggested_fix: Fit the shunt on 1-2 (STOCK) for 1999-2000 by default; say so in INSTALL.

title: A/C request input 1P: level and polarity not established, no pull-up
claim: No source gives the electrical character of 1P (12 V active, or open collector to ground). Firmware does not set acSwitch polarity or pull; the R21 pull-up is not fitted. If the stock A/C amplifier switches to ground, the A/C request is never seen.
evidence: miata_board.cpp (no acSwitchMode/invert); MSPNP, Hellen, Alex give function only
suggested_fix: Probe 1P on a car (key on, A/C button) before shipping; document the R21 option or set polarity.

title: No scan-tool, EVAP, EGR, purge or rear-heater function on NB1
claim: These cavities are open. No OBD/diagnostic link, no purge, no EGR, rear HO2S unheated, no PS idle-up. Emissions-inspection-visible and emissions-only for the driver; the repo already lists most of these.
evidence: interconnect.md cur_mb9900 NC list; README 'Still to verify'
suggested_fix: Consider a PS-switch idle-up input (1G).

title: IAC valve polarity 3M control / 3O +12 V: checked, correct
claim: The rusEFI wiki swaps 3M and 3O; Hellen, MSPNP Pro, Alex and Haltech's valve description (pin 1 signal, pin 2 12 V switched) agree with the repo. A wrong assignment would short a +12 V wire to ground through the driver, so it deserves a bench check with the stock plug before first power.
evidence: wiki 1999 page vs MSPNP 4M/4O, Alex IACV 3M, Hellen main.yaml 3M OUT_IDLE
suggested_fix: Meter the stock harness 3M/3O to the IAC connector with the key on.

title: 76P header footprint and cavity-letter positions match Hellen's footprint: checked, correct
claim: The 42 column positions and pitches equal Hellen's P2 178780-1; 20 cavities were compared against Hellen's netlist and all fall at the same positions. XA-XL are correctly open.
evidence: ext/hellen-miata-NB1/hellen64_NB1.kicad_pcb P2; evidence/cur_mb9900/pcb_pads.csv; work/PIN-9900-A-design-outward/hp3.py
suggested_fix: None.

title: IAC PWM at rusEFI default 300 Hz; stock frequency unknown
claim: No NB1 preset value for idle.solenoidFrequency; rusEFI default is used. The stock valve frequency is not documented in any source read.
evidence: rusefi_generated_*.h DEFAULT_SOLENOID_FREQUENCY 300; miata_board.cpp has no override
suggested_fix: Measure stock ECU 3M frequency or let the valve be tuned in the first startup.

title: Tach 2K: one source says stock unused
claim: Wiki, Hellen and MSPNP Pro give 2K as tach out; Alex says 'stock unused pin'. Level required by the cluster is not documented. Already listed in the repo's open items.
evidence: Alex manual p.18-19; wiki 1999
suggested_fix: Check the cluster tach input on a car.

title: Charge warning lamp never works (1Q open)
claim: Factory charge lamp is fed from IG and sunk by PCM 1Q (BR/R); the board leaves 1Q (and 1T feedback) unconnected, so the lamp never lights at key-on or on charging failure. The repo lists it as not driven but not the consequence: no warning of a flat or failed charging system.
evidence: Mazda 2000 wiring diagram pdf p.33 (Z-30 cluster: CHARGE lamp, BR/R to C-01 3B) and p.25; interconnect.md cur_mb9900 1Q/1T no net; VERIFICATION.md:1122
suggested_fix: Add a low-side lamp output on 1Q (spare ZXMS6004 channel or small FET) and a firmware charge-fail lamp rule, or warn the buyer in INSTALL.

title: Clutch switch (3I) is switched to ground; R22 not fitted
claim: Mazda diagram shows 3I BR/W going to the clutch switch (B1-21) whose other terminal is a B (ground) wire, so the input is a switch to ground. The 1999-2000 README says these inputs are 12 V driven and ships R22 unfitted, so the input floats and the clutch is not read unless R22 is fitted.
evidence: Mazda 2000 wiring pdf p.25 (B-1c: clutch switch B1-21, BR/W and B(E)); motherboards/1999-2000/README.md:130; parts_list R22 'NOT FITTED'
suggested_fix: Fit R22 by default on 1999-2000 (and tell the buyer); keep R21 (A/C) unfitted. Check polarity (clutchDownPin inverted?) in firmware.

title: VICS solenoid left de-energised: probable permanent high-rpm runner state
claim: 3Q is wired (verified W/L VICS valve B1-10, low side) but NB1 firmware sets no output; README says only 'not set up'. A forum report (unverified) says the stock solenoid is energised below about 5200 rpm and springs open above it, so a never-energised valve would leave VICS in the high-rpm state at all speeds, costing low and mid torque. No damage.
evidence: Mazda 2000 wiring pdf p.23 (VICS solenoid B1-10, 3Q W/L); search summary of mazdas247 forum (unopened); README.md:103; miata_board.cpp:269
suggested_fix: Confirm polarity and switchover rpm on a car or in the Mazda manual, then add a default GPPWM / rpm-switch rule for 3Q.

title: rusEFI wiki 1999 swaps 3M/3O, and Australian list moves fuel pump to 3P
claim: Primary diagram: 3M (orange) is IAC control and 3O (V/R) is +B for the IAC coil; the board is wired that way. The rusEFI wiki says the opposite; the Australian list puts the fuel pump relay on 3P (market difference). The board matches the US diagram.
evidence: Mazda 2000 wiring pdf p.25 B-1c (IAC B1-24 O on 3M, V/R on 3O; fuel pump LG on 3N); wiki.rusefi.com/Mazda-Miata-1999; Bartune NB8A; interconnect.md cur_mb9900 3M/3N/3O
suggested_fix: None for the board; do not take the wiki table at face value in docs.

title: Sensor grounds 3C and 3F tied to power ground
claim: Factory has separate sensor grounds (3C, 3F: TPS, CLT, IAT, knock return) apart from power grounds 3A/3B; the motherboard merges all five on one GND net, so injector and IAC return currents share the sensor return path.
evidence: interconnect.md cur_mb9900 3A/3B/3C/3F nets identical; Mazda pdf p.21/23 PCM box
suggested_fix: Check the single-point ground layout in the layout review; probably acceptable but worth a measurement of sensor-ground noise.

title: Features absent without harm: EGR, purge, CDCV, FTP, PS switch, neutral
claim: All unconnected: EGR valve stays closed (more NOx), purge valve closed (canister saturates, vapour smell), PS switch ignored (small idle dip when steering), neutral ignored. No engine damage expected.
evidence: interconnect.md cur_mb9900 nets; Mazda pdf p.21/23/25
suggested_fix: Document in INSTALL; optional purge output on spare channel.

title: Header 76-pos vs car 64-pos: consistent
claim: Car plugs are 22+16+26=64 positions; XA-XL (12) are an unconnected bay on the 76P header; ordered board uses 64P 176122-6. Checked, no mismatch found.
evidence: Mazda pdf p.21 B1-01 PCM box; motherboards/1999-2000/README.md:48; ext/hellen-miata-NB1 symbol pins 1-76
suggested_fix: None.

title: 1P is an active-high 12 V A/C request line shared with the condenser fan feed
claim: 1P joins the A/C amplifier output (through the refrigerant pressure switch), the condenser fan motor and the fan relay contact. R21 correctly not fitted; with no request the line sits near ground via the fan winding. Cluster VSS (2D) output type is unresolved.
evidence: Mazda pdf p.49 (Z-46 G section) and p.25
suggested_fix: Verify on the car that 2D idles low/high as expected before choosing R20.

title: Doc claim 'nobody uses suffix-7 STM32' is wrong
claim: rusEFI Hellen64 NB1 (rev a-c) and NA8-96 BOMs fit STM32F407ZGT7 (-40..105 C, JLC C1337111, ext., stock 34, USD 27.80@1). Also NA6 rev C used F407IGT6 and uaEFI F3 uses F407VGT6; only NA6 rev D is ZGT6.
evidence: ext/hellen-miata-NB1/bom_replace_64_NB1-c.csv U105; NA8 bom raw github; tools/lcsc.py C1337111
suggested_fix: Correct the doc; consider F407VGT7 only if the price delta is small (it is ~USD 27.8 here).

title: Miata Hellen boards fit ZXMS6005SGTA, not AUIPS2041L
claim: output module 0.3 default is AUIPS2041LTR, but all rusEFI Miata board BOMs replace Q305-312 with ZXMS6005SGTA (SOT-223, 60 V, USD 1.17@1/0.74@100, JLC ext. stock 18); AUIPS2041LTR is stock 0 at JLC. The doc's 1.4 A remark concerns a part not fitted.
evidence: ext/hellen-miata-NA6/bom_replace_hellen64_NA6_94-d.csv, NB1-c, NB2-f; ext/hellen-one/modules/output/0.3/output-BOM.csv; lcsc.py C174042/C113610
suggested_fix: Update the doc; the substitution reason (JLC availability) is inferred from early revs listing the drivers as non-JLC.

title: uaEFI MCU stated stale in doc
claim: uaEFI rev F3 bom_replace replaces the module default STM32F429VIT6 with STM32F407VGT6 ('very cheap'), the same MCU as this project; PRO uses F7.
evidence: github rusefi/uaefi bom_replace_uaefi-f3.csv; wiki uaEFI page
suggested_fix: Fix the table row.

title: uaEFI added series resistors on driver inputs after injector driver failures
claim: rusEFI uaEFI rev F (July 2026) added series resistors to protect the MCU after reports of failed injector drivers; maintainer cites the driver datasheet section 3.1. Independent confirmation that the 220 ohm resistors missing on the ordered rev 0.9 daughterboard matter; rework before first power-up is justified.
evidence: uaefi changelog.md rev F; uaefi issues #112, #114; mck1117/proteus#125
suggested_fix: Fit 150-220 ohm series resistors by hand on the ordered rev 0.9 board (documented omission, but now with field precedent).

title: Alternator/tach TC4427 outputs killed MCU pins in the field
claim: In Nov 2021 an NB2 and a Frankenso/NB1 lost MCU pins behind the 12 V TC4427 (8-10 ohm to ground, 2-20 ohm to 3.3 V). Fix: 100 ohm series + Schottky (output-0.3); NB1 also needed R23 1k removed for alternator charging (17-18 V ramps); OEM Miata alternator wire uses 1k + 100 nF. This project already has 100 ohm + B5819W; alternator ships off, which is prudent.
evidence: hellen-NB1-issues #25,#29,#30; hellen-NB2-issues #23,#31; hellen-one#118; rusefi#3558
suggested_fix: Keep alternator output off by default; when enabling, consider the OEM 1k+100nF network; document NB alternator wire behaviour.

title: Unprotected 5 V sensor outputs bricked a Hellen NA6
claim: H64b was bricked on install (TPS 5 V pin suspected shorted); no protection existed on any +5 V output; rusEFI fitted TLS115D0 tracking regulators on all boards (NA6 rev C onward). This project's second TLS115 matches the fix; polyfuse alone was judged insufficient by rusEFI.
evidence: hellenNA6_issues #22,#21; hellen-one#119; hellen-NB1-issues #32
suggested_fix: None; checked-and-consistent. Keep the TLS115.

title: rusEFI does not stock Miata plug-in boards
claim: rusEFI states it does not fabricate or stock Miata NA/NB boards (bulk orders only); NB2 and NA96 are 'somewhat abandoned'; shop offers uaEFI (USD 275 base, +50 enclosure, +40 crimp kit, +100 pigtails/WBO cable, ships from NJ) and a uaEFI NA6 adapter 'definitely has issues'.
evidence: wiki.rusefi.com Miata page; shop.rusefi.com pages fetched 2026-11-16
suggested_fix: Position USD 399 assembled plug-in against uaEFI ~USD 465 all-in universal; no direct plug-in competitor from rusEFI.

title: Cheaper injector stage in rusEFI: 1 SOT-223 per channel, no external clamp
claim: rusEFI Miata boards use ZXMS6005SGTA (USD 0.74@100) with only the in-chip clamp, on 2-layer boards; this project spends VND7NV04 + ES1D + 1.5SMC16A per injector plus 6 layers for thermal margin. Potential savings exist if 20 mH heating is acceptable, but rusEFI's field data for ZXMS6005 is not documented in issues and its datasheet clamp/current limits were not read.
evidence: NA6 bom_replace; lcsc.py prices; repo/daughterboard/README.md lines 13-16, 69-73
suggested_fix: Cross-check with R08 (low-side driver landscape) before dropping any parts.

title: Hellen modules use 2 layers and 24 V polyfuse + SMCJ30A input
claim: rusEFI input protection is polyfuse SMD1206P050TF/24 (0.5 A, 24 V), SMCJ30A, P-FET reverse switch gated by PSM712 7V/12V TVS, 6.8 V TVS on 5 V; 24 V rating is the same class as this project's documented PTC voltage limit.
evidence: ext/hellen-one/modules/power12/0.2/power12-BOM.csv; output_0.3 schematic crop
suggested_fix: None.

title: JLC stock churn forces rusEFI to substitute parts repeatedly
claim: Repeated shortage tickets (74HC2G17GW, RZ7899, 176-pin MCU, AUIPS2041 stock 0) and VND7NV04 (C155605, this project's driver) proposed as heater FET; keep second-source parts for each critical LCSC code.
suggested_fix: Maintain alternates list per BOM line.

title: Digital drive threshold issue with VNLD5160 at 3.3 V
claim: Proteus issue notes VNLD5160 input threshold up to 3.5 V is unreachable from 3.3 V GPIO; this project drives VND7NV04 via 5 V level shifter (per README), which sidesteps it. Not checked for VND7NV04 thresholds.
evidence: mck1117/proteus#125; repo/daughterboard/README.md line 175
suggested_fix: Confirm VND7NV04 VIH against 5 V buffer VOH in the driver reviewer's pass.

title: R110 pump-current shunt is a 0.62 ohm part (C25341), not 62 ohm
claim: R110 is the 62 ohm pump-current sense resistor across LSU_RT and LSU_IP, but its LCSC code C25341 (1206W4F620LT5E) is listed as 620 mOhm by both JLC and LCSC. The 62 ohm part of the same family is C17971 (620J). With 0.62 ohm the pump-current gain is about 1/100 of nominal, so lambda would stay near 1 and the wideband would not work.
evidence: tools/lcsc.py C25341 run 2026-11-16: 'Resistance 620mΩ'; ordered BOM miata-ecu-daughterboard-rev0.9_jlcpcb_bom.csv:76; design.py:64; C17971 listed as 62Ω 1206 1% in stock; R109/R108 use the same family with 'J' codes (100J=10Ω, 470J=47Ω)
suggested_fix: Hand-replace R110 on the ordered rev 0.9 board with C17971 (or a 61.9 ohm 1% 1206 part) before power-up; fix the part map in design.py and wideband.py and the current design BOM.

title: Pinned wideband firmware lacks upstream fixes
claim: The pinned wideband 27e115b (branch prod-2026-01) does not contain upstream commits 9295698 (avoid heating when battery voltage is low, 2026-04-10) and 91aa7c6 (ignore firmware-update request without ID). Issue #348 (stuck underheat after 12 V loss) was filed after the pin.
evidence: work/R02.../master_not_in_pinned_log.txt (41 commits not in the pin); github issue 348 via API
suggested_fix: Cherry-pick or bump the wideband submodule after a diff review, rebuild miata_wbo_f103.bin, and re-run the bench test.

title: Trim resistor is not read by firmware; there is no free-air calibration
claim: The firmware uses a fixed 61.9 ohm shunt constant, and a grep for trim/rcal finds nothing. The Bosch trim resistor (30-300 ohm, between IP and RT in the sensor plug) acts only through the analog sense path. The exact electrical interaction with the on-board shunt was not resolved from the Bosch drawing.
evidence: firmware grep; Bosch techinfo txt lines 61-80; FOME wiki Wideband-Module.md ('laser-trimmed resistor between pins 1 and 5')
suggested_fix: Test with the real sensor and a reference meter (bench step 5-6). Tell customers the sensor and its plug are a matched pair and the pigtail needs no resistor.

title: No independent accuracy validation of the FOME/rusEFI wideband exists
claim: The only documented accuracy is Bosch's sensor figure (+-0.007 at lambda 1, +-0.01 at 0.8, +-0.05 at 1.7). Firmware author comments claim 0.5% fit to the Bosch table. Forum validation was free air and a lighter flame only. No bottled-gas or side-by-side comparison was found.
evidence: Bosch ds lines 74-76 (kb/research/files/R15); lambda_conversion.cpp comments; forum t=1856 p.6 summary
suggested_fix: Run the bench plan in the notes, section 10, on the first boards and publish the results.

title: Field failure modes of the module are mostly heater/supply and assembly related
claim: Open or unresolved: 65 s to detect a missing sensor (295), lean blip at start (303), unprotected inputs (a heater wire on Vm destroyed an F042) (309), and ten JLC-built rev B boards reading 1.01 in free air with zero pump current (forum, cause unknown, resembles a shunt or pump-driver assembly error).
evidence: GitHub issues via API 2026-11-16; rusefi.com/forum/viewtopic.php?p=49394
suggested_fix: Keep the sacrificial resistors; check the pump driver and shunt on the first board; add the miswire tests (heater to Vm, battery to Ip) to the bench list.

title: Heater strategy and supply-voltage sensing
claim: Heater: 2 V preheat for 5 s, ramp from 7 V (9 V if hot) at 0.4 V/s, closed loop on ESR around 7.5 V, duty (Veff/Vsupply)^2. Start above 9.5 V for 0.5 s, stop below 8.5 V, hard cut at 23 V or more. Faults: no heat in 60 s, 100 C over or under target for 0.5 s. This project senses supply on its own R120/R121 divider (BOARD_HAS_VOLTAGE_SENSE).
evidence: heater_control.cpp; wideband_config.h:34-55; miata_f1/wideband_board_config.h
suggested_fix: None; the 8.5 V cut-off means cranking dips pause heating, which is acceptable.

title: Firmware update path: upstream CAN bootloader vs this project's bootloader-less image
claim: Upstream controllers carry OpenBLT and are updated over CAN by the ECU (WB_BL_ENTER, then image stream). First programming is by SWD or DFU. This project's image has no bootloader and is written from the F407 ('Flash on-board wideband'). The mechanism was not verified here (WB_BOOT0 net appears to link U1 and U102).
evidence: fome-fw rusefi_wideband.cpp (GitHub raw); repo/firmware/wideband/README.md; evidence pcb_nets WB_BOOT0
suggested_fix: Bench-verify the flash path on the first board and document recovery if the image is bad.

title: Competitor price field and open alternatives
claim: All are closed, Bosch LSU 4.9 based. AEM X-Series gauge about $200-231, Innovate LC-2 $145 controller or $170-250 kit, Spartan 3 Lite V2 about $82-135 and V2 $139 (discontinued per a retailer). Open: OWBC (STM32F3, GPL-3), BL49 (CJ125), LambdaCtrl (CC BY-NC). No RP2040 design was found and the 14point7 SLC Free page could not be found. Accuracy claims are only 'fast response', plus an EU retailer's unconfirmed 0.007.
evidence: retailer and AEM listings from search results 2026-11-16; github.com/fpoussin/OWBC
suggested_fix: None; this is for positioning the $399 ECU, whose wideband is bundled.

title: The embedded discrete circuit is the cheapest sound option found
claim: No cheaper sound alternative was found. Bought-in controllers cost $82-231, and CJ125 designs rely on a single-source ASIC. Merging the loops into the F407 would save one MCU but couples the pump and heater safety to engine firmware (not recommended). A more robust variant would be this circuit with the R110 fix, current upstream firmware, and input protection.
evidence: section 9 of the notes; competitor table
suggested_fix: Keep the F103 approach; spend effort on validation, not redesign.

title: PTC F2 in the Vm path alters the ESR constant
claim: The firmware subtracts a fixed 11.6 ohm (10 ohm R109 plus 1.6 ohm PTC typical) from the measured ESR; PTC tolerance and temperature drift make this term uncertain by roughly 1 ohm against about 300 ohm at target, so the effect on heater temperature is small.
evidence: sampling.cpp:75-83; miata_f1/wideband_board_config.h
suggested_fix: Check the real ESR at temperature on the bench; if it drifts, use a fixed resistor or move the PTC out of the Vm path.

title: Price positioning vs Speeduino Miata PNP resellers
claim: Speeduino-based Miata PNP units sell at $399 (NA8, shown out of stock), $449-489 (NA6 full kit, with AFM-delete plug, IAT, vac line, vTPS) and EUR 325 plus EUR 70 for an optional LSU 4.9 CJ125 controller. None has wideband on the base board. The official Speeduino store sells no Miata PNP. The planned $399 with LSU 4.9 on board is at parity or below, and far below MS3Pro-class units ($830-1,350).
evidence: speedyefi.com product pages (fetched 2026-11-16, kb/research/files/R03/sp_na6.html, sp_na8.html); mx5nutz thread post 2024-09-22 (maker's own figure, forum); speeduino.com/shop
suggested_fix: Position the product on the integrated wideband and the tuned base map. Match the bundle contents buyers praise (see the bundle-contents finding).

title: Hall CKP/CMP input conditioning: field instability on Speeduino Miata boards
refs: design.py lines 433-446 (R 4.7k series, 1k pull-up, 1n filter, no Schmitt or comparator); motherboards HALL1/HALL2
claim: Three independent users report rpm spikes and unstable running above about 5000 rpm in full sequential on Miatas with Speeduino boards. A vendor traced it to noisy unshielded Hall CKP/CMP wiring and fixed it with a Schmitt-trigger input stage. His first inverting circuit made starting hard until the trigger edge setting was changed. This project's Hall inputs are a plain RC plus the STM32 pin's own hysteresis, the same class as Speeduino's. Root cause is not proven, because Speeduino developers could not reproduce it on the bench.
evidence: speeduino.com/forum/viewtopic.php?t=6281 (pages 1-2, posts 2024-03 to 2025-12); repo/scripts/design.py:433-446; Speeduino NA6 v1.3 nets CRANK-IN/CAM-IN (R33-R36, C15, C16)
suggested_fix: Reserve pads or a footprint for an optional 74HCT14 or comparator stage on HALL1/HALL2, or plan a first-bench test with logged tooth-log noise. Ship with a documented trigger filter setting.

title: Fuel-pump driver killed by powering up with the ST_SIG fuse in (Speeduino NA6)
claim: On the Speeduino NA6 PNP the ST_SIG fuse must be pulled before first power-up, otherwise the smart-FET fuel-pump driver trips. Two users report a dead pump driver, and a SpeedyEFI review says the owner had to jump the pump. The 1989-95 car's stock wiring has the same hazard. If this project drives that pin, the install guide needs a prominent pre-power step, or the circuit must tolerate the feed.
evidence: MX5_PNP.md wiki (fuel pump section); forum t=4583 post #49515; sp_na6.html review 2022-05-10
suggested_fix: Check INSTALL.md and the motherboard against this trap. Add an explicit pull-fuse step with a photo, or make the pin's drive tolerant of a back-fed 12 V.

title: Speeduino NA6 PNP v1.3 architecture and what it gives up
claim: The board is an Arduino Mega on 4 x VNLD5090 dual drivers, with only the chip's own 41-52 V clamp. It has 2 x TC4424A logic-level ignition buffers (IGN3/4 on a header only, not the stock connector), a VN5160S fuel-pump driver, SP720 input arrays with 470R+0.22uF, an MPX4250 plus KP234 baro sensor, and a supply with 1N5818, MOV and SMBJ40A. It has no knock, CAN, wideband or conditioner IC, no sequential spark on the stock connector, and no alternator or VVT driver. The stock 174917-1 connector has no purchasable source even in its BOM (blank part-number cells).
evidence: NA6_v1.3_BOM.tsv; NA6_v1.3_nets.txt; base tune knock_mode Off
suggested_fix: Use as the competitive baseline in docs; no design change.

title: Speeduino v1.3 added supply TVS, flyback diodes and baro sensor over v1.0-1.2
refs: D23 SMBJ40A-Q, D15-D17 NBRS2H100T3G, U11 KP234
claim: Between v1.2 and v1.3 (2023-05) the official board added a 40 V TVS on the supply, 100 V Schottky flyback diodes on the idle, boost and fan outputs, and a KP234 baro sensor, and removed four 10R resistors. v1.0-1.2 had none of these. Why they were added is not documented. The direction (supply TVS and inductive-output flyback) supports this project's protection approach.
evidence: BOM diff NA6_v1.2_BOM.tsv vs NA6_v1.3_BOM.tsv; strings of bom_v1.0.xls and bom_v1.1.xls
suggested_fix: None; context for reviewers.

title: Dead 5 V rail on a Speeduino NA6 PNP (no prime or fan without USB)
claim: One 2024 user's NA6 PNP 5 V rail read 1.13 V key on, so the pump did not prime and the fan did not run until the USB lead was attached. A responder blamed the MC33814-based supply, and a bypass wire fixed it. Single report, root cause unconfirmed. It argues for a supply that fails visibly, and for not letting USB power mask a dead car supply.
evidence: speeduino.com/forum/viewtopic.php?t=6453
suggested_fix: Bench-test the car-supply path with USB unplugged. The repo already notes that USB-only power back-feeds +12V to about 4 V.

title: Bundle contents and options buyers value (reseller kits)
claim: SpeedyEFI sells an AFM/MAF-delete plug pinned for a GM IAT sensor, the IAT sensor, 8-10 ft of MAP vacuum line, a vTPS and adapter harness, a preloaded firmware and tune, and a TPS bracket upgrade option (+$40). Reviews praise easy install, a base map that runs on first start, and responsive support. Complaints: an outdated preloaded firmware (2018) and no Facebook-free support. Alex Engineering also sells optional Bluetooth (EUR 20) and a wideband controller option (EUR 70).
evidence: sp_na6.html, sp_na8.html; mx5nutz thread
suggested_fix: Make sure the store lists the AFM-delete and IAT solution, vacuum line, and a current firmware and tune; keep firmware current at ship time.

title: Auto-transmission cars and 4-pin vTPS fit complaint
claim: A 1-star SpeedyEFI NA6 review (2021) complains that the supplied vTPS and harness do not suit automatic-derived cars (different ECU pinout, 4-pin vTPS). The vendor's answer was a Facebook photo. This matches the repo's own open item that automatics are untested.
evidence: sp_na6.html review of 2021-06-14 and reply
suggested_fix: State plainly on the product page which cars are excluded, to avoid returns.

title: Statements about Speeduino in other_miata_pnp_boards.md checked
claim: Verified correct against the files: Mega 2560 plugged on; VNLD5090 dual drivers on injectors with no external clamp parts; indicator-LED diodes; one driver channel per paired injector pin; 1k driver-input resistors; base tune Paired, 2 squirts alternating; firmware comment on 1 squirt per revolution; wideband is an outside 0-5 V controller. Not verified: ST's own 1k input-resistor recommendation (datasheet not obtained), the 2U/2V/2Y/2Z names (no mapping table found), and the 41-52 V clamp, which the repo cites to the sibling VNL5090N3-E datasheet. I found no wrong statement.
evidence: NA6_v1.3_nets.txt, tune msq, fuel_calcs.cpp, notes section 5
suggested_fix: Optionally cite the VNLD5090-E datasheet for the clamp figure and mark the ST resistor claim unverified.

title: Incumbent Miata plug-in now costs $1,200-$1,350
claim: AMP PNP for each Miata year is $1,349.99 with internal LSU 4.9 wideband, $1,199.99 without; MaxSpark ignition kit is $674.99 extra. Refurbished MSPNP2 NB1 was $639.99 (90-day warranty, final sale, out of stock). Old MSPNP2 list was $830-900.
evidence: files/R04/products_json/amp-pnp-mazda-miata-*.json variants[].price (cents) 2026-11-16; https://diyautotune.com/products/refurbished-mspnp2-mm9900; old prices from search snippets

title: Incumbent does not reuse the stock ECU case
claim: MSPNP is its own two-board case with stock harness connectors plugged into it; mounted by firewall screws (NA) or zip ties (NB); original ECU kept; rear options connector with pre-crimped pigtails. Reusing the stock case with no drilling is a differentiator but moves connector/case sealing burden to this project.

title: No immobiliser function on 2001-05 (lamp lit/flashing)
claim: The incumbent states it has no OE immobiliser function and the dash fault indicator will illuminate/flash on 2001-05. Buyers learn this only from the manual; the repo lists immobiliser as unsupported, so same gap.

title: Check-engine lamp: incumbent does not drive it

title: Stock-function matrix per year (for product page and manual)
claim: Incumbent drives idle (PWM1 IAC), fan 1 on PWM2, A/C relay and A/C request, clutch switch, tach, fuel pump (USA/Europe jumper), O2 select; alternator field PWM3 and VVT HC1 only on 99-05/swaps; VICS solenoid only on 99-00 (Injector I, on above 5500 rpm); manual only, no automatics.

claim: Incumbent makes a timing-light check at fixed 10 deg step one of tuning and warns wrong map can cause no-start or engine damage; trigger angle adjustable 0-20 deg or rotate CAS.

title: Support model: web manuals, base tunes, strict returns
claim: Per-model web install pages (still with 'Insert ... image here' placeholders in 2026), public base-tune/firmware page, TunerStudio code included; returns 45 days only if sealed, opened electronics not returnable, 7% restocking fee, dealer diagnostic fee $75.

title: MS3Pro input clamp at 22 V blows fuse
claim: MS3-Pro operates 6-22 V, clamps input at 22 V and sustained 22 V blows replaceable fuse F1; injectors 5 A thermal-shutdown, high-current outputs clamped 36 V, ignition outputs 5 V logic max 200 mA. A 24 V jump start would blow it.
evidence: files/R04/docs/ms3pro_manual_1.4.1.txt lines 994-997, 1139-1160, 1338-1339 (manual v1.102, 2016)

claim: Forum threads report tach dropout at high throttle on a 1.6 and tach jumping after COP swap (pull-up suspected), and A/C not engaging after install due to jumper/setting mismatch.

title: Incumbent confirms integrated LSU 4.9 wideband direction
claim: AMP PNP optional internal Bosch LSU 4.9 wideband with a 6-wire cable on the rear options connector (WB1-6), earlier MSPNP2/Pro used external controllers; 48-pin options connector gives spark outputs for COP, 8 analog, 4 digital, 2 speed inputs, 9 outputs.

title: Product coverage: manual only, 1.6 B6ZE excluded on 94-97 units, Mazdaspeed separate
claim: Every Miata AMP product says Manual Transmission; 94-97 1.8 units are not compatible with the JDM/EUR 1.6 B6ZE; Mazdaspeed and 2001-05 NB2 units are mutually incompatible.

title: 399 USD undercuts all assembled competitors
claim: Cheapest assembled plug-ins: DIY-EFI GBP 400 ex VAT (about 520 USD), ME221 GBP 579 ex VAT, BMM 749 USD, AMP 1199.99, EMU Black plus adapter 1393, Link 1595, Haltech S2 2130 special.

title: Haltech includes IAT and coverage notes
claim: Haltech kits include the ECU, harness, M14 IAT sensor and aux plug. They exclude 1996-97 US OBD-II NA and manual-only; the NB list names '00-04 Aust, 01-05 USA'. 1.6 NA needs a full-range TPS.

claim: ME221 PnP is GBP 579.17 ex VAT for board plus vacuum hose; IAT, IAT boss and VTPS plate are paid options and no wideband is included.
evidence: bbr_me221-*.js

title: BMM closest US competitor but backordered
claim: BMM Miata ECU (749-825 USD) has internal wideband, MAP, SD log, VVT, USB and a harness, but ships on backorder 'several weeks' and 'up to 30 days'.
evidence: bmm_products.json
suggested_fix: Stock and fast shipping (rusEFI shop ships within 5 business days) are an advantage.

title: No Miata plug-in in rusEFI shop; no NB reflash tool found
claim: The rusEFI shop lists no NA/NB plug-in (only a NC adapter at 50 USD). No stock-ECU reflash tool for 1999-2005 was found; EcuTek covers NC/ND.
evidence: rusefi_shop_all.html; search results
suggested_fix: None.

title: Bare AO3400A injector low-side is used by Blitzbox, unproven for flyback
claim: Blitzbox drives high-impedance injectors with a bare AO3400A (30 V, SOT-23, 4k7 gate, 100k pulldown) and shows no external clamp in the injector section. AO3400A costs $0.0185-0.0325 at JLC. Flyback must be absorbed by FET avalanche, which is robustness-marginal and was not measured.
evidence: hardware/Rev0.1.9/schematics_blitzbox_v0.1.9.pdf p1 crop (kb/research/files/R06/blitzbox_v019_injector_crop.png); fabrication/V0.1.9 BOM; lcsc.py live price. README claims V0.1.2 ran on a real car (author statement).
suggested_fix: Do not adopt without a measured flyback test; keep the project's clamp or smart-FET approach.

title: Self-protected SOT-223 low-sides are cheap and used in proven open designs
claim: SPECTRE (BSP78) and the Ocelot board (NCV8402/8406) use clamped, current-limited, thermally protected low-side parts costing $0.24-1.40 at JLC. These are candidate alternatives for auxiliary outputs and for high-impedance injectors, subject to checking Vclamp and current against the Miata loads.
evidence: SPECTRE_V0.5.4 .sch value counts (11 BSP78); Ocelot-vA4 .kicad_sch (8 NCV8406 + 8 NCV8402AD); lcsc.py 2026-11-16
suggested_fix: Compare against R08 and the current output stage before swapping; field proof for SPECTRE is the author's testing of 0.5.3 only.

title: Blitzbox power chain is the cheapest observed
claim: Blitzbox protects the supply with a series SS54A Schottky, an SMBJ22A TVS and an LM2940 5 V LDO (85 C max), about $0.4 in total. The LDO has not been checked for thermal margin against this project's load.
evidence: blitzbox_v0.1.9_bom_2025-01-08.csv; lcsc.py live
suggested_fix: Use it as a cost benchmark for the current input protection; the thermal check is a separate task.

title: Cheap USB ESD part used in a car board
claim: Blitzbox uses the ESD0504F 4-channel array ($0.079) on its USB lines, and the NUF2221W1 line on the data lines. The $0.59 USBUF02W6 appears on the project's board class.
evidence: Blitzbox BOM, lcsc.py
suggested_fix: Check the project's USB ESD part against ESD0504F (capacitance 0.2 pF, 5 V working).

title: Ignition drivers across designs are TC4424-class gate drivers
claim: Blitzbox, daveecu2 and Route ECU use TC4424 gate drivers. SCG-ECU uses a 2-channel TC4427-class driver. SPECTRE and the MIC4427 listing are the cheaper alternatives. M5x PnP drives ISL9V3040 IGBTs. No cheaper ignition idiom was found.
evidence: Blitzbox BOM; SPECTRE sch; SCG schematic image; M5x BOM; Ocelot sch
suggested_fix: None; use as a price benchmark.

title: Few open designs, none strongly proven in cars
claim: Outside rusEFI/FOME/Speeduino the open-hardware ECU landscape is thin. Most repos are hobby projects, several are abandoned (daveecu2 2021, RavAGE 2013), and none documents EMC or load-dump qualification.
evidence: GitHub search results in work/R06-open-ecu-designs-sweep/dl/ghsearch; repo git logs
suggested_fix: Rely on rusEFI/FOME field history (R31) rather than these designs.

title: JLC rotation caution echoed by community PnP repo
claim: A rusEFI PnP repo tells builders to 'spin the parts round the right way' when ordering at JLCPCB, consistent with the repo's open item about unchecked placement rotations.
evidence: README.md of that repo
suggested_fix: Check every new part's rotation in the JLC 3D preview before ordering.

title: Load dump baseline: boards survive only a clamped (<=35 V) alternator
claim: ISO 16750-2 test A (79-101 V, Ri 0.5-4 ohm, td up to 400 ms) is far beyond a 400 W or 1.5 kW 10/1000us TVS. SMAJ33A (Vc 53.3 V at 7.5 A) would see about 12 A; SMCJ30A about 13 A and 640 W for hundreds of ms. Both survive test B (Us* 27-35 V) because stand-off 33 V (Vbr min 36.7 V) does not conduct below 35 V.
evidence: ISO 16750-2:2023 Tables 13/14 p.20-21; MCC AN5001 p.7-13 (Ipp=(Us-Vc)/Ri); parts manifest Vc values. 400 ms energy is extrapolated from the SM8S curve ratio (INFERRED).
suggested_fix: State in install docs that the design assumes a clamped alternator and tight battery terminals; never disconnect the battery with the engine running. Add a surge-stopper only if unsuppressed-alternator survival is required.

title: Whether a 1989-2005 Miata alternator clamps load dump is unknown
claim: Zener-avalanche clamping rectifiers existed from 1987 and ISO 7637-2:2004 says most new alternators are clamped. No source specific to the Miata alternators was found. An aftermarket or worn alternator may not clamp.
evidence: SAE 872002 abstract (Motorola, 1987); ISO 7637-2:2004 5.6.5 p.16; forum anecdote only for the Miata.
suggested_fix: Ask early customers to scope the dump on a real car, or treat the unclamped case as an accepted, documented risk.

title: Jump start in current ISO 16750-2 is 26 V for 60 s, not 24 V
claim: ISO 16750-2:2023 Table 5 specifies 26 V (60 +-6 s, RT and Tmin) for 12 V systems. ST AN2689 and older texts say 24 V. Repo analyses that use 24 V sit 2 V under the current standard.
suggested_fix: Re-run the clamp-current and series-resistor checks (N2/N6) at 26 V.

title: Reverse battery test is -14 V for 60 s through the car fuse; blown fuse allowed
refs: reverse battery path D1/D2, driver body diodes
claim: ISO 16750-2 test case 2 applies -14 V for 60 s with the DUT fused as in the car. After replacing the blown fuse, class A function is required, so the fuse may blow but nothing else may be damaged. A clamping diode with no external reverse protection is exempt from the test, which is a loophole.
suggested_fix: Reviewers should check that the fuse blows before any trace, driver or TVS is damaged in the documented reverse-battery path.

title: Cold-crank brown-out limits: 3-4.5 V for 15 ms and 6-9.5 V for 50 ms
claim: The ISO 16750-2 starting profile has four levels. Level III (aged battery, cold) dips to 3 V for 15 ms and holds 5 V. Level II dips to 4.5 V and holds 6.5 V. Each level has a minimum functional status.
suggested_fix: Check the buck's drop-out and holdup (bulk C) against 6 V continuous and a 15 ms dip to 3-4.5 V; confirm the MCU does not reset or glitch the injectors.

title: Ground offset test (+-1 V) relevant to separate sensor and power returns
claim: ISO 16750-2 4.8 applies +-1 V supply and ground offsets in 8 combinations. A +-1 V error on a 0-5 V sensor is 20% of full scale unless the sensor return is referenced at the ECU analog ground.
evidence: ISO 16750-2:2023 Table 17 p.25 (the test is optional, by agreement); the 20% figure is INFERRED.
suggested_fix: Keep sensor returns on the analog ground and tie it to power ground at a single point; verify on the motherboard netlist.

title: ESD: USB port needs automotive-grade ISO 10605 protection
claim: ISO 10605 uses 150/330 pF with 330 ohm/2 kohm, contact 2-15 kV and air 2-25 kV, with the generator referenced to battery ground. USBLC6-2SC6 is rated at IEC 61000-4-2 levels, so it is likely below ISO 10605 air-gap levels. The USB port is inside the stock case.
evidence: TI SLVA954B Tables 2-1, 2-2 p.2-3; parts manifest for U4.
suggested_fix: Accept the risk for a service-only port, or document that USB is for bench use with the car off.

title: TVS stand-off and energy selection method (pass/fail)
claim: Stand-off must be at or above the max continuous supply (16 V) and minimum breakdown above the clamped dump (33 V part, 36.7 V min Vbr). Energy is Ipp=(Us-Vc)/Ri and Ppp=Vc*Ipp, compared at the real pulse width with about 45% derating at 105 C plus 50% margin. A 1 ms rating is not a 400 ms rating.
evidence: MCC AN5001 p.7-13; Diotec brochure p.1-2; ST AN2689 p.13-15.
suggested_fix: Apply as reviewer checklist items 5 and 6.

title: Cabin temperature: measured hot-car data are far below the 85 C design figure; no footwell data found
claim: ASU/Temperature 2018: six cars parked in sun reached an average cabin air of 47 C and dashboard of 69 C after 1 h; shaded 38 C. No footwell or ECU-location measurement was found. The 85 C figure is a standards-class assumption (ISO 16750-4 not read).
evidence: news.asu.edu/node/78070 (press page, secondary); JMIE snippet of 70 C cabin air in one car (UNVERIFIED).
suggested_fix: Keep 85 C as a stated assumption; log a real board temperature in the first test car.

title: ISO 7637-2 pulse levels for review (12 V)
claim: P1 -75 to -100 V/10 ohm/2 ms; P2a +37 to +50 V/2 ohm/50 us; P3a -112 to -150 V and P3b +75 to +100 V/50 ohm/100 ns; P4 -6 to -7 V; P5a 65-87 V in the 2004 edition (79-101 V in the 2012 ISO 16750-2).
evidence: ISO 7637-2:2004 Tables 3-9 p.9-16; Nexperia AN50007 Table 1 p.4 for P1.
suggested_fix: Use as the pass/fail table for input-protection review.

title: Hobby-ECU pitfalls most likely to apply: wrong TVS stand-off, rail pump-up from input clamps, reset on crank
claim: The checklist items most often violated in hobby designs are TVS stand-off below 16 V, a 1 ms TVS rating used for a 400 ms pulse, input clamps to a rail that cannot sink the current, brown-out resets on crank and unprotected USB. This ranking is judgement from vendor emphasis, not measured frequency data.
evidence: Section D of notes; app-note emphasis (MCC, ST, Diotec).
suggested_fix: Review those items first on the schematics.

title: NCV8401B is a DPAK drop-in for VND7NV04 at less than half the price
claim: onsemi NCV8401BDTRKG (DPAK, pin 1 gate, 2 drain/tab, 3 source, 42 V clamp, 34 mohm max at 5 V, EAS 800 mJ) costs $0.9605 at 30 and $0.8099 at 100 against $2.0619 and $1.8164 for VND7NV04. That saves about $8.8 per board at 30 and $8.0 at 100, with no re-layout and the 5 V shifter kept. Stock is 2200.
evidence: datasheets/extra/NCV8401BDTRKG.txt (pin table, RDS(on) table, ILIM, EAS); JLC listing C604055 read 2026-11-15; design.py:339
suggested_fix: Swap C155605 for C604055 on the next rev; check the 25-35 A current limit (11-21 A hot) against harness and PTC behaviour, and confirm placement and rotation in the JLC preview.

title: NCV8403A in SOT-223 is the cheapest strong heavy channel and may take a 3.3 V gate
claim: NCV8403ASTT1G (SOT-223): 76 mohm max (135 hot) at 5 V, limit 10-20 A, 42 V clamp, EAS 470 mJ, Vth 1.0-2.2 V, $0.7396 at 30 and $0.6283 at 100, stock 1908. Fig. 8 typical curve shows about 80 mohm (25 C) and 130 mohm (150 C) at VGS = 3 V, so a 3.3 V GPIO can probably drive it and U11 could be deleted. Total is $11.14 at 30 against $22.11, saving about $11 per board. 3.3 V operation is typical-curve only, not guaranteed.
evidence: datasheets/extra/NCV8403ASTT1G_lcsc_C266786.txt lines 140-176; page 5 Fig. 8-13 viewed; JLC 2026-11-15
suggested_fix: Evaluate as a respin option: redraw the injector strip for SOT-223 with drain copper, rerun board_thermal.py, and bench-test 3.3 V gate drive. Keep U11 if bench results are marginal.

title: Relay level shifter U12 can be removed: ZXMS6004FF is specified for 3 V logic
claim: The Diodes ZXMS6004FF datasheet gives VIH = 3 V min, VIL = 0.7 V max, and Rds 400-600 mohm at VIN = 3 V. The 3.3 V GPIO can therefore drive the relay gates directly (CEL already does in rev 0.10). That removes one TSSOP-24 (about $0.39 at 30) and its wiring. The 10 k pull-downs keep outputs off in reset. The hardware enable gate for these channels is lost.
evidence: datasheets/extra/ZXMS6004FF_diodes.txt lines 140-160, 241-255; design.py:268-290
suggested_fix: Drive relay gates from MCU pins through 1 k like CEL, delete U12, keep RN2/RN3 pull-downs; confirm the firmware does not rely on DRV_EN_N for these channels.

title: Same die in a cheaper package fails: VNN7NV04 (SOT-223) costs the same as VND7NV04
claim: VNN7NV04PTR-E is $2.0697 at 30 and $1.8734 at 100 against $2.0619 and $1.8164 for the DPAK part, so the SOT-223 package brings no saving. Only the smaller VNN3NV04 (120 mohm max, 240 hot, 3.5-7 A limit, Eas 100 mJ) is cheaper at $1.0553 and $0.8737.
evidence: JLC lookup 2026-11-15; datasheets/extra/VNN7NV04PTR-E_lcsc_C501115.txt, VNN3NV04PTR-E_lcsc_C443999.txt
suggested_fix: Do not pursue VNN7NV04. VNN3NV04 is a second-tier option (about $8 per board saved, needs re-layout).

title: VNLD5160 and VNL5xxxN3 variants take their supply from the input pin and cannot be driven from 3.3 V
claim: For the dual VNLD5160 and the N3 (SOT-223) singles, INPUT doubles as the 3.5-5.5 V supply (Vsupply = Vin), and Rds is specified at 5 V only. They cannot replace the 5 V shifter. Only the S5 SO-8 singles (VNL5300, VNL5050, VNL5030) have a separate 5 V supply pin and VIL 0.9 V / VIH 2.1 V logic. Stock of the S5 parts is thin except VNL5050S5 (6980, $1.075).
evidence: VNL5160N3 datasheet Tables 6-10 (txt lines 289-453); VNLD5160 pin table (txt line 173); VNL5300S5 Table 6/9
suggested_fix: If a dual is wanted for the injectors, keep U11 and budget SO-8 copper for 2 x 0.5 W hot. VNLD5160 is $1.67 per package ($0.84 per channel), no better than NCV8403A.

title: Multi-channel automotive driver ICs are not stocked at JLC
claim: Live JLC lookups on 2026-11-15/16: TLE8104, TLE8110 and TLE6240 variants show stock 0; MC33810 has no listing; TLE9104SH has 535 pieces but is a high-side driver; TLE8888 is $10.13 at 30 (50 pieces); L9733 is $5.81 with 40 pieces. Option (c) is therefore not buyable, apart from ST L9826 for light loads.
evidence: work/R08-low-side-driver-landscape/jlc/TLE*.json, MC33810.json, L9733.json
suggested_fix: Do not design around TLE8104/8110/6240/MC33810 for a JLC-built product.

title: L9826 octal low-side driver could replace the light channels but protection and interface are weaker
claim: ST L9826 (SO-20, SPI, 8 x 450 mA, 1.5 ohm typ and 3 ohm max hot, clamp 45-62 V) costs $1.7313 at 30 (951 in stock) against about $3.46 for 7 ZXMS6004FF plus U12. Only outputs 1 and 2 have current limit and thermal shutdown; outputs 3-8 only have over-current/short shutdown. It needs SPI pins and firmware.
evidence: datasheets/extra/L9826_lcsc_C155567.txt features and electrical table; JLC 2026-11-15
suggested_fix: Not recommended: gain about $1.7 per board, losing per-channel limiting and adding SPI work.

title: Single-pulse clamp energy is irrelevant to driver choice given the external injector clamps
claim: With L = 20.3 mH (one published 14.8 ohm injector), I = 0.97 A gives 9.6 mJ; 12 ohm at 16 V gives 1.33 A and 18 mJ. If the driver clamp took it, the driver would dissipate about 21 mJ per event, 1.3 W average at 60 events/s. That would overheat any SOT-223, which is why the per-injector ES1D + 1.5SMC16A clamps matter. With them the drain peaks near 32 V and all 40-70 V clamp parts are equivalent; selection rests on Rds x I^2 and package heat. Only one inductance figure exists (PMC7435933).
evidence: PMC7435933 text (R/L = 14.8/0.0203); design.py:355-373; computed energies
suggested_fix: Measure one Miata injector with an LCR meter; document that driver EAS is not the selection criterion.

title: One-part-for-all (ZXMS6005DGQ-13, SOT-223, 3 V logic) is cheapest but thermally marginal for injectors
claim: ZXMS6005DGQ-13 (AEC-Q101, VIH 3 V, 250 mohm max at 3 V, limit 2.2 A min at 3 V, 490 mJ, 60-70 V clamp) is $0.3551 at 30 and $0.2995 at 100. All 19 channels cost $6.75 against $22.11, both shifters go, and the unique extended lines drop from 2 to 1 (saves $3.07 per order). At 1.33 A and 100 % duty the hot part dissipates about 0.75 W in a SOT-223 (42 to 96 C/W), and the 2.2 A limit is thin when hot. The Hellen NA6 BOM uses 8 x ZXMS6005SGTA.
evidence: datasheets/extra/ZXMS6005DGQ_diodes.txt (July 2026) and ZXMS6005DG_diodes.txt; ext/hellen-miata-NA6 BOM; JLC C3235503
suggested_fix: Consider only for the lightly loaded valves (IACV, VVT, BOOST) after checking their currents, not for injectors.

title: No pull-up on 2I for stock igniter (1989-95)
claim: The stock ECU supplies a pull-up on cavity 2I (igniter IGf/tach-related open-collector line). The project fits none (HARN_2I only reaches J1.2I and JP5; ordered boards wire OUT_TACH straight to 2I), so with the stock igniter the tach and/or IGf may be dead. Pull-up value/voltage disagree between sources (5 V vs 1 k to 12 V).
evidence: evidence/cur_mb8995/pcb_nets.txt:12; ord_mb9495 pcb_nets:48; wiki.rusefi.com Legacy-Miata-NA-48-pin-board-for-MRE s2.4; miataturbo.net tach-signal-wiring-specifics-58571; Hellen NA6 94 doc jumper 'tach pullup, used with stock coils'
suggested_fix: Add a DNP-able 1 k pull-up on 2I (rail chosen after scoping a real car), remove OUT_TACH link on ordered boards by hand, test tach with stock igniter.

title: Flat 4 ms dwell, no voltage table or max-dwell guard
claim: Firmware ships constant 4 ms dwell with voltage correction 1.0 over 8-15 V; rusEFI has no max-dwell guard for GPIO-driven igniters. Miata coil packs are reported (forum) to die from over-dwell; spark energy falls at the cranking dip.
evidence: repo/firmware/ext/rusefi/firmware/controllers/algo/defaults/default_ignition.cpp:112-115; grep maxdwell only MC33810 (engine_controller.cpp:599); forum threads miataturbo 96997, 23550
suggested_fix: Ship a voltage-compensated dwell table (draft in notes sec.5, to be scoped) and document scoping dwell before first drive.

title: Safe rest state is LOW and the stage meets it
claim: Coils charge on HIGH; rest must be LOW. Project line is low unpowered (3.3k), in reset (10k pull-down, ZXMS on) and in bootloader. 1989-95 igniter itself has ~659 ohm to ground.
evidence: design.py:297-330; FSM pin tables (0 V key on, ~0.2 V idle); Haltech constant charge falling edge
suggested_fix: None; keep a pull-down of 3.3k-class.

title: 5 V push-pull is sufficient for NB coils
claim: 2005 FSM operation test fires the NB2 coil from two 3 V dry cells; input triggers at or below 3 V. Project output is about 4-4.5 V (INFERRED). Hellen (LVC4245+10 ohm) and Speeduino NA6 (TC4424 direct) are equally 5 V push-pull.
evidence: work/R09-miata-ignition-systems/nb2_coil_bench_test.png; Mazda-Miata-2005_ignition_system.txt Fig.3; ext/speeduino-hardware NA6 Fuel_Ignition.sch; hellen ign8 schematic
suggested_fix: None.

title: Schottky+FET+74HCT04 chain exceeds proven practice
claim: No other Miata ECU needs them; simplest proven stage is buffer + series resistor + input pull-down. They protect against coil wire shorted to battery and give a low-impedance falling edge. Removal saves per-channel parts but loses protection; only two channels are used.
evidence: Speeduino NA6 TC4424 direct; Hellen ign8 10 ohm; design.py:297-330
suggested_fix: Owner decision; if removed keep 3.3k pull-down and a Schottky-free 100 ohm.

title: Igniter thresholds, NB input resistance, dwell limits unpublished
claim: No manufacturer/Mazda source found for 1989-97 igniter threshold, NB coil input resistance, max dwell or over-dwell protection; coil primary is 0.78-0.94 ohm (FSM).
evidence: FSM 1990/1994/2005 extracts; Haltech dwell tables are images
suggested_fix: Bench-measure threshold and input current on real coils before release.

title: Genuine STM32F407VGT6 stock at JLC is tiny and falling
claim: JLC stock of C12345 was 126 pcs on 2026-11-15 and 72 pcs on 2026-11-16 (LCSC 22). It is an extended part. A build of about 100 boards would use up the stock, and JLC would then need consigned parts or a different MCU.
evidence: tools/lcsc.py C12345 and search, work/R10-processor-choices/dl/jlc_extra_search.txt; kb/parts_manifest.md line 11
suggested_fix: Check stock before every order. Pre-buy genuine parts from franchised distributors and ship them to JLC as consigned parts, or split the lots. Document the second-source plan.

title: STM32F407VET6 (512 kB) cannot run current rusEFI
refs: U1 alternatives: STM32F407VET6 C28730, GD32/APM32/CKS VET6
claim: The current rusEFI F407 image is 640,368 bytes (hellenNA6 release 2026-11-16) and this project's build links to 669 kB. VET6-class 512 kB parts cannot hold it. rusEFI's own VET6 build is a legacy 450K special case with storage and RTC disabled. Only 1 MB (xG) parts qualify.
evidence: GitHub release 2026-11-16, hellenNA6_autoupdate.zip bin size; repo/VERIFICATION.md:714; config/boards/STM32F407VET6_Mini.bat
suggested_fix: Do not substitute VET6 variants, including the cheap GD32F407VET6 and APM32F407VET6.

title: No pin-compatible F407 clone is supported by rusEFI
claim: rusEFI's boards readme lists F4/F7 as supported, H7 alpha, and AT32 experimental/abandoned. The AT32 port targets F435/F437, not F407. Issue #8396 (open) reports that the 407-discovery build hard-faults and USB fails to enumerate on APM32F407 since the ChibiOS 21->22 upgrade. No rusEFI issue or report of a working GD32F407 was found, and issue search for GD32 gives 0 hits.
evidence: repo/firmware/ext/rusefi/firmware/config/boards/readme.md; https://api.github.com/repos/rusefi/rusefi/issues/8396; forum viewtopic.php?p=47209
suggested_fix: Ship only genuine STM32F407VGT6. Treat clones as a separate validated firmware variant (USB, flash writes, NVIC priority bits, ADC calibration) and keep them out of the default BOM.

title: Clones are cheaper and in stock, but the saving is small
claim: At JLC, GD32F407VGT6 costs USD 4.04/2.97/2.80 (@1/@90/@1080) with 20,600 pcs. APM32F407VGT6 costs 4.43/2.89/2.61 (@1/@90/@900). AT32F407VGT7 costs 3.97/2.59/2.34. The ST part costs 5.05/3.57/3.34. That is about USD 0.6-1.0 saved per board at 100 pcs, small against a USD 399 product and the firmware risk. JLC lists the GD32F407VGT6 as 512KB, but GigaDevice's own page says 1024K.
evidence: dl/jlc_tiers.txt; gigadevice.com product page; EEVblog APM32F407 thread (interrupt priority bits 3 vs 4, flash programming differs, ADC calibration data missing, device ID 0x413 identical)
suggested_fix: Keep ST as primary. Evaluate APM32 or GD32 only on a bench board, as the emergency second source.

title: ST 10-year longevity for F407VGT6 (secondary evidence)
claim: ST's product page reportedly shows STM32F407VGT6 as Active with 10-year longevity starting 2026-01-01, so about 2036. The ST site would not load for me; this comes from two search extractions of the page and a third-party page quoting the same start date for the F407ZGT6. ST renews the commitment annually.
evidence: web search extractions of st.com/en/microcontrollers-microprocessors/stm32f407vg.html
suggested_fix: Confirm on the ST page and keep a copy for the support documentation.

title: Distributor price and lead time for the F407VGT6
claim: Franchised prices are about 2x JLC: TME USD 9.97 @1 and 8.70 @90 (1,162 in stock); DigiKey SG SGD 21.48 @1, 14.57 @90 (1,124 in stock, 52-week lead time). Aggregators quote Newark USD about 9.25 @100 with a 32-week lead time, and Arrow and Future 52 weeks (unverified). So the fall-back cost is USD 8-10 per MCU, not USD 3.6. Brokers (Win Source) are cheaper but a counterfeit risk.
evidence: page fetch of digikey.sg and tme.eu product pages 2026-11-16; findchips search; search extractions
suggested_fix: Budget USD 8-10 for U1 when JLC stock is gone. Buy ahead for the planned volume from TME or Newark.

title: Wideband: F103C8T6 is the right choice; F042K6 is effectively unobtainable at JLC
refs: U102 C8734; upstream module part STM32F042K6
claim: F103C8T6 (C8734) has 191,011 pcs at JLC, preferred extended, USD 1.46/1.01/0.93 (@1/@250/@1000). The upstream F042K6T6 LQFP-32 has 1 pc (USD 4.05@1) and the QFN version 56 pcs. rusEFI's wideband repo already ships F1 board ports (f1_rev2, f1_rev3, f1_dual), so the F103 is upstream-supported hardware.
evidence: tools/lcsc.py C8734 C69216 C2053439; ext/wideband-rusefi/firmware/boards; hardware/board_module CPL (F042K6Tx)
suggested_fix: Keep the F103C8T6. Do not follow upstream back to the F042.

title: F103 clones (GD32/APM32/CKS32/CH32) save little and differ
claim: JLC alternatives cost USD 0.69-1.04 @1000 against 0.93 for the ST part, saving at most USD 0.15-0.35 each, and CKS32 has only 421 pcs. Reported differences: GD32F103 failed an I2C bench test and has its own system ROM; CKS32 reports SW-DP ID 0x2BA01477; CH32 reads serial number all 0xFF; APM32 and CS32 copy ST's system ROM; internal RC and bus speeds differ. This project flashes the F103 through its ROM bootloader (modelled for ID 0x410) and uses 12 MHz ADC clock and CAN, none of which is tested on a clone.
evidence: dl/jlc_search_f103_alts_2052.txt; blaatschaap.be/identifying-32f103-clones; arXiv 2008.09710 via search extraction; repo VERIFICATION.md:351
suggested_fix: Buy genuine ST parts only and do not allow JLC to substitute. If a clone is wanted, bench-test flasher, ADC accuracy and CAN first (APM32F103C8T6 C393540 is the best candidate).

title: F407 needs its HSE crystal; wideband crystal is optional
claim: F407 datasheet: the USB OTG FS clock is generated by a PLL from the HSE, and the HSI is only +-1% at 25 C and -8/+4.5% over temperature, so Y1 must stay. The wideband F103 HSI is -2/+2.5% over -40..105 C. Upstream f1_rev3 runs the wideband on HSI with no crystal, including CAN. Removing Y101 and its two caps saves about USD 0.20-0.30 per board but costs CAN timing margin and a firmware change (the repo's mcuconf.h uses the crystal deliberately).
evidence: datasheets/txt/C12345_STM32F407VGT6.txt:1893 and 6242; C8734 txt lines 3068-3082; ext/wideband-rusefi/firmware/boards/f1_rev3/mcuconf.h:41-50; repo/firmware/wideband/miata_f1/mcuconf.h; kb/parts_manifest.md:18
suggested_fix: Keep both crystals for the first build. Consider dropping Y101 later after a CAN test over temperature.

title: Second MCU for the wideband should not be eliminated
claim: The pinned rusEFI tree contains no LSU or CJ125 driver (only changelog and ini mentions). The wideband controller is a separate 26 kB firmware with its own heater and pump control. Folding it into the F407 means new firmware and puts heater safety under the main MCU's control. The saving is about USD 1 plus passives. A CJ125 IC (C22419808) costs USD 7-10 and is dearer.
evidence: grep of repo/firmware/ext/rusefi; repo/firmware/wideband/miata_wbo_f103.bin 26,348 bytes; lcsc.py -s CJ125
suggested_fix: Keep the dedicated wideband MCU.

title: Second-source plan and higher-end alternatives for U1
claim: Fall-back order: (1) genuine F407VGT6 from franchised distributors, consigned to JLC; (2) F405VGT6 (1,100 pcs, USD 5.4-7.6) or F427VGT6 (2,585 pcs, USD 6-9). The F427 is more expensive and its LQFP100 pin compatibility could not be verified (ST app note unreachable); rusEFI has F429 targets in releases. (3) clones only after validation. F429VGT6 stock is 33 pcs at USD 28-30, and the F407ZGT6 is a different package.
evidence: dl/jlc_search_st_family_2051.txt, dl/jlc_extra_search.txt; release asset list (f429-discovery bundle)
suggested_fix: Check pin-compatibility of F405/F427 against the daughterboard pin map before naming them as alternates.

title: TunerStudio .ini will not auto-detect for this custom board
claim: rusEFI's Detect downloads the .ini from rusEFI's online archive, which official CI populates with FTP secrets. EFI_EMBED_INI_MSD is FALSE by default and the board does not override it. So the ECU does not present its .ini as a USB drive, and customers must find and load the .ini from the build bundle by hand. INSTALL.md says only to open TunerStudio, connect and press the year button.
evidence: repo/firmware/ext/rusefi/firmware/config/stm32f4ems/efifeatures.h:406-407; tunerstudio/upload_ini.sh; book.pdf p.7-8 (kb/research/files/11/rusefi_book.txt lines 262-281)
suggested_fix: Publish the .ini beside each firmware release with the version in its name and add a Create Project, Browse, pick .ini step to INSTALL.md. Consider enabling EFI_EMBED_INI_MSD, or ship a ready-made TunerStudio project folder.

title: First-start timing check omits 'disable fuel / pull injector fuses'
claim: INSTALL.md's base-timing step tells the user to lock timing at 10 deg and check it with a light while cranking. rusEFI's procedure says to disable fuel injection, remove the injector fuses and pull the plugs (marked FIRE DANGER), and to enable ignition only for the check. The repo does not say this and does not warn that fixed timing must be restored to dynamic.
evidence: book.pdf p.23-25 (rusefi_book.txt lines 821-889) vs repo/INSTALL.md lines 322-326 and firmware/README.md item 11
suggested_fix: Add the rusEFI safety steps and a restore-dynamic check to INSTALL.md and firmware/README.md. Consider a firmware auto-revert of fixed timing at power cycle.

title: rusEFI LTFT compiled in by default and undocumented
claim: The pinned rusEFI enables long-term fuel trim (a learned trim table that can be applied to VE) by default on stm32f4ems. The board's prepend.txt does not disable it, and the repo docs describe only short-term trim. LTFT adds a TunerStudio page and a separate flash record. Its default switch states and flash-write behaviour on this board are unchecked. A shallow clone of FOME has no LTFT code.
evidence: rusefi long_term_fuel_trim.cpp:3-8; efifeatures.h:57 EFI_LTFT_CONTROL TRUE; tunerstudio.template.ini lines ~5328-5333; no LTFT string in repo/firmware/board (grep)
suggested_fix: Decide whether LTFT is shipped. If not, add #define EFI_LTFT_CONTROL FALSE to prepend.txt. If yes, document it and set safe defaults (gathering on, apply off).

title: TunerStudio autotune needs paid registered edition; licence is personal-use
refs: EFI Analytics store; licence page; book.pdf p.31
claim: VE Analyze Live (autotune) requires the registered TunerStudio. Today's store prices are MS USD 69.95 (sale, normally 79.95) and Ultra USD 99.95 (sale, normally 129.95). MegaLogViewer MS is USD 34.95 and HD USD 49.95.
evidence: https://www.efianalytics.com/register/browseProducts.jsp (saved work/R11-tuning-software-workflow/efi_products.html, 2026-11-16); https://www.efianalytics.com/register/license.jsp?appName=TunerStudio+MS; book.pdf p.31
suggested_fix: State the TunerStudio cost in INSTALL. Present free rusEFI tuner plus closed-loop trims as the no-cost path.

title: INSTALL suggests permanent USB cable; SD logging mode depends on power order
refs: INSTALL.md:163; Logging-Guide; FOME Data Logging page
claim: rusEFI and FOME document that SD logging runs only when the car powers the ECU first. If USB powers it first, the card appears as a USB reader and logging is off, and the card cannot log and be read at once. INSTALL.md suggests leaving a USB-C cable plugged in to the glovebox or console. If a laptop or phone powers USB at key-on, logs may silently not be recorded.
evidence: https://wiki.rusefi.com/Logging-Guide (page fetch summary); work/R11-tuning-software-workflow/fome/Basic-Features_Data-Logging.txt; repo/INSTALL.md:163
suggested_fix: Document power-up order for logging. Test it on the first board.

title: No spare TTL UART on J5, so no standard Bluetooth module
refs: README.md J5 map; INSTALL.md:332-347; rusEFI Bluetooth wiki
claim: rusEFI's Bluetooth uses an external classic-SPP module (JDY-33, HC-05) on a TTL UART. It cannot connect to an iPhone. The board's J5 gives CAN, analog and I/O but no free TTL UART; USART3 is the wideband link. Wireless tuning therefore needs a CAN-to-WiFi bridge (rusEFI's own faster suggestion) or USB. rusEFI's MSDroid wiki page says tables and gauge values do not work; Shadow Dash is dated 2018.
evidence: wiki.rusefi.com/Bluetooth (page fetch); firmware/README.md:13,151; INSTALL.md:344; EFI Analytics downloads page
suggested_fix: Mention the CAN-bridge option in the add-ons table. Consider UART pins on J5 in a later revision.

title: Ship firmware and wideband pre-flashed to remove the riskiest customer steps
refs: firmware/README.md Flashing; HOWTO-Update-Firmware; FOME Flashing notes
claim: The customer path includes DFU (BOOT/RESET), Windows driver traps (old STM DFU driver, ConfigManagerErrorCode=28), a one-time wideband flash through TunerStudio, and the .ini matching. The seller can do the DFU flash and wideband flash at assembly, shipping a unit that connects and runs on first plug-in. rusEFI notes firmware from Oct 2025 to Jan 2026 was fragile during updates with poor power.
evidence: firmware/README.md:38-43 and wideband flash section; wiki HOWTO-Update-Firmware (page fetch); FOME Software_Flashing-Software-Notes.txt
suggested_fix: Add pre-flash and verify-version to the assembly checklist. Provide a recovery guide for the customer.

title: Windows Universal Updater and snapshot channel are for catalogue boards
claim: rusEFI's Quick Start sends users to the Universal Updater installer, which uses snapshot firmware by default. For a custom board the user must use the board's own bundle and its console. Whether the Updater refuses to flash an unknown board was not verified.
evidence: book.pdf p.3-4 (rusefi_book.txt lines 84-137)
suggested_fix: Tell customers to use only the vendor bundle. Test the Universal Updater against a custom-signature board.

title: Autotune quality with rusEFI: no data; FOME fixed AFR-mode bug
claim: I found no rusEFI-specific reports on how well TunerStudio VE Analyze works. FOME's changelog lists fixes for autotune in AFR-display mode and for MegaLogViewer VE Analyze channels. That suggests autotune works through TunerStudio but depends on the .ini and lambda channel handling. A generic forum opinion says autotune gets about 60-80 percent of ideal.
evidence: work/R11-tuning-software-workflow/fome/fome-fw/firmware/CHANGELOG.md:234,244; search results (forum opinions)
suggested_fix: Test VE Analyze with the board's wideband channel on the first car. Do not promise autotune results.

title: Competitors' software is free and includes wizards or autotune
refs: Link PCLink, Haltech NSP, ECUMaster, MaxxECU MTune, MSE MEITE
claim: Link PCLink is free and Windows-only. ECUMaster says its clients are free with all functions unlocked and its V3 guide has Wizard and Autotune chapters. MaxxECU MTune release 1.160 (2026-04-21) mentions autotune from logs. Haltech NSP has a setup wizard and Quick-Tune. Motorsport Electronics' MEITE is described as free. Buyers of competing ECUs get a guided setup and autotune with no extra software cost.
evidence: linkecu.com/all-about-pc-link-tuning-software; ecumaster.com catalogue and V3 Software Guide (search results); maxxecu.com/webhelp/software_releases-1_160; support.haltech.com quick-tune; search summaries
suggested_fix: Position the year-button base tune, closed-loop trim and free rusEFI tuner as the equivalent. Consider a guided pre-start checklist.

title: Proposal: guided first-start procedure with pass/fail checks
claim: A 10-step procedure with a visible pass/fail check per step: desk check, key-on sensors, bench outputs, trigger check with fuel and ignition off, timing light, first start, idle, logged drive, cold-start mornings, trims. Plus proposed automation: pre-start checklist dialog, auto-reverting fixed-timing and fuel-off modes, per-year bench-test card, support-bundle button.
evidence: kb/research/R11-tuning-software-workflow.md section 5; built from book.pdf p.11-25 and FOME HT-First-Start-Safely.txt
suggested_fix: Adopt into INSTALL.md and the in-box card. The auto-revert and checklist features would need firmware work.

title: Base-tune weak points need cold-start and boost caution in docs
claim: rusEFI's guide only stubs cold-start and wall-wetting tuning, so the base tune from other cars is least reliable in cold starts, in the 1994-97 table (a 1.6 table) and above 100 kPa. Cold start typically needs several logged mornings (my estimate, no source). The repo already says a turbo car needs a tuner.
evidence: book.pdf p.31 (lines 1116-1124); firmware/README.md base-tune section
suggested_fix: Add a cold-start log-and-adjust section to INSTALL.md and the card.

title: 99-00 alternator overcharge on MSPNP from ground offset
refs: alternator field control, daughterboard firmware default
claim: Owners report battery voltage rising to 16 V or more and a boiling battery on 99-00 MSPNP2. The vendor engineer, relayed second-hand, blames a ground offset between the alternator body and battery negative that latches the field on. The fix given is a ground strap from alternator body to chassis. Lean stalls were also traced to the base map's battery-voltage correction.
evidence: https://www.miataturbo.net/megasquirt-18/id1050x-battery-voltage-correction-factor-alternator-overcharging-99-00-mspnp2-107805/ ; https://www.miataturbo.net/mspnp-55/99-mspnp2-blown-up-battery-voltage-regulation-issues-103610/
suggested_fix: Ship alternator control off by default (the repo already does). Add the ground-strap instruction and a voltage-correction note to the install guide. Consider a firmware over-voltage cutoff.

title: Wrong or missing base map is the top first-start failure
claim: First-start threads span many years. The 94-95 car needs throttle to start. The 91 car dies after about 10 s from warm-up enrichment, injector size and idle VE. The 99 NB 1.6 Speeduino got the wrong trigger pattern and no base tune existed. The base map and a checklist (timing light, trigger angle, injector cc) decide the first impression.
evidence: miataturbo 81863, 103709, 110352 (links in notes sections 3 and 4)
suggested_fix: Ship a per-year and per-engine base map, including NB 1.6. Add a first-start checklist and a timing-light check. Review the base map for typos.

title: Immobilizer on 2001-05 must be documented, ideally switchable
claim: AMP states the MSPNP does not handle the OE immobilizer and the dash light flashes. A forum post says the MSPNP-Pro has a jumper to allow or ignore it, and another vendor reportedly emulates it. A no-start with a flashing light will be read as a defective ECU.
evidence: https://ampenginemanagement.com/blogs/mspnp-pro-documentation/pro-mm0105-installation ; miataturbo 107244
suggested_fix: State in the docs and on the product page that the immobilizer is unsupported and what the light does. Test a car with the immobilizer. Consider a bypass or emulation option later.

title: Wideband signal ground at the ECU sensor ground is the fix for erratic AFR
claim: Erratic wideband readings on an MSPNP were fixed by grounding to the ECU sensor-ground pin (22) with the signal on pin 21. Exhaust leaks near the sensor read lean and mislead tuners. The on-board wideband removes the wiring error but the sensor placement advice stays necessary.
evidence: https://www.miataturbo.net/mspnp-55/99-mspnp2-wideband-install-82322/ ; https://www.miataturbo.net/megasquirt-18/mspnp2-91-miata-wont-idle-goes-lean-regardless-103709/
