suggested_fix: Document the sensor position, weld bung and leak check. If an external wideband is allowed, document the ground.

title: Tach on 89-95 is a real field problem
claim: Owners had no tach after an install: on a 95 (alarm tap on 2I, staff asked whether the wire is on 1F or 2I), and on 90-93 with R8 coils (a case jumper plus a 1 k resistor were needed). This matches the repo's open 2I direction question.
evidence: https://www.miataturbo.net/megasquirt-18/mspnp-installed-what-happened-my-tach-18670/ ; https://www.miataturbo.net/megasquirt-18/how-getting-tach-work-90-93-ms3pro-r8-coils-107309/
suggested_fix: Resolve the cavity and direction on a real car for 1989-93 and 1994-95. Document the aftermarket-coil case.

title: Price anchors for tuning and hardware
claim: Remote tunes are quoted at about USD 300-400 typically (2024 thread), with 400-1000 range and 'start and idle' at about 400 (summary). MSPNP Gen2 costs USD 830 and the MSPNP-Pro USD 1150 (listings). Link plug-in units cost GBP 975-1374 or USD 1255-1595, and the 400 USD price point undercuts all of them.
evidence: https://www.miataturbo.net/ecus-tuning-54/remote-tuner-recommendation-108939/ ; vendor listings in search results
suggested_fix: Position as hardware plus self-tune with a published base map, and list remote tuners that accept the rusEFI format.

title: A/C idle-up stalls are a recurring complaint
claim: About eight forum threads cover stalls with A/C on. The fixes are idle-up delay and duty, min-rpm threshold and PID delay. Summaries say MSPNP lacks true A/C idle-up.
evidence: https://www.miataturbo.net/megasquirt-18/great-c-faq-20954/ and related threads (search summary only)
suggested_fix: Wire the A/C request to a dedicated input, enable idle-up in the base maps, and document the settings.

title: Vendor service reputation: repair time, USB bootloader
claim: One poster reported a repair of over six months. Diagnostics are about USD 50 (one poster). A rusEFI Hellen owner lost USB or DFU access after reflash trouble and fell back on the reset and boot buttons.
evidence: https://www.miataturbo.net/megasquirt-18/ms2pnp-repair-109226/ ; https://rusefi.com/forum/viewtopic.php?p=42004
suggested_fix: Publish a repair policy and give easy access to the boot and reset buttons or the USB port.

title: Public NB base ignition maps disagree by about 18 deg at WOT
refs: miata_nb_tune.cpp, mazda_miata_vvt.cpp, Speeduino NB8B PNP base tune.msq
claim: The rusEFI NB ignition table (used by the repo for NB1 and NB2) has 28 deg at 99.5 kPa, 4144-4884 rpm, and 30-31 deg at 6800-8000 rpm. Speeduino's NB8B PNP tune has only 11 deg at 96 kPa, 4700-5200 rpm, and 9 deg at 7200 rpm. The Speeduino NA PNP tunes have 29 deg. None of them states test conditions.
evidence: Computed from files/R14/rusefi_src/mazda_miata_vvt.cpp (mapBased18vvtTimingTable) and files/R14/speeduino_tunes/NB8B PNP base tune.msq (advTable1); notes section 5.1
suggested_fix: Tell users the base map is a starting point, with the first WOT pulls only after wideband and knock checks. Consider a more conservative shipped table above 80 kPa for the first start.

title: Injector dead time has no primary source and public tables differ up to 2x
claim: rusEFI's NB lag table (the repo's) is 1.5 ms at 12 V and 1.25 ms at 14 V. FOME's is 1.04 ms at 12.8 V and 0.90 ms at 14.4 V. Speeduino uses 1.0 ms open time with about 100 % at 13.9 V. I found no Denso or Mazda dead-time or flow-at-pressure datasheet for 195500-1970, -2180, -3310 or -4060.
evidence: files/R14/rusefi_src and fome_src mazda_miata_vvt.cpp; Speeduino msq injOpen/injBatRates; notes section 2
suggested_fix: State in the install and tuning guide that dead time is a community estimate. Give a wideband-at-idle correction procedure and avoid presenting the table as measured.

title: Stock injector part numbers and flows (conflicting cc figures)
claim: 1990-93 is 195500-1970 (230 cc miataturbo, 212 cc rusEFI). 1994-97 is 195500-2180 (265 cc, with 254 cc in a second table and in rusEFI NA94). 1999-00 is 195500-3310 (260 cc, repo 256). 2001-05 is 195500-4060 (265 cc). All are high-impedance, about 12-16 ohm (about 14.5 ohm for -3310, UNVERIFIED).
evidence: files/R14/miataturbo_fuel-injectors.txt; rusEFI mazda_miata_1_6.cpp, na8.cpp, vvt.cpp; Haltech NA8 page lists 230 cc
suggested_fix: Use 230 / 265 / 260 / 265 cc as defaults, noting the source. Check flow-pressure assumptions (cc figures presumably at 300 kPa).

title: NA 1.6 preset inherits 212 cc injectors; NA94 and NA96 flows differ for the same injector
claim: rusEFI sets injector.flow 212 for 1.6 (miataturbo and Haltech say 230 cc, a 9 % fuel difference), 254 for NA94 and 265 for NA96, although 94-97 use one part (195500-2180).
evidence: mazda_miata_1_6.cpp (212, 254), mazda_miata_na8.cpp (265); miataturbo page
suggested_fix: Override flow in the repo presets: 230 for NA6, 265 for NA94 and NA96, after the owner confirms.

title: NB1 does not get fixed-pressure injector compensation although it has the in-tank regulator system
claim: Only NB2 sets fuelReferencePressure 400 kPa and ICM_FixedRailPressure. NB1 (1999-00) also uses a single feed line with an in-tank, non-vacuum-referenced regulator, but this is INFERRED because the Radium kit is titled 01-05. The NB1 flow of 256 cc differs from miataturbo's 260 cc.
evidence: Radium NB regulator PDF (files/R14/radium_nb.pdf); miata_board.cpp
suggested_fix: Confirm the 1999-00 fuel system from a manual and set the same compensation, or document why not.

title: Trigger definitions verified from source; repo input assignment matches rusEFI
claim: NA uses TT_MAZDA_MIATA_NA: primary is the 2-pulse cam signal (SGC), secondary is the 4-pulse crank signal (SGT). NB uses TT_MIATA_VVT with the 4-tooth crank (alternating 70/110 deg) and a 3-pulse cam (VVT_MIATA_NB). Speeduino's Miata 99-05 decoder describes the same pattern. The repo's HALL1/HALL2 mapping matches rusEFI. The NB vvtOffsets is 98 in rusEFI and 95 in FOME; FOME also uses globalTriggerAngleOffset 10.
evidence: rusEFI trigger_mazda.cpp:27-57, 60-79, 164-180; Speeduino decoders.cpp:435-441, 644-650 and src/decoders/miata9905.cpp
suggested_fix: None. Note the 98 vs 95 vvtOffsets and the FOME angle offset when a customer's timing light disagrees.

title: Compression ratio differs between sources
claim: 1.6: Moss and Wikipedia 9.4, FOME 9.0, rusEFI default 9.1. 94-97: Moss 9.0. 99-00: Moss, Wikipedia and FOME 9.5. 01-05: Moss 9.5 (probably copy-forward) vs FOME 10.0.
evidence: Moss spec pages (files/R14/m1990.html, m1999.html), Wikipedia B-engine and NB pages, FOME mazda_miata_vvt.cpp
suggested_fix: Set 9.4 / 9.0 / 9.5 and leave 2001-05 documented as unresolved (10.0 probable).

title: Fuel pressure: Moss gives 38-46 psi for all years; NB code uses 400 kPa
claim: Moss lists regulator pressure 38-46 psi for 1990-2004, probably copy-forward for NB. rusEFI and FOME use 400 kPa (58 psi) for NB2. A Radium PDF confirms an in-tank, non-vacuum-referenced OEM regulator, but gives no psi figure (a 60 psi figure came from a search summary, UNVERIFIED).
evidence: Moss m1990/m1999 pages; rusEFI mazda_miata_vvt.cpp comment; files/R14/radium_nb.pdf
suggested_fix: In the documentation tell users to measure rail pressure and enter it. Do not claim a stock figure for NB.

title: Base timing spec and check method
claim: All years list 10 +/- 1 deg BTDC at 850 +/- 50 rpm with the TEN connector jumpered to ground (Moss spec sheets); miata.net says timing on 1999+ is not settable (search summary only, UNVERIFIED).
evidence: mossmiata.com/miata-1990 ... 2004; notes section 1
suggested_fix: Install guide: instruct a timing-light check against the rusEFI fixed-timing mode with the 10 deg trigger offset; note that FOME adds an offset of 10 deg for NB.

title: Alternator control reference gains
claim: rusEFI NB: target 14.0 V (14.2 V NA96), offset 20, P 16, I 8, D 0.1, period 10 ms; FOME uses P 20. The repo copies the rusEFI values and ships the control off, with PWM 250 Hz commented as 'as stock ECU'. No Mazda-sourced stock alternator control data were found.
evidence: mazda_miata_vvt.cpp, FOME mazda_miata_vvt.cpp
suggested_fix: None; keep it off until the pull-up behaviour is verified on a car.

title: NB2 VVT reference gains and target table differ between rusEFI and FOME
claim: rusEFI and the repo use PID P 2, I 0.005, D 0.002, offset 33, min 20, max 90 and an 8x8 target table with up to 33 deg. FOME uses min 10, vvtControlMinRpm 400 and a different table peaking at 29 deg. Speeduino NB8B uses closed-loop KP 0.8125, KI 0.09375, 300 Hz, 20-80 % duty.
evidence: files/R14/rusefi_src and fome_src mazda_miata_vvt.cpp; Speeduino NB8B msq
suggested_fix: Consider starting VVT disabled or at a mild table for the first start and say the table is a community starting point.

title: Closed-loop lambda is off in all reference Speeduino tunes
claim: All five Speeduino Miata tunes ship egoAlgorithm 'No correction', AFR targets 14.7 at idle/cruise, 13.6 at 70 kPa and 12.6 (or 13.0-13.1) at 100 kPa, and EGO active only above 1200 rpm. NA6/NA8 tunes have knock off.
evidence: files/R14/speeduino_tunes/key_constants_extract.txt
suggested_fix: Make sure rusEFI closed-loop defaults in the repo are no more aggressive than these on first start.

title: Idle target and idle valve frequency vary widely between sources
claim: Warm idle target: Moss 850 +/- 50, Speeduino 800, rusEFI NA table 950 (1180 cold). Idle valve PWM frequency: Speeduino 120-170 Hz (NA/NB8B) or 500 Hz (99-00), FOME NB 500 Hz. Stock IACV is a 2-wire BAC valve (Haltech).
evidence: mazda_miata_base_maps.cpp, Speeduino msq iacCLValues/idleFreq, FOME idle.solenoidFrequency 500
suggested_fix: Check the repo IACV frequency against the harness valve (output driver and any flyback); pick 850 rpm for warm idle.

title: Missing data: MSPNP maps, rusEFI online tunes, Mazda manual, stock fan temperatures
claim: MSPNP base maps, the rusEFI online tune repository, Mazda factory manual PDFs, stock coil dwell, stock fan switching temperatures, NB rev limit and idle MAP values were not obtained. Speeduino PNP tunes use fan on 93-94 C (older) or 80 C (newer, not stock), rusEFI NA94 fan on 100/off 96 C; none is a primary figure.
evidence: notes 'Not checked'
suggested_fix: A follow-up should obtain an FSM or a MSPNP .msq.

title: AEM 30-3427 gauge-end connector identity is inferred, not verified
claim: AEM manuals give the 8-way pin/colour table (VERIFIED) but the JST SPUD-001T-P0.5 sentence appears under the wiring notes next to the 10-way Power/IO connector; the 30-0302 manual (only connector A) repeats it for connector A. No source read names the 8-way sensor connector's housing, so J2 = PUD for 30-3427 is only inferred. AEM's page was unreadable (403).
evidence: kb/research/files/R15/aem_30-0300_fae.txt lines 105-113; AEM 30-0302 manual (read, not kept) 'optional extras' beside Connector A; web search for PUDP-08V-S + AEM found nothing
suggested_fix: Plug one real 30-3427 into a sample J2 (or into an S08B-PUDSS-1 header) before claiming fit; otherwise ship or specify a seller-made pigtail with PUDP-08V-S.

title: Seller-made pigtail about 9-20 USD vs AEM harness 36 USD
refs: LCSC C490532 PUDP-08V-S, C267125 SPUD-001T-P0.5; Bosch BAK 1.5 plug
claim: A pigtail with the Bosch 6-way plug and a JST PUDP-08V-S end costs about 9-20 USD parts (Bosch plug kit 7.30-17.99, housing 0.17-0.29, contacts 0.01-0.02 each, wire) versus 35.96 USD for AEM 30-3427. LCSC stocks housing (12,171) and contacts (131,221). Contacts accept only 22-26 AWG.
evidence: tools/lcsc.py 2026-11-16; Ballenger CONN-75762 17.99/16.25@100; ProWire 9.85/7.30@100 (snippet); onefastshop AEM30-3427 35.96
suggested_fix: Make or have made a PUDP-08V-S to Bosch 6-way pigtail (1.5-2 m, 22 AWG) as the default lead, document AEM 30-3427 as an alternative.

title: AEM 30-3427 patchy availability
claim: On 2026-11-16 onefastshop lists 30-3427 at 35.96 USD out of stock, ships week of Nov 30; iagperformance out of stock (contact for ETA); prices 22-51 USD elsewhere; made in China, single source.
evidence: onefastshop.com/products/aem-sensor-harness-for-x-series-wideband-gauge-30-0300-30-0334; iagperformance.com 30-3427 page
suggested_fix: Do not make the product depend on one retail part; name a second lead option.

title: Genuine LSU 4.9 sensor price and sources
claim: Genuine 0 258 017 025: Ballenger 69.97 x1, 63.99 x100 (USD); efihardware AUD 130 ex GST; ECUMaster kits 111.20 (with 6 ft harness, list 139) or 103.20 (with plug, list 129); MaxxECU 124.40, urotuning 119.20. Counterfeit rate claims are anecdotal.
evidence: bmotorsports.com products_id=1645; ecumasterusa.com WHPWB491/492; urotuning.com; kartsportnews 2025-11-20 fake-sensor bulletin
suggested_fix: Source genuine sensors from Bosch Motorsport distributors only; update R05's 119.20 anchor.

title: Mating plug part numbers and prices
claim: Harness-side plug: Ballenger CONN-100321 housing 15.99/13.99@100, kit CONN-75762 17.99/16.25@100, pre-wired 12 in pigtail CONN-85762 19.99/17.99@100; Bosch Motorsport kit 1 987 280 016 / D261.205.356-01; Bosch 1 928 404 669 (one UK distributor, unverified). Not stocked at LCSC/JLC. Crimp tool needed (MCP 1.5K die per ICT Billet).
evidence: bmotorsports.com ids 2081, 2082, 2080; Bosch Motorsport data sheet p.1; auto-click.co.uk; tools/lcsc.py searches empty
suggested_fix: Buy pre-crimped Bosch pigtails (or kits at 100 pcs) rather than loose plugs if no crimp tool.

title: Bosch pinout, trim resistor location, J2 table consistent
claim: Bosch pins 1 IP, 2 VM, 3 H-, 4 H+, 5 RT, 6 UN; trim resistor (30-300 ohm) lives in the sensor's own connector module; AEM colours green RT, white H-, orange COM, red IP, black UN, brown H+ map one to one to the repo table. Checked, correct.
evidence: Bosch Y 258 E00 015e p.2; Bosch Motorsport ds p.2; aem_30-0300_fae.txt Connector B table
suggested_fix: None; keep the colour print beside J2.

title: INSTALL.md lacks Bosch mounting rules
claim: Missing Bosch rules: at least 10 deg from horizontal with connector up, 40-60 Nm with high-temp grease, boss 10.5-13 mm stainless, gas under 930 C, hexagon under 600 C, plug under 120 C, cable under 250 C, no silicone sealants, cover sensor when undercoating, heater not before engine start. AEM differs on torque (30 ft-lb) and on vertical mounting.
evidence: Bosch Technical Product Information Y 258 E00 015e sections 2.2, 4.3-4.11; aem_30-0300_fae.txt:319-345
suggested_fix: Add a short rules box to INSTALL.md section 6; trust Bosch numbers over AEM's where they differ.

title: Exhaust pressure shifts reading (turbo conversions)
claim: Pump-current error vs absolute pressure: about +3 % at 1.2 bar, +9-11 % at 1.5 bar, -10 % at 0.7 bar (lambda>1 curve), limit 2.5 bar continuous; +4 %/100 C of ceramic temperature. NA Miata back-pressure effect is small (inferred about 1-6 % of Ip).
evidence: kb/research/files/R15/bosch_lsu49_techinfo.pdf p.8 graph (read from image)
suggested_fix: Mention in tuning notes that readings read high-ish at boost; no board change.

title: Free-air calibration not needed
claim: AEM calls trim-resistor calibration default and recommended; free-air only for aged sensors. The FOME/mck1117 wideband firmware has no free-air function and uses the RT trim pin, so no user calibration step is needed.
evidence: aem_30-0310.txt:136-140,349; grep of firmware/*.cpp,h for calibrat/free air returned nothing relevant
suggested_fix: Do not add a free-air procedure to the docs.

title: Wideband heater may auto-start without CAN allow
claim: Heater preheat is 2 V for 5 s then ramps from 7 V, and rusEFI sends allow only when the engine is running (matches Bosch 4.3.2). But with no CAN command the wideband auto-starts from battery voltage, so a CAN fault could heat a cold sensor before engine start (against Bosch).
evidence: heater_control.cpp lines 60-69, 169-170; wideband_config.h:45 HEATER_PREHEAT_TIME 5; rusefi controllers/algo/engine.cpp:169
suggested_fix: Have the firmware owner confirm the battery-voltage auto-start constants in the shipped image.

title: How rival ECUs sell the wideband lead
refs: ECUMaster WHP kits; MaxxECU; uaEFI options
claim: Competitors with built-in wideband sell the sensor and lead as an add-on kit (ECUMaster 103-111 USD sale, 129-139 list; uaEFI pigtails+wideband cable +100 USD) or in a premium bundle (MaxxECU Premium). Buyers expect a ready lead and a named sensor.
evidence: ecumasterusa.com WHPWB491/492 fetched; work/R05 rusefi_p_uaefi.html; MaxxECU snippets (unverified)
suggested_fix: List a wideband kit (sensor + pigtail) as an optional add-on next to the 399 USD ECU.

title: 1989-93 map uses cavities that have no stock wire (1L fan, 1M VSS, 2T pump, 2M TPS)
claim: Manual (F-128..F-130) lists 1I,1L,1M,1T,2F,2M,2R,2S,2T,2Y,2Z as unused; Lakey 90-93 MT chart shows no wire in 1L,1M,2T,2M,2F. The board comments label 1L fan relay, 1M VSS, 2T fuel pump relay, 2M automatic TPS as stock functions and ties 2F to GND as AFM ground, while the manual's ground is 2J.
evidence: kb/research/files/R16/wm1990_pdfpage273_F-129.png, wm1990_pdfpage274_F-130.png; Lakey PDF conn #1/#2
suggested_fix: Relabel these as add-on/unused on 1989-93; confirm 2F/2J on the car's harness before keeping 2F tied to GND (2F carries no wire on the Lakey chart; 2J is the manual's ground).

title: Stock fan is thermoswitch-controlled; 1R is a monitor node
claim: The ECU does not control the radiator fan: a water thermoswitch drives the relay; the ECU monitors terminal 1R (0 V when fan on, coolant above 97 C or TFA grounded). A low-side output on 1R therefore only forces the fan on in parallel with the switch.
evidence: wm1990 F-129 (1R row), djvu lines ~18771 (TFA jumper), 9444
suggested_fix: Document that stock thermoswitch remains in control; a stuck-on output runs the fan; 1L fan claim for 89-93 has no source.

title: Fuel pump is driven by the circuit-opening relay, not the ECU
claim: ECU terminal 2T is empty on 1989-93; the pump is powered via the circuit-opening relay (fed from the airflow meter switch and the start signal on 1C). The board's OUT_FP on 2T has no stock counterpart; with the AFM removed the pump would stay unpowered unless the user wires a relay.
evidence: wm1990 F-129/F-130 tables (2T -), Lakey chart 1C note; manual outline lists COR as separate device
suggested_fix: Explain in INSTALL: keep stock COR, or wire a relay to the AUX output when the vane meter is deleted; do not claim 2T is stock.

title: Igniter interface confirmed: ECU sources base drive, 2I is IGf input, igniter drives tach
claim: 1G/1H feed the igniter transistor bases (about 659 ohm to ground, 0 V key on, ~0.2 V avg idle); 2I is the IG(f) confirmation input (<0.5 V key on, ~1 V idle); the igniter's TAC output feeds the tach directly. A 5 V push-pull TC4427 drive and JP5 left open match this.
evidence: wm1990 F-128/F-129 (1G,1H,2I); Lakey igniter diagram
suggested_fix: None; keep JP5 open. The IGf return must be read or code 01 logic is moot in rusEFI.

title: Stock idle-up inputs not mapped (P/S 1P, blower 1S, headlights 1U, stop lamp 1O, TEN 1K)
claim: The stock ECU raises idle for power steering, A/C, blower and electrical load and reads the TEN terminal for fixed timing; the board leaves 1O,1P,1S,1U,1K unconnected, so these idle-up compensations are lost unless mapped to AUX inputs.
evidence: wm1990 F outline (input list), F-128/F-129 rows 1K,1O,1P,1S,1U; mb_na6.py HARNESS empty strings
suggested_fix: Wire 1P/1S/1U through the existing spare inputs with pull-ups and add firmware idle-up; document that stock TEN jumper does nothing.

title: Terminal voltage and diagnosis reference (manual) saved
claim: Full 48-pin terminal-voltage table, physical cavity layout, diagnosis connector TEN (fixed 10 deg BTDC, 850 rpm, output check) and TFA (fan on), codes 01,02,03,08,09,10,14,15,17,26,34 with fail-safes, are scanned under kb/research/files/R16/.
evidence: kb/research/files/R16/wm1990_pdfpage271..274 and 224 PNGs
suggested_fix: Use for bench tests: with the stock ECU removed, AFM 5 V on 2K, O2/ECT/IAT ranges apply to the board's input scaling.

title: Hardware internals, case size, year part numbers not established
claim: Only seller-listing part numbers (B61P-18-881A/B manual, B6AW-18-881 1993 California) and forum guesses on the processor were found; case dimensions, construction, maker and the electrolytic cap values for the 1.6 board remain unverified; miata.net was blocked.
evidence: redlineautoparts and ebay listings via search; kb notes
suggested_fix: Measure donor cases with calipers before ordering enclosures; inspect donor boards for cap leakage.

title: Ordered 94-95 board drives 2I, which is an ECU INPUT in the stock manual
claim: Mazda workshop terminal-voltage tables for 1994 (Igniter) and 1995 (Ignition control module) list 2I as an Input to the PCME. The ordered 1994-95 motherboard rev 0.9 connects net OUT_TACH directly to J1.2I with no jumper, so a configured tach output would fight the igniter. Current rev 0.12/0.13 has JP5 (open), which is correct.
evidence: charm_1994_09 and charm_1995_09 PNGs in kb/research/files/R17 (row 2I, Input column ticked); rusEFI wiki 'Tach Input'; evidence/ord_mb9495/pcb_nets.txt:48 'OUT_TACH 2 J1.2I JD1.11'
suggested_fix: Before first power-up cut the OUT_TACH link to J1.2I on the ordered board and keep the tach output unconfigured in firmware; check the car's wiring diagram. Do not drive 2I.

title: 1994 and 1995 manuals disagree on 2I and IAC voltages
claim: 2I igniter signal: 1994 reads below 0.5 V ign-on and about 1 V idle, 1995 reads about 10 V and about 11 V. IAC 2W: 1994 about 7 V ign-on and 9 V idle, 1995 about 1.0 V and 10 V. Forum says a late-95 ECU in a 94 gives no-IGf and no tach, so the igniter/coil type differs.
evidence: charm_1994_09/12 vs charm_1995_09/12 PNGs; forum summary via search (miata.net pages blocked)
suggested_fix: Document that 1994 and early-1995 igniter coils may differ; do not assume 2I electrical levels; test on the car.

title: 1996-97 case outline: best available data is Hellen64 template
claim: No stock 96-97 case dimensions or photos with scale were found. rusEFI's working hellen64_NA8_96 KiCad board has outline 154.2 x 159.2 mm, 7 mm corners and six 5 mm holes at (26.10,16.81), (170.10,16.81), (26.10,98.81), (170.05,98.81), (26.10,165.61), (170.10,164.81) mm. The NA6_94 board has an identical outline, so it is a generic template; it only indicates the case interior is at least about that size.
evidence: work/R17-stock-ecu-1994-97/repos/na_hellen-miata-NA8/hellen64_NA8_96.kicad_pcb (pcbnew); wiki Hellen-NA96 'good to drive'
suggested_fix: Measure a real 96-97 ECU case (outer size, stud positions, lid, heat sink recess) before ordering the next 96-97 board; the rusEFI outline is a better placeholder than the NA one.

title: 1994-95 and 1996-97 connectors/pinouts are unrelated; full tables available
claim: 94-95: 22+26 = 48 pins, igniters #1,4 on 1G and #2,3 on 1H, separate injectors 2U/2V/2Y/2Z, IAC 2W, PRC 2R, purge 2X, fuel pump 2T, fans 1L and 2S, one narrowband O2 on 2N, MAF 2O/2P. 96-97: 22+16+26 sites (a 12-pos site is unused), IGT1 4N, IGT2 4R, injectors 4U-4X, IAC 4Q, PRC 4J, purge 4T, EGR vent/vacuum 4O/4P, tach 4L, fans 1A/1B, fuel pump 1U, MAF 3B, front/rear O2 3C/3D, heaters 3M/4Z, K-line 1D. No knock input on either.
evidence: CHARM terminal ID and voltage PNGs in kb/research/files/R17; notes sections 2 and 3; rusEFI wiki Mazda-Miata-1996 agrees
suggested_fix: Diff the tables in the notes against the repo's mb_na6.py / mb_na96.py pin maps.

title: 1996 vs 1997 table differences
claim: 4Z is the rear O2 heater only in the 1997 table (unused in 1996). IAC 4Q voltages are swapped between years (1996 ign-on <4.8 V, idle ~10 V; 1997 ign-on ~10 V, idle ~4.8 V). 3J/3K/3N values differ slightly. Otherwise identical; 1997 page 2 (1L-3E) not viewed.
suggested_fix: If the 96-97 board gets a rear-O2 heater driver, wire it to 4Z (1997 only); no change for 1996.

title: ECU location and removal
claim: 94-95 and 96-97 ECUs sit under the carpet behind the passenger seat: three 10 mm nuts, connector has a release tab pushed from underneath while prying the other side. Mitchell 1994 says 'under passenger-side footwell' (disagrees; AMP and Mitchell 1997 say behind the seat). rusEFI's 48-pin adapter needs 3 x M4 washers on one screw (recessed thread, stock heat sink) and an 8 mm lid hole for USB.
evidence: AMP MSPNP install pages (dl/web/amp9495.html.txt, amp9697.html.txt); dl/m1997_electrical_component_locations.txt:46; rusEFI wiki Legacy-Miata-NA-48-pin-board-for-MRE
suggested_fix: Add the location, removal steps and the recessed-thread/washer warning to INSTALL.md; check the heat-sink recess on both cases.

title: OBD-II features the 96-97 board does not serve
claim: 96-97 ECM has K-line on 1D to DLC-2 (protocol ISO 9141-2 only INFERRED), MIL on 1E (low-side, B+ = off), rear O2 and heaters, EGR boost/position sensors, NE+/NE- crank sensor, and AT-only TCM lines 1R/1T/4Y. No immobiliser pin exists in the 94-97 tables.
evidence: CHARM 1996/1997 tables; DLC-2 diagram PNG
suggested_fix: State these in the 96-97 README (no OBD-II readiness, MIL stays off unless configured, automatic unsupported).

title: Stock part numbers are only seller-level
claim: Reported ECU numbers: 1994 BPE8-18-881, 1995 BPL9-18-881(A/B), 1996 BPS1-18-881A/B, 1997 BP3A-18-881A/B; a separate auto-trans series is mentioned. No California/federal split found; MT/AT is selected by pin 1K (94-95) or 1O (96-97).
evidence: search snippets of redlineautoparts, partrequest, miata.net (pages blocked)
suggested_fix: Do not print part numbers as fact in the store; ask the customer for photos of their ECU label.

title: 1H is constant-battery B+2, 3K is fuel-tank-level input (repo calls them unclear)
claim: Mazda PID table: B+2 (PCM back-up positive voltage, constant B+) is on 1H; FTL V (fuel tank level) is on 3K; wiring: 1H = G/R from 30 A FUEL INJ fuse, 1A = L/R from ROOM 10 A fuse. Repo labels 1H 'unclear' and 3K 'N/C or fuel gauge, low'. 2K = wire G/O to cluster, DLC and TCM (tach), contradicting Alex Engineering 'unused'.
evidence: files/R18/charm1999_pid_terminal_1*.png, _2*, _3*; wiring2000_B1a_top.png, wiring2000_B1a_connector1_table.png (read by eye)
suggested_fix: Update pinouts_9605.md and motherboard docs: 1A and 1H both always-hot B+ (do not drive), 3K tank-level input, 2K tach.

title: No terminal-voltage table exists for NB1; PID map is the primary pin source
claim: The 1999-2001 manual has only a PID-to-terminal table with conditions, no key-on/idle terminal-voltage table; the 2000 wiring manual gives wire colours for every cavity.
evidence: files/R18/INDEX.md, charm1999_pid_*.png, wiring2000_*
suggested_fix: Cite these files as the NB1 primary source in the repo docs.

title: Crank, cam and MAF sensors are 12 V powered 3-wire parts
claim: CKP: A = W/R (main-relay 12 V), B = signal GY/R to 2J, C = ground B/L. CMP: signal GY/L 2H. MAF: C = W/R 12 V, B = LG/B signal 2L, A = B/L ground. CMP gives 25/50/75 Hz at 1000/2000/3000 rpm (3 pulses per cam revolution inferred); idle 750-850 rpm gives 18-22 Hz.
evidence: wiring2000_B1b_cmp_maf.png; sm1999-2001 pp 01-40-13, 01-40-16 (low-res); PID table
suggested_fix: Confirm input conditioning accepts open-collector Hall signals and the 0.9-2.4 V MAF level.

title: EGR valve is a 4-coil stepper, VICS 3Q low-side
claim: EGR stepper coils on 2M V, 2N W/G, 2O P/B, 2P P with W/R common feed on C/D; VICS solenoid W/L on 3Q with W/R feed; EGR boost sensor 3S and its solenoid 3T.
evidence: wiring2000_B1b_connector2_table_egr.png; PID SEGRP, VICSV
suggested_fix: Document EGR as unsupported; leaving 2M-2P undriven only logs faults on a PCM that is gone.

title: Alternator field (1O), generator sense (1T) and charge lamp (1Q) are PCM-driven
claim: Generator connector has D and P; key on D about 0 V and P <1 V; idle P 3-8 V. Lamp is ON key-on, OFF after start via PCM 1Q. Mazda does not say what happens if 1O is undriven; forum says lamp current can seed the field on some alternators (unverified).
evidence: sm1999-2001_p271_generator.png (01-17-3); PID ALTF/ALTT V/CHRGLMP
suggested_fix: Keep the lamp path (1Q low-side) functional so the field is excited; test on car.

title: Maker, teardown, case dimensions and board outline not found
claim: No source gave NB1 PCM dimensions, internal hardware or maker; only the mounting (two fasteners, under driver dash by steering column) is documented.
evidence: AMP MM9900 install page; searches
suggested_fix: Measure a physical stock BP4W-18-881 unit before ordering outlines.

title: Connector part numbers only from rusEFI wiki
evidence: files/R18/rusefi_wiki_OEM-connectors.md lines 317-342, 417-423
suggested_fix: Verify on TE datasheets and with a stock board.

title: No immobiliser evidence for US 1999-2000; NB1 reflash tool not found
claim: Only a European-immobiliser jumper in AMP docs (3P fuel pump relay variant); no reflash read/write tool found for NB1.
evidence: AMP MM9900 page; web searches
suggested_fix: State US-only in docs.

title: 2001-02 vs 2003-05 main relay and 4S differ
claim: The 2002 manual shows 3H and 4S unused (relay switched by key); the 2003 manual shows 3H main relay control (B+ key off, <1 V key on) and 4S as IG1 sense. One 2001-05 board must handle both.
evidence: files/R19/charm_2002_pcm_voltage_2.png vs charm_2003_pcm_voltage_2.png and _5.png; wiki.rusefi.com Mazda-Miata-2002
suggested_fix: Check the 2001-05 motherboard and firmware for per-year handling of 3H and 4S, and document the jumper or setting.

title: Immobiliser pairs PCM and unit; cannot be deactivated
claim: Mazda manual: unit and PCM store key IDs and a code word, swapping between cars means no start, and the system cannot be deactivated. A failed system starts once and stalls, with no start after the third crank. Security lamp is driven by the immobiliser unit.
evidence: charm.li 2002 Miata, Antitheft Service Precautions, Programming and Relearning, Reading DTC pages
suggested_fix: Keep 3S and 3Q undriven and tell customers to leave the immobiliser unit connected.

title: Standalone swap leaves security lamp flashing
claim: MSPNP-Pro MM0105 docs say the dash fault indicator will illuminate or flash. A MiataTurbo thread reports intermittent flashing on a standalone, and owners pull the bulb. No source found for a fuel cut after seconds, and the engine is reported to run.
evidence: ampenginemanagement.com pro-mm0105-installation; miataturbo.net thread 84178
suggested_fix: Add to the install guide that the lamp may flash, that bulb removal is the common fix, and that the unit stays connected.

title: 2003 manual lists TP at 4Y, others say 4V
claim: The 2003 manual page lists TP on 4Y with 4V unused, while the 2002 manual, 2005 FSM and rusEFI wiki say 4V. Likely a manual typo, unresolved.
evidence: files/R19/charm_2003_pcm_voltage_5.png vs charm_2002_pcm_voltage_5.png
suggested_fix: Keep 4V; ask 2003 owners to confirm with a continuity check.

title: 2001-02 only: 3E CDCV output and 4AB FTP sensor
claim: The 2002 table has 3E CDCV control and 4AB FTP sensor (about 2.5 V at 0 kPa). The 2003 table shows 3E unused and the 2005 table has no 4AB entry.
evidence: files/R19/charm_2002_pcm_voltage_2.png and _5.png; charm_2003_pcm_voltage_2.png
suggested_fix: Leave undriven; list in the docs as unsupported EVAP items.

title: Cruise control and OBD-II are not in this PCM path
claim: The manual tree shows cruise control as its own module with servo and switches. OBD-II is the K-line on 3Q (DLC KLN), with no CAN pins in the tables.
evidence: charm.li 2002 tree (Cruise Control Module/Servo); 2002 table 3Q
suggested_fix: None; note in the docs that cruise keeps working with the stock module if its inputs are retained.

title: Reflash alternative costs $275-800 (dated)
claim: Forum posts 2012-2016 quote Bell Tuning $795, Dynotronics about $550-600 and TDR $275-495 for stock-ECU reflashes, limited for heavy modifications.
evidence: web search summaries of miata.net / miataturbo threads, not fetched
suggested_fix: Re-check vendor sites before using in marketing.

title: Case dimensions, maker and part numbers not found
claim: No primary source for the NB2 case size, board outline or maker. Forum or seller hints only for part numbers (BP7F-18-881 2003, BP7V-18-881 2004 CA MT, BTT3-18-881 2001-02 MT). AMP says the ECU sits under the driver dash by the steering column with two bolts.
evidence: ampenginemanagement.com MM0105 page; web search listings
suggested_fix: Measure a physical NB2 ECU before the outline is finalised.

title: NB 2001-05 CKP/CMP/MAF are 3-wire, supplied from the main relay (about 12 V), not from the ECU
claim: CKP, CMP and MAF each have A = main-relay terminal D (switched battery), B = signal to PCM, C = PCM GND 4A. The board must only provide the input pull-up/conditioning and the ground; it must not supply the sensor. CKP air gap is 0.5-1.5 mm.
evidence: Mitchell 2005 manual text lines 2986-2990, 3181-3184, 2710-2714; CHARM 2002 CKP inspection page
suggested_fix: Check that the Hall input circuit (1k pull-up to sensor 5 V) still reads correctly when the sensor is powered from 9-16 V main relay output and when 5 V sags in cranking; document that the sensor 12 V comes from the stock harness.

title: 1994-97 CAS: SGT 4 and SGC 2 pulses per sensor rev, about 5 V
claim: The workshop manual gives SGT approx 5 V, 4 pulses/rev and SGC approx 5 V, 2 pulses/rev. The sensor supply and output transistor type are not stated; the repo's 'hall, 12 V fed' wording is unverified.
evidence: CHARM 1994, 1995, 1996 'Camshaft/Crankshaft Position Sensor' spec pages (kb/research/files/R20/charm_199x_electrical_specs.txt)
suggested_fix: Scope the CAS on a real car (open-collector or push-pull, supply) before relying on the pull-up design.

title: 1996-97 separate NE crank sensor is a 500-600 ohm (VR-type) coil, left unconnected by the repo
claim: The OBD-II crank-pulley sensor reads 500-600 ohm at 20 C, which indicates a two-wire magnetic sensor. Leaving it unconnected limits crank sync to the CAS (4 pulses per cam rev), which is a trade-off rather than an error.
evidence: CHARM 1996 'Crankshaft Position Sensor' spec; repo/scripts/mb_na96.py:30
suggested_fix: Document the resolution trade-off; optionally expose 4H/4E to a VR input if the pins are free.

title: Vane airflow meter output level conflicts between 1990 and 1994-97 manuals
claim: 1990 manual voltages (via R16) are 3.8 V key on and 3.3 V idle; the 1994 and 1996 manuals give below 1 V key on and 1.0-2.0 V at idle. Lakey's measurements follow the 1990 direction. Either the meter polarity changed or a transcription is wrong; the VAF input scaling cannot be confirmed from documents alone.
evidence: wm1990 OCR/R16 terminal table vs CHARM 1994 'Air Flow Meter/Sensor' and CHARM 1996 spec pages
suggested_fix: Measure a real meter on a 1989-93 and a 1994-97 car before the next order; check the input divider and clamp against 0-5 V full range.

title: 2004-05 PCM has actuators the repo does not cover: stepper EGR, EVAP leak pump, EGR-boost solenoid, fuel-level input
claim: The 2005 BP table lists four EGR coil drives, an EVAP leak-detection pump and solenoid, an EGR boost sensor solenoid, a VTCS solenoid and vacuum switch input, and a fuel tank level input to the PCM (4AD). The repo documents 'no EGR/purge' but not the fuel-level and EVAP items.
evidence: Mitchell 2005 PCM terminal tables, text lines 1190-1640
suggested_fix: List these cavities as unsupported in the 2001-05 documentation; check whether the fuel gauge needs 4AD passed through.

title: IAC 2P/2Q: manual calls both PCM terminals (positive/negative), repo treats 2P as a fused 12 V feed
claim: Mitchell lists 2P 'IAC (positive)' and 2Q 'IAC (negative)' with the scope measured between them; the repo and rusEFI wiki treat 2P as +12 V supply and 2Q as the low-side. Which one holds is not settled by the documents; coil resistance and drive frequency are not found for 1999-2005.
evidence: Mitchell 2005 lines 1254-1263, 2259-2263; mb_nb2.py:47; rusEFI wiki Miata 2002
suggested_fix: Measure 2P at key-on with the harness connected to a stock ECU before first power-up; fall back to a documented jumper if it is switched.

title: Switch and relay polarities for 2001-05 are mixed; per-input polarity needed
claim: Brake 4B is B+ when pressed; PSP 4C is B+ straight, <1 V turned; neutral 4H is <1 V in neutral; clutch 4I is B+ pedal depressed; A/C request 4F is <1 V on; relay outputs (A/C 2K, fuel pump 2M, fans 2B/2C, main relay 3H) are low-side (<1 V = on), and 3H is B+ with ignition off.
evidence: Mitchell 2005 PCM table text lines 1230-1520
suggested_fix: Set a per-input polarity table in the firmware defaults and write it into the install guide.

title: Sensor resistance and curve references: ECT/IAT 2.2-2.7 kohm at 20 C, 0.29-0.35 kohm at 80 C; implied PCM pull-ups
claim: 1990: IAT -20 C 13.6-18.4 kohm, 20 C 2.21-2.69 kohm, 60 C 0.493-0.667 kohm; ECT 2.2-2.7 kohm at 20 C. 1994-96 and 2005: 2.21-2.74 kohm at 20 C, 0.287-0.349 kohm at 80 C. 2005 PCM voltages imply a pull-up near 1.5 kohm (ECT) and 2.7 kohm (IAT). The 33 kohm IAT No.2 curve belongs to turbo cars only.
evidence: wm1990 OCR p.F-91/92 excerpt; CHARM 1994/1996; Mitchell 2005 pp.59-73
suggested_fix: Use the 2.5 kohm @20 C table and check the board's ECT/IAT pull-ups against 1.5 kohm and 2.7 kohm.

title: Actuator coil resistances: injectors 12-16 ohm, IAC 10.7-13 ohm, purge 23-27 ohm, coil primary 0.78-0.94 ohm
claim: Injectors 12-16 ohm at 20 C in 1990-96 (high-impedance, voltage drive); IAC 11-13 ohm (1990) and 10.7-12.3 ohm (1994/96); purge and fuel-pressure-control solenoids 23-27 ohm; 1994 coil primary 0.78-0.94 ohm; HO2S heater about 13 ohm (1994-96), 2-20 ohm front and 2-50 ohm rear (2005); 1994-96 alternator rotor 3.5-4.5 ohm. No inductance, flow or 1999-2005 injector value was found.
evidence: wm1990 OCR, Mitchell 1994 specs, CHARM 1994/95/96, Mitchell 2005 p.92
suggested_fix: None needed; add to the driver margin notes (the repo already lists injector inductance as unknown).

title: 2005 alternator terminals: 4T manual disagrees with itself (3-8 V vs about 14 V at idle)
claim: 3M is the field coil control (duty 0-100 %, rises with electrical load); 4T is generator output voltage (terminal P): the terminal table says 3-8 V at idle with no load while the PID table says about 14 V. The input range and divider must handle both until measured.
suggested_fix: Measure 4T on a car before relying on a divider ratio; keep alternator control off by default as the repo does.

title: Tach and VSS: 1989-95 tach comes from the igniter; 1994 VSS is 4 pulses per shaft rev; cluster thresholds not found
claim: rusEFI wiki states NA6 and 94/95 NA8 tach is generated by the igniter and the ECU provides only a 5 V pull-up; 1994 VSS is 4 pulses per shaft revolution; 2005 tach (3O) and VSS (3T) scope shapes are square waves, levels only read from images (low confidence). No source gives the cluster tach threshold per year, and forums disagree (12 V square wave vs pulled to ground).
evidence: rusEFI wiki NA48 section 2.4; CHARM 1994 'Vehicle Speed Sensor'; Mitchell 2005 Figs 22-23 images
suggested_fix: Measure the tach wire on stock cars per year and state the threshold in the docs.

title: Chargeable Extended lines are the main fixed cost
refs: 37 non-preferred Extended LCSC lines of 44 (7 are Preferred, no fee on Economic)
claim: On Economic PCBA each unique non-preferred Extended part costs $3.07 per order. 37 lines on rev0.10 come to $113.59 per order, about $11.4/board at q=10 and $2.3 at q=50. Each line merged away saves $3.07 per order.
evidence: https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/pcb-assembly-price (2026-10-22); kb/parts_manifest.json jlc_library and jlc_preferred flags
suggested_fix: Consolidate duplicate-function Extended lines (3 BAT54 variants, 3 LED colours, 3 1206 resistor values, ES1D/B360A/SMAJ/SMCJ/1.5SMC lines) and prefer Basic or Preferred parts.

title: Quantity 100 forces Standard PCBA
claim: Economic PCBA is limited to 2-50 boards (some options 2-30), single-sided placement and a fixed 255 C reflow. 100 boards go to Standard: setup $25.56, stencil $8.21, $1.53 per unique line (92 lines on the DB, $141), fixtures $41.04, packing $0.50+ per board, and edge rails are required. Standard is never cheaper than Economic for the same design (at least $14.93 handling gap).
evidence: https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-assembly-capabilities; pricing page 2026-10-22; blog reduce-pcb-assembly-cost-prototype
suggested_fix: Order in batches of 50 or less (compare two 50s against one 100 in the quote tool); check parts against a 255 C reflow peak if on Economic.

title: Per-board cost model, daughterboard rev0.10 (6L)
claim: Total per daughterboard excluding shipping and tariff: $83.05, $66.06, $52.31, $48.29, $45.11. At q=10 the split is PCB $7 (estimate), assembly $14, parts $45. The ordered rev0.9 4L board is $74.5, $59.8, $47.6, $44.1, $41.6.
evidence: work/R21-jlcpcb-cost-model/model.py; fees verified, PCB price is an estimate; JLC's own Oct-2026 4L 140x75 test board quoted $94.97/bd at 5 and $37.36 at 50 for comparison
suggested_fix: Run the real quote with the Gerbers to replace the PCB estimates.

title: Motherboard cost and fixed fees
claim: With JLC fitting SMD only, a 2L 154x162 motherboard is about $9.2/$6.4/$4.6/$4.0/$4.7 at q=5/10/30/50/100. Fixed fee is about $22-25 per design (4 designs about $93 per order round). Panelising cannot help, because two boards exceed the 250x250 mm panel limit.
evidence: model.py; pricing and capabilities pages; manifest
suggested_fix: Use Combine Shipping to merge the five orders into one parcel; do not move the 4-5 SMD Extended parts to hand assembly at q>=10 (labor exceeds the $12-15 per order saved).

title: Bare PCB prices not obtainable; 6L restrictions
claim: JLCPCB's quote tool needs a login and no public price table exists. Only official anchor: 6L 100x100 ENIG 5 pcs from $35.1. HASL is not available for 6+ layers (ENIG 2u). Via-in-pad is the free default for 6+ layers. The 100x100 step cannot be reached (DB 125x76 with 101.6 mm headers; motherboard 154x162).
evidence: https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities; https://jlcpcb.com/6-layer-pcb; https://jlcpcb.com/resources/multiple-layer-pcb
suggested_fix: Get a real quote and record the PCB lines for 4L vs 6L; do not budget on the estimates (about +-40%).

title: 6L vs 4L is a small lever
claim: Going 6L to 4L saves about $3.4/board at q=10 and $2.4 at q=50 (UNVERIFIED PCB estimates). Assembly and parts do not change. 6L also forces ENIG, which is fine.
evidence: model.py A10; 6-layer page
suggested_fix: Quote both stackups; keep 6L if the routing needs it.

title: US duty: JLC prepays 35% on PCB and SMT
claim: JLC pre-collects 35% on PCB and SMT lines (stencil 90%), flat with no true-up; individuals must use DDP. My stack for a PCBA is MFN about 2-3% + Section 301 25% + 12.5% forced-labor Section 301 (since 2026-07-24), about 40%. Range 12.5% to about 55% if Section 232 auto parts applies. Section 122 expired 2026-07-23; IEEPA duties have been off since 2026-02-24; de minimis is gone. At q=10 the duty on a set is about $25 (range $9-40).
evidence: https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/us-tariff-policy-faq (2026-10-29) and Tariff-us.png (verified); gingercontrol.com tariff guide (secondary); HTS classification unverified
suggested_fix: Budget 35-40% of goods value; get an HTS classification from a broker or CBP ruling (8537.10.91 vs 8543.70 and 232 status); keep a company/CPT option with an EIN.

title: Buy high-value THT parts domestically to avoid duty
claim: JLC fitting all motherboard THT adds $3.1/bd + $3.58/order for 190 joints, but puts about $31/bd of parts (MAP $29) into the dutiable JLC order (about $10/bd duty at 35%; whether JLC applies the rate to parts is unstated). The TE harness header is not in the LCSC library, so JLC cannot fit it. Stock is 65 sockets (32 boards) and 155 MAP sensors.
evidence: manifest; pricing page; us-tariff FAQ
suggested_fix: Keep MAP, sockets and headers on the seller's own sourcing and hand-fit them; consider JLC only for low-value THT.

title: Stock limits for a 100-board run
claim: Live JLC stock for the STM32F407VGT6 is 126, TCAN1042 257 and TLS115B0EJ 556; attrition overage is on top. A 100-board batch would exhaust the MCU stock and needs global sourcing or two lots.
evidence: kb/parts_manifest.json (live 2026-11-15)
suggested_fix: Check stock before ordering; split lots or use JLC global sourcing.

title: Placement count is 330, not about 430
claim: Rev0.10 JLC CPL has 330 placed parts (1042 SMD pads); rev0.9 has 302 (976 pads). The ~430 figure overstates SMT joints by about 30%.
evidence: evidence/cur_db/fab_miata-ecu-daughterboard-rev0.10_jlcpcb_cpl.csv (331 lines), pcb_pads.csv
suggested_fix: Use 330 / 1042 in the cost sheet.

title: Seller-fitted J1/J2 headers should stay with the seller
claim: JLC fitting J1/J2 would add $1.67/bd + $0.41 parts at q=10. The repo's self-order BOM says they must be soldered while plugged into the motherboard to come out straight, which JLC cannot do.
evidence: model.py; repo self-order BOM notes; pricing page
suggested_fix: Keep hand-fitting.

title: UK/EU landed costs
claim: EU: no low-value exemption since 2026-07-01; B2C parcels up to EUR150 pay a EUR3 temporary duty per HS code, B2B pay standard duty. VAT is collected by JLC for individuals and by customs for companies. 8537.10 duty is about 2.0-2.1% (UK/EU, aggregators only) plus 19-25% VAT.
evidence: https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/eu-customs-reform-faq (2026-10-28); https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/customs,-duties-and-taxes (2026-11-10)
suggested_fix: Confirm duty on the official TARIC / UK Trade Tariff before quoting EU or UK prices.

title: Shipping cost is not public
claim: JLC shows shipping only in the quote after choosing Ship to. My estimate (UNVERIFIED, +-40%) is $35/$45/$75/$100/$180 for 5/10/30/50/100 sets, about $7 down to $1.8 per set. Combine Shipping (15 days free storage) can merge the five orders.
evidence: https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/how-much-does-shipping-cost; https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/combine-shipping-service
suggested_fix: Read the real Shipping Estimate in the quote tool.

title: JLC can place the THT harness header, sockets and other connectors itself
claim: JLC capabilities say THT and mixed SMD+THT assembly is available under Economic and Standard; FAQ prices it at $3.5 hand-soldering per order + per-joint fee (R21 table: $3.58 + $0.0164/joint). The repo hand-fits these parts and marks J1 [self-order], although C592838 is in the JLC library.
evidence: jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-assembly-capabilities (THT FAQ); jlcpcb.com/help/article/pcb-assembly-faqs (wave soldering item); tools/lcsc.py C592838 live: Extended, stock 32, $12.92@1; kb/parts_manifest.md:123 [self-order]
suggested_fix: Test a JLC quote with J1/sockets/MAP as library THT parts (watch preview rotation/footprint); saves seller labour. Stock of J1 (32) limits this to small batches; buy rest from Newark and consign or hand-fit.

title: No Western assembler published prices; only MacroFab and CircuitHub can take the 6-layer DB
claim: MacroFab (2-36 layers, THT selective/wave, coating, programming, consignment, no minimum) and CircuitHub (Grid max 215x199 mm, SMT+THT, qty 1-1000+) fit both boards. Aisler prices only 2/4-layer boards and Eurocircuits only assembles its own boards (max 800 THT placements). None of them publish price for a 330-placement board, so price parity at 30/100 is unverified.
evidence: macrofab.com/pcba/; circuithub.com; community.aisler.net/t/our-simple-pricing/102; eurocircuits.com PCB Assembly Capabilities page
suggested_fix: If a Western route is considered, get an instant quote for the 6-layer DB at 30 and 100 before deciding; do not assume it is competitive.

title: Chinese alternatives are similar in capability, none published prices; PCBWay and NextPCB list conformal coating
refs: PCBWay, NextPCB, Elecrow, Makerfabs, ALLPCB, Seeed
claim: PCBWay (min 5 pcs, kitted/consigned/combo, coating, FCT to customer's procedure), NextPCB (no MOQ, partial/full consignment, IC programming, FCT, coating machine, IATF16949 claim) and Elecrow/Makerfabs (programming/testing, $0.03 per pad Makerfabs, ICT fixture $300-1000 Elecrow) are viable but publish no setup/part fees for our size; Seeed publishes nothing usable.
evidence: pcbway.com/assembly-capabilities.html and /oem/electronics-manufacturing; nextpcb.com/pcb-assembly; makerfabs.com/pcb-assembly.html; elecrow.com/pcb-assembly.html; seeedstudio.com/fusion_pcb.html
suggested_fix: Keep NextPCB/PCBWay as a second quote source for 100+ batches or stock-outs; request a written quote including setup, THT and coating fees.

title: JLC stock limits a 100-unit build for J1 and sockets
claim: JLC's C592838 stock is 32; with the socket and MCU stock from R21 a 100-unit batch cannot be sourced from JLC alone. Newark/Farnell/RS hold stock and a Chinese turnkey house can buy from distributors (NextPCB lists Digikey/Mouser/Newark sources).
evidence: tools/lcsc.py C592838 today; kb R21 item 8; R24 stock table; nextpcb.com/pcb-assembly
suggested_fix: Buy headers and sockets from authorised distributors in advance; consign to JLC only if needed (HK warehouse, 2% fee min $10, refundable duty deposit).

title: JLC consignment from outside China is costly and one-way
claim: Consigning parts requires shipping to JLC's Hong Kong warehouse, a price review, a refundable duty/VAT deposit (13% VAT on value plus duty), a non-refundable 2% handling fee (min $10), and JLC may resell leftovers only back to the seller.
evidence: jlcpcb.com/help/article/how-to-consign-parts-to-jlcpcb sections 2.1-2.3
suggested_fix: Use consignment only for scarce parts such as genuine TE headers when JLC stock is short; otherwise hand-fit.

title: MCU programming and functional test at the assembler are limited
claim: JLC supports MCU hex programming only 'partially' on Standard orders after engineering evaluation; PCBWay and Elecrow functional test follows only the customer's procedure (Elecrow fixture $300-1000). The seller needs their own test procedure/jig anyway and can flash by USB-DFU after assembly.
evidence: jlcpcb.com capabilities FAQ (MCU programming); pcbway.com/assembly-capabilities.html (FCT); elecrow.com/pcb-assembly.html (testing section)
suggested_fix: Document a bench test and DFU flashing step; consider a fixture only when per-unit test time exceeds a few minutes at 100+.

title: Counterfeit/clone risk: use authorised distributors for TE headers
claim: Genuine TE headers are available from authorised distributors and LCSC; turnkey houses will also buy clones if cheaper (Makerfabs states it may substitute connector brands, flagged Y/N). Standards (SAE AS6081/ARP6178) recommend authorised sources over brokers; no quality data exists for Chinese clone headers (R24).
evidence: makerfabs.com/pcb-assembly.html (parts note 1); SAE G-19 / ANSI summary pages (secondary); kb R24
suggested_fix: Specify TE MPN with 'no substitution' on any quote and buy cut quantities from Newark/Farnell/RS.

title: Fulfilment cost: home vs small 3PL vs assembler-ship
claim: Home shipping all-in is about $15-18 domestic (R26) plus 10-20 min labour; a 3PL adds about $2-3.2 pick/pack (survey average 3.20), storage $18-25/pallet/month, receiving $5-15/pallet, setup $250-1000 for about half of providers and monthly minimums, with real invoices 20-50% over the rate card. Assembler direct-ship (PCBWay, Rapid Direct) has no published price and raises customs/importer-of-record and RMA problems for a $399 consumer parcel.
evidence: fulfill.com/3pl-pricing (2026 guide, survey-based); redstagfulfillment.com guide via search; kb R26; pcbway.com/oem/electronics-manufacturing (direct shipping claim)
suggested_fix: Pack at home up to about 100 units; use a 3PL when volume is steady at tens of orders per month; have assemblers ship to you or the 3PL in bulk, not to buyers.

title: Staged plan: when to leave JLC plus hand assembly
claim: Stage 1 (10 units): JLC Economic, headers from Newark, hand fit, DFU flash, home test and pack. Stage 2 (10-30): have JLC fit THT library parts to save labour. Stage 3 (30-100): JLC (100 forces Standard) with second quotes from NextPCB/PCBWay when stock is short. Stage 4 (100+): quote MacroFab/CircuitHub/EU house only if coating, FCT, serialisation or quality escapes justify a premium. Tariff (35% DDP on China PCBA, R21) is the same for all Chinese houses.
evidence: R21 fee/tariff model; this note sections B, C, F
suggested_fix: Adopt the staged plan; define triggers: quality escapes on THT joints, stock-outs, need for coating/FCT, or tariff cost above labour saving.

title: Aisler cannot do the 6-layer daughterboard; Eurocircuits needs its own PCBs
claim: Aisler's published prices list 2- and 4-layer boards only (older 2023 post), customer-supplied parts carry a EUR 15 fee per assigned part there; Eurocircuits assembles only boards it fabricated, with max 200 BOM lines for instant pricing.
evidence: community.aisler.net/t/our-simple-pricing/102; eurocircuits.com capabilities page
suggested_fix: Exclude Aisler for the 6-layer board; EU route would have to be Eurocircuits full flow or MacroFab/CircuitHub.

title: Harness headers are buyable from stock today
refs: TE 174917-6, 178780-1, 353830-5, 174915-6; README line 174-177; review brief section 6
claim: The review brief/README statement that headers are 'hard to buy / salvage-clone only' is wrong for 174917-6, 178780-1 and 353830-5. Newark/Farnell list 471, 160 and 153 pieces in stock, RS AU showed 178 of 174917-6, LCSC/JLC lists 32 of 174917-6, and Greenchips shows 2,929 of 174917-6. TE's own pages say Active but 'not currently available'.
evidence: Findchips snapshots 2026-11-16 (kb/research/files/R24/); te.com product pages via page fetch; tools/lcsc.py C592838. Newark CAD at qty 1/10/100: 174917-6 10.66/9.36/7.90, 178780-1 20.85/18.60/15.09, 353830-5 14.03/13.03/11.05. Aggregator data, so live pages should be checked before ordering.
suggested_fix: Name Newark/Farnell/RS/LCSC as the sources in INSTALL and the BOM. Quote 100-piece prices. Re-check stock the day before ordering.

title: 176122-6 (ordered 1999-2000 board) has no cut-quantity source
claim: The ordered 1999-2000 motherboard specifies TE 176122-6 (64-pos). Authorised distributors list it only as reels or trays (Avnet and Newark MOQ 1600, $9.2-10.1; Sager min 160, $12.61), with 0 stock. LCSC shows 0 stock at a bogus $0.04. The current rev 0.9 switched to the 76-pos 178780-1, which Newark stocks (160).
evidence: Findchips 176122-6 and 178780-1 snapshots 2026-11-16; README.md line 176 says the car's own header is the 64-pos 176122-6.
suggested_fix: For the ordered boards, check that the 178780-1 or 174915-6 footprint matches before substituting. Ballenger CONN-100747 (64-way NA header, $29.99 in stock) may be the equivalent, but its identity is unverified. Request Sager/Mouser quotes for 10-20 pieces of 176122-6 or 174518-7.

title: Salvaging headers or a core programme is uneconomic
claim: Used ECUs cost about $150-190 (NA6/NB1) and $285-450 (NB2, some immobilizer-locked), against $6-15 for a new header. Salvaging the header costs far more than buying one. A core programme is justified only if the donor case is wanted, which a $12-35 new shell does better.
evidence: eBay.ca B61 $189.99; Redline BP4W $149.99; Importapart $169.99/$284.99; Redline BTT3 $399.99; Partrequest $449.90. Asking prices (secondary-source search results), not sold prices. Desoldering time estimated at 10-20 min, with no source.
suggested_fix: Do not plan a core programme. Buy 2-3 used ECUs only to measure the case outline, hole pattern and height.

title: Hobby vendors do not sell the 48-way header; clone quality unknown
claim: Ballenger sells 64-way NA ($29.99) and 72-way NB ($59.99, special order) ECU headers without terminals, and no 48-way. Loopy's NB board with connector ($85) has been sold out since 2026-09-14. rusEFI says it neither makes nor stocks Miata hardware. Kinkong's 174917-6 clone is quote-only with no brand or plating stated, and no quality reports were found anywhere.
evidence: bmotorsports.com products 3454 and 4740; tindie.com Loopy listing; wiki.rusefi.com/Miata; kinkong-connector.com page ID7458.
suggested_fix: Use TE genuine from Newark/RS. If a clone is considered, test a sample for pin fit, retention force and plating first.

title: Conflicting descriptions of what 174917-6 is
claim: Digi-Key calls 174917-6 a 3.50 mm pitch right-angle header, RS and Farnell call it a 'female housing', Newark mislabels it 'Rcpt 40Pos', and LCSC says pitch 4.5 mm. TE's description is 'Hybrid I/O cap assy 48P'. Pitch and gender are inconsistent across sources and were not checked against the TE drawing.
evidence: Search results and snapshots 2026-11-16; TE page summary.
suggested_fix: Open the TE product drawing (te.com 174917-6 drawing PDF) and confirm pitch, row spacing and contacts against the footprint before reorder.

title: Customer-supplied stock case: high effort, no measured dimensions anywhere
refs: INSTALL.md section 3; rusEFI MRE wiki; Miata Turbo NB2 case thread
claim: Every hobby vendor (rusEFI, DIY-EFI, Alex Engineering, Speeduino) relies on the customer opening the stock case, removing the PCB and cutting USB/MAP/WB holes. No stock case outline, height or bracket pattern is published for any generation. A Miata Turbo poster found a Speeduino board slightly too tall for the case, and the rusEFI NA board needs a 3 x M4 washer stack at one screw because of a recessed thread. Fit risk for the 154x162 mm board is unmeasured.
evidence: wiki.rusefi.com/Legacy-Miata-NA-48-pin-board-for-MRE; miataturbo.net NB2 case dimensions thread (question only, no answers); R17 notes.
suggested_fix: Buy one used ECU per generation (about $190 / $400 / $285) and measure outline, holes, internal height and the heat-sink contact point before shipping. Offer an optional supplied shell.

title: Recommended enclosure path with numbers
claim: First 10 units: ship the board with an optional MJF-printed shell (est $20-35 each) and keep own-case reuse as a cheaper choice. At 100: a laser-cut and bent 5052 two-piece shell (est $12-25) or printed (est $12-25). Extruded Hammond 1455T2201 is about $42 plus end plates, so it costs more. An external ECU with adapter harness is about $60-100 more. All of these are estimates and need real quotes.
evidence: SendCutSend 5052 benchmarks ($8.38 at 10, $6.45 at 100 for a 9x6.6 in 0.063 in part); DigiKey Hammond 1455T2201 $42.25 (aggregator, June 2026); JLC3DP publishes no per-cm3 rate; UK MJF rate 0.20 GBP/cm3 (not JLC).
suggested_fix: Upload a CAD shell to JLC3DP and JLCCNC for quotes at 10 and 100. Measure the stock cases first. Compare to the BMM 3D-printed case at +$50 for billet.

title: Printed shell has no EMI shield and poor heat path
claim: A plastic shell loses the stock aluminium case's shielding and heat spreading. rusEFI's note about a heat sink under one case screw shows the stock case is a heat path, and the repo flags the 1989-93 paired wiring as the hottest case. If a printed shell is used, it needs a metal lid or plate and a thermal pad to the hot parts.
evidence: rusEFI NA 48-pin wiki (heat sink at J27 location); review brief section 6 (hot case).
suggested_fix: Choose bent aluminium for the 1989-93 board, or add an aluminium lid with a thermal pad to the driver and regulator area.

title: 1123038-2 is a second 72-pos header option
claim: The Speeduino and rusEFI wikis list TE 1123038-2 (040 III HD 72-pos cap assy, tin) as an alternative to 353830-5. Authorised sources show Avnet and RS at MOQ 2520 and 0 stock ($7.95-8.64). Footprint equivalence was not checked.
evidence: Findchips 1123038-2 snapshot 2026-11-16; Speeduino ECU Connectors page (search result).
suggested_fix: Prefer 353830-5 (stocked). Compare TE drawings before any substitution.

title: Use metal-in shielding bags, not pink bags, for the populated stack
claim: Pink antistatic poly only limits charging of the bag. Uline's pink 8x10 bag is listed 'does not meet MIL-PRF-81705D & E'. Shielding bags (MIL-STD-3010, ANSI/ESD S20.20) block external fields. They cost $0.056 (LCSC 210x240) to $0.57 (Uline 9x12 reclosable).
evidence: Uline S-5891 vs S-2149/S-2509 (fetched 2026-11-16); LCSC C7543868; vendor ESD comparisons (secondary)
suggested_fix: Ship every unit in a zip shield bag; put a 1/8 in pink foam pouch (Uline S-12583, $0.33-0.39) inside against pin punctures.

title: 9x9x4 in RSC is the right stock box for 25 mm cushioning
claim: Inside 229x229x102 mm leaves 37/33 mm sideways and 33 mm above and below the 154x162x35 stack, enough for 25 mm foam. 10x10x4 and 12x12x4 are larger and heavier for no benefit.
evidence: Uline S-21587, S-4595, S-4346 pages; geometry computed
suggested_fix: Order 9x9x4 32 ECT for spec A, 200 lb test for spec B.

title: ESD pick-and-pluck foam from US stock dominates pack cost
claim: A 24x24x1 in sheet is $15 (6+ cartons $13). At 4 pads of 9x9 per sheet, a top+bottom kit costs about $7.5. Custom die-cut EPE/EVA kits are listed at about $0.2-1.3 per piece with an MOQ of about 100 and need resistance test data.
evidence: Uline BL_8006 table; Alibaba listings via search (UNVERIFIED)
suggested_fix: Use cradle plus bubble at 25 units; order a custom die-cut kit once the run is 100 or more; request surface resistance data.

title: UPS/FedEx bill 3-4 lb dimensional weight; USPS does not
claim: Rounded up that is 10x10x5 = 500 in3, which is 4 lb at divisor 139. Rounded to nearest it is 405 in3, 3 lb. Actual packed weight is about 1-1.5 lb. USPS applies DIM only above 1,728 in3, so these boxes are weight-priced.
evidence: USPS DMM 283 (7-12-26) and FedEx page fetched; UPS divisor only from secondary summaries
suggested_fix: Default to USPS Ground Advantage for domestic parcels; keep the box at or below 9x9x4 outside; compare UPS/FedEx quotes.

title: Cost per shipped unit for three specs
claim: Materials per unit at 25/100/500: A cheapest safe $1.33/1.33/1.31; B recommended $3.58/3.26/2.93; C premium $11.87/6.16/5.20. Several lines are my estimates (tape, labels, custom foam).
evidence: notes section 7, cost.py in work/R25-packaging-design
suggested_fix: Start with B; use A only if drop test passes.

title: Foam must carry load at standoff points and rim, not on pins
refs: HD1-HD4, harness header, MLCCs near mounting holes and edges
claim: Standard X7R MLCCs crack at 2-3 mm board bend (flex-termination 5-10 mm, vendor claims). The 1.6 mm 154x162 board with a heavy header is the flex risk. Pins under the board and the header latch must not bear load.
evidence: Syfer/AVX/Vishay/NASA summaries via search (secondary); kb/interconnect.md standoff geometry
suggested_fix: Design the foam cavity to support at HD1-HD4 and rim with pin relief. Ask the layout reviewers to check MLCC placement near holes and edges.

title: Weight estimate lower than the task assumption
claim: FR4 mass estimates (74 g + 28 g) plus connectors give about 180 g (range 170-260 g), not 250-400 g. Packed weights come to 0.45-0.65 kg.
evidence: computation, density 1.85 g/cm3; header and MAP masses unverified
suggested_fix: Weigh the first real stack and update DIM calculations.

title: Moisture and tamper accessories are cheap but need minimum buys
claim: Humidity cards $37/200; 1/6 unit desiccant $150/1,200 ($0.125 each); tamper labels $36 per 100 (not for plastic surfaces); tamper tape needs 18 rolls minimum. A shield bag is not a moisture barrier bag.
evidence: Uline pages fetched 2026-11-16
suggested_fix: Use tamper labels and the humidity card only in the premium spec or for sea freight.

title: Home drop and vibration test procedure
claim: Test a dummy stack in the packed box: about 10 drops from 76 cm (corner, edges, faces) plus rough-road vibration, and check pins, MLCC values and cracks. The ISTA drop heights come from third-party summaries and I did not read ISTA itself.
evidence: hqts and ISTA summary pages via search
suggested_fix: Run before the first sale; escalate the spec on any failure.

title: Domestic budget about 15 USD per order
refs: USPS Ground Advantage, Signature Confirmation, insurance
claim: USPS Ground Advantage commercial for <16 oz is 7.33-8.95 USD (zones 1-9), retail 10.05-13.65. Add Signature Confirmation 4.15 and insurance to 399 USD at 6.05, plus a box. All-in about 14-18 USD, i.e. 3.5-4.5% of the price.
evidence: https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/Notice123.htm (Notice 123 effective 2026-10-04, includes holiday increase to 2027-01-17); kb/research/files/R26/usps_notice123_2026-10-04.txt
suggested_fix: Quote free domestic shipping in the 399 price. Buy labels via a discounted platform (commercial prices). Re-check after 2027-01-17, when the temporary increase ends.

title: Include 399 USD cover and a signature; 100 USD is included only
claim: USPS includes only 100 USD of cover. Full cover to 399 costs 6.05 (USPS fee table) and Signature Confirmation 4.15 electronic. Without them a loss or porch theft leaves about 299 USD uninsured.
evidence: Notice 123 insurance table (300.01-400 = 6.05) and usps.com insurance-extra-services page; ParcelGuard 0.55 per 100 is a vendor claim
suggested_fix: Always buy Signature Confirmation plus cover to full value. Compare third-party cover (about 2.20 per 399 USD, unverified).

title: UPS/FedEx are not competitive for this parcel
refs: UPS Ground Saver, FedEx Ground Economy
claim: At 189 cu in with divisor 139 (secondary), UPS/FedEx bill 2 lb. List 1 lb prices are 12-16 USD (secondary). USPS commercial is 7-9 USD.
evidence: UPS/FedEx PDFs returned Access Denied. Aggregator figures: darrigoconsulting, ship.com, branvas
suggested_fix: Use USPS GA, or Priority as the premium option (9.44-16.07 commercial, 1 lb).

title: International shipping cost, with full-value cover
claim: Retail FCPIS 9-16 oz: Canada 26.00, UK 31.95, DE 29.95, FR 29.40, JP 33.95, AU/NZ 41.25. PMI 1 lb: Canada 43.55, AU/NZ 70.65, JP 66.05, FR 69.50, UK 69.70, DE 82.30. PMI includes 200 USD cover; 17.55 more reaches 400. Full-cover PMI is about 61 USD to Canada and about 87 USD to the UK.
evidence: Notice 123 international tables and country price groups (Canada 1, AU/NZ 12, FR 15, DE 16, JP 17, UK 20)
suggested_fix: Charge calculated or zone-flat international shipping; do not absorb it. Use PMI or PMEI for insured service. Verify whether FCPIS can be insured (not found).

title: USPS DDP exists for Canada, Germany, UK and many EU countries, not AU/NZ/JP
claim: From 2026-07-01 USPS DDP covers PMEI, PMI and FCPIS. It is required for dutiable items to FR, BE, DK, FI, PT, LU and others, and to Germany. It is optional for AT, IT, NL, ES, SE and Canada. UK is available only for 135-900 GBP on PMI/PMEI. No fee is stated. Australia, NZ and Japan are not listed.
evidence: https://about.usps.com/postal-bulletin/2026/pb22707/html/updt_002.htm
suggested_fix: Use DDP where offered so buyers get no border bill. For AU/NZ/JP warn buyers of GST/consumption tax, or use an express DDP service. Express DDP fees (DHL min 17 USD, UPS 2%/min 7-11.5, FedEx 15 USD or 2%) are secondary and unverified.

title: Buyers pay import VAT at the border for a 399 USD item almost everywhere
refs: UK, EU, Canada, AU, NZ, JP
claim: UK point-of-sale VAT covers only consignments up to 135 GBP; EU IOSS and the 3 EUR duty target consignments up to 150 EUR; 399 USD is above both. So the UK and EU buyer pays import VAT (UK 20%, duty 2%) plus carrier fees (Royal Mail 8 GBP and similar, secondary). AU (A$1000) and NZ (NZ$1000) low-value regimes do cover this item, but seller registration applies only above 75,000 AUD / 60,000 NZD of sales.
evidence: gov.uk VAT and overseas goods page; UK trade tariff API; Consilium and ATO/IRD only via search snippets (direct fetches blocked)
suggested_fix: State on the store that import taxes are the buyer's. Offer DDP where available.

title: US de minimis suspended for all countries and modes; China boards pay 2.7% + 12.5% at least
refs: CBP interim final rules 2026-12669/12670; USTR Section 301 notice 2026-15181
claim: The de minimis exemption is indefinitely suspended: non-postal from 2026-06-24, mail from 2026-07-24 (new postal informal entry). A 12.5% Section 301 forced-labour tariff on products of China applies from 2026-07-24. With the 2.7% MFN rate, assembled controller boards would pay at least 15.2%, plus 25% if the HTS is on a legacy 301 list (not verified).
evidence: Federal Register API documents 2026-12670, 2026-12669 and 2026-15181; USITC HTS API
suggested_fix: Budget at least 15% duty on Chinese-made assembled boards. Check the legacy 301 list for the chosen HTS. Plan formal entry with a broker. Ask JLCPCB/the courier for DDP quotes.

title: Free shipping vs calculated shipping policy
claim: Domestic shipping is about 4% of the 399 price, so build it in (free shipping). International is 26-87 USD, 7-22% of the price, so charge it separately or by zone. Returns cost about the outbound price each way, and international returns add customs hassle.
evidence: Notice 123 numbers above
suggested_fix: Domestic free; international calculated at checkout with taxes disclosed.

title: Dimensions and weight fit the cheapest tiers
claim: The parcel is 0.109 cu ft, so it is well below dimensional-weight thresholds (USPS 1 cu ft). Staying under 16 oz keeps the lowest GA price. Priced weight over 16 oz moves to the 1 lb+ rows (8.01-11.22 commercial).
evidence: Notice 123 GA commercial table
suggested_fix: Weigh the packed box. Keep it under 16 oz (about 450 g).

title: No public teardown of any aftermarket ECU board found
refs: Link G4X, Haltech Elite, EMU Black, MaxxECU, AEM, Syvecs, ME442
claim: Searched standard and extended modes, vendor docs, forums and FCC-ID: no board photo or IC identification of any aftermarket ECU exists in reachable sources. Their internals are known only through spec sheets. Any claim about what competitors use for these is unverified.
evidence: R29 notes section 3; dl/fcc_search_*.html returned only wireless products
suggested_fix: Do not cite competitor driver ICs in the store or docs. If real data is wanted, buy or borrow one unit and photograph it.

title: 1990 Mazda ECU power stage is fully discrete
refs: 079721-2351 (B63H): T712/T722 2SD1415, T001 stud-mounted to case, 684K100 film caps, HC244 block
claim: The 1990 Miata ECU uses discrete Darlington injector drivers bolted to the aluminium case, TO-92/TO-126 pre-drivers, custom Mazda ASICs, 74HC/4000 logic, film caps plus radial electrolytics, a 27 V 5 W zener (value 'about', per netlist) and no multi-channel driver IC.
evidence: third-party KiCad netlist 079721-2351.xml; photo crops work/R29-ecu-teardown-survey/img/b63h_crop_*.png (684K100 and 'HC244 9L17' legible; 2SD1415 type not legible, from netlist)
suggested_fix: None required; use as reference for what the stock injector stage can drive.

title: 1999 NB1 ECU internals mostly unidentified
claim: Only CPU (160-pin semi-custom D151806-5740) and flash (Fujitsu 29F200BA) are identified; both are coated. Power transistors are tab-mounted but their markings are not legible. NB driver and ignition parts remain unknown.
evidence: vkmotorsports.com 2019-05-22 post and photos (saved in kb/research/files/R29/bp5r_*.jpeg)
suggested_fix: Rely on FSM voltage/current data (R17-R19) rather than assumed stock driver types.

title: Shipped/open designs use single or dual drivers, never multi-channel ICs
refs: MS2 V3.0 BOM, rusEFI Hellen, Speeduino, Trionic 5.5
claim: MS2 V3.0: IRFIZ34G + IXDI404 gate driver; rusEFI: ZXMS6005/AUIPS2041 then VNLD5090 duals; Speeduino: VNLD5090 duals; Trionic 5.5 (secondary source): 10 x MTD3055VL DPAK. Multi-channel ICs (L9842, TLE8104/8110, MC33810) are not used in low-cost ECUs and are not stocked at JLC.
evidence: msextra MS2V30_Hardware-3.4.pdf p.197-200; R01/R03/R08; Wikipedia Trionic_T5.5
suggested_fix: Keep single-channel drivers; pursue R08 cheaper replacements.

title: Per-channel injector cost is above what shipped designs spend
claim: Project spends about USD 2.06 (VND7NV04) plus ES1D and 1.5SMC16A clamp per injector channel (about USD 3), vs rusEFI Hellen NA6 using ZXMS6005 at about USD 0.35-0.74 with no external clamp. Self-clamped single-channel parts are the norm.
evidence: evidence/cur_db/sch_bom_grouped.csv; R08 table (VND7NV04 2.06 @30, ZXMS6005DGQ 0.355); R01 hellen-one output module
suggested_fix: Adopt R08 replacement; evaluate dropping ES1D + 1.5SMC16A once the driver clamp energy is checked against real injector inductance (unknown, 8 vs 20 mH).

title: MegaSquirt V3.0 protection set is smaller than this project's
refs: MS2 V3.0 BOM: MOV1 22 V, 7 x 1N4001, 24/36/22 V 1 W zeners, 2 x RXE050 polyswitch
claim: A long-running kit ECU protects with a 22 V 20 mm MOV, series 1N4001 diodes, several 1 W zeners and two 0.5 A polyswitches; no per-input TVS. This project's SMCJ30A + SMAJ33A + B360A + SS34 + 33 V polyfuse is at least as strong.
evidence: ms2v30.pdf p.197-200 (copy in kb/research/files/R29/)
suggested_fix: No change; do not add protection parts on the basis of competitor practice.

title: EMU Black claims AEC-Q100 grade 2 and ISO 7637 immunity
claim: ECUMaster specifies 6-22 V, immunity to ISO 7637 transients, AEC-Q100 grade 2 (-40..+105 C), IP60 aluminium, user-fitted 5 A/15 A fuses. If store copy implies 'automotive grade', most JLC parts here are not AEC-Q qualified (not checked part by part).
evidence: kb/research/files/R29/emu_black_manual.txt lines 62-67
suggested_fix: Avoid 'automotive-grade' wording in store copy; document the fuse recommendation.

title: MaxxECU GEN2 RACE: IP68 case, Superseal 1.0, 30 V flyback regulation
claim: Sealed aftermarket ECUs use IP68 aluminium and Superseal; injector outputs 10 A peak/5 A continuous with 30 V auto-regulated flyback and short-circuit protection. The stock-case, cabin-mounted approach here needs none of this, matching the unsealed Mazda original.
evidence: dl/web/maxx.txt lines 61-64, 144-157
suggested_fix: None.

title: All-ceramic daughterboard avoids the classic ECU capacitor age failure
claim: The 1990 Mazda ECU uses radial aluminium electrolytics (33/47/220 uF) of the kind reported leaking in 1990s Japanese ECUs; the daughterboard has no aluminium electrolytics. Failure statistics specific to Miata ECUs not found (forum-level only).
evidence: B63H netlist C2, C4, C7, C801; sch_bom_grouped.csv; R16 forum titles
suggested_fix: Optional documentation point; claim cautiously.

title: Conformal coating: only anecdotal evidence in shipped ECUs
refs: NB1 CPU/flash coating; EMU Black reseller claim
claim: NB1 CPU and flash carry a coating compound (author text). EMU Black 'protective coating' is a reseller statement. No documented coating process found for low-cost ECUs, so no coating is not out of line for a cabin-mounted unit.
evidence: vkmotorsports.com post; tegiwa.com search snippet
suggested_fix: Consider coating only if the humidity analysis in R07/R25 calls for it.

title: Survey wrong: Hellen Miata boards use ZXMS6005SGTA injector drivers, not AUIPS2041L
claim: All four Hellen Miata BOM-replace files swap injector drivers Q305-Q312 to ZXMS6005SGTA (60/65/70 V clamp, 480 mJ, ILIM min 2.2 A at 3 V gate / 3.3 A at 5 V, 150-200 mOhm). The survey's AUIPS2041L (1.4 A) reasoning does not describe the shipped boards.
evidence: ext/hellen-miata-NA6/bom_replace_hellen64_NA6_94-d.csv, NB1-c, NB2-f, NA8-a; ZXMS6005SG datasheet kb/research/files/R30/ZXMS6005SGTA_C174042.pdf
suggested_fix: Correct the survey table and the clamp-voltage comparison (60-70 V, not 63-75 V of a sibling part).

title: Survey wrong: suffix-7 STM32 is used by NB1 and 1996-97 Hellen boards
refs: U105 STM32F407ZGT7 C1337111 vs project F407VGT6
claim: hellen-miata-NB1 rev c and hellen-miata-NA8 rev A are built with STM32F407ZGT7 (-40..105 C, JLC extended, 34 in stock, USD 27.80@1) against 6.26 for the -6 grade, so 'nobody uses the 105 C grade' is false; the owner's processor decision (VGT6) was justified partly by this claim.
evidence: bom_replace_64_NB1-c.csv and bom_replace_64_NA8_96-a.csv line U105; tools/lcsc.py C1337111, C19156
suggested_fix: Fix the survey; re-state the grade decision as cost (about USD 20 per board on the sibling part) vs margin, not as 'everyone does it'.

title: rusEFI 1996-97 board exists (hellen-miata-NA8), survey omits it
claim: Hellen NA96 rev A exists, wiki calls it 'somewhat abandoned'; ZXMS6005 injectors, F407ZGT7, tach from PP2 push-pull, options port 4A-4L. Speeduino has only an NA6 (89-95) PNP; no Speeduino NB board was found.
evidence: cloned repo hellen64_NA8_96.xml; wiki_Hellen-NA96.md; Speeduino ext/speeduino-hardware/PNPs only 'Miata NA6'
suggested_fix: Add the board to the survey as a comparison for 1996-97.

title: 1996-2005 tach and alternator: project open-collector without pull-up, Hellen drives push-pull 12 V
refs: OUT_TACH 4L/2K/3O, OUT_ALT 1O/3M; Hellen OUT_PP2 tach, OUT_PP1 alternator
claim: Hellen NA8/NB1/NB2 drive the tach from PP2 and the NB alternator from PP1 (TC4427 push-pull on +12V_PROT). The project uses open-collector low sides and only the 1989-95 board has a 1k pull-up (R37). If the cluster or regulator input does not idle high, the tach reads zero. Whether the car supplies a pull-up is not known.
evidence: nb1_nets.txt /OUT_TACH M5.S6(OUT_PP2), /OUT_ALTERNATOR M5.W6(OUT_PP1); NB2/NA8 same; kb/interconnect.md mb9697/mb9900/mb0105 parts lists (no tach pull-up)
suggested_fix: Fit an R to VBAT_IN (1k, as R37) or a jumper-selectable push-pull on 1996-2005 tach/alternator, keep tach default off until checked on a car.

title: Pin-table conflicts on 1999-2000: 1U and 3Q
refs: 1U OUT_VVT, 3Q OUT_MAINRLY vs rusEFI NB1 1U front O2 heater, 3Q VICS, 4E VVT
claim: rusEFI's NB1 table and netlist put VICS on 3Q and VVT on 4E, and the front O2 heater on 1U; the project maps 1U to a VVT output and 3Q to the main-relay output (J5.5). One of the two tables is wrong; a wrong output on a heater or VICS wire could matter.
evidence: repo/firmware/ext/rusefi/.../hellenMiataNB1/connectors/main.yaml; nb1_nets.txt /OUT_VICS P2.47(3Q), /OUT_VVT P2.67(4E); kb/interconnect.md lines 576-656
suggested_fix: Check against the 1999-2000 Miata wiring diagram before first power-up; leave the cavities unconnected until confirmed.

title: 1996-97: knock cavity and 3M VVT output unresolved vs rusEFI NA8 table
claim: rusEFI NA8 lists a knock input at 1S (ts_name '2M - KNOCK'); the project has no knock pad on 1996-97 and routes OUT_VVT to 3M (= rusEFI 2M by the cavity offset). The 1996-97 engine has no VVT.
evidence: hellenMiataNA96/connectors/main.yaml; kb/interconnect.md lines 374-455
suggested_fix: Check against the 1996-97 wiring diagram; if 3M is knock, route it to IN_KNOCK instead of an output.

title: Survey 'nobody puts two drivers on one wire' is true only by default
refs: Hellen NA6 R12, R17 (DNP), R25, R26
claim: The Hellen NA6 frame has DNP 0-ohm footprints tying OUT_INJ1 to OUT_INJ3 and OUT_INJ2 to OUT_INJ4, so a paired-driver option exists; default build is one driver per wire, as the survey says.
evidence: na6_nets.txt /OUT_INJ3: M5.S17 R12.1 R26.1; /OUT_INJ1 includes R12.2; comps R12/R17 'MyCommnet=DNP'
suggested_fix: Reword the survey.

title: Project-unique injector clamp: improvement vs all proven boards, with cost and risk
claim: Hellen (ZXMS6005, 60-70 V, 480 mJ) and Speeduino (VNLD5090) use no external injector clamp; the project's per-injector diode+TVS to battery is a deviation from every proven board. Improvement: 8.8 vs 15.3 mJ in the driver (repo simulation). Cost: 8 parts and 0.16 ms slower closing (dead-time retune). Risk: untested, TVS is a 150 C part.
