evidence: daughterboard README rev 0.10; Hellen/Speeduino netlists show no external clamp
suggested_fix: Keep only if the simulation is trusted; otherwise compare cost of removing 8 parts against the thermal margin.

title: Trigger pull-ups: project 1k matches Speeduino, stronger than Hellen
refs: IN_HALL1/2 pull-up; Hellen R3, PULL_CRANK; Speeduino R33/R34
claim: Hellen: crank 680k via module PULL_CRANK (+ LED path), cam 4.7k (R3) to +5VA, 4.7k series, SRV05-4 ESD. Speeduino: 220R series, SP720, 1k to +5V. Project: 1k via protected 5V, 4.7k series, 1N4148 clamp. No deviation of concern.
evidence: na6_nets.txt IN_CAM R3.1(+5VA); input module schematic; sp_na6.kicad_pcb R33/R34/R35/R36
suggested_fix: None; note that Hellen's crank 680k works on the NA6 in the field, so the CAS may supply its own pull-up (not checked).

title: 1989-95 tach: Hellen and Speeduino also drive 1k to +12V, Hellen fits it by default
refs: R37 1k, JP5; Hellen R21/R27/R24/R48; Speeduino R53/JP1
claim: All three boards drive the tach as an open-collector output with a 1k pull-up to +12V; the direction question (rusEFI wiki says input) is shared. The project ships it off; Hellen NA6 fits all tach jumpers (0R, LCSC C17477) by default.
evidence: na6_nets.txt Net-(R24-Pad2): R24.2 R27.1 R48.1, R21 1k to +12V_PROT; sp_na6.kicad_pcb R53 1k 12V-SW, JP1
suggested_fix: Keep default off; resolve direction from the wiring diagram.

title: Idle valve flyback: all proven boards use an on-board Schottky to +12V, as the project does
refs: D1 SS34; Hellen D25/D36 B5819W; Speeduino D15 NBRS2H100
claim: Hellen (B5819W 1 A 40 V to +12V_PROT), Speeduino (2 A 100 V to 12V-SW) and the project (SS34 3 A 40 V to VBAT_IN) all freewheel on the board; no deviation. The NB2 IAC/OCV feed fuses (2 A F2/F3) are project-only.
evidence: na6/nb2/na8 nets /OUT_IDLE D25.2(A); sp_na6 D15; kb/interconnect.md D1,D2,F2,F3
suggested_fix: None.

title: Protected ignition outputs and 5 V level-shifted gates are project-only
claim: Hellen ign8 is LVC4245 + 10R straight to the igniter; Speeduino is TC4424A + 2.4k. Hellen injector gates are driven from the 3.3 V MCU net. The project's extra protection and 5 V gates are improvements for fault tolerance and Rds(on), at the cost of about a dozen more parts and untested drive timing.
evidence: ign8 BOM (10R x8, U460 LVC4245); output module schematic; daughterboard README rev 0.8
suggested_fix: Optional: assess if the extra parts are worth it for the ignition path.

title: A/C: project reads a 12 V switch, Hellen a 5V pull-up input, Speeduino hard-wires A/C through
refs: IN_SW2 vs Hellen IN_AUX3 / Speeduino AC-Jump
claim: Hellen A/C request: 4.7k series, SRV05-4, 10k pull-up to 5VA; Speeduino bridges J1 pins 9 and 29; project: 4.7k to VBAT and 22k/10k divider. Both Hellen and project accept a 12 V signal; logic is firmware in all.
evidence: na6_nets.txt /IN_AC_SW, M1.J8(PULL_AUX3) on +5VA; sp_na6 AC-Jump J1.9 J1.29
suggested_fix: None; document that Speeduino does not interpose.

title: Closed-maker rows (AMP, ME221, Link) not re-verifiable today
refs: survey rows AMP EFI, ME221, Link MX5X
claim: Maker pages returned 403/429 or said nothing on alternator, A/C, fans, tach, knock; those survey statements stay unverified.
evidence: page fetch results this pass
suggested_fix: Re-read maker PDFs if those rows are to be relied on.

title: Shorted sensor 5 V destroyed a Hellen NA6
refs: U14 TLS115 harness 5 V; stock TPS
claim: A customer left the stock non-variable TPS connected on a Hellen NA6. Sensor 5 V shorted to ground and the board was damaged. The reporter wrote there was no circuit protection on any +5 V output. Rev C added a tracker regulator. The README says this project has a protected harness 5 V (U14).
evidence: https://github.com/rusefi/hellenNA6_issues/issues/22 ; https://github.com/andreika-git/hellen-one/issues/119
suggested_fix: Production test: short each sensor 5 V cavity to ground and to +12 V on a sample unit. Install guide: identify and remove stock TPS wiring.

title: Long dwell at sync loss and stuck ignition after clock failure are open upstream
claim: uaEFI shows 150-460 ms dwell at sync loss while cranking. rusEFI discussions say an oscillator or PLL failure can leave ignition outputs stuck active. Proposed cures include CSS, a hardware watchdog and an MC33810 ignition IC. Two smoke incidents were reported. One was an M73 board with hardware damage and one an IGBT set on fire. Causes were not established.
evidence: https://github.com/rusefi/rusefi/issues/6349 ; /5730 ; /5728 ; /5729 ; https://www.rusefi.com/forum/viewtopic.php?p=48645
suggested_fix: First-article test: short the oscillator and check ignition pins go low. Check the pinned firmware for a dwell cap and CSS. Use a spare coil or igniter at first start.

title: USB drops and FATAL under EMI have no board-level cure upstream
claim: hellen88bmw (4-layer) showed red FATAL and a USB descriptor failure next to a 3-phase VFD. Proteus lost the TunerStudio link when the engine ran. A USB isolator (ADuM3160) cured it for the reporter and a second forum user, a single post. Maintainers could not reproduce it on the bench.
evidence: https://github.com/rusefi/rusefi/issues/4310 ; https://www.rusefi.com/forum/viewtopic.php?p=47554 ; https://www.rusefi.com/forum/viewtopic.php?p=48645
suggested_fix: Support page: use a battery-powered laptop or a USB isolator, keep the cable short. Bench-test USB with a coil firing. Check the USB-C ESD and filter parts in the design.

title: Load-dump crowbar on H72 failed short at about 22 V on the bench
refs: power input TVS, F1, PTC fuses
claim: A reporter ramped a bench supply on an h72b and heard a pop at about 22 V. The fault measured 0.5-0.7 ohm. The TVS was fine, and removing the crowbar MOSFETs cleared the short. The maintainer said the power12 module is the same on B and C. Hellen documents more than 24 V may damage the module.
evidence: https://github.com/andreika-git/hellen-one/issues/47 ; /121
suggested_fix: Bench-test the 24 V jump-start and 35 V load-dump cases with current limiting on a first article. Resolve the documented open item on PTC fuse ratings of 24-33 V.

title: Low-side output driver failures: backfeed, shorts and second sources
claim: The ULN2003 does not survive a short to +12 V (hellen-one #360). The alternator push-pull output fed energy back into MCU pins on the NB2, and the series 1k added as the fix later stopped the alternator charging. A ZXMS6005 substitute for the AUIPS2041 was not pin-compatible when the tab is used. A live wire can back-power the board through an output diode.
evidence: https://github.com/andreika-git/hellen-one/issues/360 ; https://github.com/rusefi/hellen-NB2-issues/issues/23 ; https://github.com/rusefi/hellen-NB1-issues/issues/29 ; https://github.com/rusefi/hellen-NB2-issues/issues/34 ; /20
suggested_fix: Keep alternator control off by default. Do not add series R on a field line without a charging test. Forbid substitute driver parts at JLCPCB. Test every output for back-feed on the key-off state.

title: JLCPCB assembly problems seen on Hellen boards
claim: On a Hellen NA6 rev B, a wideband analog input read 0 V from a poor resistor joint plus a flux blob on an MCU pin. JLC queried diode polarity during production. An NB2 was built with LMV324 instead of MCP6004. Only the polarity queries relate to rotation. I found no public rotated-part failure for these boards.
evidence: https://github.com/rusefi/hellenNA6_issues/issues/29 ; /23 ; https://github.com/rusefi/hellen-NB2-issues/issues/4
suggested_fix: Check the JLC placement preview, inspect the first article for flux and joints, allow no substitutions, and test every analog input against a known voltage.

title: Wideband module behaviour on USB-only power and cable faults
claim: rusEFI wideband #71 reports the module falling into SensorUnderheat with no way out when the ECU is powered from USB only. The thread's explanation is heater supply 0 V with Force heating set. The issue is still open. A uaEFI wideband that blinked once was a poorly pinned cable. Single units transmit as dual, using CAN IDs 190-193.
evidence: https://github.com/rusefi/wideband/issues/71 ; /65 ; /67
suggested_fix: Test the wideband on USB-only power and after engine start. Pin the wideband firmware version. Continuity-test the sensor connector pins in production.

title: F407 DFU entry failed with a slow 8 MHz crystal, and bootloader behaviour differs by batch
claim: The F407 ROM bootloader waits about 800 us for the HSE. The 8 MHz crystal needed about 900 us, so the bootloader reset. Hellen moved to a 20 MHz crystal. Separately, two assembly batches with the same MCU part number differ in auto-reboot after DFU. Whether this project's crystal avoids the problem was not checked.
evidence: https://github.com/andreika-git/hellen-one/issues/79 ; https://github.com/rusefi/hellen-NB2-issues/issues/5 ; https://github.com/rusefi/rusefi/issues/4847
suggested_fix: Check the crystal frequency and start-up time in the design. Test DFU entry on every unit, with BOOT button and by software.

title: Speeduino Miata PNP forum record: failures are mostly installation errors
claim: Forum answers say there are hundreds of units and issues are generally user error. One fuel pump driver was killed because the installer left the fuse in. A UA4C IAC needed a flyback diode. A 0.4.4c lost all ignition outputs with LEDs lit solid and the cause was not found. This is the evidence quality available: single posts, no per-unit failure rate.
evidence: https://speeduino.com/forum/viewtopic.php?t=4583 ; https://speeduino.com/forum/viewtopic.php?t=4426
suggested_fix: Install guide: fuse out and wiring check list. Handle the IAC valve flyback and idle valve in the motherboards. Ship with a first-power procedure using a current-limited supply.

title: Recommended production test and support list from field history
claim: The public failure record maps to a per-unit test list: sensor 5 V short, continuity of every hand-fitted connector pin, DFU entry, SD card, wideband heater test, analog input check, USB with the engine on, and ignition outputs low at clock failure. Add a wiring-first-power checklist and a returns policy for ESD and arrival damage, for which I found no public cases.
evidence: Case table C1-C33 in kb/research/R31-field-failures-open-ecus.md
suggested_fix: Write the test list into the assembly procedure and keep a fault log per serial number.
